column1: It is vital to your continued existence.  Which may not continue much longer with foolish notions like these.
column2: 此物攸關你的存續。若總是存著這等愚蠢念頭，你的存續怕是撐不了多久。

column1: How can you part with something you do not possess?
column2: 你根本不曾擁有它，又怎能捨棄？

column1: It is in your possession.
column2: 此物你已持有。

column1: That is not here.
column2: 此處並無此物。

column1: If you had a purse, you would be able to acquire money to give away.
column2: 若你身上備有錢囊，方能取得錢財贈人。

column1: Never heard of such a coin.  Must be Turkish or some other heathen denomination.
column2: 從未聽聞這種錢幣，想必是土耳其或某個異教之地的幣制。

column1: You cannot give away what you do not possess.
column2: 你不曾擁有之物，如何贈與他人？

column1: It may be empty now, but a man's fortune can change. Best to hold onto it.
column2: 它此刻雖空，人的運勢終究會變，還是留著的好。

column1: Think carefully before offering to give away all that you have.
column2: 在提出捨盡所有之前，先仔細想清楚。

column1: To use it, you must recite the Message of the Rose.
column2: 若要使用它，你必須誦念玫瑰箴言。

column1: I see no reason to use it now.
column2: 此刻並無使用它的理由。

column1: You cannot use what you do not possess.
column2: 你不曾擁有之物，如何使用？

column1: You have no reason to do that.
column2: 你沒有理由這麼做。

column1: Talk to whom?
column2: 要與誰交談？

column1: There is no need.
column2: 沒有這個必要。

column1: Your horse is here.
column2: 你的坐騎就在此處。

column1: Your horse is not here.
column2: 你的坐騎不在此處。

column1: Mohammed has your mule.
column2: 你的騾子在穆罕默德那裡。

column1: Nay, you can ill afford the time to do so.  You must go on with your mission.
column2: 不可，你耗不起這時間。你必須繼續你的使命。

column1: Your mule is not here.
column2: 你的騾子不在此處。

column1: The word "%s" sounds familiar, yet I cannot fathom your purpose in it.
column2: 「%s」這個詞聽來耳熟，我卻猜不透你此意何指。

column1: Perhaps you should move closer.
column2: 或許你該再靠近一些。

column1: First, you must have it. I cannot simply conjure it out of thin air for you.
column2: 你得先擁有它才行。我不能憑空為你變出來。

column1: There is nothing of import to you here and urgent matters await you elsewhere.
column2: 此處並無要事，別處還有急事等著你。

column1: You have further fortifications and docks along the edge of the lake.  You may come here again someday, if happier times return.
column2: 湖畔另有防禦工事與碼頭。若有朝一日時局好轉，你或許還會再回到這裡。

column1: This is the ladies' tower and you have no business there at the moment whatsoever.
column2: 這是女眷居住的高塔，此刻你與此處毫無瓜葛。

column1: This is the front gate and tunnel, heavily guarded and sealed with gates and a portcullis.  You reach it through the outer courtyard.
column2: 這是前門與甬道，守衛森嚴，以城門與閘門封鎖。你得經外庭方能抵達。

column1: You have granted possession of this small tower room to me where only the brave dare to tread. And even then, with caution.
column2: 你已將這間小塔室賜給了我，唯有勇者敢踏入此地，即便如此，仍須萬分小心。

column1: This is the hilltop on which Camelot rests.
column2: 這是肯萊特城堡所在的山丘。

column1: It is your own room, King Arthur.
column2: 這是你自己的寢室，亞瑟王。

column1: Here is your Treasury.
column2: 這是你的寶庫。

column1: It is part of the road leading down the hill.  You will find yourself here soon enough, when your preparations are complete.
column2: 這是下山道路的一段。待你準備就緒，自然會來到此處。

column1: Often Gwenhyver may be found here, in the Queen's Bower.
column2: 昆海兒常在此處，這是後宮花園。

column1: This is the Chapel of the Two Gods.
column2: 這是雙神神殿。

column1: This is the lake that surrounds the peninsula on which Camelot sits.  Now it is nearly gone, dried to a few stagnant pools.
column2: 這是環繞肯萊特所在半島的湖泊。如今幾已乾涸，只剩幾窪死水。

column1: This is the inner courtyard.  You have no business there at present.
column2: 這是內庭，此刻你與此處無關。

column1: These protected grounds serve many purposes.  There are practice grounds for fighting and jousting, areas of garden, areas for animals in case of seige.  None of this is of import to your mission.
column2: 這片受保護的場地兼具多種用途：有供練武與馬上長槍比武的場地、花園，以及圍城時圈養牲畜之處。這些都與你的使命無關。

column1: This is the outer courtyard, adjacent to the stables.
column2: 這是外庭，緊鄰馬廄。

column1: Many of your soldiers barrack here.  Also, there are storage rooms.  But there is nothing you need here for this mission.
column2: 你的許多士兵駐紮於此，此處也有倉房。但此行你在這裡找不到需要的東西。

column1: 'Tis the floor plan of your stronghold, Camelot.  Waste no time in preparing for your vital mission, m'lord.
column2: 這是你的要塞肯萊特的平面圖。莫再蹉跎，速速為這攸關重大的使命做好準備，吾王。

column1: I am as I appear.
column2: 我便如你所見。

column1: If I mean for you to have it, you shall know.
column2: 若我有意讓你擁有它，你自會知曉。

column1: That pathetic whine tells me you are sorry.  But do not do it again!
column2: 那可憐兮兮的哀鳴，我曉得你是在道歉。但休得再犯！

column1: What for?
column2: 為了什麼？

column1: That did not sound like an apology.
column2: 那聽起來可不像道歉。

column1: Try that and I shall turn you into a slug!
column2: 膽敢一試，我便把你變成一隻鼻涕蟲！

column1: I am waiting for your apology.
column2: 我在等你道歉。

column1: You attempt a whine, but Merlin just sneers at you.
column2: 你試著哀鳴，梅林卻只對你冷笑。

column1: The search for the Grail will be long and difficult. Though I will not physically travel with you, my spirit will be with you to guide and advise as I am able.
column2: 尋找聖杯之路漫長而艱險。雖然我不會隨你同行，但我的心神將與你同在，盡我所能為你指引、獻策。

column1: Choose carefully where your search will take you, for once you leave Camelot, you may not return.
column2: 謹慎選擇你此行的去向，因為一旦離開肯萊特，你便無法回頭。

column1: Arthur, might it not be wise to make your farewell to Gwenhyver? Let it be so before I impart what you must know for the journey.
column2: 亞瑟，向昆海兒辭行，豈非明智之舉？在我告訴你此行所需知曉之事前，且先如此吧。

column1: You are nearly ready, but on a journey such as this you will require money. I will await you while you visit the Treasury.
column2: 你已幾近準備就緒，但這樣的旅程需要盤纏。你先去一趟寶庫，我在此等候。

column1: Your clothing will not do for a long journey. And what of Excaliber? Truly, I have much to tell you, but not until you are fully prepared.
column2: 你這身衣著不適合長途跋涉。還有，聖劍呢？說真的，我有許多話要告訴你，但得等你萬事俱備才行。

column1: Surely you would not dream of beginning a journey of such magnitude without the blessings of the gods? See to this, then return.
column2: 如此重大的旅程，你總不會夢想著在未得諸神庇佑之下便貿然啟程吧？先辦妥此事，再回來見我。

column1: Only half your preparations are complete. Return to me when you are in complete readiness.
column2: 你的準備才完成一半。待你萬事齊備，再回來見我。

column1: Your preparations are only begun. Finish what you must do. Then I will have more to tell you.
column2: 你的準備才剛起步。先把該做的事做完，我還有更多話要說。

column1: There is much I must tell you before you leave, but first, you have other preparations to make.
column2: 在你啟程之前，我還有許多話要告訴你，但你得先完成其他準備。

column1: When you are more fully prepared, return to this room. I will await you.
column2: 待你準備得更周全時，再回到這房裡來，我會在此等候。

column1: I am no mere man.  I am Merlin.
column2: 我並非凡人，我是梅林。

column1: You are most welcome.
column2: 不必言謝。

column1: Ah...hrmm....I am not the one to ask, Arthur. I know much of the world, but little about women.
column2: 啊……嗯……這事你問錯人了，亞瑟。我雖識盡天下事，卻不解女人心。

column1: It is, ahem, virgin territory for me. So to speak.
column2: 這，咳，對我來說是塊未曾涉足之地，算是這麼說吧。

column1: According to the writer of this scroll, a mule is of great value in Jerusalem. The writer says, 'so great is the value of a mule that is sure of foot and gentle of nature that it is above all the gold and treasures of the earth.' Sounds a bit exaggerated to me, but that is the gist of it.
column2: 依這卷軸的作者所言，騾子在耶路撒冷極為貴重。他寫道：『腳程穩健、性情溫馴的騾子，其價值凌駕世間一切金銀財寶之上。』依我看是誇張了些，但大意便是如此。

column1: My books are not for you to touch.  However, feel free to consult your own Liber ex Doctrina (known in the vulgar as the Book of Lore) whenever you like.
column2: 我的藏書不容你碰觸。不過，你儘可隨時翻閱自己那本《Liber ex Doctrina》——俗稱《智典》。

column1: I seek the ultimate answer to life, the universe and everything.
column2: 我在尋求生命、宇宙及萬事萬物的終極解答。

column1: Your land is cursed and only the Grail can cure it.
column2: 你的國土受了詛咒，唯有聖杯能夠解除。

column1: This symbol, the labarum, was commonly used by Roman soldiers with whom the worship of Mithras was extremely popular.
column2: 這個符號叫拉巴倫，羅馬士兵之間常見使用，米夏拉信仰在他們之中極為盛行。

column1: The circle with descending cross is the symbol of the goddess, Venus.  She is mentioned, I believe, in your Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 這個下垂十字加圓圈的符號，是女神維納斯的標識。我記得你的《Liber ex Doctrina》裡有提及她。

column1: This rug contains mystic symbols, primarily the pentangle - the five-pointed star.  Because it is made of a single unbroken line, it affords strong protection from spirits who cannot find a place to enter in.
column2: 這張地毯上有神秘的符號，主要是五芒星。因為它是由一筆不間斷的線畫成，能有力地防範鬼靈——牠們找不到縫隙可以侵入。

column1: There is a decorative pattern in the small rug.
column2: 小地毯上有一個裝飾圖案。

column1: There are a number of symbols in my room. Upon the tapestry is a fylfot and labarum, the symbol of Mithras. Upon the small square rug is another fylfot. Upon the large round rug is a pentacle and the symbol of Venus and a few others not worth mentioning.
column2: 我房裡有幾個符號。掛毯上是卍字紋與拉巴倫，也就是米夏拉的標識。小方地毯上是另一個卍字紋。大圓地毯上則有五芒星與維納斯的標識，還有幾個不值一提的。

column1: There are two rugs upon my floor.
column2: 我的地板上有兩張地毯。

column1: The beams are part of the roof structure of this tower.
column2: 這些橫樑是這座塔屋頂結構的一部分。

column1: As you see, my room is quite full.   Take care that you do not disturb any of the objects within.
column2: 如你所見，我這房裡東西不少。小心別碰亂了裡頭的物件。

column1: The scroll is written in ancient Aramaic which I am attempting to decipher. It seems to be a dissertation upon the value of mules.
column2: 這卷軸以古亞蘭文寫成，我正試著解讀。看來是一篇論述騾子價值的文章。

column1: England is a land of many tribes: Celts from Eire to the west and untamed Bretogne to the east, Jutes and Angles and Saxons settled in the south and east, wild Picts and Scots to the north, but alas, little is left of the conquering Romans.
column2: 英格蘭是諸多部族之地：西有愛爾蘭來的凱爾特人，東有未馴的布列塔尼人，南方與東方住著朱特人、盎格魯人與撒克遜人，北方則是狂野的皮克特人與蘇格蘭人——只可惜，昔日征服此地的羅馬人如今已所剩無幾。

column1: The scroll is from Jerusalem, written in Aramaic. You may read my translation of it, scribbled there in the margins.
column2: 這卷軸來自耶路撒冷，以亞蘭文寫成。我的譯文就潦草地寫在頁邊，你可以讀讀看。

column1: Both your horse and a pack mule are being readied for your journey.
column2: 你的坐騎與一頭馱運的騾子，都已為你此行備妥。

column1: Here I conduct my delicate experiments in alchemy. The table is covered with beakers and flasks.
column2: 我在這裡進行精細的煉金實驗。桌上擺滿了燒杯與燒瓶。

column1: Upon my desk is a scroll recently brought to me from the Far East.
column2: 我書桌上有一卷最近從遠東送來的卷軸。

column1: It is in the Far East, a very long way from here.
column2: 它在遠東，離這裡非常遙遠。

column1: I have bowls of elements used in my alchemy experiments.  They contain such things as sulfur, arsenic and mercury.
column2: 我這裡有幾碗煉金實驗用的元素，裝著硫磺、砒霜與水銀之類的東西。

column1: That is a small dragon's skull and a large crystal on top of the shelves. My books fill the shelves below. The other objects are no affair of yours.
column2: 架子頂上是一顆小龍頭骨與一塊大水晶，下方架上擺滿了我的藏書。其餘物件與你無關。

column1: It is simply a large and beautiful chunk of quartz, nothing more.
column2: 這不過是一大塊美麗的石英，僅此而已。

column1: I dry herbs for both medicinal and culinary purposes.   If you truly wish to know more, please feel free to ask about them.
column2: 我曬乾藥草，既作藥用也作烹飪之用。你若真想多知道些，儘管問我。

column1: There is mint, which some believe can cure the bite of mad dogs. It comes from the legend of Minthe, a river nymph.
column2: 這是薄荷，有人相信它能治瘋狗咬傷。它的名字源自河仙子敏西的傳說。

column1: Pluto, lord of the underworld, made love to her, whereupon Pluto's jealous queen, Proserpine, changed Minthe into a plant.
column2: 冥界之主普魯托與她相戀，普魯托善妒的王后普洛塞庇娜得知後，便將敏西化為一株植物。

column1: And basil, which the untutored mistakenly believe causes scorpions to breed. In India, it is sacred to the gods Vishnu and Krishna. Delicious with beans, peas and other vegetables.
column2: 這是羅勒，未經教化之人誤以為它會招來蠍子。在印度，它是毗濕奴與克里希納兩位神祇的聖草。配豆子、豌豆等蔬菜食用格外美味。

column1: And marjoram, thought useful in healing wounds and many other illnesses, though I like its delicate flavor with fowl and in sausages.
column2: 這是馬鬱蘭，據信有助療傷及治療諸多疾病，不過我偏愛它配禽肉與香腸時那股細緻的香氣。

column1: And sage, which the Egyptians believe will make women fertile, and others think it gives immortality. Personally, I like the flavor it imparts to beer and sausages.
column2: 這是鼠尾草，埃及人相信它能助婦女受孕，也有人認為它能賜人長生。至於我，則喜歡它為啤酒與香腸添上的風味。

column1: And no collection would be complete without bay. To the Greeks and Romans it was the laurel and they would crown their victors with laurel wreaths.
column2: 少了月桂，這收藏便不算齊全。在希臘人與羅馬人眼中，它便是桂冠所用的月桂樹，他們會以月桂編成的花冠加冕勝利者。

column1: Young girls have been known to burn leaves to make lovers return to them. Prophets, diviners and the priests of Apollo considered it to have magical properties. The dry leaves make an excellent flavoring in stews.
column2: 據說少女會焚燒它的葉子，好讓情人回心轉意。先知、占卜師與阿波羅的祭司都認為它具有魔力。乾葉更是燉菜絕佳的調味。

column1: The pentangle, the five-pointed star, is considered strong protection from spirits who cannot find a place to enter in because it is made of a single unbroken line.
column2: 五芒星以一筆不間斷的線畫成，被認為能有力地防範鬼靈，讓牠們找不到縫隙可以侵入。

column1: In the center is a labarum, the symbol of Mithras. The circle with the descending cross is the symbol of Venus.
column2: 正中央是拉巴倫，米夏拉的標識。下垂十字加圓圈，則是維納斯的標識。

column1: Which rug?
column2: 哪一張地毯？

column1: I am sure you have seen enough candles in your life to realize that mine are no different.
column2: 你這輩子想必見過不少蠟燭，該明白我這些也沒什麼不同。

column1: It is a lovely, but empty pot.
column2: 這是個漂亮的罐子，但空空如也。

column1: From either window you see the grounds and outer bastion of Camelot.
column2: 從任一扇窗望出去，都能見到肯萊特的庭院與外圍堡壘。

column1: Upon one wall are drying herbs, a map of Britain and Ireland. Upon the other wall is my sword and a tapestry.
column2: 一面牆上掛著風乾的藥草與一幅不列顛與愛爾蘭地圖，另一面牆上則掛著我的劍與一幅掛毯。

column1: I use it for my experiments in alchemy in which I seek to unravel the mysteries of the elements and life itself.
column2: 我用它來進行煉金實驗，藉此探究元素乃至生命本身的奧秘。

column1: You have kindly closed it for me.
column2: 你已好心替我關上了。

column1: That is my personal chest. I keep various odds and ends in there. Look inside, if you like.
column2: 那是我的私人箱子，裡頭放著些零碎雜物。你若想看，儘管打開瞧瞧。

column1: The other items are personal mementos and do not concern you. Do not touch them.
column2: 其餘物件都是我的私人紀念品，與你無關，休得碰觸。

column1: We have no time to waste on trivia. Take the lodestone and turn your attention to your mission.
column2: 我們沒有時間浪費在瑣事上。拿起指北針，把心思放回你的使命上。

column1: I have many mementos, but you have no time to waste on trivia.
column2: 我有許多紀念品，但你沒有時間浪費在瑣事上。

column1: These mysterious stones may come from the stars.   Always some part of a lodestone will point to true north.  It is therefore a very useful thing to have on a long journey.
column2: 這些神秘的石頭，或許來自星辰。指北針總有一端會指向正北，因此在長途旅程中極為有用。

column1: If you take it with you, you can look at it all you like.
column2: 你若把它帶在身上，便能隨時想看就看。

column1: Ah, so glad you reminded me. Did I put it on the....nay...perhaps it is on top of....nay.
column2: 啊，多虧你提醒。我把它放在……不……或許是放在……不對。

column1: Forgive me, Arthur. I seem to have forgotten where I put it. It must be around here somewhere.
column2: 原諒我，亞瑟，我似乎忘了放到哪去了。想必就在這附近某處。

column1: That is my sword and perfectly ordinary.  My weapons are of a less physical nature.
column2: 那是我的劍，再平凡不過。我的武器，性質可不那麼具體。

column1: That is rather a vague request. There are many kinds of weapons, yet knowledge can be the most potent weapon of all.
column2: 這要求含糊得很。武器種類繁多，但知識往往才是最強大的武器。

column1: It is the skull of a small dragon, a gift from St. George.
column2: 那是一顆小龍的頭骨，是聖喬治所贈之物。

column1: Aye, that is where I sit to study my scrolls and books.
column2: 正是，我便是坐在那裡研讀卷軸與書籍。

column1: Here?  Are you sure you are in your right mind?
column2: 在這裡？你確定自己神智清醒？

column1: What dog?  I keep no dog.
column2: 什麼狗？我沒養狗。

column1: I have a cluttered room, never enough space for everything.
column2: 我這房間雜亂得很，總嫌空間不夠擺下一切。

column1: I have my table of beakers and flasks, my shelves of books and also a small dragon skull and a large crystal, a map of your kingdom, my desk with a scroll I am studying upon it, my personal chest, and various other items.
column2: 我有擺著燒杯與燒瓶的桌子、堆滿書的架子，還有一顆小龍頭骨與一塊大水晶、一幅你王國的地圖、擺著我正在研讀的卷軸的書桌、我的私人箱子，以及其他各式物件。

column1: It is the study of the nature of elements, their interactions and transmutations.  The name "alchemy" traces back to "Khemennu" which means "Land of the Moon", an ancient name for Egypt.
column2: 那是探究元素本質、其相互作用與嬗變之學。「煉金術」一詞可追溯至「赫曼努」，意為「月之地」，是埃及的古名。

column1: The Arabs learned of alchemy from the Egyptians, though also at the same time it was developed in China. However, the best tract I have read to date is by the Arab scholar, Jabir ibn Hayyam, for the Arabs are quite advanced in this science.
column2: 阿拉伯人從埃及人那裡習得煉金術，同一時期中國也自行發展出這門學問。不過，我至今讀過最好的論著，出自阿拉伯學者賈比耳·伊本·哈耶姆之手——阿拉伯人在這門學問上頗有造詣。

column1: Ask me not for advice in love, for I know little of women.  Ask me not for advice about battle or war, for you know more than I of these matters.
column2: 莫向我求教愛情之事，我對女人所知甚少。也莫向我求教戰陣征伐，這方面你懂得比我多。

column1: Ask me not for advice about the obvious, for I am short-tempered. But if you seek advice about that which is mystic, obscure, arcane, or simply puzzling, then I shall do my best to help you.
column2: 莫問我顯而易見之事，我這人性子急。但你若為神秘、晦澀、隱奧或單純費解之事求教，我必竭盡所能相助。

column1: It was a reminder that your moral and spiritual choices during your search will be as important as finding the Grail itself.
column2: 那是在提醒你：這趟尋找途中，你的道德與心靈抉擇，將與尋得聖杯本身同等重要。

column1: It is your sacred duty, as vital as the search for the Grail itself, that you find and rescue your three Knights.
column2: 尋回並救出你的三位騎士，是你神聖的職責，其重要性不亞於尋找聖杯本身。

column1: If you seek visions, you must go to the Chapel of the Two Gods.
column2: 你若尋求異象啟示，須前往雙神神殿。

column1: I can add nothing to what is written in your Liber ex Doctrina.  You should have it with you at all times.
column2: 你那本《Liber ex Doctrina》裡寫的，我無可補充。你應時時將它帶在身邊。

column1: I believe the Treasurer is a good friend of Sir Gawaine and would have the latest news, if any.
column2: 我想司庫與高文爵士交情不錯，若有最新消息，他應當知曉。

column1: I do not wish to be indelicate, but the Queen might be the best person to ask.
column2: 我不想失禮，但王后或許是最適合詢問的人。

column1: He is very popular among your guards and they would be first to hear rumour of him.
column2: 他在你的衛兵之間極受愛戴，若有他的傳聞，衛兵們必是最先聽聞的人。

column1: She is usually to be found in her bower about this time of day.
column2: 這個時辰，她通常都在後宮花園。

column1: What would you have me tell you? You are a warrior, a man of the real world. You must rely upon your wits, skill, strength and virtue of character to combat any magick that you might encounter.
column2: 你要我如何跟你說？你是個戰士，一個活在現實世界裡的人。面對可能遭遇的任何魔法，你必須仰賴自己的機智、技藝、力量與德行來應對。

column1: I am sure you can find one of your own guards in your own stronghold.
column2: 在自己的要塞裡，你想必找得到自己的衛兵。

column1: He is where a Treasurer usually is. In the Treasury.
column2: 他就在司庫平常所在之處——寶庫裡。

column1: Worship of the Christ god arose in the Far East about 700 years ago and has spread west ever since. To some he is a prophet, to others the son of God. He preached much of love, of compassion, and forgiveness for the sins of others.
column2: 基督信仰約在七百年前興起於遠東，自此便向西方傳播不絕。在某些人眼中，他是先知；在另一些人眼中，他是神之子。他傳揚愛、憐憫，以及寬恕他人罪愆的教誨。

column1: Mithras is a warrior-god which only men are allowed to worship and in great secret. He was most popular among the Roman soldiers who brought this worship with them to our island centuries ago.
column2: 米夏拉是一位戰神，只有男子才被允許崇拜他，而且須極為隱密。此信仰在羅馬士兵之間最為盛行，數世紀前由他們帶到我們這座島上。

column1: Glastonbury Tor has been a sacred hill for centuries. The legend of Joseph of Arimathea claims the Grail is hidden there.
column2: 格列斯登伯利山數世紀以來一直是座聖山。亞利馬太的約瑟的傳說宣稱，聖杯就藏於此處。

column1: It is a body of water to the north where currently the Lady of the Lake dwells.
column2: 那是北方的一片水域，湖中女神如今便棲居於此。

column1: It is your major port in the south where you must go to take the ship to other lands.
column2: 那是你南方的主要港口，你須經此搭船前往他方國度。

column1: This dark and dangerous forest borders Glastonbury Tor and you must pass through it to reach the sacred hill.
column2: 這座陰暗而危險的森林與格列斯登伯利山相鄰，你必須穿越此處才能抵達那座聖山。

column1: If you wish to know more about that place, study the map, and I shall instruct you.
column2: 你若想多了解那個地方，仔細研究地圖，我便會指引你。

column1: Let us leave discussion of that for another time.
column2: 此事容後再議。

column1: I know you would not be so rude.
column2: 我知道你不會如此無禮。

column1: Say rather godspeed, for I shall be with you in spirit-voice throughout your mission.
column2: 不如說「一路順風」吧，因為在你此行途中，我將以心神之聲與你同在。

column1: Aye, may the god you worship speed you to your destiny, Arthur.
column2: 正是，願你所信奉的神明，助你抵達命運所在，亞瑟。

column1: Use your eyes, Arthur, it's already closed.
column2: 睜大你的眼睛，亞瑟，它已經關上了。

column1: You have taken the only thing I wish you to have.
column2: 我要你擁有的東西，你已經拿到了。

column1: Use your eyes, Arthur.  It IS open.
column2: 睜大你的眼睛，亞瑟，它確實開著。

column1: Hmmm....it is around here somewhere. I simply cannot remember where I put it.
column2: 唔……應該就在附近某處。我實在想不起放到哪去了。

column1: It is attached to my wall.
column2: 它就掛在我的牆上。

column1: King you may be, but do not lay hands upon that which belongs to Merlin the enchanter.
column2: 你或許貴為王者，但休想染指屬於魔法師梅林之物。

column1: The lodestone is the only object in this room which you may take. The rest belongs to Merlin the Enchanter and you are not to lay hands upon them.
column2: 指北針是這房裡唯一你可以拿走的東西。其餘皆屬魔法師梅林所有，你不得染指。

column1: But....you must excuse an old man. I have forgotten where I put the lodestone. It is around here somewhere.
column2: 但……你得原諒一個老人。我忘了把指北針放到哪去了，應該就在附近某處。

column1: Search if you like, but DO NOT TOUCH ANYTHING ELSE!
column2: 你要找便找，但除此之外什麼都不准碰！

column1: By the Red Dragon, I will not warn you again! Do not lay hands upon anything that is not meant for you.
column2: 以紅龍之名起誓，我不會再警告你第二次！不屬於你的東西，休得伸手。

column1: You were thinking of spending the rest of your life as a toad, perhaps?
column2: 你該不會是想餘生都當隻蟾蜍度過吧？

column1: My darling boy, I did not know you cared.
column2: 我親愛的孩子，我不知道你竟如此在乎我。

column1: I never kiss men with beards.
column2: 我從不親吻蓄鬍的男子。

column1: What a completely ridiculous notion.
column2: 這想法簡直荒唐至極。

column1: I enjoy the mingling of scents: the fumes of alchemy, the herbs drying upon my wall, burning candles, even the musty odor of the old scroll I am studying.
column2: 我喜愛這些氣味交融：煉金的煙氣、牆上風乾的藥草、燃燒的蠟燭，甚至我正在研讀的那卷古老卷軸散發的霉味。

column1: Ah, the symbol of love.
column2: 啊，愛的象徵。

column1: You had best keep it.
column2: 你最好留著它。

column1: Now why would you want to give me something that I have given you?
column2: 你為何要把我送你的東西，又送還給我？

column1: You have greater need of it than I.
column2: 你比我更需要它。

column1: A most gracious gesture, but I have no need of it.
column2: 此舉甚是慷慨，但我並不需要它。

column1: If I am ever in need of help, rest assured you will be the first to know.
column2: 若我有朝一日需要幫助，放心，你必是第一個知曉的人。

column1: You do not have your sword.
column2: 你並未佩劍。

column1: There will be time enough for that later and I am not fond of cold steel in my presence.
column2: 此事來日方長，況且我不喜冷鐵近身。

column1: Truly, I think your hearing is impaired. Have I not warned you against this once?
column2: 說真的，我看你耳朵是出了毛病。我不是警告過你一次了嗎？

column1: I am your mentor and advisor, but I will not tolerate being threatened in this fashion.
column2: 我是你的導師與謀士，但我不會容忍被如此威脅。

column1: Inside my chest is a lodestone, a magical stone that will always show you where true north lies.  This one is shaped like a tiny sword, the tip of which will point to north as it dangles from a string attached to its center.
column2: 我箱子裡有一枚指北針，一種能指出正北方向的魔法石。這一枚打造成小劍形狀，以繩繫在中心懸垂，劍尖便會指向北方。

column1: Take it, Arthur.   I prepared it especially for you.
column2: 拿去吧，亞瑟。這是我特地為你準備的。

column1: It is a map of the Summer Lands, as your kingdom is often known;
column2: 這是夏地的地圖——你的王國常被如此稱呼；

column1: Cornwall to the west, and some lands beyond, including the island of Eire.
column2: 西邊是康瓦爾，再往外還有一些土地，包括愛爾蘭島。

column1: However, you should study it very closely before you leave and determine where your search for the Grail should take you.
column2: 然而，你在啟程前應仔細研究此圖，判斷你尋找聖杯之路該往何處去。

column1: Since you cannot keep your hands to yourself, you can do without them for awhile.
column2: 既然你管不住自己的手，那就讓你暫時沒有手可用。

column1: When you apologize, I will consider returning you to your native form.
column2: 待你道歉之後，我會考慮讓你恢復原形。

column1: It would seem you refuse to learn a lesson.  Be gone from my sight.
column2: 看來你是不肯記取教訓。從我眼前消失。

column1: Your stubbornness defies belief. I will waste no more time upon you, fool of a king.
column2: 你的頑固簡直令人難以置信。我不會再在你身上浪費時間了，愚昧的王啊。

column1: PRESS F6 TO EXIT
column2: 按 F6 離開

column1: Use arrows to move, or select with mouse.
column2: 使用方向鍵移動，或用滑鼠點選。

column1: You see the Summer Lands, as your kingdom is often known, with Cornwall to the west and river Thames coming from the east.
column2: 你看見夏地——你的王國常被如此稱呼，西邊是康瓦爾，泰晤士河則從東邊流入。

column1: Take careful note of the locations that may be of import to your search. This will prevent you from wasting much time later.
column2: 仔細留意那些可能對你的尋覓有重要意義的地點，這能省下你日後不少時間。

column1: Do I really need to tell you that this is the rack upon which your mail tunic was hung?
column2: 我真有必要告訴你，這是掛你鎖子甲的架子嗎？

column1: Your mail tunic is made of overlapping metal scales, a design copied from Roman cavalry armour.
column2: 你的鎖子甲是以層疊的金屬鱗片製成，這設計仿自羅馬騎兵的鎧甲。

column1: Upon this shield is the Red Dragon, in token of your surname, Pendragon, which comes from the Welsh words meaning "supreme war chief".
column2: 這面盾牌上繪著紅龍，象徵你的姓氏「潘德拉貢」，此名源自威爾斯語，意為「至高的戰爭統帥」。

column1: You received your sword, Excaliber, from the Lady in the Lake.  By Her Blessings, may it serve you well.
column2: 你的劍——聖劍，得自湖中女神。願蒙她的祝福，這把劍將不負所用。

column1: Your purse remains where you last put it, upon your table.
column2: 你的錢囊仍在你上次放置之處——你的桌上。

column1: When you are in need of solitude, this is your room.  It is sparsely furnished, as befits a warrior-king.
column2: 當你需要獨處時，這便是你的房間。陳設簡樸，正合戰士之王的身分。

column1: They are made of the same grey stone as the rest of Camelot.
column2: 它們與肯萊特其餘部分一樣，皆以灰石砌成。

column1: There are two stands in your room. One holds your mail tunic. In the other corner is the rack holding your clothes.
column2: 你房裡有兩座衣架。一座掛著你的鎖子甲，另一角的架子則掛著你的衣物。

column1: The Celts, like many others, worshipped a Triple Goddess in her three forms: virgin, mother, and crone, which in turn represent creation, life and death.
column2: 凱爾特人和許多其他民族一樣，崇拜以三種樣貌顯現的三重女神：處女、母親與老嫗，分別象徵創造、生命與死亡。

column1: From these windows you see the outer wall of Camelot and the hills, fields and forest beyond.
column2: 從這些窗戶望出去，你能見到肯萊特的外牆，以及牆外的丘陵、田野與森林。

column1: Unfortunately, you cannot see the Queen's bower from here.  Rumour in the palace has it that she placed her bower deliberately out of your sight.  But that is only rumour.
column2: 可惜從這裡看不見王后的閨閣。宮中流言說，她是刻意把閨閣安置在你視線之外。但那終究只是流言。

column1: Aye, they are nice trees. Now, kindly get your mind on your mission.
column2: 是啊，那些樹確實不錯。現在，請將心思放回你的使命上。

column1: It is a heavy wood and metal door.
column2: 這是一扇沉重的木製鐵門。

column1: Your court clothes hang upon the stand in the corner.
column2: 你的朝服掛在牆角的衣架上。

column1: A sturdy set of travelling clothes hangs upon a wooden stand in the south corner of your room. Another stand against the northeastern wall holds your tunic and armour.
column2: 一套堅韌的行裝掛在你房間南角的木架上。東北牆邊另有一座衣架，掛著你的鎖子甲與鎧甲。

column1: Aye, the lack of helmet is a serious oversight, m'lord.   You will have to compensate with extra caution.  You must keep your head if you are to keep your head.
column2: 正是，缺了頭盔確實是一大疏漏，吾王。你得加倍謹慎以為彌補。你得保持頭腦冷靜，才能保住你的項上人頭。

column1: Your bedspread was lovingly made by your wife.
column2: 你的床罩，是你的妻子悉心縫製而成。

column1: Alas, the queen is not here now.
column2: 可惜，王后此刻不在這裡。

column1: You cannot see it from here.
column2: 從這裡看不見它。

column1: You should have a word with your servant. A great deal of dust has been swept under this rug.
column2: 你該找僕人談談了，這地毯底下掃進了不少灰塵。

column1: Aside from stirring up the dust, this will not accomplish much.
column2: 除了揚起灰塵之外，這樣做不會有什麼用處。

column1: There is clearly nothing under the table.
column2: 桌子底下顯然什麼都沒有。

column1: Gwen is in the bower, not here.
column2: 昆海兒在閨閣裡，不在這裡。

column1: It is a bed, of course.  Even a King must sometimes sleep alone when the Queen is indisposed.
column2: 這當然是張床。即便貴為國王，王后偶有不適時，也得獨自安眠。

column1: Your purse lies where you tossed it upon the table last night.
column2: 你的錢囊，就躺在你昨晚隨手扔在桌上的地方。

column1: It is a sturdy, oak table.
column2: 這是一張堅固的橡木桌。

column1: Closet? Sounds like the French word "clos", but there is no enclosure in this room.
column2: 衣櫃？聽起來像法文的「clos」，但這房裡並沒有這樣的隔間。

column1: A three-armed Celtic symbol adorns your rug, perhaps a reminder of the three-fold Great Goddess of creation, life and death.
column2: 你的地毯上飾有一個三臂凱爾特符號，或許是在提醒創造、生命與死亡的三重大女神。

column1: There are two symbols here. One is upon your shield, the other upon your rug.
column2: 這裡有兩個符號，一個在你的盾牌上，另一個在你的地毯上。

column1: The red dragon upon your shield is your symbol. You are Arthur Pendragon.
column2: 盾牌上的紅龍是你的象徵。你是亞瑟·潘德拉貢。

column1: Preparation is vital.  Body, heart, mind, and spirit must all be in readiness before you leave Camelot.
column2: 準備至關重要。在離開肯萊特之前，身、心、意、靈皆須齊備。

column1: Just walk through it.
column2: 直接穿過去便是。

column1: It is a heavy door which swings shut by its own weight.
column2: 這是一扇沉重的門，會因自身重量而自行關上。

column1: The floor beneath it is the same as the rest of your floor.
column2: 它底下的地板，與房裡其餘地板並無不同。

column1: This is no time for a nap.  Your mission is urgent and every second you delay, your people suffer.
column2: 現在不是小憩的時候。你的使命刻不容緩，每耽擱一秒，你的子民便多受一分苦。

column1: What an incredibly foolish notion.
column2: 這想法真是愚蠢至極。

column1: That would get you nowhere fast.
column2: 那樣做只會讓你原地打轉。

column1: It is quite satisfied being where it is.
column2: 它待在原處便挺自在的。

column1: A token from Gwenhyver is better kept close to your heart.
column2: 昆海兒所贈的信物，最好貼身珍藏。

column1: They are not sturdy enough for your mission. Leave them here.
column2: 它們不夠堅韌，無法應付你的使命，留在這裡吧。

column1: You are already wearing them.
column2: 你已經穿在身上了。

column1: You are wearing your armour...as if I should need to tell you that.
column2: 你已經穿著鎧甲了……這種事還用我來提醒嗎。

column1: Why?
column2: 為什麼？

column1: I sincerely hope you have made up your mind this time.
column2: 我誠心希望你這回已經拿定主意了。

column1: Your servants are already preparing a pack for your journey.  It will surely contain a sturdier blanket than this.
column2: 你的僕從已在為你此行備妥行囊，裡頭想必會有一條比這條更堅實的毯子。

column1: A bit large to carry about, one would think.
column2: 想來這東西帶著走未免太過龐大。

column1: It would only get in the way.
column2: 那只會礙手礙腳。

column1: It's not here.
column2: 它不在這裡。

column1: Your shield is upon your arm.
column2: 你的盾牌已戴在臂上。

column1: A shield gets in the way of putting on other armour. You need to get your mail tunic and sword first.
column2: 盾牌會妨礙你穿戴其他鎧甲。你得先穿上鎖子甲、佩好劍才行。

column1: Your sword is strapped at your side.
column2: 你的劍已繫在腰間。

column1: Before you can strap on your sword, you need to be wearing your mail tunic.
column2: 在佩劍之前，你得先穿上鎖子甲。

column1: You are already wearing your armor.
column2: 你已經穿著鎧甲了。

column1: You cannot wear armour over your court clothes. Your travelling clothes are in the south corner of your room.
column2: 你不能把鎧甲套在朝服外頭。你的行裝就在房間南角。

column1: They would not do for this trip. Leave them here.
column2: 這趟旅程用不上它們，留在這裡吧。

column1: You already are wearing them.
column2: 你已經穿在身上了。

column1: That is not a very good reason.
column2: 這理由可不怎麼站得住腳。

column1: How wise of you.
column2: 你可真是明智。

column1: Hmmph.  That was truly pointless.
column2: 哼，那真是白費工夫。

column1: I am certain that if you talk to your Treasurer or question him correctly, you will learn all you need.
column2: 我確信，只要你去找司庫問個明白，便能得知你所需的一切。

column1: Remember, 25 copper coins equals 5 silver coins and 5 silver coins equals one gold coin.
column2: 記住，二十五枚銅幣等於五枚銀幣，五枚銀幣等於一枚金幣。

column1: It is made of heavy oak planks, with a trapdoor for the only entrance.
column2: 此處以厚重橡木板築成，唯一的入口是一道活板門。

column1: This tower stronghold was built to protect your store of coins and other valuables. The bundles on the right are new, however.
column2: 這座塔樓要塞建來守護你的錢幣與其他財物。不過，右邊那幾捆包裹是新添的。

column1: They are made of the same grey stone as the rest of Camelot.  Only thicker.
column2: 它們與肯萊特其餘部分一樣，皆以灰石砌成，只是更為厚實。

column1: You cannot see much of it from this tower stronghold.
column2: 從這座塔樓要塞裡，你看不太到外頭的景象。

column1: The trap door is heavy and easily defended.
column2: 這道活板門十分沉重，易守難攻。

column1: Aye, 'tis a torch.
column2: 正是，這是一支火把。

column1: The huge jars contain your entire wealth of gold, silver and copper coins. The chests contain other forms of wealth. I do not know what is in the bundles.
column2: 這幾口大甕裝著你全部的金、銀、銅幣財富。箱子裡則是其他形式的財物。至於包裹裡是什麼，我就不得而知了。

column1: The pillars of this tower are quite strong and thick.
column2: 這座塔樓的柱子相當堅固粗實。

column1: They are bundles that are stored here.
column2: 那些是存放在此處的包裹。

column1: They lead down to the main floor of Camelot.
column2: 它們通往肯萊特的主樓層。

column1: The chests contain gems and jewels set in gold and silver, plates and goblets of gold and silver and other such fine items.
column2: 箱子裡裝著鑲嵌於金銀之中的寶石與珠玉、金銀打造的盤碟與高腳杯，以及其他諸如此類的珍品。

column1: He is a powerfully built man, well able to defend this tower and your treasure. Heed his advice.
column2: 他體格強健，足以守衛這座塔樓與你的財寶。你該聽從他的建言。

column1: There is gold in the jar on the right.
column2: 右邊的甕裡裝著金幣。

column1: There is silver in the middle jar.
column2: 中間的甕裡裝著銀幣。

column1: There is copper in the leftmost jar.
column2: 最左邊的甕裡裝著銅幣。

column1: The three large jars contain gold, silver, and copper coins.
column2: 這三口大甕裝著金幣、銀幣與銅幣。

column1: Your treasurer has a huge sword and knows how to use it.
column2: 你的司庫佩著一把巨劍，而且深諳用劍之道。

column1: In this enclosed room, the odor of a sweaty man, oily torch, and cold metal is most concentrated.
column2: 在這密閉的房間裡，汗味、油煙火把味與冷硬金屬味格外濃重。

column1: Arthur, you are here to prepare for your journey, not to play with trinkets of wealth.
column2: 亞瑟，你來此是為了準備啟程，不是來把玩這些身外財物的。

column1: The trap door is already open.
column2: 活板門已經開著了。

column1: That is the Treasurer's only source of light.
column2: 那是司庫唯一的光源。

column1: You could, if you were holding it.
column2: 你若拿著它，倒是可以。

column1: There is too much metal all around and it confuses the workings of the lodestone.
column2: 四周金屬太多，擾亂了指北針的運作。

column1: The Treasurer needs it more than you do.
column2: 司庫比你更需要它。

column1: You have no business doing that until you know Gawaine is dead.
column2: 在確知高文已死之前，你無權這麼做。

column1: I am sure you could find one anywhere in Camelot if you looked hard enough.
column2: 我相信只要你用心找，在肯萊特任何角落都能找到一個。

column1: When you have seen one rodent, you have seen them all.
column2: 見過一隻齧齒動物，便等於見過牠們全部。

column1: You have more important things to think about.
column2: 你還有更要緊的事該想。

column1: Is this some sort of odd Pictish word?
column2: 這是某種古怪的皮克特語詞彙嗎？

column1: Which one first, m'lord?
column2: 吾王，先要哪一種？

column1: Coins of tin?  Never heard'o such a thing.
column2: 錫幣？老朽從未聽聞這種東西。

column1: We have no coins made of bronze, sire.
column2: 陛下，我們沒有青銅鑄造的錢幣。

column1: You have coins already, my king, but if you wish to change them, please give me the purse.
column2: 我王，你已經有錢幣了，但若你想兌換，請把錢囊交給我。

column1: Aye, gladly, if you will but provide me with the purse to fill.
column2: 是，樂意之至，只要你把錢囊交給我裝滿。

column1: Your purse is full, my liege.
column2: 吾主，你的錢囊已經滿了。

column1: I have no purse to give you. If you have brought your own, I can fill it for you.
column2: 我沒有錢囊可以給你。你若帶著自己的，我可以替你裝滿。

column1: But you have it, sire.
column2: 但陛下，錢囊在你身上。

column1: I have no purse to give you, m'lord.
column2: 吾王，我沒有錢囊可以給你。

column1: You must come closer, m'lord.
column2: 你得再靠近些，吾王。

column1: Here you are, m'lord, but the purse is empty. I beg you to let me fill it for you ere you go.
column2: 拿去吧，吾王，但錢囊是空的。趁你尚未啟程，容我為你裝滿。

column1: There is room for more, m'lord, but here it is, as you command.
column2: 還裝得下更多，吾王，但既然你這麼吩咐，錢囊便交給你了。

column1: Here it is, m'lord, as you command.
column2: 遵命奉上，吾王。

column1: Steal?  But, my lord, it is already yours.
column2: 偷？可是，吾王，這東西本就是你的。

column1: But, m'lord, you have coins in your purse. Still, if you wish to change what you have, you have but to give me the purse again.
column2: 可是，吾王，你的錢囊裡已經有錢幣了。不過，你若想兌換手上的錢，儘管把錢囊再給我便是。

column1: What coins would you be wantin', m'lord?
column2: 吾王想要哪種錢幣？

column1: Your purse is full and I have no other purses or bags to fill.
column2: 你的錢囊已經滿了，我也沒有別的錢囊或袋子可裝了。

column1: Travelling with bulging moneybags would only bring bandits and outlaws down upon you like a plague of locusts.
column2: 帶著鼓脹的錢袋上路，只會招來強盜與亡命之徒，如蝗蟲過境般撲向你。

column1: Take your purse and cease badgering your Treasurer. He is wise in these matters and greed does not become a King.
column2: 拿好你的錢囊，別再纏著你的司庫了。他深諳此道，貪婪可配不上一位國王。

column1: I have it in hand, m'lord. I await your commands.
column2: 已在我手中，吾王，靜候你的吩咐。

column1: You do not have the purse with you, Arthur.
column2: 亞瑟，你身上並沒有帶著錢囊。

column1: Thank you, m'lord. I shall fill it according to your wishes.
column2: 多謝，吾王，我這就依你的心意裝滿它。

column1: I have emptied the purse, so we may begin again. What is your command?
column2: 我已將錢囊倒空，可以重新開始了。你有何吩咐？

column1: No need to give me money, m'lord. You reward me well enough.
column2: 不必給我錢，吾王，你待我已經夠厚了。

column1: You must get money before you can give money.
column2: 你得先有錢，才能給人錢。

column1: I am the one who should be giving you money, m'lord. What are your commands?
column2: 該給你錢的人是我，吾王。你有何吩咐？

column1: I have no need to take any for myself. You reward me well enough already.
column2: 我用不著為自己拿一分一毫，你待我已經夠厚了。

column1: As you wish. Give me the purse, then.
column2: 悉聽尊便。那麼，把錢囊給我吧。

column1: You do not even have the purse.
column2: 你連錢囊都沒帶在身上。

column1: The purse is empty, m'lord. I await your commands.
column2: 錢囊是空的，吾王，靜候你的吩咐。

column1: There are silver coins in your purse.
column2: 你的錢囊裡有銀幣。

column1: You now have gold coins, my King.
column2: 我王，你現在有金幣了。

column1: I have given you copper coins, m'lord.
column2: 吾王，我已經給了你銅幣。

column1: The purse has coins in it, m'lord, but if that is your wish...
column2: 錢囊裡已經有錢幣了，吾王，但既然這是你的心意……

column1: The purse is now empty. What is your command?
column2: 錢囊現在是空的。你有何吩咐？

column1: Ah, a good luck charm! I thank you, m'lord.
column2: 啊，一個護身符！多謝，吾王。

column1: Ah, a good luck charm!
column2: 啊，一個護身符！

column1: Here you are, m'lord.
column2: 拿去吧，吾王。

column1: My king, if you seek my advice, I say this -- take with you coins of all three value: copper, silver and gold. Each has its use.
column2: 我王，若你想聽我的建言，我要說：三種面額的錢幣都該帶上——銅、銀、金，各有各的用處。

column1: If you have brought your purse with you, m'lord, I will be happy to fill it for you.
column2: 你若帶著錢囊來，吾王，我很樂意為你裝滿。

column1: I am here to serve you as I may, though, to speak bluntly, I hope you will soon be in search of the Grail.
column2: 我在此盡我所能為你效勞，不過老實說，我盼你早日踏上尋找聖杯的旅程。

column1: Please tell me how I may serve you.
column2: 請告訴我該如何為你效勞。

column1: Hands that shed innocent blood will never touch the Grail.
column2: 沾染無辜鮮血的雙手，永遠碰不到聖杯。

column1: He is your loyal servant.  Why would you want to fight him?
column2: 他是你忠心的僕人，你為何想跟他動手？

column1: Gar!  Keep away, you pox-cursed pooftah!
column2: 哼！滾開，你這染上瘡病的斷袖孽徒！

column1: Where I come from, that is not a manly thing to do.
column2: 在我的家鄉，這可不是男子漢該做的事。

column1: Pardon me, Sire, but that would take months.
column2: 恕罪，陛下，但那得花上數月光陰。

column1: It was sealed by Sir Gawaine when he left it here, and he charged me to see that the seal is not broken except by his own hand...unless he is dead.
column2: 這是高文爵士離去時親手封上的，他囑咐我務必守著，除非他親自解封……或是他已經身故。

column1: Nay, leave it be. Your mission must be kept humble, for safety as well as your soul's sake.
column2: 不可，別去動它。你的使命必須保持謙卑，這既是為了安全，也是為了你的靈魂。

column1: By your leave, m'lord, I keep it open so that fresh air may enter the room.  And so the mice may leave it.
column2: 容稟，吾王，我讓它開著，好讓新鮮空氣進來房裡，也好讓老鼠有路可出去。

column1: Those bundles belong to Sir Gawaine. They are all his worldly possessions which he left in my keeping, for I was the last man to see him ere he left.
column2: 那些包裹是高文爵士的。那是他所有的身外之物，他離去前交由我保管，因為我是他啟程前見到的最後一人。

column1: I have it, Sire, and await your instructions.
column2: 已在我手中，陛下，靜候你的指示。

column1: The bags contain gold and silver cups and platters and other booty from the battles you have won.
column2: 袋裡裝的是金杯銀盤，以及你征戰得勝所獲的其他戰利品。

column1: Each jar before me is filled with coins: one with gold coins, one with silver coins and one with copper coins.
column2: 我面前的每個罐子都裝滿了錢幣：一罐金幣、一罐銀幣、一罐銅幣。

column1: Greetings, my King.  The jar to your left contains copper coins, the jar in the center holds silver coins and the jar to your right is filled with gold coins.
column2: 見過我王。你左手邊的罐子裝著銅幣，中間的罐子裝著銀幣，右手邊的罐子則裝滿金幣。

column1: One gold coin is worth 5 silver coins or 25 copper coins.
column2: 一枚金幣值五枚銀幣，或二十五枚銅幣。

column1: You have forgotten my name after years of service? Awr, you are having a joke. Hawrh! Hawrh! Hawrh!
column2: 小人伺候陛下多年，陛下竟忘了小人的名字？啊呀，陛下真會說笑。哈！哈！哈！

column1: I was the last to see Sir Gawaine.  He made sure to take copper coins along with silver and gold.  He told me he planned to search for the Grail in the ruins of Glastonbury Tor.
column2: 我是最後見到高文爵士的人。他特意帶上了銅幣，連同銀幣與金幣一起。他告訴我，他打算前往格列斯登伯利山的廢墟尋找聖杯。

column1: That is the last that I, or any man, has heard of him.
column2: 那便是我，或任何人，最後聽聞他的消息了。

column1: I wish I could tell you something useful, m'lord.
column2: 但願我能告訴你些有用的事，吾王。

column1: In memory of Graham Chapman
column2: 謹以此紀念葛拉罕·查普曼。

column1: I pray to all the powers that be that you will return safely, that the Grail will be yours, as surely it must be.
column2: 我向天地間的一切神靈祈求，願你平安歸來，願聖杯終將屬於你，此事必成。

column1: And may you find and bring back all the noble knights who have gone before you on this holy mission.
column2: 也願你尋回、帶回所有先你踏上這神聖使命、卻杳無音訊的高貴騎士。

column1: Your fate will be always in my mind during the long and lonely hours.
column2: 在那些漫漫長夜、形單影隻的時刻，我心中將永遠掛念你的命運。

column1: I will add prayers for your return to those I have already made everyday for Sir Launcelot.
column2: 我會在每日已為蘭斯洛特爵士祈禱之外，再加上為你平安歸來的祈禱。

column1: And Sir Gawaine and Sir Galahad, of course.
column2: 當然，還有高文爵士與葛拉漢爵士。

column1: There is no more I can bear to say.  Dally no more with me, my lord.  Fare thee well.
column2: 我再也說不下去了。莫再與我流連，吾王，願你一路平安。

column1: A lodestone?  I have no need of it, but you surely might.  I insist you keep it.
column2: 一個指北針？我用不著，但你想必用得上，我堅持要你收下。

column1: But it is I who give it to you.  I have whispered secrets to it and nourished it with my tears.  It is imbued with the power of my love.
column2: 但這是我要送給你的東西。我曾對它低語心事，以淚水滋養它，它已注滿了我愛的力量。

column1: Indeed not, husband.  That would be most undignified.
column2: 確實不會，夫君，那樣未免太失體統。

column1: I will cherish those words always.
column2: 這些話，我將永遠珍藏在心。

column1: I have for you all the loving devotion a wife could have for a husband.
column2: 我對你懷有妻子對丈夫所能付出的一切摯愛與忠貞。

column1: Girl?  I am Gwenhyver -- your queen, your woman, your wife.  I am no girl.
column2: 女孩？我是昆海兒——你的王后、你的女人、你的妻子。我不是什麼女孩。

column1: Is this some sort of odd Moorish word?
column2: 這是某種古怪的摩爾語詞彙嗎？

column1: Goodbye, my love.  May you fulfill your destiny.
column2: 再會了，我的愛人。願你完成你的天命。

column1: There is no need to steal that which is already yours.
column2: 本就屬於你的東西，無須用偷的。

column1: It is written in the Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 這寫在《Liber ex Doctrina》裡。

column1: Alas, my husband, all but one of my roses has withered and fallen.  My garden is dying, even as our kingdom slowly dies.
column2: 唉，夫君，我的玫瑰已全數凋零墜落，只剩最後一朵。我的花園正在枯萎，一如我們的國家正緩緩走向衰亡。

column1: We are completely private within these walls.  You need not worry about the window behind us.  Within is only a sewing room and empty at present.
column2: 這幾道牆內完全屬於我們的私密之地，你不必擔心身後那扇窗。裡頭只是間縫紉室，此刻空無一人。

column1: There is nothing inside save the ladies' sewing room, of no interest to a warrior.
column2: 裡頭除了女眷的縫紉室之外別無他物，對一名戰士毫無意趣。

column1: My fountain is as parched and dry as the lakes and rivers of our poor kingdom.
column2: 我的噴泉，如同我們可憐王國裡的湖泊與河流一般，乾涸枯竭。

column1: It is a stone bench and not very comfortable.
column2: 這是一張石凳，並不怎麼舒適。

column1: You planted that tree for me when Camelot was first built.  I pray it will survive.
column2: 肯萊特初建成時，你為我種下了那棵樹。我祈禱它能撐過這一切。

column1: Wear it next to your heart. In time of need, it will guide you through danger if you recite the Message of the Rose.
column2: 把它戴在貼近心口之處。危難之時，只要你誦念玫瑰箴言，它便會指引你穿越險境。

column1: You have taken the only rose.
column2: 你已經摘走了僅存的那朵玫瑰。

column1: It is the last and most beautiful of my red roses.  It would please me if you took it as a token of my love.
column2: 這是我最後、也是最美的一朵紅玫瑰。你若肯收下它，當作我愛的信物，我會很欣慰。

column1: If I knew the least thing, I would gladly tell you.
column2: 我若知道哪怕一丁點消息，也會樂意告訴你。

column1: Ah...uhmmm....we are just good friends.
column2: 啊……呃……我們只是好朋友。

column1: However, it is true that I was the last person to talk to him before he went seeking the Grail.  He said he would seek information from the Lady of the Lake.
column2: 不過，確實是我最後與他交談——就在他啟程尋找聖杯之前。他說他打算向湖中女神打聽消息。

column1: The watery tart.
column2: 那水裡的蕩婦罷了。

column1: It is your Book of Lore, full of many things you need to know, including the Message of the Rose.
column2: 這是你的智典，裡頭記載著你需要知曉的諸多事物，包括玫瑰箴言。

column1: I would gladly speak more, but I beg you to delay not another moment in beginning your mission.
column2: 我很樂意再多說些，但求你莫再遲延片刻，速速展開你的使命。

column1: Move closer to her.
column2: 再靠近她一些。

column1: Her lips do not reach that far.
column2: 她的唇夠不到那麼遠。

column1: Nay, Arthur.  You must go now, before the sin of lust makes you unworthy to find the Grail!
column2: 不可，亞瑟。你必須立刻離開，免得色慾之罪讓你失去尋得聖杯的資格！

column1: Get a little closer.
column2: 再靠近一點。

column1: As nice as this is, Arthur, it does not further your mission.
column2: 這固然美好，亞瑟，但無助於你的使命。

column1: Violence in the soul will place the Grail forever beyond your reach.
column2: 心中一旦有了暴戾之氣，聖杯便將永遠遙不可及。

column1: Jealousy is a poison to the heart and does not become your noble character.
column2: 嫉妒是侵蝕人心的毒藥，配不上你高貴的品格。

column1: Really, husband.  There will be time enough for that if....I mean, when you return.
column2: 真是的，夫君。等你……我是說，等你歸來之後，有的是時間做這些事。

column1: Truly, if you wish to help me and your kingdom, you will search for the Grail at once!
column2: 你若真心想幫助我與你的王國，此刻就該立刻啟程尋找聖杯！

column1: Such delights must wait until you have returned with the Grail.
column2: 這樣的歡愉，得等你帶著聖杯歸來之後才行。

column1: You have no good reason to insult the woman you love and your queen.
column2: 你沒有理由這樣侮辱你所愛的女人，也是你的王后。

column1: Gwenhyver looks puzzled.  I know I am.
column2: 昆海兒露出困惑的神情。老實說，我也是。

column1: There is only one rose left in her garden, but I have no doubt she would be glad for you to have it.
column2: 她的花園裡只剩最後一朵玫瑰，但我毫不懷疑，她會樂意讓你擁有它。

column1: Why what?  Why do we live?  Why do we die?  If you wish to ask me about something specific, fine.  Otherwise, save the sweeping philosophical questions for another time.
column2: 為什麼什麼？為什麼我們活著？為什麼我們終將一死？你若想問些具體的事，儘管問。否則，這種漫無邊際的哲學問題，還是留到別的時候再說吧。

column1: Aye, the sky is overhead as usual.
column2: 是的，天空一如往常懸在頭頂。

column1: Your land is cursed and only the Grail can heal it.
column2: 你的國土受了詛咒，唯有聖杯能夠治癒它。

column1: The ground is made of soil, as most ground is.
column2: 這地面由泥土構成，如同大多數地面一樣。

column1: There are no berries, only dying leaves.
column2: 沒有漿果，只有正在枯萎的葉子。

column1: Gwenhyver awaits you in her bower.  The blight on Camelot has not spared this place, once the most beautiful garden in the land.
column2: 昆海兒在她的花園裡等著你。肯萊特的枯朽之災，也沒有放過這裡——曾是全國最美的花園。

column1: Without the queen here, this dying bower is a sad and empty place.
column2: 沒有王后在此，這座垂死的花園顯得格外淒涼、空蕩。

column1: They are such gossips. And none are pure in heart as your queen.
column2: 她們最愛說長道短。而且沒有一個像你的王后那樣心地純正。

column1: If there is any news of Launcelot, Gwenhyver is bound to know it.
column2: 若有蘭斯洛特的消息，昆海兒必定知曉。

column1: But she's gone.
column2: 但她已經不在了。

column1: She is no longer here. Perhaps she went to the Chapel to pray for your success.
column2: 她已不在此處。或許她去了神殿，為你的成功祈禱。

column1: She's not here.
column2: 她不在這裡。

column1: The bushes are dying from the curse upon Camelot.
column2: 這些灌木正因肯萊特所受的詛咒而枯萎。

column1: The walls, not surprisingly, are made of grey stone.
column2: 這些牆，不出所料，是灰石砌成的。

column1: This tower houses ladies of the court, unmarried girls and spinster women, mainly.
column2: 這座塔主要住著宮廷仕女，多是未婚少女與未嫁的婦人。

column1: You cannot actually see in from here, but I believe it is the ladies' sewing room inside.  Hardly of interest to you.
column2: 你在此處看不進去，但我想裡頭是女眷的針線房。你對此應無興趣。

column1: The fountain has run dry, like most of Camelot's water.
column2: 這座噴泉已然乾涸，如同肯萊特大半的水源。

column1: There is none.  The Queen's fountain has dried up, like so many of Camelot's lakes and rivers.  It is one more reminder of the curse which you alone can undo by finding the Grail.
column2: 沒有了。王后的噴泉已經乾涸，如同肯萊特眾多的湖泊與河流一般。這又提醒你：唯有尋得聖杯，才能解除這詛咒。

column1: It is a plain stone bench.
column2: 這是一張樸素的石凳。

column1: They are dying from the curse upon Camelot.
column2: 它們正因肯萊特所受的詛咒而枯死。

column1: You often hunt those hills, even as far as the distant Mendip Hills. But this is no time to be daydreaming.
column2: 你常在那片丘陵狩獵，甚至遠至門迪普丘陵。但此刻不是耽於幻想的時候。

column1: I have all the wealth I need and desire no more earthly goods, only the salvation of our land.
column2: 我所需的財富已然足夠，不再渴求塵世的財物，只盼我們的國土得到拯救。

column1: You have better things to do than peek into the ladies' sewing room.
column2: 你有更要緊的事得做，何必窺探女眷的針線房。

column1: This is not the time for scrambling about like a boy.
column2: 此刻不是像個孩子般東奔西跑的時候。

column1: Wanton violence taints the soul.
column2: 恣意的暴力會玷污靈魂。

column1: Though you may desire to sit in the sun, your mission is too urgent to wait.
column2: 你或許渴望坐下曬曬陽光，但你的使命緊迫，容不得等待。

column1: None of these leaves has any particular value.
column2: 這些葉子並無特別的價值。

column1: The only rose has already been picked.
column2: 唯一的那朵玫瑰已經摘下了。

column1: You don't need to.
column2: 你不需要這麼做。

column1: You would be a poor husband indeed to be so careless.
column2: 若你如此粗心大意，實在稱不上是個好丈夫。

column1: She was being poetic, Arthur. She meant only to carry it with you.
column2: 她只是說得詩意些罷了，亞瑟。她的意思不過是要你隨身帶著它。

column1: There is nothing quite as exciting as a man with a long sword.
column2: 沒有什麼比佩著長劍的男子更令人心動的了。

column1: Fond as I am of your sword, Arthur, I would rather that you save it for a better use.
column2: 亞瑟，我雖鍾愛你的劍，但寧可你將它留待更好的用處。

column1: Your sword is unequalled in all of Christendom.  But for my peace of mind, I prefer to see it sheathed.
column2: 你的劍在整個基督教世界裡無人能及。但為了我心安，我還是希望見它入鞘。

column1: Arthur, the gods are jealous of their gold. It would be the greatest sacrilege, one which cannot be undone. Think again before you try this.
column2: 亞瑟，諸神看重他們的金子。此舉將是莫大的褻瀆，一旦犯下便無可挽回。動手之前，再三思量。

column1: Since you are determined to commit this sacrilege, I will say nothing more. Your doom is your own.
column2: 既然你執意要犯下這等褻瀆，我便不再多言。你的劫數，自行承擔。

column1: Fool.
column2: 愚蠢。

column1: Arthur, it is not wise to insult a god. Think before you do this.
column2: 亞瑟，觸怒神明並非明智之舉。動手之前，先想清楚。

column1: Alas, I fear you bring much evil upon yourself by such an unwise act.
column2: 唉，恐怕你這般輕率之舉，會為自己招來重重災禍。

column1: Unwise, Arthur, unwise.
column2: 不智啊，亞瑟，太不智了。

column1: The sacred fire of Mithras is lit. The blessing has been given.
column2: 米夏拉的聖火已然點燃，恩賜已然降下。

column1: Only the blessing of Mithras can light this candle.
column2: 唯有米夏拉的恩賜，才能點燃這支蠟燭。

column1: The sacred fire of Christ is lit. The blessing has been given.
column2: 基督的聖火已然點燃，恩賜已然降下。

column1: Only the blessing of Christ can light this candle.
column2: 唯有基督的恩賜，才能點燃這支蠟燭。

column1: The ceiling arches over your head like the great vaults of heaven.
column2: 天花板在你頭頂拱起，宛如浩瀚的天穹。

column1: The floor is made of inlaid stones.
column2: 地板由鑲嵌的石塊鋪成。

column1: There is nothing but a dark space.
column2: 那裡除了一片黑暗，什麼也沒有。

column1: Those are pads to kneel upon.
column2: 那些是供人跪拜的墊子。

column1: Look again.  Methinks you are confused.
column2: 再看仔細些，我看你是糊塗了。

column1: There is only one thing more deadly than offending a god.
column2: 世上只有一件事，比觸怒一位神明更為致命。

column1: Offending two gods.
column2: 那便是同時觸怒兩位神明。

column1: The cross is an ancient symbol that has been adopted by the followers of the Christ god.
column2: 十字是個古老的符號，後為基督信徒所採用。

column1: The symbol of Mithras has emblazoned many a warrior's shield, for he has been primarily a soldier's god.
column2: 米夏拉的標識曾裝點過無數戰士的盾牌，因為他向來是軍人的守護神。

column1: Those are symbols of Isis and Vesta. What they are doing in this chapel, I do not know.
column2: 那些是艾西斯與維斯塔的標識。它們為何會出現在這座神殿裡，我也不得而知。

column1: This is a relatively new religion, but it has grown enormously in power over the last few centuries. Most of your people now worship the Christ god.
column2: 這是一個相對年輕的信仰，但在過去幾個世紀裡勢力大增。如今你的子民多半信奉基督。

column1: Mithras the warrior god has been worshipped for many, many centuries and was the favorite of Roman soldiers.
column2: 戰神米夏拉受人供奉已有數百年之久，向來深受羅馬士兵愛戴。

column1: On the right is the altar of Christ.  On the left is the altar of Mithras.
column2: 右側是基督的祭壇，左側是米夏拉的祭壇。

column1: The double altar in the Chapel of the Two Gods reflects the power struggle between an old and new religion.
column2: 雙神神殿裡的這座雙祭壇，映照出新舊信仰之間的權力角力。

column1: Most of this room is made of stone: the altars, the floor, the pillars.
column2: 這房間大半以石造成：祭壇、地板、廊柱皆然。

column1: The walls are lined with decorative columns.
column2: 牆邊立著一排裝飾用的廊柱。

column1: They hold up the ceiling.
column2: 它們撐起了天花板。

column1: The intertwining lines upon the double altar is Celtic knotwork.
column2: 雙祭壇上交纏的線條，是凱爾特結紋。

column1: The highly decorative pillar is one of the main supports for the ceiling.
column2: 這根裝飾繁複的廊柱，是支撐天花板的主要柱子之一。

column1: The vision is sent to remind you that you must be morally pure to possess it.  Every deed and decision in your mission will be weighed in judgement.
column2: 這異象是要提醒你：唯有心靈純淨之人才配擁有它。你此行的一言一行、每個抉擇，都將受到審判衡量。

column1: Mithras shows you perils that have befallen or will befall your three knights.  He reminds you that, as king, you are responsible for their lives.
column2: 米夏拉向你展示你三位騎士已經或即將遭遇的險境，提醒你身為君王，須對他們的性命負責。

column1: I hope you are not seeing something that I do not see. It would not bode well for your mission.
column2: 我盼你所見並非我未曾見過之物，否則對你的使命絕非吉兆。

column1: They are not bowls.  They are altar candles.
column2: 那些不是碗，是祭壇上的蠟燭。

column1: Upon the right is the cross, symbol of the Christ god who was crucified upon one.
column2: 右邊是十字，基督便是被釘死在十字架上，因而成了祂的標識。

column1: Upon the left is the symbol of Mithras, formerly carried upon banners into battle.
column2: 左邊是米夏拉的標識，昔日曾被繡上軍旗、隨軍出征。

column1: Only the blessing of Mithras can light the candle on the left.
column2: 唯有米夏拉的恩賜，才能點燃左側的蠟燭。

column1: Only the blessing of Christ can light the candle on the right.
column2: 唯有基督的恩賜，才能點燃右側的蠟燭。

column1: I am sure you will think of something to offer the gods.
column2: 我相信你會想出該獻給諸神什麼供品。

column1: The labarum is the symbol of Mithras.
column2: 拉巴倫是米夏拉的標識。

column1: The skulls are reminders of the death that awaits us all.
column2: 這些骷髏頭提醒著世人，死亡終將降臨眾生。

column1: And may the god of your choice protect you.
column2: 願你所選的神明護佑於你。

column1: That is beyond your powers. Or mine.
column2: 那超出了你的能力範圍，也超出了我的。

column1: That can be arranged.
column2: 這可以安排。

column1: Not in this place. You need all the help you can get.
column2: 此處不可。你需要一切能得到的助力。

column1: The gods are always fond of offerings.  Depending, of course, upon what it is you intend to offer.
column2: 諸神向來喜愛供品，當然，這得看你打算獻上什麼。

column1: That is not the sort of offering the gods desire.
column2: 那並非諸神所欲的供品。

column1: The candle is not lit.
column2: 這支蠟燭並未點燃。

column1: I do not understand what you hope to gain by having burnt fingers.
column2: 我不明白你燙傷手指究竟想換得什麼。

column1: It is said that the gods prefer prayers offered upon bended knee.
column2: 據說諸神偏愛跪地獻上的禱告。

column1: Perhaps the gods need more tangible proof of your devotion before they will grant a blessing.
column2: 或許諸神在賜下恩典之前，需要更實質的證明，證明你的虔誠。

column1: The lighting of the sacred fire is the god's way of telling you that your prayers are heard.
column2: 聖火燃起，便是神明告訴你祂已聽見你禱告的方式。

column1: The gods prefer to hear prayers from bended knee.
column2: 諸神偏愛聽見跪地獻上的禱告。

column1: Arthur, pay attention.  You are already on your knees.
column2: 亞瑟，留意些。你已經跪著了。

column1: It does not require a wizard to see that you ARE standing.
column2: 不必是巫師也看得出，你現在正站著。

column1: Humbling yourself is the first step in dealing with any god.
column2: 謙卑自抑，是與任何神明打交道的第一步。

column1: Your prayers have been heard and the blessing given.
column2: 你的禱告已蒙垂聽，恩賜已然降下。

column1: You have incurred Mithras' wrath.  Nothing can help you now.
column2: 你已招來米夏拉的怒火，如今再無挽回餘地。

column1: I suspect that an earthly gift may help your prayers to reach the heavens.
column2: 我猜想，一份塵世的供品或許有助於你的禱告上達天聽。

column1: You have incurred Christ's wrath.  Nothing can help you now.
column2: 你已招來基督的怒火，如今再無挽回餘地。

column1: You have no money.
column2: 你身無分文。

column1: Before a god will accept money, he must be shown the proper reverence.
column2: 神明接受供奉之前，須先受到應有的敬意。

column1: The vision was a gift, not a purchase. It will not appear again.
column2: 那異象是一份恩賜，並非可以買來的東西，它不會再度出現。

column1: You would not listen to warnings.  Now you are under Mithras' curse and nothing can undo it.
column2: 你不聽勸誡，如今已受米夏拉的詛咒，再無法解除。

column1: You have already been blessed.
column2: 你已蒙受恩賜。

column1: The dull clunk of a copper coin does not seem to excite much interest from the gods of this chapel.
column2: 一枚銅幣落地的悶響，似乎難以引起這神殿諸神的興趣。

column1: The vision was a gift, not a purchase.  It will not appear again.
column2: 那異象是一份恩賜，並非可以買來的東西，它不會再度出現。

column1: You would not listen to warnings.  Now you are under Christ's curse and nothing can undo it.
column2: 你不聽勸誡，如今已受基督的詛咒，再無法解除。

column1: That would require preparations and priests and too much time. The blessing of the god is enough to ask for.
column2: 那需要諸多準備、祭司主持，還要耗費太多時間。只求神明的恩賜便已足夠。

column1: And bring down the curse of the god? Do not even think it!
column2: 還要招來神明的詛咒？想都別想！

column1: Your doom is now sealed.
column2: 你的劫數已然註定。

column1: There are no gold coins upon the altar.
column2: 祭壇上沒有金幣。

column1: There are no silver coins upon the altar.
column2: 祭壇上沒有銀幣。

column1: The gods may not notice the loss of a bit of copper.
column2: 少了一點銅幣，諸神或許不會察覺。

column1: There are no copper coins upon the altar.
column2: 祭壇上沒有銅幣。

column1: If you wish to get more money, you must go to the Treasury. In this place, you should think only in terms of giving.
column2: 你若想取得更多錢財，須前往寶庫。在此處，你該想的只有給予。

column1: Which coin do you want?
column2: 你要哪一種錢幣？

column1: It would make a lovely offering, but is not quite what the gods want.
column2: 這雖是件討喜的供品，卻不是諸神真正想要的。

column1: You're not close enough to a flame and you do not want to be.  Trust me.
column2: 你離火焰還不夠近，而你也不會想要靠得更近。相信我。

column1: The fire is not lit on this candle, Arthur
column2: 這支蠟燭上並未點著火，亞瑟

column1: Burn a gift of love from Gwenhyver?  I would seriously reconsider.
column2: 燒掉昆海兒所贈的愛的信物？我勸你三思。

column1: Nothing is left but ashes.  I sense you have angered the gods and no good will come of this.
column2: 只剩下一堆灰燼。我感覺得到，你已觸怒了諸神，此事絕無好結果。

column1: You have not yet been given the blessing of the flame.
column2: 你尚未獲得聖火的恩賜。

column1: Are you mad?  It is a sign that Christ has heard your prayers and given his blessing.
column2: 你瘋了嗎？那是基督已聽見你禱告、賜下恩典的徵兆。

column1: Mithras has ways of punishing fools who tamper with his holy fire.
column2: 米夏拉自有懲罰之道，對付膽敢褻瀆他聖火的愚人。

column1: There. You have nothing better to show for it than burnt fingers.
column2: 瞧，除了燙傷的手指，你什麼也沒換到。

column1: That belongs here and is of no use to you.
column2: 那東西屬於此處，對你毫無用處。

column1: Those are not bowls.  Those are altar candles and must be left on the altars.
column2: 那些不是碗，是祭壇上的蠟燭，必須留在祭壇上。

column1: Only the blessing of a god can do that.
column2: 唯有神明的恩賜，才能做到這一點。

column1: The Christ god does not approve of such things.
column2: 基督不贊同這樣的事。

column1: Once, in very ancient times, the sacrifice of a white bull would have been proper.  But there is no time for that now.
column2: 遠古之時，獻上一頭白牛原本才是合宜的祭品。但如今，已沒有時間這麼做了。

column1: You cannot draw your sword from your knees.
column2: 你跪著時無法拔劍。

column1: You annoy the gods by brandishing a weapon in this sacred place.
column2: 在這神聖之地揮舞兵刃，會惹惱諸神。

column1: Your knees must be getting sore.  Perhaps you should consider doing something.
column2: 你的膝蓋想必已經跪痠了。或許你該考慮做點什麼。

column1: The flame is lit and the blessing given, but wait....
column2: 聖火已點燃，恩賜已降下，但且慢……

column1: Mithras sends you visions of your missing knights. And listen! Their voices call out to you in distress!
column2: 米夏拉向你展示你失蹤騎士們的異象。且聽！他們的聲音正痛苦地向你呼喚！

column1: Save me, most valiant king! I am injured unto the death by a black fiend. The green leaves will cover my bones unless you are quick.
column2: 救救我，至勇的王啊！我為一個黑暗惡魔所傷，命在旦夕。你若不快，青葉終將覆蓋我的白骨。

column1: Arthur, I cannot move. I cannot escape. And I am so cold, so terribly cold. Ah, how can she be so heartless?!
column2: 亞瑟，我動彈不得，無法逃脫。我好冷，冷得徹骨。啊，她怎能如此狠心？！

column1: I am lost in the darkness, hidden from light and life, with only the rats to lust for my flesh and blood. I will die here unless you help me, my king.
column2: 我迷失在黑暗之中，不見天光，不見生機，唯有鼠群覬覦著我的血肉。吾王，你若不來救我，我將死在此處。

column1: The flame is lit. You have been blessed, and now something shimmers in the air....
column2: 聖火已點燃，你已蒙受恩賜，此刻空氣中似有什麼正閃爍著微光……

column1: A vision of the Grail appears to you. Christ sends it to remind you that only a man of purity may attain this sacred cup.
column2: 聖杯的異象在你眼前浮現。基督藉此提醒你：唯有心靈純淨之人，方能得到這只聖爵。

column1: Remember, the fate of Camelot rests not only upon your finding the Grail, but your worthiness to possess it.
column2: 切記，肯萊特的命運不僅繫於你能否尋得聖杯，更繫於你是否配得擁有它。

column1: That is quite impossible.
column2: 那絕無可能。

column1: The gods do not provide visions upon demand.  Accept what you have been given or you will anger them.
column2: 諸神不會應人所求便賜下異象。接受你已得到的，否則將觸怒他們。

column1: The gods give visions to those who please them.
column2: 諸神只將異象賜給令祂們喜悅的人。

column1: What you saw and heard may have happened or is yet to happen. To learn more, you must find the knights themselves.
column2: 你所見所聞，或許已經發生，或許尚未發生。若想知道更多，你必須親自找到那幾位騎士。

column1: The sacred flame is lit. You and your mission have been blessed.
column2: 聖火已然點燃。你與你的使命，皆已蒙受恩賜。

column1: The guards stand at attention in your presence.
column2: 衛兵們在你面前肅立戒備。

column1: The guard has the air of a man who wants to speak, but is afraid to speak without permission.
column2: 這名衛兵神情像是有話想說，卻又不敢未經允許便開口。

column1: You can't take your horse in the castle.
column2: 你不能把坐騎帶進城堡裡。

column1: The stables are nearby, but your servants tend to all your needs there. You have other, more important concerns.
column2: 馬廄就在附近，但那裡有僕從為你打理一切所需。你還有其他更要緊的事得操心。

column1: Your mule is not yet here.
column2: 你的騾子尚未到此。

column1: My pleasure, m'lord.
column2: 樂意效勞，吾王。

column1: Beggin' your pardon, m'lord?
column2: 恕小人失禮，吾王？

column1: The skies are clear.  'Tis a good day to begin your search.
column2: 天色晴朗。正是啟程尋覓的好日子。

column1: Considering how much of Camelot is made of this grey stone, there must have been a great deal of it around at one time.
column2: 肯萊特有大半是以這種灰石建成，想當年此地想必蘊藏甚豐。

column1: The inner courtyard is guarded by your loyal men.
column2: 內庭由你忠誠的士兵把守。

column1: Your warhorse and a pack mule have been prepared for your journey.
column2: 你的戰馬與一頭馱運的騾子，都已為此行備妥。

column1: It does not look happy about being chosen for this mission, nor about carrying your pack of provisions.
column2: 牠似乎不太樂意被選中執行此行，也不情願馱著你的補給包。

column1: Your mule is being prepared for the journey.
column2: 你的騾子正為此行做準備。

column1: Aye, those are stairs.
column2: 正是，那是階梯。

column1: I can sense the mingling of pride and despair that fills you as you look upon your stronghold and home.
column2: 我能感受到，你望著這座要塞與家園時，心中驕傲與絕望交織。

column1: The thick, stone walls make Camelot virtually impregnable against normal attack.
column2: 厚重的石牆使肯萊特幾乎無懈可擊，尋常攻勢難以攻破。

column1: Against this curse of plague and drought, however, the thickest of stone walls is no defense.
column2: 然而面對這場瘟疫與乾旱的詛咒，再厚的石牆也無濟於事。

column1: It is the main entrance to your castle proper.
column2: 這是通往城堡本體的正門。

column1: The window in the tower is a lookout.
column2: 塔上的窗口是瞭望口。

column1: This tunnel leads to the portcullis which is your outside gate.
column2: 這條甬道通往閘門，也就是你的外門。

column1: It is part of the defensive system of Camelot.
column2: 這是肯萊特防禦體系的一部分。

column1: Your horse is a sturdy and well-trained stallion, bred to be steady in danger and battle.
column2: 你的坐騎是一匹強健且訓練有素的公馬，育種便是為了臨危與臨陣皆能沉穩不亂。

column1: Your grooms prepare the horse and pack mule.  When you are ready, they will be here.
column2: 馬伕正在備妥坐騎與馱運的騾子。待你準備就緒，牠們便會在此候命。

column1: You should know your horse better than that, Arthur. He is a stallion.
column2: 你該比這更了解自己的坐騎才是，亞瑟。牠是匹公馬。

column1: Your guards bear the Royal shields of Camelot.
column2: 你的衛兵持著肯萊特的皇家盾牌。

column1: Your own shield is familiar to you. Your guards, of course, bear the Royal shields of Camelot.
column2: 你對自己的盾牌再熟悉不過。至於你的衛兵，自然持著肯萊特的皇家盾牌。

column1: Your guards have little need for their lances these days.
column2: 你的衛兵近來已鮮少用得上長槍。

column1: It contains water, food, blankets, extra clothing and such things as you may want on a long journey.
column2: 裡頭裝著水、糧食、毛毯、備用衣物，以及長途旅程中你可能用得上的物件。

column1: Your servants are preparing a pack for your trip. It will be ready to go when you are.
column2: 你的僕從正為此行備妥行囊，待你準備完畢，行囊也將備妥待發。

column1: Your own special tack has been used.
column2: 你專屬的馬具已然備上。

column1: There is no tack here.
column2: 此處並無馬具。

column1: Galahad is well liked amongst the guards.  They would be most likely to have news of him.
column2: 葛拉漢在衛兵之間頗受愛戴，他們最有可能得知他的消息。

column1: A clumsy weapon for a long trip. Excaliber is the best weapon you could want.
column2: 長途跋涉帶這種笨重武器不甚妥當。聖劍才是你能擁有的最佳武器。

column1: There will be time enough for that on the journey.
column2: 此事路上自有時間再說。

column1: What the devil for?  Have you lost all common sense?
column2: 這究竟是為了什麼？你莫非失了常識？

column1: There is no pack here.
column2: 此處並無行囊。

column1: Your horse is already here.
column2: 你的坐騎已在此處。

column1: Your mule is already here.
column2: 你的騾子已在此處。

column1: It is being prepared. When your own preparations are complete, it will surely be ready and waiting for you.
column2: 牠正在備妥中。待你自己準備就緒，牠必已備妥候著你。

column1: It is not only difficult, but pointless.
column2: 此事不僅困難，更是毫無意義。

column1: Lead and it will follow.
column2: 你只管引路，牠自會跟上。

column1: Your grooms have seen to such details, though you are wise to think of it.
column2: 這類細節馬伕早已辦妥，不過你想到這一點也算明智。

column1: A horse is for riding.
column2: 馬是用來騎的。

column1: Why would you want to ride a bony little mule when you have your fine stallion?
column2: 你既有這匹駿馬，何苦去騎那頭瘦骨嶙峋的小騾子？

column1: Nay, 'tis the other way around. The mule follows you.
column2: 不，恰恰相反。是騾子跟著你走。

column1: Why do you draw your sword here?  You are safely surrounded by your own men.
column2: 你為何在此拔劍？你身邊盡是自己的士兵，安全無虞。

column1: This is no time for sword practice with your men.
column2: 此刻不是與士兵練劍的時候。

column1: The legend says that a man with violence in his soul will be destroyed if he touches the Grail.
column2: 傳說中，心懷暴戾之人若觸碰聖杯，必遭毀滅。

column1: It is a rather ordinary shield.
column2: 這是面相當普通的盾牌。

column1: It is a rather ordinary spear.
column2: 這是柄相當普通的長矛。

column1: Forgive me, sire, I do not understand.
column2: 恕臣不解，陛下。

column1: Standing closer to a guard would help.
column2: 靠近某位衛兵些，或許有幫助。

column1: You are my king, sire.
column2: 你是臣的君王，陛下。

column1: I am your faithful and loyal servant, my liege.
column2: 臣是陛下忠誠效命的僕從，吾主。

column1: Your horse, mule and pack are being prepared.
column2: 你的坐騎、騾子與行囊都在備妥中。

column1: Your horse is saddled and ready. The mule bears your pack of provisions.
column2: 你的坐騎已備鞍待發，騾子則馱著你的補給行囊。

column1: I have no news of him, m'lord.
column2: 小人並無他的消息，吾王。

column1: She should be in the castle, m'lord.
column2: 她應當在城堡裡，吾王。

column1: I am sure you know more than me about that, sire, me being only a guard and all.
column2: 陛下想必比小人更清楚此事，畢竟小人不過是個衛兵。

column1: The man yonder, to the left of the arch, is the smartest of all of us, m'lord.
column2: 拱門左側那人，是我們當中最機靈的一個，吾王。

column1: May God protect you, m'lord.
column2: 願上帝保佑你，吾王。

column1: May God lead you to the Grail, my King.
column2: 願上帝引領你尋得聖杯，吾王。

column1: We pray for your success, King Arthur.
column2: 我們為你的成功祈禱，亞瑟王。

column1: Mithras guide and protect you.
column2: 願米夏拉引導並庇佑你。

column1: Such miserliness does not become a king.
column2: 如此吝嗇，實非人君之風。

column1: All the armour gets in the way, fortunately.
column2: 所幸這身甲冑正好擋路，礙手礙腳。

column1: They have no use for it.
column2: 他們用不著這個。

column1: Very sweet of you, m'lord.
column2: 你真是體貼，吾王。

column1: You don't have any money.
column2: 你身上沒有錢。

column1: Bless you, m'lord!
column2: 願神保佑你，吾王！

column1: Thank'ee most kindly, m'lord!
column2: 多謝吾王厚賜！

column1: Praise be your generosity, King Arthur!
column2: 讚頌你的慷慨，亞瑟王！

column1: Arthur, will you please stop trying to give away your most valuable possessions.
column2: 亞瑟，別再想著把你最貴重的物件送人了。

column1: As you command.
column2: 遵命。

column1: Their weapons are inferior to Excaliber.
column2: 他們的武器比不上聖劍。

column1: Besides which, they need them to defend Camelot in your absence.
column2: 何況你不在時，他們還得靠這些武器防守肯萊特。

column1: You guard needs it.
column2: 你的衛兵需要它。

column1: They are unable to do that.
column2: 他們辦不到此事。

column1: Their place is here, guarding Camelot.
column2: 他們的崗位在此，守衛肯萊特。

column1: Is this some odd Celtic word, m'lord?
column2: 這是什麼古怪的凱爾特語嗎，吾王？

column1: Greetings, my liege.
column2: 向吾主問安。

column1: Uh....no, thank you, m'lord.
column2: 呃……不了，多謝，吾王。

column1: What a thoroughly disgusting idea.
column2: 好個令人作嘔的念頭。

column1: These are not the thoughts of a pure man.
column2: 這可不是清白之人該有的念頭。

column1: The Christians say that stealing is a sin and no sinner may lay hands upon the Grail and live.
column2: 基督徒說偷竊是一種罪，罪人若碰觸聖杯，必難逃一死。

column1: You can only help us by bringing back the Grail before it is too late.
column2: 你唯有趁一切還來得及，將聖杯尋回，才能真正幫上我們。

column1: Your horse is trained only to fight your enemies, not your friends.
column2: 你的坐騎只受過與敵人交戰的訓練，不會對付你的朋友。

column1: You're not on the horse.
column2: 你並未騎在馬上。

column1: That is not becoming of a king.
column2: 此舉有失人君之儀。

column1: His horse was sent back to our care by the Harbourmaster of Southampton.
column2: 南安普頓港的港務司已將他的坐騎送回，交由我們照料。

column1: Along with a message from the Harbourmaster that Sir Galahad took ship to the Far East.
column2: 港務司還捎來口信，說葛拉漢爵士已搭船前往遠東。

column1: Very well, m'lord.
column2: 遵命，吾王。

column1: My Lord King, I have news of Galahad, if you would care to hear it.
column2: 吾王陛下，臣有葛拉漢的消息，不知陛下是否願聞。

column1: That is all I know, m'lord.  Godspeed you on your mission.
column2: 小人所知僅此而已，吾王。願你此行一路平安。

column1: My pleasure, m'lord.  I only thought to mention in case no-one else had told you, sir.
column2: 樂意效勞，吾王。小人只是想著，若無人稟報，還是說一聲的好。

column1: Your horse and mule are being prepared for the journey.
column2: 你的坐騎與騾子正為此行備妥。

column1: Your horse and mule await you in the courtyard.
column2: 你的坐騎與騾子在庭院中候著你。

column1: The skies are clear and the weather holding good. A fine time to begin a journey.
column2: 天色晴朗，天候良好，正是啟程的好時機。

column1: Amazingly enough, it is also paved with stone.
column2: 說來也是，這裡同樣鋪著石板。

column1: Here your journey begins in earnest. Search your soul and be sure you are ready.
column2: 你的旅程將自此正式展開。捫心自問，確認自己已準備就緒。

column1: Once you leave Camelot, I will seal the castle with a powerful spell of protection. You will not be able to re-enter until you have the Grail.
column2: 你一旦離開肯萊特，我便會以強大的護城法術封印城堡。在你尋得聖杯之前，你將無法再度進入。

column1: This is the main gate of Camelot.
column2: 這是肯萊特的正門。

column1: It stands tall, strong and proud. Yet if you fail, it will not endure.
column2: 它高聳、堅固、巍然而立。然而你若失敗，它終將不保。

column1: The top of the tunnel is also stone.
column2: 甬道的頂部同樣是石造。

column1: It is fairly dark in here. There is not much to see.
column2: 這裡相當昏暗，沒什麼好看的。

column1: It leads to the courtyard and the main door to the castle.
column2: 它通往庭院與城堡的正門。

column1: The boulders are part of the castle's foundation.
column2: 這些巨石是城堡地基的一部分。

column1: This heavy portcullis was built to withstand even a battering ram.
column2: 這座沉重的閘門，就連攻城槌也難以撼動。

column1: You surely know your own symbol, Arthur, the red dragon of Pendragon.
column2: 你當然認得自己的家徽，亞瑟，那是潘德拉貢的紅龍。

column1: The walls are massive and built of stone.
column2: 城牆雄偉厚重，以石砌成。

column1: Travel on and the map will guide you.
column2: 繼續前行，地圖自會為你指路。

column1: There is no moat. Your protection is in the high walls and steep cliffs.
column2: 這裡沒有護城河，你的屏障在於高聳的城牆與陡峭的懸崖。

column1: Camelot was designed without a drawbridge.
column2: 肯萊特建造之初便未設吊橋。

column1: He is safe within. Worry not.
column2: 他在裡頭很安全，無須擔憂。

column1: And fall to your death? Ridiculous.
column2: 摔下去送命？荒唐。

column1: You already are on your horse.
column2: 你已騎在馬上。

column1: You don't need to get off your horse.
column2: 你不必下馬。

column1: It IS open.
column2: 它確實是開著的。

column1: You may not return, Arthur, until you have found the Grail...or died in trying. To turn aside or abandon your sacred mission means the certain death of all you hold dear.
column2: 亞瑟，除非你尋得聖杯……或死於途中，否則你不得回返。若你轉身逃避或放棄這項神聖使命，你所珍愛的一切必將盡數殞落。

column1: You can hardly begin a long and arduous journey in your court clothes.
column2: 你穿著宮廷袍服，如何踏上這般漫長艱辛的旅途。

column1: Do you think this is a fairytale where you can simply run off without preparation?
column2: 你以為這是童話故事，可以毫無準備便說走就走？

column1: Certainly.  As soon as you have a horse under you, as common sense would require.
column2: 當然可以，只消你胯下有匹馬便行，這是常理所需。

column1: This is no time for petulance or foolishness.   The lives of all your people hang in the balance.
column2: 此刻不是任性胡鬧的時候。你全體子民的性命，皆懸於一線。

column1: It IS lowered
column2: 它確實已經放下。

column1: It will be done.  You need not worry.
column2: 此事必會辦妥，你無須擔憂。

column1: Excaliber is a powerful sword, but even it cannot break this portcullis.
column2: 聖劍雖是把威力強大的劍，卻也劈不開這座閘門。

column1: There is no need.  It will follow.
column2: 無此必要，牠自會跟上。

column1: It is on the mule which follows you.
column2: 它就在跟著你的那頭騾子身上。

column1: It is rather early for that.  You have not even begun to travel.
column2: 現在說這個還太早，你連旅程都還沒展開。

column1: If it is ready, it will be in the courtyard.
column2: 若已備妥，便會在庭院裡。

column1: What an utterly ridiculous idea.
column2: 好個荒唐透頂的念頭。

column1: They are at their posts where they belong.
column2: 他們都在自己該駐守的崗位上。

column1: This is your mission alone, Arthur.  They cannot help you.
column2: 這是你獨自的使命，亞瑟，他們幫不上忙。

column1: It is terribly unwise to start a sacred mission without the blessings of the gods.
column2: 未得諸神庇佑便展開這神聖的使命，實在極不明智。

column1: The Christ god does not like being ignored.  His vengeance is swift and final.
column2: 基督之神不喜受人漠視，祂的報應迅速而不容轉圜。

column1: Alas, Mithras is a bad god to offend.  Remember this, in your next life.
column2: 唉，米夏拉可不是能輕易冒犯的神祇。這一點，留待你來世牢記吧。

column1: One does not get far when the gods are offended.
column2: 觸怒了神明，是走不了多遠的。

column1: Widdershins is a forest sprite.  It must inhabit this shrine.
column2: Widdershins 是森林精靈，想必就棲居在這座神龕裡。

column1: It is an old, bronze statue of Cernunnos and he holds out a cup for offerings.
column2: 這是一尊古老的青銅像，塑的是 Cernunnos，祂伸出雙手捧著一只杯子，等候供品。

column1: Ah!  Of course!  The idol is bronze.  That explains Widdershins's toll of copper or tin.
column2: 啊！這就對了！這尊神像是青銅所鑄，難怪 Widdershins 收的過路費，非銅即錫。

column1: This shrine contains a bronze statue of the Celtic god, Cernunnos, within a stone housing.
column2: 這座石造神龕裡，供奉著凱爾特神祇 Cernunnos 的青銅像。

column1: 'Tis a rock.
column2: 這是一塊岩石。

column1: 'Tis a tree.
column2: 這是一棵樹。

column1: 'Tis a bush.
column2: 這是一叢灌木。

column1: The forest sprite is not a man.
column2: 這森林精靈並非凡人。

column1: There is no one here.
column2: 此處空無一人。

column1: The miserable sprite has turned everything but your copper coins into pebbles!
column2: 這可惡的精靈把你身上除了銅幣之外的東西全變成了石子！

column1: Your copper coins are untouched by the spell.
column2: 你的銅幣未受此咒波及。

column1: I would worry less about the pebbles than about how to get Widdershins to undo his trick.
column2: 與其擔心那些石子，不如想想該如何讓 Widdershins 收回這個惡作劇。

column1: You have more important things to worry about than pebbles.
column2: 比起石子，你有更要緊的事該操心。

column1: Mercifully, he is gone.
column2: 所幸，他已經離開了。

column1: Widdershins only wants a bit of copper.  I would not be stingy, if I were you.
column2: Widdershins 要的不過是一點銅幣。若我是你，可不會這麼小氣。

column1: Try not to disturb Widdershins again.
column2: 盡量別再驚動 Widdershins 了。

column1: The mischievous forest sprite, Widdershins, is perched upon the shrine, waiting for you to pay his toll.
column2: 頑皮的森林精靈 Widdershins 蹲踞在神龕上，等著你繳納過路費。

column1: It should look familiar.  This is where you entered the forest and there is the little shrine.
column2: 這裡你該不陌生。你就是從這裡踏入森林的，那座小神龕也在此處。

column1: Let us hope Widdershins is asleep.
column2: 但願 Widdershins 正在沉睡。

column1: You must pass through the Forest Perilous to reach Glastonbury Tor.  The forest is so named because of the many dangers hidden within.
column2: 你必須穿越派瑞樂斯森林，才能抵達格列斯登伯利山。這座森林之所以如此命名，正因其中潛藏著重重危機。

column1: In this clearing, there is a very old forest shrine.
column2: 這片林間空地上，立著一座古老的森林神龕。

column1: He has returned to his hiding place inside the shrine.
column2: 他已退回神龕裡的藏身之處。

column1: It is empty
column2: 此處空無一物

column1: The statue of Cernunnos has antlers, representing the fertility of the stag.
column2: Cernunnos 的塑像頭生鹿角，象徵雄鹿的豐饒生機。

column1: Cernunnos is an ancient Celtic god of the hunt or sometimes of the underworld.
column2: Cernunnos 是凱爾特人古老的狩獵之神，有時也被視為冥界之神。

column1: The bronze statue is of the Celtic god, Cernunnos.
column2: 這尊青銅像塑的是凱爾特神祇 Cernunnos。

column1: If he passed this way, he left no traces.
column2: 縱使他曾路過此地，也未留下任何痕跡。

column1: It is not very powerful, but such sprites are quite mischievous and will play small, but nasty tricks upon those who displease them.
column2: 他法力不算高強，但這類精靈生性頑皮，遇上惹惱自己的人，便會使出些雖小卻惡毒的把戲。

column1: The idol is bronze and bronze is an alloy made of copper and tin.  Widdershins has become obsessed, I would say, with making bronze.
column2: 這尊神像是青銅所鑄，青銅乃銅與錫合煉而成的合金。依我看，Widdershins 是著了鑄造青銅的魔。

column1: It does not speak.  It does not even hear.
column2: 它不會說話，甚至聽不見。

column1: You have none to give.
column2: 你身上並無可以奉上之物。

column1: Get closer to the front of the shrine.
column2: 再靠近神龕正面一些。

column1: You will never see that money again.
column2: 那筆錢，你是再也見不著了。

column1: Ah, how pleasant.  He has gone away for now.
column2: 啊，真是清靜。他這會兒已經走了。

column1: That is of no use here.
column2: 此物在此毫無用處。

column1: You have only just entered the Forest Perilous. That can wait until later.  For now, be on your guard.
column2: 你才剛踏入派瑞樂斯森林，那事不妨稍後再議。眼下，還是提高警覺為要。

column1: You cannot really harm such an elemental creature with mere force.
column2: 單憑蠻力，你傷不了這種元素精怪。

column1: Besides, you would have to catch it first and that is nearly impossible.
column2: 再說，你得先逮住牠才行，而那幾乎是不可能的事。

column1: I could do so with a spell, but only if I were there in person.  You will never do so otherwise.
column2: 我倒是能施法辦到，但得親身在場才行。否則，你是絕無可能做到的。

column1: You have not the means to shatter stone or break bronze.  Besides, the shrine is holy and not to blame that Widdershins has taken up residence in it.
column2: 你沒有能耐擊碎岩石或毀壞青銅。再說，這神龕本是聖地，Widdershins 選中此處棲身，也怪不得它。

column1: You will find it is too heavy and solidly rooted in the ground.
column2: 你會發現它重不可舉，且深深扎根於地。

column1: You cannot harm a sprite with mere steel.
column2: 區區鋼鐵，傷不了精靈。

column1: Copper or tin! Copper or tin! Copper or tin for Widdershins!
column2: 銅也好，錫也好！銅也好，錫也好！Widdershins 只要銅或錫！

column1: Single-minded creature, is he not?
column2: 這傢伙倒是心無旁騖，是吧？

column1: The sprite has struck!  He has afflicted you with an attack of stinging ants!
column2: 精靈出手了！他放出一群螫人的螞蟻襲擊你！

column1: By my beard!  You no sooner put the copper in the shrine than the sprite made off with it.
column2: 我的鬍子啊！你才剛把銅幣放進神龕，那精靈轉眼便捲著它跑了。

column1: Ah, did you feel a tingling?  The trick has been undone, but check your purse, if you wish to make sure.
column2: 啊，你感覺到一陣刺麻了嗎？這惡作劇已經解除，但你若想確認，不妨查看一下錢囊。

column1: There is no sign of the sprite, yet you know he must stil be about.
column2: 精靈不見蹤影，但你明白他必定仍在附近。

column1: Copper is mine! Copper divine! Go your way, No trick I will play.
column2: 銅幣歸我，銅幣是寶！你儘管上路，惡作劇到此為止。

column1: Silver and gold do not pay my toll! Copper or tin is my only whim!
column2: 金銀寶物付不了我的過路費！我只鍾情銅與錫！

column1: You found nothing, of course.
column2: 你自然是什麼也沒找到。

column1: Do make up your mind.
column2: 拿定主意吧。

column1: It is a forest sprite.  It must inhabit this shrine.
column2: 這是一名森林精靈，想必就棲居在這座神龕裡。

column1: Copper or tin!  Keep your useless human stuff.  Copper or tin!
column2: 銅也好，錫也好！你那些沒用的凡人玩意兒，留著自己用吧。銅也好，錫也好！

column1: Aye, copper!  Give me copper!
column2: 是的，銅幣！把銅幣給我！

column1: My toll you pay or a trick I play!
column2: 繳了過路費，不然就等著挨我的把戲！

column1: Going out or coming in, Copper or tin for Widdershins! You had better heed my whim, Pay the toll of Widdershins! If no copper or no tin, You get a trick from Widdershins!
column2: 不論是出是進，Widdershins 都要銅或錫！你最好順著我的心意，繳清 Widdershins 的過路費！若是沒銅也沒錫，Widdershins 就讓你嚐嚐把戲！

column1: Why would you want to do that?
column2: 你何必這麼做？
