column1: There is a spear leaning on the rack behind the Hunter.
column2: 獵人身後的架子上，斜倚著一支長矛。

column1: From the simplicity of the Hunter's clothing and his worn face, I would say that he is a poor man.
column2: 從獵人樸素的衣著與滿是風霜的面容看來，我猜他是個窮苦人。

column1: It is a makeshift rack.
column2: 這是個臨時搭成的架子。

column1: The hunter has several pelts drying upon simple racks made of sticks.
column2: 獵人用幾根木棍搭成簡陋的架子，上頭晾著幾張獸皮。

column1: Did you expect the spear to be here?  You were warned that it could not leave the forest.
column2: 你以為長矛會在這裡？早有人警告過你，它離不開這座森林。

column1: The spear remains wedged in the carcass of the boar.
column2: 那支長矛仍卡在野豬的屍身裡。

column1: He is clearly not here.
column2: 他顯然不在這裡。

column1: It would be best to avoid the creature, unless you have copper or tin to give it.
column2: 除非你備有銅或錫可以奉上，否則最好避開這東西。

column1: In this small clearing, a Hunter has set up his skins on racks to dry.  Next to him are three spears.  He is a bold man or a desperate one to seek his living in the Forest Perilous.
column2: 這片小小的空地上，一名獵人架起木架晾曬獸皮，身旁擺著三支長矛。能在派瑞樂斯森林裡討生活，這人不是膽識過人，就是走投無路。

column1: It is the same as when you passed through here before.  The Hunter is still here with his spears and his skins.
column2: 這裡的景象和你先前經過時一樣。獵人依舊守在這裡，帶著他的長矛與獸皮。

column1: This clearing seems larger without the Hunter in it.
column2: 少了獵人，這片空地似乎顯得開闊了些。

column1: The Hunter has left and taken everything with him.
column2: 獵人已經離去，並帶走了他所有的家當。

column1: Like a true man of the forest, he has vanished leaving no trace that he was ever here.
column2: 一如真正的林中人，他消失得無影無蹤，彷彿從未來過此地。

column1: There is no lance here, nor did the Hunter have one.
column2: 這裡沒有長槍，獵人本來也不曾有過。

column1: Your best source of such information, the Hunter, is now gone.
column2: 你打聽此事最好的線索——那位獵人，如今已經離開了。

column1: There is no use for it here.
column2: 此物在此派不上用場。

column1: If you are threatened by a boar, that will be the time to make use of it.
column2: 若遭野豬威脅，正是用上它的時候。

column1: You cannot use what you do not have.
column2: 你不曾擁有之物，如何使用？

column1: You are talking nonsense.
column2: 你這是在胡言亂語。

column1: I am sure you will find a likely bush somewhere in the forest for that.
column2: 我想，森林中不乏合適的灌木叢可供此用。

column1: I know who you are, Arthur.
column2: 我知道你是誰，亞瑟。

column1: I did not know that trees could pay taxes.
column2: 我倒不知道樹木也得納稅。

column1: There is no one here save you and the mule.
column2: 此處除了你與騾子，別無他人。

column1: From whom? There is no-one here.
column2: 向誰要？這裡空無一人。

column1: Difficult, since he is not here.
column2: 這可難了，畢竟他人不在這裡。

column1: He is no longer here, though a trace of him does linger on.
column2: 他已不在此處，但仍留下幾分蹤跡。

column1: But the Hunter is gone.
column2: 但獵人已經離開了。

column1: Is something wrong, m'lord?
column2: 有什麼不對勁嗎，吾王？

column1: I sense no danger here, but you are wise to be at readiness at all times in this forest.
column2: 我未感應到此處有何危險，但你時時保持戒備，在這座森林裡是明智之舉。

column1: The staff of this boar spear is made of the sacred oak and the spearhead forged by the Black Knight himself.
column2: 這支獵豬矛的矛桿取自聖橡木，矛頭則由黑武士親手鍛造。

column1: I will fasten it beneath your steed's trappings, so it will be secure until needed.
column2: 我會將它繫在你坐騎的鞍具下方，妥善收好，待用時取出。

column1: 'Tis done.  But be warned, m'lord, the spear draws its power from the Forest itself and cannot be taken away from it.
column2: 辦妥了。但吾王須知，這支長矛的力量源自森林本身，不能被帶離此地。

column1: I am called Hugo the Bold.
column2: 人稱我作「無畏雨果」。

column1: Ask the Hunter.
column2: 去問那獵人吧。

column1: The Hunter would likely know more than I.
column2: 獵人知道的，多半比我還多。

column1: This boar spear once belonged to the Black Knight and is powerful enough to kill even the giant boars of this Forest.  He has laid an enchantment on it so that it belongs to the Forest and cannot be taken from here.
column2: 這支獵豬矛曾屬於黑武士所有，威力足以誅殺這座森林裡的巨型野豬。他在矛上施了法術，使它歸屬於森林，無法帶離此地。

column1: We are very poor and I have five children to feed.
column2: 我們家境貧寒，還有五個孩子要養活。

column1: I have no lances, only my spears.
column2: 我沒有長槍，只有這些長矛。

column1: You see the results of many weary days of work, m'lord -- hare, fox and squirrel pelts.
column2: 吾王您瞧，這是我多少個勞苦日子的成果——野兔、狐狸與松鼠的毛皮。

column1: I notch together branches and sticks and use them for drying skins.
column2: 我把樹枝與木棍刻榫拼接，用來晾曬獸皮。

column1: That is a most unhappy looking mule you have, m'lord.
column2: 吾王您這頭騾子，瞧著可真是愁眉苦臉。

column1: I fear the danger of the forest was too much for it. That is one reason I never bring a pack animal with me.
column2: 恐怕是這森林裡的凶險嚇壞了牠。這也是我從不帶馱獸同行的原因之一。

column1: Aye, it is a noxious pest.  I give it bits of tin to keep it happy.
column2: 是啊，那是個惹人厭的討厭鬼。我拿些碎錫餵牠，好讓牠消停。

column1: Cernunnos is the God of the Hunt.
column2: Cernunnos 乃狩獵之神。

column1: Even one copper coin would be of much use to me, sire, and help greatly to loosen my tongue.
column2: 哪怕一枚銅幣，對我都大有用處，陛下，也能讓我這張嘴更樂意開口。

column1: The forest is full of terrible dangers. I survive by remaining carefully upon the outskirts of it.
column2: 這座森林充滿可怕的危險。我之所以能活下來，全靠謹慎地待在林緣一帶。

column1: He is a part of this forest, binding its power to him with dark magicks.  You must face his challenge, m'lord, if you wish to reach the Tor.
column2: 他已與這座森林融為一體，以黑暗法術將其力量繫於己身。吾王若想抵達那座山，就必須迎戰他的挑戰。

column1: Which knight, m'lord?
column2: 是哪一位騎士，吾王？

column1: Aye, that goodly knight came this way and rode on into the Forest to reach the Tor where he hoped to find the Grail.
column2: 是的，那位良善的騎士確實經過此地，策馬深入森林，欲往山上尋找聖杯。

column1: But I fear he has met an evil fate, for he did not pass this way again.
column2: 但恐怕他已遭逢不幸，因為此後再也不曾見他經過此地。

column1: I know nothing of him, m'lord.
column2: 我對他一無所知，吾王。

column1: The local legend goes that Joseph of Arimathea brought the holy cup here from Jerusalem and hid it upon Glastonbury Tor.  That is all I know of it.
column2: 當地流傳的傳說是，亞利馬太的約瑟從耶路撒冷將聖杯帶到此地，藏於格列斯登伯利山上。我所知的僅止於此。

column1: I would not dare to search there myself, because of the Mad Monk.
column2: 我自己是不敢前去搜尋的，因為那瘋僧侶在那裡盤據。

column1: Sire, a strange monk has taken up residence in the ruins atop Glastonbury Tor.  He has surrounded the base of the Tor with a sorcerous barrier and stones that speak!
column2: 陛下，一名古怪的僧侶已在格列斯登伯利山頂的廢墟中住了下來。他在山腳布下了法術屏障，還有會說話的石頭！

column1: The giant boars of this forest are especially dangerous.  Only a boar spear of the greatest strength is effective against them.
column2: 這座森林裡的巨型野豬格外凶險，唯有最強韌的獵豬矛才能制服牠們。

column1: Aye, there is a dreadful hag that turns men to stone. Beware of her.
column2: 是的，這裡有個可怕的老巫婆，能把人變成石頭。務必提防她。

column1: The bones of knights vanquished by the Black Knight are often left in the forest as a warning.  I pray yours will not be amongst them.
column2: 那些被黑武士擊敗的騎士，屍骨常被棄置林間以示警戒。我祈求您的骨骸不會添列其中。

column1: Nothing I can tell you about that would be of value to you, m'lord.
column2: 關於此事，我實在說不出什麼對吾王有用的話。

column1: What a mean and petty demand for a king to make. Leave such venal matters to your tax collectors.
column2: 這等卑劣瑣碎的要求，豈是一位君王該提的？這類貪鄙之事，就交給你的稅吏去辦吧。

column1: Forgive me, m'lord, but the tax collector came by last week and took my last copper coin.
column2: 恕罪，吾王，稅吏上週才來過，把我最後一枚銅幣也收走了。

column1: Leave that to the tax collectors, Arthur.  It is far beneath your dignity to do such a job.
column2: 這種事就交給稅吏去做吧，亞瑟。親自過問，實在有失你的身分。

column1: A strange word, m'lord.  I do not understand its meaning.
column2: 這詞真怪，吾王。我不明白它的意思。

column1: Tis an honor to be acknowledged by you, m'lord.
column2: 承蒙吾王垂顧，實乃莫大榮幸。

column1: Aye, m'lord.  So I judged from your royal bearing, magnificent horse, and the symbol of Pendragon upon your shield.
column2: 正是，吾王。我是從您那王者的氣度、雄駿的坐騎，還有盾牌上潘德拉貢的紋章看出來的。

column1: Having spoken with Sir Gawaine, I know something of what you seek.  You have but to ask and I will gladly share what I know, especially about the Mad Monk of Glastonbury and the Grail.
column2: 我曾與高文爵士交談過，因此略知您所尋為何物。您只管開口相問，我必樂意告知所知一切，尤其是格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶與聖杯之事。

column1: I am but a poor man, m'lord, but perhaps in some small way I may be of service to you.  Aye, tis a hard life in the forest to earn a few thin coins to feed my family.
column2: 我不過是個窮苦人，吾王，但或許還能盡些微薄之力為您效勞。是啊，在這森林裡討生活著實艱苦，為了幾枚薄幣養家糊口。

column1: He is a good fellow, but smells a bit gamy.
column2: 他是個好人，只是身上有股獵物的腥氣。

column1: From the impoverished look of him, that might best be accomplished by giving him money.
column2: 從他窮困的模樣看來，給他些錢財，或許是最好的辦法。

column1: You have no cause to attack his man.  If you are angry for some reason, look to your own faults and remember that a king must set an example by his behavior.
column2: 你沒有理由攻擊他的人。若你有什麼緣故動怒，該先反省自身的過失，別忘了君王須以身作則。

column1: By Cernunnos, I am a true man, not a bloody courtier!
column2: 以 Cernunnos 之名起誓，我是個道地的漢子，不是什麼該死的朝臣！

column1: I may be a loyal servant, but if you dare to insult me in such a fashion, you may find an intimate portion of yourself skinned and hung to dry!
column2: 我雖是忠心的僕從，但你若膽敢如此羞辱於我，小心自己身上某個隱私部位被剝了皮、掛起來風乾！

column1: There is no room in your pack.  The Hunter has sworn to deliver them to Camelot and that is good enough.
column2: 你的行囊已無空間。獵人已立誓將它們送至肯萊特，這樣便已足夠。

column1: They do not belong to you.
column2: 此物並非你所有。

column1: But, m'lord, you already have the spear.
column2: 但，吾王，長槍已在你手中。

column1: You are the king, Arthur, not some common bandit. The Hunter seems a reasonable man.  Obtain the spear in a manner that befits you.
column2: 你是國王，亞瑟，不是什麼尋常的盜賊。這獵人看來是個通情達理之人。你當以合乎身分的方式取得那把長槍。

column1: What rubbish is this? You are a king.  Behave like one.
column2: 這是什麼胡言亂語？你是一國之君，該有一國之君的樣子。

column1: I gave my last bit of tin to Widdershins.
column2: 我把最後一點錫器都給了 Widdershins。

column1: My racks are but a few branches notched together. Nothing of worth to you, m'lord.
column2: 我這些架子不過是幾根刻了痕的樹枝拼湊而成，於吾王而言不值一提。

column1: As you have guessed, I do carry a knife for hunting and skinning, but I could not part with it and still practice my trade.
column2: 如你所料，我確實隨身帶著一把獵刀，用來剝皮宰殺，但少了它，我這行當便做不下去了，恕難割愛。

column1: They are yours, m'lord.  I will deliver them to Camelot for you, by my oath as your loyal man.
column2: 它們是吾王的了。我以忠僕之名立誓，會替你把它們送到肯萊特。

column1: You have generously given me the price of the skins already, m'lord.  Consider them yours.
column2: 吾王已慷慨付清了這些獸皮的價錢，就當它們是你的吧。

column1: Since your mission is clearly urgent, I give you my oath of honor to deliver them safely to Camelot for you.
column2: 既然你的使命顯然十萬火急，我便以名譽立誓，會安全地替你送到肯萊特。

column1: I would be happy to sell them to you, m'lord, for but a single silver coin.
column2: 吾王若肯出一枚銀幣，我很樂意割愛。

column1: You have been more than generous to me.  Allow me to give the spear to you.
column2: 你待我已是仁至義盡，容我將這把長槍奉上。

column1: I would sell this spear to no other man save you, m'lord.  Forgive my audacity, but the spear is of such value, I could not part with it for less than the price of a gold coin.
column2: 這把長槍，除了吾王，我誰也不賣。恕我斗膽直言，此槍價值不菲，若非一枚金幣，我實難割捨。

column1: But sire, you have not asked to buy anything from me.
column2: 但陛下，您還沒開口向我買什麼東西呢。

column1: Your entire purse, m'lord? I could not!  I am not a greedy man, only a needy one.
column2: 吾王的整個錢囊？這萬萬使不得！我並非貪婪之人，只是手頭拮据罷了。

column1: I am not a man of war.  Such things are not for me.
column2: 我不是個好戰之人，這些東西與我無緣。

column1: I would not dare to even lay hands upon it!
column2: 我連碰都不敢碰它！

column1: I beg your pardon, sire, but I see no horse.
column2: 恕我直言，陛下，我沒見著什麼馬。

column1: A noble offer!  Yet as a poor man, I could never afford to care for such a huge beast.
column2: 好慷慨的提議！只是我不過一介窮人，實在養不起這麼大的牲畜。

column1: I have never been fond of mules since I was badly bitten by one.  I beg you to keep it.
column2: 自從被一頭騾子狠狠咬過之後，我便對牠們無甚好感。還請你自己留著吧。

column1: Even if you find the mule, what use would I have for a creature that would run away when I enter the Forest?
column2: 就算找回那頭騾子，牠一進森林便要逃竄，我留著又有何用？

column1: Without a horse, m'lord, such things are of no use to me.
column2: 沒有馬，吾王，這些東西對我毫無用處。

column1: Your generosity is a credit to your name, but you will need it more than I.
column2: 你的慷慨足以為你的名聲增光，但你比我更需要這個。

column1: Tis a lovely thing, but of no use to me.
column2: 這東西是挺可愛，只是對我沒什麼用處。

column1: I have heard of such wondrous things, but I will not touch it, thank you all the same.
column2: 我聽聞過這等奇物，但還是不碰為妙，多謝美意。

column1: Nay, pardon me, but I shall not touch this lady's sleeve.  It belongs to a man who died for her love at the hands of the Black Knight and I would not disturb his ghost.
column2: 不，恕我不能碰這條夫人的絲巾。它屬於一位為她的愛情、死於黑武士之手的男子，我不願驚擾他的亡魂。

column1: Nay, m'lord.  It is yours now.  May it serve you well.
column2: 不必了，吾王。這如今是你的了，願它能為你所用。

column1: My racks are naught but a few branches notched together.  Nothing of worth to you, m'lord.
column2: 我這些架子不過是幾根刻了痕的樹枝拼湊而成，於吾王而言不值一提。

column1: Though I love to barter as much as the next man, I sense that your mission is important and you are anxious to ride on.
column2: 雖說我和誰都愛討價還價，但我看得出你的使命重大，急著上路。

column1: The price of a silver coin is all I ask.
column2: 我只求一枚銀幣的價錢。

column1: I am open to offers, m'lord, if you can but make them clear to my simple mind.
column2: 吾王若有意出價，儘管明說，我這粗淺的腦子自會明白。

column1: Why, m'lord?
column2: 為何，吾王？

column1: For what, m'lord?
column2: 所為何事，吾王？

column1: Thank you, m'lord!  And by my word as your loyal man, I will deliver them personally to Camelot.
column2: 多謝吾王！我以忠僕之名立誓，必親自將它們送到肯萊特。

column1: With all respect, sire, this is not quite enough.
column2: 恕我直言，陛下，這還不太夠。

column1: Bless you, m'lord!  I will fetch the spear.
column2: 願神保佑吾王！我這就去取長槍來。

column1: I--I am nearly speechless at such a gift!  A thousand blessings upon you!  My family and I will pray for you every night and light candles in your name at church.
column2: 我——這樣的厚禮，教我幾乎說不出話來！千萬個祝福都不足以回報你！我全家將每夜為你祈禱，並在教堂為你點上蠟燭。

column1: Bless you, m'lord, bless you!  I shall sing your praises to every man I meet!
column2: 願神保佑吾王，保佑吾王！我逢人便要傳頌你的美名！

column1: May Cernunnos, God of the Hunt, bless you!  If there is any advice I may give you, you have but to ask.  And heed this warning: beware the Mad Monk of Glastonbury!
column2: 願狩獵之神 Cernunnos 保佑吾王！若有什麼建言，只管開口便是。還有一句忠告，請務必謹記：小心格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶！

column1: Listen! There is a rustling in the bushes. Something heavy approaches.
column2: 聽！灌木叢裡傳來窸窣聲，有什麼沉重的東西正在靠近。

column1: The spear has sunk deeply into the carcass. Your final blow was your most powerful.
column2: 長槍深深沒入了屍體。你這最後一擊，是全程中最有力的一下。

column1: Where there is decay, there will be flies.
column2: 有腐敗之處，必有蒼蠅聚集。

column1: Sorrow not over the death of these savage creatures. They would just as readily have gutted you.
column2: 不必為這些凶殘野獸的死而傷懷，牠們同樣會毫不猶豫地開膛破你的肚腹。

column1: Continue your search.
column2: 繼續你的搜尋。

column1: There is the inevitable aftermath of battle -- blood and death.
column2: 這是戰鬥過後在所難免的景象——鮮血與死亡。

column1: You fought well, but it is not a pretty sight.
column2: 你這一戰打得漂亮，但眼前的景象卻不忍卒睹。

column1: It has sunk deeply into the carcass. Your final blow was your most powerful.
column2: 它深深沒入了屍體。你這最後一擊，是全程中最有力的一下。

column1: There is plenty of it.
column2: 這東西多得是。

column1: Boars have deadly tusks and an evil temperament to match.
column2: 野豬有致命的獠牙，脾性也同樣兇惡。

column1: Ridiculous.
column2: 荒謬。

column1: Forget the spear. It will serve you no more.
column2: 別管那把長槍了，它再也派不上用場。

column1: The battle is over.
column2: 戰鬥已經結束。

column1: The boars are dead. What would that accomplish?
column2: 野豬已經死了，這麼做又有何意義？

column1: It is too firmly wedged inside the boar. You must leave it there, I fear.
column2: 它牢牢卡在野豬的屍身裡，恐怕你只能就此放棄了。

column1: That would be a long, tedious and bloody job. Your mission is urgent. Leave the spear as it is.
column2: 那將是一件冗長、繁瑣又血腥的工作。你的使命緊急，就讓長槍留在原處吧。

column1: Although the flesh of the wild pig is delicious, it would take much time and effort which you do not have to spare.
column2: 野豬肉雖然美味，但處理起來費時費力，你並沒有多餘的時間。

column1: Your humor leaves much to be desired.
column2: 你這玩笑開得，實在不怎麼高明。

column1: How unsavory. Even the followers of Mithras no longer practice this. Now they drink wine instead of blood in their resurrection rituals. The Christians have followed this tradition as well.
column2: 真是令人作嘔。就連米夏拉的信徒如今都已不再這麼做，他們在復活儀式中改以酒代血，基督徒也沿襲了這個作法。

column1: Your ferocious battle has driven any other boars away, luckily for you.
column2: 你這場凶猛的搏鬥，已把其餘的野豬都嚇跑了，算你走運。

column1: That would be boring.
column2: 那未免太乏味了。

column1: The normal sounds of the forest have returned, along with the buzzing of the flies.
column2: 森林恢復了尋常的聲響，還夾雜著蒼蠅的嗡嗡聲。

column1: All is deathly silent in the aftermath of this struggle.
column2: 這場搏鬥過後，四下一片死寂。

column1: The strong, foul odor of the boars overwhelms all else.
column2: 野豬身上濃烈的惡臭，蓋過了一切其他氣味。

column1: You cannot help such creatures. The giant boars of the Forest Perilous live only to kill.
column2: 這種生物你幫不了。派瑞樂斯森林裡的巨型野豬，生來便只為殺戮。

column1: If this were a hunt, perhaps it would be worth the toil, but you are on a sacred mission. It is time to move on.
column2: 若這只是一場狩獵，或許值得如此費力，但你身負神聖的使命，該是啟程的時候了。

column1: Mighty as Excaliber is, it is not long enough to kill the boar before it can reach you.
column2: 聖劍雖然威力強大，卻不夠長，來不及在野豬撲到你身前將牠擊殺。

column1: Listen! There is a rustling in the bushes.  Something heavy approaches.
column2: 聽！灌木叢裡傳來窸窣聲，有什麼沉重的東西正在靠近。

column1: The boars have trampled the ground here keeping it clear of the thick undergrowth which borders it.
column2: 野豬在此地踐踏出一片空地，四周濃密的灌木叢因而不得侵入。

column1: The boar has gored you to the core. Alas, King Arthur is no more.
column2: 野豬的獠牙深深刺穿了你的要害。唉，亞瑟王，就此殞落。

column1: That is one crow we can do without.
column2: 少了這隻烏鴉，倒也無妨。

column1: Heed the words of the crow, for it is no ordinary bird.  It is the voice of the Black Knight.
column2: 留意這烏鴉所言，牠並非尋常飛禽，而是黑武士的化聲。

column1: 'Tis a Father Tree.  Sometimes, if you are worthy enough, such wise and ancient beings will even speak with you.
column2: 這便是老父樹。有時，若你夠格，這等睿智的古老生靈甚至願意開口與你交談。

column1: Clearly, he was once a stout knight.  Naught is left but a bit of armour, his bones picked clean by the crow.
column2: 顯然，他生前曾是位健壯的騎士。如今只剩下幾片盔甲，骨頭早被烏鴉啄得乾乾淨淨。

column1: Clearly, he was once a stout knight.  Naught is left but a bit of armour, his bones picked clean by the crow, and a bit of brightly colored silk.
column2: 顯然，他生前曾是位健壯的騎士。如今只剩下幾片盔甲、被烏鴉啄得乾乾淨淨的骨頭，還有一小片色彩鮮豔的絲巾。

column1: The rock juts from the heart of the forest like a jagged tooth.  There is evil power within it.
column2: 這塊岩石從森林深處突出，宛如一顆參差的獠牙，其中蘊藏著邪惡的力量。

column1: These mushrooms are of the species Amanita Muscaria. They are very dangerous at the best of times, and said to cause madness or death.
column2: 這些蕈菇屬於毒蠅傘一類，即便在最尋常的情況下也極為危險，據說會致人瘋狂或死亡。

column1: The clearing is as you left it, but now, to your everlasting shame, this poor soul is no longer the only dead knight in the forest.
column2: 這片空地一如你離去時的模樣，但如今，令你永生蒙羞的是，這可憐的亡魂已不再是森林裡唯一的亡故騎士。

column1: I fear the lady may well have found her dead knight and it has brought her only grief.  Alas, alas, this life is but a vale of tears.
column2: 我恐怕那位夫人已經找到她亡故的騎士，卻只換來滿心悲痛。唉，唉，人生不過是一場淚水的谷地。

column1: Little has changed, except for signs that your horse passed this way bearing Sir Gawaine back to Camelot.
column2: 此地大致如舊，唯有些痕跡顯示你的坐騎曾馱著高文爵士自此經過，返回肯萊特。

column1: You have reached the heart of the forest where its dark power dwells.  It seems another unfortunate soul was here before you.
column2: 你已抵達森林深處，這股黑暗力量的所在。看來在你之前，還有另一個不幸的靈魂曾到過此地。

column1: Only his bare bones remain, rattling in their shell of iron.
column2: 只剩下光禿禿的骸骨，在鐵甲的軀殼裡喀啦作響。

column1: There is a piece of brightly colored silk tucked inside the armour.
column2: 盔甲裡塞著一片色彩鮮豔的絲巾。

column1: There is nothing to gain by that.
column2: 這麼做並無所得。

column1: He is the evil power that makes this forest so perilous.
column2: 他正是讓這座森林如此凶險的邪惡力量。

column1: Once it was fine metal, now it is rusted and useless.
column2: 它曾是精良的金屬，如今已鏽蝕不堪，毫無用處。

column1: The piece of silk was a lady's sleeve, a token to wear into battle.  We can only wonder what sad story was his, what favour he sought to win, and the sorrowful fate of the lady that may have awaited him with fading hope.
column2: 這片絲巾是一位夫人的衣袖，是他佩戴上戰場的信物。我們只能猜想，他有著怎樣悲傷的故事、渴望贏得誰的青睞，還有那位懷抱漸漸消逝的希望等待著他的夫人，又遭逢了何等悲涼的命運。

column1: You cannot see what is not there.
column2: 不存在的東西，你看不見。

column1: They are of the species Amanita Muscaria, a very dangerous mushroom at the best of times, said to cause madness or death.
column2: 它們屬於毒蠅傘一類，即便在最尋常的情況下也極為危險，據說會致人瘋狂或死亡。

column1: But here in the Forest Perilous, they are doubly dangerous.  For if you so much as touch these mushrooms, you will be compelled to eat them.
column2: 但在派瑞樂斯森林裡，它們危險加倍——只要你一碰觸這些蕈菇，便會身不由己地把它們吃下肚。

column1: There are no flowers nearby--only mushrooms.
column2: 附近沒有花，只有蕈菇。

column1: It cannot be moved.
column2: 它無法被移動。

column1: It juts from the heart of the forest like a jagged tooth.  There is evil power within it.
column2: 它從森林深處突出，宛如一顆參差的獠牙，其中蘊藏著邪惡的力量。

column1: Most of the trees here are quite ordinary, but this one hoary, leafless tree may well be the eldest of them all.
column2: 這裡的樹大多平凡無奇，唯獨這株灰白、落盡了葉的老樹，很可能是其中最古老的一株。

column1: It will be a grievous moment when Lady Elayne find the remains of her beloved knight.
column2: 當艾蓮公主找到她心愛騎士的遺骸時，那將是何等椎心之痛的一刻。

column1: You already have a sleeve.
column2: 你已經有一條絲巾了。

column1: You cannot get what is not there.
column2: 不存在的東西，你拿不到。

column1: Odd.  Although this lady's sleeve has surely been here as long as the dead knight, it is as new as the day the lady wore it.  There is magick involved here.
column2: 奇怪。這條夫人的絲巾理應和亡故的騎士一同留在此地已久，卻新得彷彿夫人才剛佩戴過一般，其中必有魔法在作祟。

column1: Your arms are not quite that long.
column2: 你的手臂沒有那麼長。

column1: He said all he needed to say.  He will return nevermore.
column2: 他該說的話都已說完，不會再回來了。

column1: Who dares to speak to Old Father Tree? You are but a twinkle in time, mortal.  Let me sleep the long and dreamless sleep of deep roots and sun on branch.
column2: 何人膽敢與老父樹交談？凡人啊，你不過是時光中一閃即逝的微光。且讓我沉入那深根與枝頭陽光交織的漫長無夢之眠吧。

column1: Do not disturb him further, Arthur.  He is an old and weary tree.
column2: 別再驚擾他了，亞瑟。他是一株年邁而疲憊的樹。

column1: That would not be much of a conversation.
column2: 那算不上什麼交談。

column1: If you are greeting the dead knight, I fear he has long since ceased to care about such things.
column2: 你若是在向亡故的騎士問候，恐怕他早已不再在意這些事了。

column1: They are dangerous.  Leave them be.
column2: 它們很危險，別去招惹。

column1: I warn you most strongly, the merest touch of these mushrooms will compel you to eat them with the most dire results.
column2: 我要嚴正警告你，這些蕈菇哪怕只是輕輕一碰，都會逼得你把它們吃下肚，後果不堪設想。

column1: There is no need to desecrate this poor dead knight.
column2: 沒有必要褻瀆這位可憐的亡故騎士。

column1: Long has this unfortunate knight lain here, but you have not the time now to do him such a service.
column2: 這位不幸的騎士已在此長眠許久，但你此刻沒有時間為他做這件事。

column1: This unfortunate knight is beyond your ability to help or hinder.
column2: 這位不幸的騎士，已非你的能力所能相助或妨礙。

column1: The dead knight's armour is old and rusted and of no use to you.
column2: 亡故騎士的盔甲已老舊鏽蝕，對你毫無用處。

column1: It would be futile to try.
column2: 嘗試也是徒勞。

column1: He is gone, as I would hope you noticed.
column2: 他已經走了，我想你也該注意到了。

column1: This stone would defy you.  You are well advised to leave it alone.
column2: 這塊石頭會與你對抗，你最好別去招惹它。

column1: That is beyond your power or mine.
column2: 這已超出你我的能力範圍。

column1: The knight has been dead far too long to be a threat to you.
column2: 這位騎士死去已久，早已構不成任何威脅。

column1: Rawk!  I have no need for mortal toys.
column2: 呱！凡人的玩物，我用不著。

column1: I doubt the dead knight has any interest in it.
column2: 我看那位亡故的騎士，對此不會有什麼興趣。

column1: He is long past help, Arthur.
column2: 他早已無法可救了，亞瑟。

column1: Rarawk!  Try it if you dare.  You will never touch me.
column2: 呱啦！有膽你就試試看，你永遠碰不到我。

column1: The creature deserves it, but is not here for the attempt.
column2: 這畜生是罪有應得，只是牠此刻並不在此，由不得你動手。

column1: O Fool, you seek death by coming here.  Turn back now or die!
column2: 愚者啊，你來到此地，便是自尋死路。速速回頭，否則便是一死！

column1: Hear me, then, O Brave Fool.  The Black Knight is the greatest of all knights.  None have beaten him.  He is invincible.  Even Sir Gawaine was grievously wounded.
column2: 那便聽好了，勇敢的愚者。黑武士是天下第一的騎士，從無人能勝過他，他所向無敵。就連高文爵士也被他重創。

column1: The Black Knight awaits you for a joust to the death.  Do you accept the challenge?
column2: 黑武士正等著與你來一場生死決鬥。你可願接受挑戰？

column1: Then you must turn back, for you cannot pass this way through the forest without facing the Black Knight.
column2: 那你便得回頭，因為不與黑武士一戰，你休想從這條路穿越森林。

column1: Crawk!  I shall delight in feeding on your bones when the Black Knight has finished with you!  I shall pluck out your eyes and peck at your bloody heart!
column2: 嘎呱！待黑武士收拾了你，我便能歡歡喜喜地啃食你的骨頭！我要啄出你的雙眼，啄食你血淋淋的心臟！

column1: I have no time to waste on fools.  Turn back now or face him and die.
column2: 我沒空浪費在愚者身上，快回頭，否則便去見他，一死了之。

column1: Would I tell such a fool as you even if I knew?
column2: 就算我知道，我又何必告訴你這樣的愚人？

column1: He is a prisoner of the Black Knight and dies slowly of the wounds he received.
column2: 他是黑武士的階下囚，正因所受的傷勢緩緩步向死亡。

column1: I know nothing of this knight.  Another fool like Gawaine and you, no doubt.
column2: 我對這位騎士一無所知。想必又是個像高文和你這樣的傻子。

column1: It will not answer.  It is sent by the Black Knight to taunt you, nothing more.
column2: 牠不會回應。牠是黑武士派來嘲弄你的，僅此而已。

column1: You must answer the crow, Arthur.
column2: 你必須回應那隻烏鴉，亞瑟。

column1: Of all the stubborn fools there be, I never saw such a fool as thee, You shall keep yon knight good company, And nourish the roots of Old Father Tree.
column2: 天下冥頑之徒何其多，卻不曾見過你這般執迷不悟；你將與那騎士結伴長眠，去滋養老父樹深埋的根。

column1: There is no escape, unless I allow you to pass.  But the price of safe passage is high indeed.
column2: 此地無法脫逃，除非我允你通行。但安然通行的代價著實高昂。

column1: Waste no time with empty words of politeness.
column2: 莫要浪費時間在虛情假意的客套話上。

column1: That is not within your power.
column2: 那不在你的能力範圍之內。

column1: You cannot joust with a sword.  If you accept the joust, he must perforce provide you with a jousting lance.
column2: 你不能用劍進行馬上比武。若你接受比武，他勢必得為你備妥一支比武用的長槍。

column1: By this, I assume you mean a jousting lance.
column2: 如此看來，我猜你指的是一支比武用的長槍。

column1: Were I with you in person, I could overcome this spell, but this is your mission and you alone must make the choices and seek the path to the Grail.
column2: 若我能親自隨你在此，或許能破除這道咒法，但這是你的使命，唯有你能自行抉擇、尋得通往聖杯的道路。

column1: I have no use for money.
column2: 我用不著錢財。

column1: I have no use for it.
column2: 我用不著這個。

column1: For that insult, I shall take special pleasure in slaying you.
column2: 為了這番侮辱，我將格外樂於取你性命。

column1: I will give you my ultimatum soon enough.
column2: 我很快便會向你下最後通牒。

column1: Not even I know where the Grail is hidden.
column2: 就連我也不知聖杯藏於何處。

column1: He is my prisoner.
column2: 他是我的階下囚。

column1: I know nothing about this knight.
column2: 我對這位騎士一無所知。

column1: My crow warned you.  You should have heeded the warning.
column2: 我的烏鴉早已警告過你，你本該聽從那警告的。

column1: I am the Black Knight, fool.
column2: 我便是黑武士，蠢貨。

column1: I have no equal in jousting.  You shall surely die.
column2: 馬上比武無人能與我匹敵，你必死無疑。

column1: The black knight does not respond.
column2: 黑武士並未回應。

column1: You disgust me.
column2: 你令我作嘔。

column1: Praise all the powers that be! You are victorious, my king.
column2: 讚頌一切神明的力量！吾王，你得勝了。

column1: This is no natural foe.  Nothing can be seen inside his dark, bat-winged helm and his voice is like an echo from the grave.
column2: 這絕非凡俗之敵。他那頂飾有蝙蝠翼的黑色頭盔內漆黑一片，什麼也看不見，聲音則彷彿來自墳塋深處的回響。

column1: The Black Knight has caused a hedge to grow into a natural jousting lane divider.
column2: 黑武士使一道樹籬生長成天然的比武賽道分隔。

column1: The Black Knight is gone.
column2: 黑武士已然離去。

column1: Hurry on, Arthur! Gawaine must be close by!
column2: 快走，亞瑟！高文必定就在附近！

column1: What advice can I give a fool?
column2: 我能給一個蠢貨什麼忠告？

column1: You must joust the Black Knight if you would save Gawaine.
column2: 你若想救高文，就必須與黑武士一決比武。

column1: Your foe awaits you at the other end of this jousting hedge.
column2: 你的對手正在這道比武樹籬的另一端等著你。

column1: The Black Knight's body has vanished, as is to be expected with such a supernatural being.
column2: 黑武士的軀體已然消失，這等超凡之物，如此結局本在意料之中。

column1: Only the jousting hedge remains as proof that the Black Knight was ever here.
column2: 唯有那道比武樹籬留下，證明黑武士確曾在此。

column1: You have seen the last of him.
column2: 你已見過他最後一面。

column1: He bears no special device.
column2: 他身上並無特殊的紋章。

column1: I see nothing here but forest and hedge.
column2: 我在此處除了森林與樹籬，什麼也沒看見。

column1: His helmet is adorned with two bat-like wings.
column2: 他的頭盔飾有兩片狀似蝙蝠翼的裝飾。

column1: There is nothing to be seen there.
column2: 那裡什麼也看不見。

column1: The jousting lane on the other side is exactly the same.  The Black Knight has not taken any unfair advantage.
column2: 另一側的比武賽道與此處完全相同，黑武士並未佔任何不公的便宜。

column1: It is the same as this side.
column2: 與這一側相同。

column1: It takes two to joust.
column2: 比武需要兩人方能成局。

column1: You will pass unmolested, thanks to your cowardice. I do not know how you can bear the shame of it.
column2: 憑著你的懦弱，你將得以安然通過。我實在不明白，你如何承受得起這份恥辱。

column1: The Black Knight is vanquished.  There is no need to escape.
column2: 黑武士已被擊敗，無須再逃。

column1: The Black Knight is gone and left nothing behind.
column2: 黑武士已經離去，未留下任何東西。

column1: You will not find one here.
column2: 此處找不到那樣東西。

column1: That you can only do if you defeat the Black Knight.
column2: 唯有擊敗黑武士，你才能這麼做。

column1: You have a chance now to save Gawaine.  Do not delay!
column2: 你現在有機會救出高文，切莫遲疑！

column1: You have done all you could.  His fate is no longer in your hands, but that of Camelot is.  Seek the Grail.
column2: 你已盡了全力，他的命運已不再操於你手，但肯萊特的命運仍是。去尋找聖杯吧。

column1: You can try, King Arthur, as others have died trying.
column2: 你儘管一試，亞瑟王，正如許多人曾因此一試而喪命。

column1: You have already won your victory.
column2: 你已然贏得了這場勝利。

column1: Too late for a show of bravado now.  The evil deed is done.
column2: 此刻逞英雄已為時已晚，惡行已然鑄成。

column1: Your sword is of no use here.  The Black Knight has set the terms of combat as a joust.
column2: 你的劍在此無用武之地。黑武士已定下以馬上比武決勝負的條件。

column1: Hold, King Arthur.  Do not seek to move.  Not even Merlin can free you from my power in this place.
column2: 且慢，亞瑟王。休要妄動。在此地，就連梅林也無法將你從我的力量中解救出來。

column1: Here are your choices.
column2: 這是你的選擇。

column1: In the forest beyond me, I have imprisoned your friend, Sir Gawaine.  He is sorely injured and shall die soon without help.  To free him, you must joust with me.
column2: 在我身後的森林裡，囚著你的摯友，高文爵士。他傷勢慘重，若無人相助，不久便將喪命。要救他，你必須與我比武。

column1: Three times you must unhorse me before I can die.  Three times must I unhorse you to slay you.  The first knight to strike the third blow is the victor. No matter who wins, Gawaine will go free.
column2: 你須將我三度擊落馬下，我方能一死；我也須三度將你擊落馬下，方能取你性命。誰先擊出第三擊，誰便是勝者。無論誰勝，高文都將獲釋。

column1: But if you joust with me, you will surely die.  Therefore I give you one other choice:  I will let you pass untouched.....but I will take Gawaine's life in exchange.
column2: 但若你與我比武，你必死無疑。因此我給你另一個選擇：我可讓你安然通過……但代價是高文的性命。

column1: I lay the challenge before you.  Will you joust with me for the life of Sir Gawaine?
column2: 我在此向你下戰帖。你可願為高文爵士的性命，與我一戰？

column1: Will you joust with me? Answer aye or nay.
column2: 你可願與我比武？請輸入「aye」或「nay」作答。

column1: You are a weakling and a coward.  Gawaine's life is mine and you are free to go.
column2: 你是個弱者，也是個懦夫。高文的性命歸我了，你可自行離去。

column1: Will you joust with me? Answer aye or nay.  You have no other choices.
column2: 你可願與我比武？請輸入「aye」或「nay」作答，你別無他選。

column1: You are held fast by the power of the Black Knight.
column2: 你被黑武士的力量牢牢禁錮住了。

column1: You are a worthy opponent.  Take up your lance and let the joust begin!
column2: 你是個夠格的對手。持起你的長槍，比武開始！

column1: Dead men tell no tales.
column2: 死人不會洩露秘密。

column1: Though I....did not reach the Tor....I believe it is in the possession.....of the Mad Monk of Glastonbury.
column2: 雖然我……未能抵達那座山……我相信它落在……格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶手中。

column1: Alas....I have not seen or heard of him since I left Camelot.
column2: 唉……自我離開肯萊特後，便再也沒見過他，也沒聽過他的消息。

column1: Though I....did not reach the Tor....I believe the Grail is held.....by the Mad Monk of Glastonbury.
column2: 雖然我……未能抵達那座山……我相信聖杯落在……格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶手中。

column1: Ah...my story is not a happy one. To be defeated....by the Black Knight....I cannot bear to speak of it yet.
column2: 啊……我的遭遇並不順遂。竟敗在……黑武士手下……我此刻還無法對此啟齒。

column1: Please, M'lord.  You must continue on with your quest.
column2: 求求你，吾王。你必須繼續你的探尋。

column1: Now that you have saved Gawaine, concentrate once more upon your search.
column2: 如今你已救出高文，該再度專心於你的尋索之上了。

column1: Gawaine is close to death and urgently needs help.
column2: 高文命在旦夕，亟需援手。

column1: You let Gawaine die. I have nothing to give you at this moment but contempt.
column2: 你任由高文死去。此刻我除了鄙夷，再也給不了你別的。

column1: This place should look familiar. It was here that you freed Gawaine and sent him back to Camelot.
column2: 這地方你應當眼熟。正是在此處，你救出了高文，並送他回肯萊特。

column1: Gawaine's injuries are serious. Only the physicians of Camelot may be able to save him.
column2: 高文傷勢嚴重，唯有肯萊特的醫師或許還能救他。

column1: In spite of his injuries, Gawaine has been left shackled to a massive tree.  The Black Knight shows little mercy.
column2: 高文雖已負傷，卻仍被鎖鏈拴在一株巨樹之上，黑武士毫不留情。

column1: Naught but the proof of your shame awaits you here.  The massive tree before you marks the place where Gawaine's bones shall lie.
column2: 此處只餘你恥辱的證明。眼前這株巨樹，便是高文屍骨將要長眠之地。

column1: He is not here.
column2: 他不在這裡。

column1: The Black Knight still rules supreme in this forest, thanks to your cowardice.
column2: 拜你的懦弱所賜，黑武士依舊在這片森林裡稱王稱霸。

column1: You have vanquished him, to your great glory.
column2: 你已擊敗了他，這是你莫大的榮耀。

column1: The shackles are made of metal, sunk too deeply into the tree to pull them free, but the metal itself is not thick.
column2: 這鎖鏈是金屬打造的，深深嵌入樹身，難以硬拔脫離，但金屬本身並不厚實。

column1: The remains of the shackles shall serve as a reminder of suffering ended.
column2: 這殘留的鎖鏈，將成為苦難已然終結的提醒。

column1: He is safe.  Worry not.
column2: 他安然無恙，不必擔心。

column1: I am so filled with contempt that you allowed your great friend and noble knight to die, that I can offer you no words of wisdom or comfort.
column2: 你竟任由摯友、那位高貴的騎士死去，我心中滿是鄙夷，再也給不出任何忠告或慰藉之言。

column1: The most important thing to do is see that Gawaine reaches Camelot as quickly as possible.  But you must continue to search for the Grail.
column2: 眼下最要緊的，是設法讓高文儘快抵達肯萊特。但你仍須繼續尋找聖杯。

column1: Gawaine is gone.
column2: 高文已經不在了。

column1: Gawaine is still alive, barely.  Hanging from the shackles must pain him cruelly.
column2: 高文尚存一息，僅此而已。懸吊在這鎖鏈上，想必令他痛苦不堪。

column1: Gawaine is very ill and weak.  He must go back to Camelot and be tended by a healer at once, or he will die here, but he will never make it back on foot.
column2: 高文病重體弱，必須立刻回肯萊特由醫者診治，否則便會死在此地；但他絕無可能徒步走回去。

column1: The Black Knight has taken his life. Aye, well you should tremble at the sight. This crime lies heavily upon your own soul and will never be cleansed, no matter how you seek to right it.
column2: 黑武士已取走他的性命。是的，你見此情景理當心驚。這樁罪責將沉沉壓在你自己的靈魂之上，無論你如何試圖彌補，都永難洗清。

column1: Alas, Gawaine, the noble Gawaine is dead.   Perhaps he died of his injuries, but I fear it was your indifference that struck the final blow.
column2: 唉，高文，高貴的高文死了。或許他是傷重不治，但我擔心，真正給予最後一擊的，是你的漠然。

column1: He has returned to Camelot for healing.
column2: 他已回到肯萊特接受療傷。

column1: Though he is cut and bleeding, I fear his most serious injuries may not be as obvious to the eye.
column2: 雖然他身上有傷口在流血，但我擔心他最嚴重的傷勢，未必是肉眼能看得出來的。

column1: Does it matter how he died, be it of injuries or grief that his own king betrayed him?  He is dead.
column2: 他究竟是死於傷勢，還是死於得知自己的王背叛了他的哀痛，這重要嗎？他已經死了。

column1: It is a huge tree.
column2: 這是一株巨樹。

column1: Your horse has disappeared. It must have went back to Camelot.
column2: 你的坐騎已經消失了，想必是自行回了肯萊特。

column1: I cannot believe such filth... from the lips of my own king!
column2: 我不敢相信……這等污穢之言，竟出自我王之口！

column1: The smell of blood, sweat and illness is nearly overwhelming.
column2: 血腥、汗臭與病氣的味道幾乎令人難以承受。

column1: I fear... I am not... my usual fragrant self.
column2: 恐怕……我此刻……並非平日那般芬芳。

column1: The odor of human death is not a pleasant one.
column2: 人之將死所散發的氣味，並不好聞。

column1: I am disturbed by the labored quality of Gawaine's breathing.  He must reach Camelot as quickly as possible.
column2: 高文那沉重艱難的呼吸令我不安，他必須儘快抵達肯萊特。

column1: The pall of solemn death enshrouds this place.
column2: 一股肅穆的死亡氣息籠罩著此地。

column1: Sir Gawaine needs more than trivialities.
column2: 高文爵士所需要的，遠不止這些瑣碎之物。

column1: He is nearby.
column2: 他就在附近。

column1: You are the only one who can help him.  If he does not reach Camelot quickly, he will die.
column2: 唯有你能幫助他。他若不能盡快抵達肯萊特，便將喪命。

column1: It is too late for that.  Gawaine is dead.
column2: 那已為時已晚，高文已經死了。

column1: Concern yourself with such things after you have freed Gawaine from his suffering.
column2: 待你解救高文脫離苦難之後，再去掛心這些事吧。

column1: All the money in the world will not restore Sir Gawaine to life.
column2: 縱有天下所有的財富，也無法使高文爵士死而復生。

column1: Nay, m'lord.  I will not take....your money....for you may yet need it.
column2: 不，吾王。我不會收下……你的錢……你日後或許還用得著。

column1: Gawaine needs no gift so greatly as he needs the gift of healing, which you cannot give him, I fear.
column2: 高文最需要的，莫過於痊癒這份禮物，恐怕那並非你所能給予的。

column1: It is of no use to a dead man.
column2: 這東西對死者毫無用處。

column1: It can do nothing for Gawaine.
column2: 這對高文於事無補。

column1: What morbid thoughts.
column2: 好陰鬱的念頭。

column1: It cannot wash the stain of Gawaine's death from your soul.  He will be enfolded into the body of mother earth and this ancient tree shall be his monument.
column2: 這洗不去高文之死在你靈魂上留下的污點。他將回歸大地之母的懷抱，這株古樹便是他的紀念碑。

column1: For what you have allowed to happen, there can be no forgiveness.
column2: 對於你所縱容發生的事，沒有寬恕可言。

column1: You have no need of forgiveness. Your virtue, at the moment, is intact.
column2: 你不需要寬恕。此刻，你的德行仍完好無損。

column1: You do not have your mule.
column2: 你的騾子不在你身邊。

column1: Nothing can help him until he is free of the shackles.
column2: 除非先解開鎖鏈，否則什麼都幫不了他。

column1: Only the healers of Camelot can save him, if he can reach them in time.  He will never make it back on foot.
column2: 唯有肯萊特的醫者能救他，前提是他能及時抵達。他絕無可能徒步走回去。

column1: Have no fear. Gawaine will be tended well in Camelot.
column2: 不必擔憂，高文在肯萊特會受到妥善照料。

column1: My, your memory is short. You have already shattered the shackles.
column2: 哎呀，你的記性可真差，你早已打碎那鎖鏈了。

column1: Nothing you do now can restore Sir Gawaine to life.
column2: 你此刻做什麼，都無法讓高文爵士死而復生。

column1: You have dealt with the shackles.
column2: 你已經處理過那副鎖鏈了。

column1: These shackles do not unlock.
column2: 這副鎖鏈並無鎖孔可開。

column1: I am sure you will find a way.
column2: 我相信你會想出辦法的。

column1: The shackles are securely anchored.  Can you think of nothing better to try.
column2: 這副鎖鏈固定得十分牢靠，你就想不出更好的辦法嗎？

column1: Not all the sword brandishing in the world will return Gawaine to life. Be still.
column2: 縱使揮盡天下劍術，也無法使高文死而復生，且靜下心來吧。

column1: There is no danger for the moment. Best to put up your sword lest it make Gawaine uneasy.
column2: 此刻並無危險，還是收起你的劍為好，免得讓高文心生不安。

column1: There is no danger for the moment. Or did you have some other purpose in drawing your sword?
column2: 此刻並無危險。還是說，你拔劍另有別的用意？

column1: This is one place where it would be best to use your sword on foot.
column2: 這是個最好徒步持劍應戰的地方。

column1: There is no danger here. Be more specific about what non-violent use you portend.
column2: 此處並無危險。請說明白些，你打算做何種非暴力的用途。

column1: Help me, Arthur. The pain....is terrible.
column2: 救救我，亞瑟。這痛楚……難以忍受。

column1: Beware....the Mad Monk....of Glastonbury.
column2: 小心……格列斯登伯利的……瘋僧侶。

column1: I believe he has....the Grail.
column2: 我相信他……手裡有聖杯。

column1: Sir Gawaine shall never speak again.
column2: 高文爵士再也無法開口說話了。

column1: Consider how you might best do that.
column2: 仔細想想，該如何做才是上策。

column1: Aye, Gawaine must be helped. If he does not reach Camelot soon, he will die of his injuries.
column2: 正是，高文亟需救助。他若不能盡快抵達肯萊特，傷勢終將奪去他的性命。

column1: He is beyond help.
column2: 他已無藥可救。

column1: First, you must dismount.
column2: 首先，你必須下馬。

column1: Uh... surely you have mistaken me... for someone else.
column2: 呃……你想必是……認錯人了。

column1: Do not add necrophilia to your list of sins.
column2: 莫在你的罪過之上，再添褻瀆亡者之舉。

column1: Have you gone completely mad!?!
column2: 你莫非已經瘋了不成！？！

column1: He is already dead.  Your shame is great enough without adding evil thoughts to it.
column2: 他已然離世。你的恥辱已經夠深重了，不必再添邪念。

column1: That is hardly what he needs.
column2: 這絕非他此刻所需要的。

column1: Though it is a common practice to kiss farewell to the dead, it is hardly right for you to do so when you have caused his death.
column2: 雖說親吻亡者道別是常見的習俗，但你正是致他於死的人，此舉實在不妥。

column1: That would cause him even more pain than he is already suffering.
column2: 那只會讓他承受比此刻更深的痛楚。

column1: Your sorrow is meaningless.  It will not bring him back from the dead.
column2: 你的哀傷毫無意義，不能讓他死而復生。

column1: Aye, he is indeed in need of help.  He will not live hanging from those shackles much longer.
column2: 正是，他確實亟需援手。再這樣吊在鎖鏈上，他撐不了多久了。

column1: You have freed him, but he will not live long if left here.
column2: 你已將他釋放，但若留他在此，他活不了多久。

column1: Nothing you can do now can wash the sin of Gawaine's death from your soul.
column2: 如今你再做什麼，都無法洗淨高文之死加諸你靈魂上的罪。

column1: It may ease your conscience, but will change nothing.
column2: 此舉或能寬慰你的良心，卻改變不了任何事。

column1: Let us hope your god heeds your silent prayers.
column2: 但願你的神明能聽見你無聲的禱告。

column1: He will go nowhere until free of the shackles.
column2: 在鎖鏈解開之前，他哪裡也去不了。

column1: It makes no sense to bear the burden yourself when you have a powerful horse nearby.
column2: 身邊既有一匹壯健的坐騎，何必自己扛起這重擔？

column1: Though bearing Gawaine's body is a burden you well deserve, your mission must not be abandoned.  This tree will mark the place where his bones lie.
column2: 縱然背負高文的遺體是你理應承受的重擔，你的使命卻不容棄置。這棵樹，將標記他長眠之處。

column1: What does it matter? Gawaine is dead.
column2: 這又有什麼要緊？高文已經死了。

column1: Though Gawaine is free of the shackles, his ordeal is far from over. His life depends on your actions, King Arthur.
column2: 雖然高文已脫離鎖鏈，他的苦難卻遠未結束。他的性命，繫於你接下來的作為，亞瑟王。

column1: Aye, it would be best to get him free of the shackles as quickly as possible. Seek the most direct method.
column2: 正是，當務之急是盡快解開他身上的鎖鏈。尋一個最直截了當的辦法吧。

column1: Better to leave Gawaine's body beneath a tree than slung like baggage on a mule.
column2: 與其讓高文的遺體像行囊般掛在騾背上，不如將他安葬於樹下。

column1: King....Arthur....I knew....you would come.
column2: 王……亞瑟……我就知道……你會來。

column1: You have shattered the shackles.
column2: 你已擊碎了鎖鏈。

column1: May...god be with you, Arthur. Tarry not with me. Go at once....to the Tor. Find...the Grail, I beg you.
column2: 願……神與你同在，亞瑟。莫在我身邊耽擱。速速……前往那座山丘。尋得……聖杯，我懇求你。

column1: He is right. Your horse will carry him safely back to Camelot. Even if you must go on foot, you must continue your search without delay, but be assured that this noble sacrifice brings blessings upon you.
column2: 他說得對。你的坐騎會平安地將他送回肯萊特。即便你必須徒步前行，也不可耽延你的追尋；但請放心，這番高尚的犧牲，將為你帶來庇佑。

column1: Beware, Arthur! I like not the look of this old hag who stands upon the pedestal.
column2: 當心，亞瑟！我不喜歡這座台座上老婦人的模樣。

column1: These are runes of a very ancient type, probably a warning or incantation.
column2: 這些是極為古老的符文，恐怕是某種警示或咒語。

column1: An inscription in runes has appeared upon the pedestal where the witch stood.
column2: 女巫先前所立的台座上，浮現出一段符文銘刻。

column1: The forest witch stands upon a pedestal of some kind. I cannot say what purpose it may have had, though it does seem to be covered in badly weathered carvings.
column2: 森林女巫立在一座台座上。我說不出它原本有何用途，不過台座上似乎滿是風化嚴重的雕刻。

column1: This small stone was once a man, but will never be so again.
column2: 這塊小石頭曾是一個人，如今卻再也不會是了。

column1: These large standing stones are megaliths. It means simply 'big stone'.
column2: 這些巨大的立石就是巨石。這個詞的意思很簡單，就是『大石頭』。

column1: Ye shall never move again, unless ye offer me what I desire.
column2: 汝將永不得動彈，除非獻上我所渴求之物。

column1: Do not be daunted. This reads to me more like an instruction than an incantation. Let your own wits serve you.
column2: 莫要氣餒。依我看，這與其說是咒語，更像是一則指引。憑你自己的機智去解讀吧。

column1: The runes might be important. If you ask, I could translate them.
column2: 這些符文或許十分重要。你若開口詢問，我可以為你翻譯。

column1: You had best think of something to satisfy the old hag.
column2: 你最好想個辦法，滿足這老婦人的要求。

column1: There is no danger within this stone circle now that the witch is gone. Alas, that her previous victims could not be freed.
column2: 如今女巫已去，這圈立石之內再無危險。只可惜，她先前的犧牲者已無法獲釋。

column1: There is terrible power in this old hag. She is a forest witch drawing upon the powers within this stone circle.
column2: 這老婦人身上蘊藏著可怖的力量。她是森林女巫，汲取著這圈立石之中的力量。

column1: The foliage has crept back from these stones, but it is difficult to see what lies beyond.
column2: 枝葉已從這些石頭邊悄悄退去，但仍難以看清外頭有些什麼。

column1: Though human hands once placed these stones, your two hands will not move them.
column2: 雖然這些石頭當初是人手所立，但單憑你雙手，是搬不動它們的。

column1: You are not tall enough to do that.
column2: 你的身高不夠，做不到這件事。

column1: The sky is open overhead. Not a single tree grows close enough to overhang this stone circle.
column2: 頭頂天空一片開闊，沒有一棵樹長得夠近，能遮蔽這圈立石。

column1: Evidently, she has decided to follow you again.
column2: 看來，她又決定跟隨你了。

column1: Happily, you have set her free. The witch will not plague this forest again.
column2: 值得慶幸的是，你已將她釋放。這女巫再也不會為禍這片森林了。

column1: Those three small stones were once men, but will never be so again.
column2: 那三塊小石頭曾是三個人，如今卻再也不會是了。

column1: I fear the lovely lady's search for her beloved knight will end in misery and she will weep o'er his bones.
column2: 我恐怕這位佳人尋找心上騎士的旅程，終將以悲劇收場，她只能在他的枯骨前灑淚。

column1: Do you call this ugly and withered old crone a girl? Truly, you have been in this forest too long.
column2: 你竟稱這乾癟醜陋的老太婆為姑娘？看來你在這片森林待得太久了。

column1: This circle of standing stones must be at the very edge of the Forest Perilous. But it has no henge, for a henge is a circular embankment.
column2: 這圈立石想必正位於派瑞樂斯森林的邊緣。不過它算不上是『環壘』，因為環壘指的是環形的土堤。

column1: There is no monolith, but there are many megaliths.
column2: 這裡沒有單一的巨石柱，卻有許多巨石。

column1: The large standing stones are megaliths. It means simply 'big stone'.
column2: 這些巨大的立石就是巨石。這個詞的意思很簡單，就是『大石頭』。

column1: They are not pillars, they are standing stones. Unlike a cromlech or dolmen, these are arranged in a circle.
column2: 它們不是石柱，而是立石。不同於克倫勒克石冢或支石墓，這些石頭是排成一個圓圈的。

column1: These standing stones have but one entrance which is a trilithon: two upright stones with a capstone or lintel-stone over the top of them.
column2: 這些立石只有一處入口，那是一座『三石塔』：兩根直立的石柱，上方架著一塊冠石或楣石。

column1: It means 'three stones' and is a structure of two upright stones capped by a lintel-stone.
column2: 這個詞意為『三塊石頭』，指的是兩根直立石柱、上方覆蓋一塊楣石的結構。

column1: Dolmen comes from two Bretogne words: 'tol' meaning 'table' and 'men' meaning 'stone'. It refers to a tomb made of upright stones covered by a slab for a roof, then covered over with soil to make a mound.
column2: 『支石墓（dolmen）』一詞源自兩個布列塔尼語詞：'tol' 意為『桌子』，'men' 意為『石頭』。指的是以直立石塊搭建、上覆石板為頂的墳墓，再覆土堆成塚。

column1: Cromlech comes from the Welsh words: 'crom' meaning 'bent' and 'llech' meaning 'flat'. It refers to a tomb made of upright stones covered by a slab for a roof, then covered over with soil to make a mound.
column2: 『克倫勒克（cromlech）』一詞源自威爾斯語：'crom' 意為『彎曲』，'llech' 意為『平坦』。指的是以直立石塊搭建、上覆石板為頂的墳墓，再覆土堆成塚。

column1: These are not natural rocks, as should be obvious. They are standing stones arranged in a circle.
column2: 顯而易見，這些並非天然岩石，而是排成圓圈的立石。

column1: I regret I know nothing that would help you.
column2: 很遺憾，我沒有任何能幫上你的知識。

column1: I cannot. You must rely upon your own wits.
column2: 我做不到。你必須仰賴自己的機智。

column1: Cease prattling and give me what I desire.
column2: 休再喋喋不休，把我所渴求之物獻上。

column1: Betimes I worry about you, Arthur. You set the Lady Elayne free, remember?
column2: 亞瑟，我有時真為你擔心。還記得嗎，你曾釋放過艾蓮公主。

column1: Alas, you cannot.
column2: 可惜，你辦不到。

column1: The Lady Elayne seemed much too overjoyed to listen, did she not? Nor would you have taken much pleasure in telling her the sad fate of her beloved knight.
column2: 艾蓮公主當時似乎欣喜得聽不進任何話，不是嗎？何況，把她心上騎士的悲慘下場告訴她，你自己也未必忍心。

column1: I know not to whom ye would speak, but ye had best deal with me if ye wish to pass this circle.
column2: 我不知汝欲與誰交談，但汝若想通過此圈，最好先應付我。

column1: You will see nothing special from there. You would only obscure the runes carved upon the top of the pedestal.
column2: 從那裡你什麼特別的也看不見，只會擋住台座頂端所刻的符文。

column1: Ye must deal with me first!
column2: 汝須先應付我！

column1: The runes on the pedestal say this...
column2: 台座上的符文寫著……

column1: Five poets bold Did come astray. Five standing stones Now bar the way. Of limbs bereft, Yet voice I left. To pass through the middle You must ask for.......
column2: 「五位大膽詩人，誤入歧途流連。五尊立石而今，擋住去路向前。四肢盡失無存，唯留一縷聲喚。欲從中央穿行，你須開口求……」

column1: Alas, it fades out here. The last flurry of magick which caused it to appear must not have been enough to bring out the full inscription.
column2: 可惜，銘文到此便消散了。看來喚出它的那陣法力餘波，並不足以顯現完整的銘刻。

column1: I see no writing here.
column2: 我在此處看不見任何文字。

column1: There is nothing left of her, fortunately.
column2: 所幸，她已經什麼都不剩了。

column1: And how do ye propose to do that, arrogant one?
column2: 汝這狂妄之人，打算如何做到？

column1: That is not what you came here to do. Remember your mission.
column2: 你來此並非為了這件事。莫忘你的使命。

column1: I care naught for what ye desire. Give me what I desire.
column2: 汝所欲為何，我毫不在乎。把我所渴求之物獻上。

column1: That is beyond your strength.
column2: 那超出了你的力量所及。

column1: Too late to think of that.
column2: 此刻再想這個，已經太遲了。

column1: I care nothing for pretty words. If ye wish to pass, ye must give me what I desire.
column2: 花言巧語於我毫無用處。汝若想通過，就得獻上我所渴求之物。

column1: Betimes I worry about you, Arthur. You set her free, remember?
column2: 亞瑟，我有時真為你擔心。還記得嗎，你曾釋放過她。

column1: Ye shall not pass through this circle unless ye give me what I desire.
column2: 除非獻上我所渴求之物，汝休想穿過此圈。

column1: And what may this be that I desire, ye wonder? Hah! If ye be so cunning a knight, ye shall know.
column2: 汝在想，我所渴求的究竟是何物？哈！汝若真是機智的騎士，自會知曉。

column1: King of paupers! Ye offer nothing.
column2: 窮鬼之王！汝獻上的什麼也不是。

column1: If ye would buy a safe passage, ye must offer nothing less than an entire purse.
column2: 汝若想以財買得安然通行，非得獻上整個錢囊不可。

column1: For this, I shall let ye pass.
column2: 為此，我便放汝通過。

column1: Ye think ye be a grand prize, but ye do not be what I most desire.
column2: 汝自以為是件了不起的獻禮，但汝並非我最渴求之物。

column1: Ye be a fool to part with this gift of love, but for it I shall let ye pass.
column2: 捨得這份愛的信物，汝真是個傻子，但為此我便放汝通過。

column1: For this magical stone, I shall let ye pass.
column2: 為這塊有魔力的石頭，我便放汝通過。

column1: Ye part with the very heart of the Lady of the Lake, but for this gift I shall let ye pass.
column2: 汝竟捨得湖中女神的心，但為這份獻禮，我便放汝通過。

column1: Ye please me not with this offer.
column2: 這獻禮，不能令我滿意。

column1: Seek ye not to bargain with me. I take, I do not give.
column2: 休想與我討價還價。我只取，不予。

column1: If ye be so cunning a knight, ye shall know.
column2: 汝若真是機智的騎士，自會知曉。

column1: I care nothing for the petty doings of men. Give me what I desire or ye shall suffer.
column2: 凡人瑣事，我毫不在乎。獻上我所渴求之物，否則汝將自食苦果。

column1: Look all ye want, mortal man. These three by me, see ye them? Once they too were men.
column2: 看個夠吧，凡人。我身旁這三個，汝可看見？他們也曾是人。

column1: They dared enter my circle, but did not give me what I desired. Will ye end like them?
column2: 他們膽敢闖入我的石圈，卻未獻上我所渴求之物。汝也要落得同樣下場嗎？

column1: You cannot get back what you have not given.
column2: 你不曾獻出之物，如何取回？

column1: Seek to take back what ye have given and ye shall be stone before ye can blink.
column2: 汝若想討回已獻出之物，眨眼間便會化為石頭。

column1: But she does not have it.
column2: 但她並沒有這東西。

column1: What ye have given, ye have lost.
column2: 汝已獻出之物，便已失去。

column1: It is ye who smell of warm blood and mortal flesh. Ye reek of life. I shall like ye better when ye smell of cold stone.
column2: 汝身上散發著溫熱鮮血與凡人血肉的氣味，滿身生氣逼人。待汝渾身化作冰冷石頭的氣味，我才會更喜歡汝。

column1: I think it is you who needs the help.
column2: 我看，需要幫助的人是你才對。

column1: It is a good thought, Arthur, but your mission is far more important.
column2: 這念頭是好的，亞瑟，但你的使命遠比這重要得多。

column1: Try it if ye dare, arrogant one.
column2: 有膽便試試看，狂妄之人。

column1: What a disgusting notion.
column2: 多麼令人作嘔的念頭。

column1: Put up thy sword! Put it away this instant or ye shall become stone!
column2: 收起汝的劍！立刻收起，否則汝將化為石頭！

column1: Halt! Ye shall not pass me unhindered, king though ye be.
column2: 止步！縱然汝貴為國王，也休想毫無阻攔地從我身旁通過。

column1: Aye, rage if you will, but until ye give me what I desire, ye shall not move another step.
column2: 盡管動怒吧，但汝若不獻上我所渴求之物，便再也休想向前踏出一步。

column1: And if ye give me not what I desire, a stone ye shall be.
column2: 汝若不獻上我所渴求之物，便將化為石頭。

column1: Aye! Aye! That is what I most desire! Bring it here at once!
column2: 是了！是了！那正是我最渴求之物！速速取來獻上！

column1: Bless you, valiant knight! I am the Lady Elayne, transformed into the forest witch by a hideous spell cast upon me by the Black Knight.
column2: 感謝你，英勇的騎士！我是艾蓮公主，被黑武士施下的邪惡咒語，變成了這森林女巫。

column1: Only this sleeve, which I gave to my true love, could set me free.
column2: 唯有這件我贈予真愛之人的衣袖，才能使我獲得解脫。

column1: And if my sleeve is here, my beloved knight cannot be far away. I must find him at once! Fare thee well!
column2: 既然我的衣袖在此，我心愛的騎士必定就在不遠處。我得立刻去尋他！珍重了！

column1: Now be gone!
column2: 如今，去吧！

column1: No man can best me with cold steel. Pay the price for thy arrogance.
column2: 無人能憑冷冽鋼刃勝過我。為汝的狂妄，付出代價吧。

column1: A tongue so foul should never utter another vowel!
column2: 如此污穢的舌頭，再不配吐出一個字音！

column1: Ye have not given me what I desire. Stone ye shall be for all eternity!
column2: 汝未獻上我所渴求之物。汝將永世化為石頭！

column1: Defeated by an ugly crone, From mortal man to standing stone, With sun and rain upon you blown,
column2: 被一個醜陋的老太婆擊敗，從血肉之軀化為佇立的石頭，任由日曬雨淋加諸其身，

column1: Through carven locks the wind shall moan, Here you will be through years unknown, And slowly crumble when time has flown.
column2: 風聲將在你雕鑿的髮絲間低吟，你將在此屹立千古歲月，直到光陰流逝，你才緩緩崩塌碎裂。

column1: Your sudden disappearance was too much for even your well-trained horse. He has run all the way back to Camelot.
column2: 你的突然消失，饒是你那匹訓練有素的坐騎，也承受不住，牠已一路奔回肯萊特了。

column1: The eerie glow must mean that you have solved this stone's riddle.
column2: 這詭異的光芒，想必意味著你已解開這塊石頭的謎題。

column1: I cannot help you here.
column2: 此處我幫不上你。

column1: What riddle? Your request is a riddle to me.
column2: 什麼謎題？你這要求對我來說才是個謎。

column1: Only so much help can I give. This is your test and yours alone.
column2: 我能給的幫助有限。這是屬於你自己的考驗，唯你一人能過。

column1: There is some sort of sorcerous barrier barring you from the Tor.
column2: 有某種巫術屏障，擋住了你通往那座山丘的路。

column1: There are no markings or carvings upon them. They are quite plain.
column2: 它們上頭並無任何標記或雕刻，樸實無華。

column1: The only riddle to read here is that there is no riddle here to read.
column2: 此處唯一的謎題，就是這裡根本沒有謎題可讀。

column1: You are once more at the base of Glastonbury Tor.
column2: 你再次來到格列斯登伯利山腳下。

column1: You have reached the base of Glastonbury Tor on the edge of the Forest Perilous.
column2: 你已抵達派瑞樂斯森林邊緣、格列斯登伯利山的山腳下。

column1: And I see your mule grazes as it waits for you. She must have found her way safely through the forest on her own.
column2: 我看見你的騾子正一邊吃草一邊等你。牠想必是自己安然穿過了這片森林。

column1: These stones were placed here by magick. You will not move them by human means.
column2: 這些石頭是魔法安放於此的，你無法以凡人之力搬動它們。

column1: Easy to do, but to little purpose.
column2: 做起來容易，卻毫無用處。

column1: You are out of the Forest Perilous with an open sky overhead.
column2: 你已走出派瑞樂斯森林，頭頂是一片開闊的天空。

column1: I suspect your mule is more intelligent than she appears.
column2: 我猜你的騾子，其實比看起來聰明。

column1: The larger trees have been left behind in the forest. These are mere shrubs in comparison.
column2: 高大的樹木已留在森林裡了，這些相比之下不過是灌木叢。

column1: The magical glow around the stone must mean that you have solved its riddle.
column2: 石頭周圍的魔光，想必是你已解開了它的謎語。

column1: That effect is the mystical barrier which prevents you from climbing the Tor.
column2: 那股力量正是阻止你攀上山丘的神秘結界。

column1: Where? I see nothing.
column2: 在哪裡？我什麼也沒看見。

column1: This clump of rock looks quite ordinary.
column2: 這叢岩石看來相當尋常。

column1: There are five of these standing stones.
column2: 這裡共有五塊立石。

column1: As you have cleverly realized, these five stones were once men. Their riddles mark them as poets.
column2: 正如你機敏地看出，這五塊石頭曾經是人。他們出的謎語，透露出詩人的身分。

column1: I see no other human being here.
column2: 我在此處不見其他人影。

column1: Have you forgotten already? You sent Gawaine back to Camelot upon it.
column2: 你這麼快就忘了？你讓高文騎著牠回肯萊特去了。

column1: I would hazard that your sudden disappearance spooked it, and that it is halfway home by now.
column2: 我猜你突然消失，把牠嚇著了，此刻大概已經走了一半的路回家。

column1: Beyond the standing stones the base of the tor rises steeply.
column2: 越過這些立石，山丘的坡基便陡然上升。

column1: You have neither the time or tools for such a venture.
column2: 你既無時間，也無工具，做不了這等事。

column1: This is not a barrier that you can hack your way through with Excaliber.
column2: 這道結界，不是揮舞聖劍便能劈開的。

column1: I doubt a stone has much use for it.
column2: 我想石頭用不上這東西。

column1: She looks content grazing her way through a goodly section of Glastonbury Tor.
column2: 牠看來心滿意足地一路吃著草，啃過了格列斯登伯利山好一片草地。

column1: No need. She will follow now, I think.
column2: 不必了，我想牠現在會跟上來。

column1: She does not seem to pay much attention.
column2: 牠似乎沒怎麼理會。

column1: Mules are obstinate creatures. At best, you can hope she will follow of her own will.
column2: 騾子生性倔強，你至多只能盼牠自願跟隨。

column1: Bend your will to your mission. Everything else can wait for the time being.
column2: 把心思放回你的使命上，其餘的事都可以暫且擱下。

column1: There is the smell of grass and fresh air.
column2: 空氣中有青草與清新的氣息。

column1: Had you been turned to stone, would you appreciate such a thing?
column2: 若你被化成了石頭，還會在意這種事嗎？

column1: I see no poet, unless you perceive something that I do not.
column2: 我沒看見什麼詩人，除非你看出了我沒看出的東西。

column1: Nothing happens. Perhaps you are not close enough to one of the stoned poets.
column2: 什麼也沒發生。或許你離某個化石詩人還不夠近。

column1: With the spell broken, the stones maintain a sullen silence.
column2: 咒語已解，石頭只剩一片悶悶的沉默。

column1: Move closer to a stone.
column2: 靠近某塊石頭。

column1: Arthur, this is no time to ask me for something as frivolous as a riddle.
column2: 亞瑟，此刻不是向我討謎語這等閒事的時候。

column1: There is no man here.
column2: 此處無人。

column1: Arthur? Arthur! Where are you?
column2: 亞瑟？亞瑟！你在哪裡？

column1: Once we were poets, Men free and gay, The witch has left us Stony and grey, And now we pose riddles, To block the way.
column2: 我們曾是詩人，自由自在逍遙；女巫將我們留下，化為灰石一片荒涼；如今我們出謎，只為擋住去路。

column1: Hmmph. If that is a sample of their poetry, they deserve their fate.
column2: 哼，若這便是他們詩才的樣本，那也是自作自受。

column1: There are five of these stones, each roughly man-sized. Perhaps they WERE men once.
column2: 這裡有五塊石頭，大小約莫與人相當。或許它們曾經真的是人。

column1: The magical glow around this stone means that you have solved its riddle.
column2: 這塊石頭周圍的魔光，意味著你已解開了它的謎語。

column1: Ah, there you are!  That was not my doing.  You have been brought by another power to the center of the ruins on Glastonbury Tor.
column2: 啊，你在這裡！這不是我的手筆。是另一股力量，把你帶到了格列斯登伯利山廢墟的中心。

column1: The ruins offer little in the way of defense or concealment.
column2: 這片廢墟提供不了什麼防禦或掩蔽。

column1: You are in the center of the ruins on Glastonbury Tor.
column2: 你正身處格列斯登伯利山廢墟的中心。

column1: The ruins are nothing but bits of wall and fallen rock with only the Tor beneath them.
column2: 這片廢墟不過是斷牆殘石，底下便是山丘本身。

column1: What remains would have been the arch of a doorway.
column2: 殘存的部分，想必曾是一道門拱。

column1: This arch is the frame of a doorway.
column2: 這道拱是一扇門的框架。

column1: You are in another part of the ruins.
column2: 你來到了廢墟的另一處。

column1: You have opened the well.
column2: 你已打開了這口井。

column1: The well lid is iron, with a solid iron bar and a lock holding it in place.
column2: 井蓋是鐵製的，以一根結實的鐵條與一把鎖固定住。

column1: It has the shape and look of a well, though covered with a heavy iron lid.
column2: 看形狀與樣貌是口井，只是覆著一面沉重的鐵蓋。

column1: The cold waters of the sacred well are dark and reveal nothing.
column2: 聖井中的冷水幽暗深沉，什麼也看不出。

column1: It is fit into the iron bar and would therefore be impossible to break open by ordinary means.
column2: 它嵌合在鐵條之中，尋常手段不可能將它砸開。

column1: A good idea, though difficult to do unless you can remove the lid.
column2: 這主意不錯，但除非能移開井蓋，否則難以做到。

column1: It would help to be on the other side of the well.
column2: 若能到井的另一側，會有幫助。

column1: It would help to be next to the well.
column2: 若能站在井邊，會有幫助。

column1: Nay, if this is the thorn planted by Joseph of Arimathea, it would be tantamount to sacrilege.
column2: 不可，若這真是亞利馬太的約瑟親手栽下的荊棘，如此行事無異於褻瀆聖物。

column1: It is full of thorns.
column2: 上面滿是荊棘。

column1: I cannot imagine how you would do that.
column2: 我實在想不出你要如何辦到。

column1: Besides roots and shadow, there is not much to see.
column2: 除了樹根與陰影，沒什麼好看的。

column1: The sacred well is covered with a heavy lid and a solid iron bar in the shape of interlocked circles, held in place by a lock.
column2: 這口聖井覆著一面沉重的井蓋，上面有一根鑄成環環相扣圖案的結實鐵條，並以一把鎖固定。

column1: We can only assume there is water in this well until it is opened.
column2: 在井打開之前，我們只能猜測裡頭是否有水。

column1: It would help to be on the other side the well.
column2: 若能到井的另一側，會有幫助。

column1: The covered well is in this section of the ruins.
column2: 這片廢墟裡，有一口覆蓋著的井。

column1: There is the well and thorn tree, as before.
column2: 井與荊棘樹依然在此，一如先前。

column1: There is the cowled figure of a monk near a covered well.
column2: 一口覆蓋著的井旁，站著一個披著兜帽的僧侶身影。

column1: The arch is all that remains of a doorway.
column2: 這道拱，是一扇門僅存的殘跡。

column1: The one small tree is covered in thorns.  The legend of Joseph of Arimathea has it that when he hid the Grail, he also stuck his staff into the ground and from that place a thorn tree grew.
column2: 這株小樹渾身是刺。傳說亞利馬太的約瑟藏起聖杯之時，也將手杖插入地中，那地方便長出了這株荊棘樹。

column1: It is covered with a heavy iron lid.
column2: 它覆著一面沉重的鐵蓋。

column1: The well is filled with cold, dark water.
column2: 井中滿是幽暗的冷水。

column1: There is nothing more to be gained by looking at it now.
column2: 此刻再看下去，也看不出什麼名堂了。

column1: It is held in place by a locked iron bar.
column2: 它由一根上了鎖的鐵條固定著。

column1: The iron bar forms a design of interlocking circles.  Lovely, but too solid to break.
column2: 這鐵條鑄成環環相扣的圖案，精美，卻堅實得無法砸斷。

column1: You could, if the well were open.
column2: 若井是開著的，你便能如此。

column1: The well opening is upon the other side.
column2: 井口在另一側。

column1: You cannot pick this lock.
column2: 你撬不開這把鎖。

column1: That is not a very useful idea.
column2: 這主意用處不大。

column1: Do your eyes fail you?  The well is closed.
column2: 你的眼睛不管用了嗎？這口井是關著的。

column1: This well is both ancient and sacred.  A bit of decorum is called for.
column2: 這口井既古老又神聖，理當保持幾分敬重。

column1: One does not swim in sacred wells, and this one has been revered for centuries.
column2: 沒有人會在聖井裡游泳，何況這口井已受人敬奉了數百年。

column1: Beyond the pleasure of being stuck by them, I can see no purpose in that.
column2: 除了讓自己被刺一身之外，我看不出這麼做有什麼意義。

column1: I cannot imagine how one would do that.
column2: 我實在想不出該如何辦到這件事。

column1: Do your eyes fail you?  It IS open.
column2: 你的眼睛不管用了嗎？它是開著的。

column1: The latch and lock are upon the other side.
column2: 門閂與鎖都在另一側。

column1: To lift the lid, you must remove the bar.  To remove the bar, you must open the lock.  You will not open the lock by wishful thinking.
column2: 要掀開井蓋，得先移開鐵條；要移開鐵條，得先打開鎖。光憑一廂情願，是打不開這把鎖的。

column1: Leave it open, Arthur, so that others who follow may drink from the sacred waters.
column2: 讓它開著吧，亞瑟，好讓後來的人也能飲得這聖水。

column1: It is already locked.
column2: 它已經鎖上了。

column1: The well is already unlocked.
column2: 這口井已經解鎖了。

column1: You do not have the means.
column2: 你沒有辦法做到這件事。

column1: Do your eyes fail you?  It IS closed.
column2: 你的眼睛不管用了嗎？它是關著的。

column1: The lid closes from the other side.
column2: 井蓋要從另一側才能關上。

column1: That would only damage Excaliber.
column2: 那麼做只會損傷聖劍。

column1: What nonsense is this?
column2: 這是什麼胡言亂語？

column1: The key turned easily and the lock is now open.
column2: 鑰匙輕易轉動，鎖已經打開了。

column1: From the shiver that just ran through you, I gather the water was ice-cold.
column2: 從你剛才那陣顫抖看來，我猜這水冷得刺骨。

column1: Did I not say the Grail was not here?  You have only a wet hand to show for your stubbornness.
column2: 我不是說過聖杯不在這裡嗎？你這般固執，換來的不過是一隻濕淋淋的手。

column1: So THIS is the Mad Monk's treasure!  A beautiful, glittering crystal heart.  How cold it is to the touch!
column2: 原來這就是瘋僧侶的寶物！一顆美麗、閃著光芒的水晶心。摸起來竟是這般冰冷！

column1: Alas, Arthur, this is the object of power that created the Spell of Circular Entrapment.  The Grail is not here.
column2: 唉，亞瑟，這正是造出困環咒的力量之物。聖杯不在此處。

column1: You are in another part of the ruins.  There are ancient carvings of skulls in one wall.
column2: 你來到了廢墟的另一處。一面牆上刻著古老的骷髏雕飾。

column1: Memento mori is a Latin phrase meaning:   "Remember that thou must die".
column2: 「Memento mori」是句拉丁文，意為：「勿忘你終有一死。」

column1: An object, such as a skull, is commonly called a memento mori because it is a reminder of inevitable death.
column2: 像骷髏這樣的物件，一般稱作「memento mori」，因為它提醒著世人死亡終不可免。

column1: The carved skulls are memento mori, reminders of the death that awaits us all.
column2: 這些雕刻的骷髏便是 memento mori，提醒著等待眾人的死亡。

column1: The arch is the remnant of a doorway.
column2: 這道拱，是一扇門遺留下的殘跡。

column1: This is no time to be plundering religious ruins.
column2: 此刻不是洗劫宗教廢墟的時候。

column1: They are bushes.
column2: 那些是灌木叢。

column1: They are rocks.
column2: 那些是岩石。

column1: The flowers seem cheerful amid the ancient ruins.
column2: 這些花朵在古老的廢墟間，顯得生氣盎然。

column1: The arch supports its roof no longer.
column2: 這道拱早已撐不起屋頂了。

column1: Unwise.  Desecrating a sacred object is a good way to bring a curse down upon yourself.
column2: 不智之舉。褻瀆聖物，是招來詛咒上身的好辦法。

column1: Not in this place or you will offend your own god by kneeling to false gods.
column2: 此地不可如此，否則你向偽神下跪，便是冒犯了你自己的神。

column1: I hope your god is listening.
column2: 但願你的神正在聆聽。

column1: The Old Ones have taken their silver and gone away.
column2: 古代幽靈已取走了他們的銀子，離去了。

column1: The Old Ones have taken it.
column2: 古代幽靈已將它取走了。

column1: You cannot take back what you have not given.
column2: 你未曾給出之物，如何取回？

column1: The Monk had not the means to buy his freedom, so we kept him as our servant.  He was mad, but any servant is better than none.
column2: 那僧侶無力贖回自由，於是我們便將他留作僕役。他雖瘋癲，但有僕役總比沒有的好。

column1: Of what are you speaking?  There is nothing like that here.
column2: 你在說什麼？此處並無這樣的東西。

column1: What an utterly foolish notion.
column2: 這念頭實在愚蠢至極。

column1: It is too heavy for that.
column2: 它太重了，辦不到。

column1: It is solid stone.
column2: 這是實心的石頭。

column1: There is nothing but grass and weeds.
column2: 這裡除了野草雜叢，什麼也沒有。

column1: They are too old and weathered to be made out.
column2: 它們太過古老、風化得太厲害，已經辨認不出了。

column1: An iron key lies upon the altar in place of your silver.
column2: 一把鐵鑰匙擺在祭壇上，取代了你的銀子。

column1: In this part of the ruins there are the remains of some kind of altar.
column2: 廢墟的這一處，有座祭壇的殘跡。

column1: Your silver coins lie upon the altar.
column2: 你的銀幣擺在祭壇上。

column1: It is a key, Arthur.
column2: 這是一把鑰匙，亞瑟。

column1: Some of your silver lies upon the altar.
column2: 你的一部分銀子擺在祭壇上。

column1: It is an extremely ancient altar, of a most peculiar configuration.  Its three parts may hint at the worship of a trinity of some sort.
column2: 這是一座極為古老的祭壇，形制十分特異。它分作三個部分，或許暗示著某種三神一體的信仰。

column1: Ask the Old Ones.
column2: 去問古代幽靈吧。

column1: Copper is for the lowest spirits of the earth.  Gold is for young gods.  You cannot appease us with those metals.
column2: 銅是獻給地底最卑微的精怪，金是獻給年輕的神祇。這些金屬平息不了我們。

column1: We three are the eldest servants of mother-moon.  We love most dearly the metal that gleams cold and pure like hardened moonlight.
column2: 我們三人是月亮之母最年長的僕從。我們最鍾愛那如凝結月光般，泛著冷冽純淨光澤的金屬。

column1: It is the purest of metals.  Silver shines with the light of mother-moon.  You may win your freedom by giving us as much silver as the mother-moon had children.
column2: 那是最純淨的金屬。銀子閃耀著月亮之母的光輝。你若獻上與月亮之母子女數目相當的銀子，便能贏得自由。

column1: Moonlight is the gift of mother-moon, so that total darkness will never rule upon the earth.
column2: 月光是月亮之母的贈禮，好讓黑暗永不能徹底統治這片大地。

column1: Mother-moon had five children: earth, wind, water, fire and spirit.
column2: 月亮之母育有五個孩子：土、風、水、火與靈。

column1: We do not want that!  There is only one metal we cherish.
column2: 我們不要那個！我們珍視的金屬只有一種。

column1: Stay and be our servant and we will tell you wondrous secrets.
column2: 留下來做我們的僕役，我們便告訴你奇妙的秘密。

column1: Ignore them, Arthur.  Such spirits are notorious liars.
column2: 別理睬牠們，亞瑟。這些靈素以說謊聞名。

column1: We need more silver to appease us.
column2: 我們還需要更多銀兩，才能息怒。

column1: Glorious silver!  How pure and perfect it is!  Having silver is better than having a servant!
column2: 燦爛的銀啊！何等純淨完美！擁有銀子，勝過擁有一個僕從！

column1: We release you from our service and leave you a gift.
column2: 我們解除你為我們服役的義務，並留下一份禮物給你。

column1: The ice here is smooth and unbroken.
column2: 這裡的冰面光滑完整，未見裂痕。

column1: Your horse does not want to go in that direction. It must not trust what lies beneath the snow.
column2: 你的坐騎不願朝那個方向前進，想必牠不信任積雪底下藏著什麼。

column1: The snow is too deep to go that way.
column2: 積雪太深，無法從那邊過去。

column1: You will find the trip even longer and more tiring without your horse, Arthur.
column2: 沒有坐騎，這趟路只會顯得更漫長、更疲累，亞瑟。

column1: It is a glittering palace of ice, rising from the center of the lake.
column2: 那是一座閃耀的冰宮，聳立在湖心。

column1: You have nearly reached the edge of the lake called Ot Moor.  Through a gap in the bushes, you can catch a glimpse of a palace in the middle of the lake.
column2: 你已經接近那座名叫奧特摩爾的湖畔。透過灌木叢間的縫隙，你瞥見湖心有一座宮殿。

column1: Already, there is a touch of warmth returning to this area, but it will take some time for the ice and snow to melt.
column2: 這一帶已經漸漸有了一絲暖意回歸，但冰雪要完全消融，還需要一段時日。

column1: That would not be safe in all your heavy gear.
column2: 你這身沉重的裝備，這麼做並不安全。

column1: A ridge of ice prevents you from going any further in this direction.
column2: 一道冰脊擋住了你，無法再朝這個方向前進。

column1: A huge bank of snow blocks your path.
column2: 一大片積雪堵住了你的去路。

column1: You have reached what would normally be the shore of the lake known as Ot Moor.  It is entirely frozen over.
column2: 你來到了平時該是奧特摩爾湖岸的地方，如今整片湖面全結了冰。

column1: It will take longer to remove the ice than to make it.  But the thaw begins slowly and the ice is surely more dangerous than it was before.
column2: 融去這片冰，要比造出它費上更長的時間。不過解凍已經緩緩展開，這片冰想必也比先前更為危險。

column1: Your horse is too wise to venture onto the ice.
column2: 你的坐騎太過聰慧，不會冒險踏上冰面。

column1: Your mule is too intelligent to follow you onto dangerous ice.
column2: 你的騾子太過機靈，不會跟著你踏上危險的冰面。

column1: Your horse knows better than to walk upon thin ice.
column2: 你的坐騎深知不該在薄冰上行走。

column1: You can observe ice pushed upward into a ridge by the pressure of freezing too quickly.
column2: 你可以看出，這道冰脊是急速結凍的壓力將冰面向上推擠而成。

column1: Having reached the towering palace of ice, I must caution you.  In this cold manifestation, the Lady of the Lake may not be the benefactress you have known in the past.
column2: 既已抵達這座聳立的冰宮，我必須提醒你：在這副冰冷的化身之中，湖中女神或許已不再是你過去所熟知的那位恩人。

column1: I would guess that the triangular objects on the doors are door handles, though being made of ice do not seem very useful.
column2: 我猜門上那些三角形的物件是門把，不過既是冰所製成，似乎派不上什麼用場。

column1: The doors are made of solid ice, the same as the rest of the palace.
column2: 這扇門是實心的冰塊所製，與宮殿其餘部分並無二致。

column1: I cannot say what meaning this symbol has.  Perhaps it is a warning, perhaps mere decoration.
column2: 我說不出這個符號有何含意，或許是個警示，也或許只是裝飾。

column1: The stairs are made of ice.  Tread carefully.
column2: 這階梯以冰築成，小心踩踏。

column1: In the far distance, you glimpse part of the Cotswold Hills.
column2: 遠方，你隱約望見科茲沃爾德丘陵的一角。

column1: The Ice Palace is even more beautiful and impressive up close than at a distance.
column2: 這座冰宮近看比遠望更加瑰麗懾人。

column1: I would say the two small pyramids of ice are purely decorative.
column2: 我想這兩座小冰錐純粹只是裝飾。

column1: This door cannot be opened.
column2: 這扇門打不開。

column1: It does not open.  Indeed, there was no reason for you to have returned at all.
column2: 它打不開。事實上，你根本沒有理由回到這裡。

column1: Try the other door.
column2: 試試另一扇門。

column1: Your arms do not reach that far.
column2: 你的手臂搆不到那麼遠。

column1: It is already closed.
column2: 它已經關上了。

column1: Gwenhyver is a girl. I am far more than that.
column2: 昆海兒不過是個女子，我可遠不止如此。

column1: Remember that finding the Grail is but half the task.  You must also be worthy to possess it.
column2: 切記，尋得聖杯不過完成了一半的使命，你還必須配得上擁有它。

column1: Nothing can help, save the return of the object of power which was stolen from me.
column2: 唯有歸還那件從我這裡被奪走的力量之物，此外別無他法可以相助。

column1: That which enables me to feel warmth and love, such as the hopeless love I have for Sir Launcelot.
column2: 那件事物讓我得以感受溫暖與愛——就像我對蘭斯洛特爵士那段無望的愛戀。

column1: Only the Old Ones had the power to do that.
column2: 唯有古代幽靈才有這樣的力量。

column1: Having told you what I know of the Grail, there is but one more boon you can desire of me -- the life of Sir Launcelot.
column2: 我已將自己所知關於聖杯之事悉數告訴你，如今你能向我求取的，只剩一項恩惠——蘭斯洛特爵士的性命。

column1: I am loathe to release him.  I offered him my love and he spurned it, for he has given his whole heart to your queen.
column2: 我不甘願放他離去。我曾獻上我的愛，他卻棄之不顧，因為他早已將整顆心交給了你的皇后。

column1: If you leave him here, Pendragon, you will be free of him and need never share Gwenhyver's love with him again.
column2: 若你把他留在這裡，潘德拉貢，你便能擺脫他，再也不必與他分享昆海兒的愛。

column1: I sense that you possess something that belongs to me.  Give it to me and I will tell you what even Merlin does not know -- where to search for the Grail.
column2: 我感覺得到，你身上帶著一件屬於我的東西。將它交還給我，我便告訴你連梅林都不知道的事——該到何處尋找聖杯。

column1: But if you withhold it, you will have neither help nor knowledge from me.
column2: 但你若執意扣留不還，我既不會相助，也不會透露半點消息。

column1: He cannot answer you. I have sealed his heartless lips forever, unless you choose to win his freedom.
column2: 他無法回答你。我已將他無情的雙唇永遠封住，除非你選擇為他贏得自由。

column1: Blessed be.
column2: 願蒙祝福。

column1: That would not help you much.
column2: 這對你幫助不大。

column1: Launcelot will never go free, unless you find and return the object of power that was stolen from me.
column2: 蘭斯洛特永遠無法獲釋，除非你尋得那件從我這裡被奪走的力量之物，並將它歸還。

column1: No weapon made, not even Excaliber, can shatter this ice formed by my will.
column2: 世間沒有一件兵器——即便是聖劍——能夠擊碎這由我意志所凝成的冰。

column1: Money is meaningless to me.
column2: 金錢對我毫無意義。

column1: I will not touch it, for it has Gwenhyver's spell upon it.
column2: 我不會碰它，因為它身上帶著昆海兒的咒法。

column1: Nay, keep it. I have no use for such a thing.
column2: 不必，留著吧。這種東西我用不上。

column1: Aye, that is my heart and contains much of my power. Give it to me and I shall tell you where to search for the Grail.
column2: 正是，那便是我的心，蘊藏著我的大半力量。將它交給我，我便告訴你該到何處尋找聖杯。

column1: To free Launcelot will require first my good will. Do not anger me with attempts at bargaining.
column2: 要放蘭斯洛特自由，須先贏得我的善意。休得以討價還價來觸怒我。

column1: He is worth far more than that to me.
column2: 對我而言，他的價值遠不止於此。

column1: He can accept nothing while frozen in ice.
column2: 他被凍在冰中，什麼都無法接受。

column1: I thank you again for the return of the crystal heart, for much of my power is invested within it.
column2: 我再次感謝你歸還水晶心，我的大半力量都寄託其中。

column1: If you can return it to me, you will win my help.
column2: 你若能將它還給我，便能贏得我的相助。

column1: The ice and cold reflects my mood of late.
column2: 這片冰霜寒意，正映照著我近來的心境。

column1: I gave you Excaliber because it is a sword worthy of a king.  Now make sure you are a king worthy of the sword.
column2: 我將聖劍賜給你，因為它是一柄配得上君王的劍。如今，你該確保自己是一位配得上這柄劍的君王。

column1: Did you not listen?  Go to Jerusalem, I said.
column2: 你沒聽清楚嗎？我說過，前往耶路撒冷。

column1: Bring me the object of power that was stolen from me, and I will tell you where to search.
column2: 把那件從我這裡被奪走的力量之物帶來給我，我便告訴你該往何處尋找。

column1: You have but to leave and I will keep Launcelot here, far from Gwenhyver.  I will not harm him, but you will be free of him.
column2: 你只需離去，我便會把蘭斯洛特留在此處，遠離昆海兒。我不會傷害他，但你將從此擺脫他。

column1: Launcelot is my prisoner because he has spurned my love and given his heart to your wife, Gwenhyver.  You should thank me, Pendragon, for thus removing your rival for her love.
column2: 蘭斯洛特之所以成為我的囚徒，是因為他棄絕了我的愛，把心交給了你的妻子昆海兒。你該感謝我，潘德拉貢，我這是替你除去了情敵。

column1: He did not come here.  Therefore I know nothing of him.
column2: 他沒有到過這裡，因此我對他一無所知。

column1: Merlin is your advisor, not I.
column2: 梅林才是你的謀士，不是我。

column1: Here stands the Ice Maiden, a cold and unloving manifestation of the Lady of the Lake.  Near her is Sir Launcelot, imprisoned in ice.
column2: 此處立著冰霜仙子，那是湖中女神一副冷漠無情的化身。她身旁，蘭斯洛特爵士被囚於冰中。

column1: To reach Jerusalem, you must take ship to the port nearest it in that part of the world.
column2: 要抵達耶路撒冷，你得搭船前往那一帶離它最近的港口。

column1: It is dark and cold and uninviting.
column2: 那裡陰暗、寒冷，令人不敢靠近。

column1: She looks quite frigid.  But if you are to free Launcelot, you must find a way to win her good will.
column2: 她看來十分冷峻。但你若想救出蘭斯洛特，就得設法贏得她的善意。

column1: He is caught in a living death, spellbound in a frozen limbo.
column2: 他陷入生死交界的境地，被咒法禁錮在一片冰封的虛無之中。

column1: Everything is ice, formed from the frozen body of the lake by the Ice Maiden's magicks.
column2: 這裡的一切皆是冰，是冰霜仙子以法術將湖水凍結而成。

column1: Your good friend and heroic knight, Sir Launcelot, is frozen inside a pillar of ice.
column2: 你的摯友、英勇的蘭斯洛特爵士，被凍在一根冰柱之中。

column1: The inside of her palace is lined with stalagmites, stalactites and pillars of ice.
column2: 她的宮殿內部，滿佈石筍、鐘乳與冰柱。

column1: These unyielding pillars of ice were formed by the Ice Maiden's will.
column2: 這些堅不可摧的冰柱，是冰霜仙子以意志凝成。

column1: This ice pillar no longer holds the frozen body of Launcelot.
column2: 這根冰柱裡，已不再封著蘭斯洛特冰封的身軀。

column1: Sir Launcelot is imprisoned in a living death within this pillar of ice.
column2: 蘭斯洛特爵士被囚禁在這根冰柱之中，陷入生死交界的境地。

column1: The recesses of the ice palace fade into a shrouded glimmer of frozen shadow.
column2: 冰宮深處，隱沒於一片朦朧幽微的冰封暗影之中。

column1: Your lips would stick.
column2: 你的雙唇會黏在上面。

column1: She is frigidly disinterested.
column2: 她一臉冷漠，毫無興致。

column1: Do you think to threaten ME with the very sword I gave you from my own hand?  Once only will I tolerate this, or you will suffer the fate of Launcelot.
column2: 你竟想拿我親手所賜的劍來威脅我？這種事我只容忍一次，否則你將落得與蘭斯洛特相同的下場。

column1: You are a noble man, Pendragon.  But we will see how true is your desire to save Launcelot when you are put to the test.  Follow me.
column2: 你是個高尚的人，潘德拉貢。但你救蘭斯洛特的心意究竟有多真切，得等你通過考驗才見分曉。跟我來。

column1: You should have heeded my warning!
column2: 你早該聽從我的警告！

column1: As icy fingers seize your spine And coldness numbs your brain You wish instead in battle hot You nobly had been slain.
column2: 冰冷的指尖扼住你的脊骨，寒意麻痺了你的神智，你多麼盼望，自己是命喪炙熱的戰場，慷慨捐軀，死得其所。

column1: Alas, your ears are filled with ice You hear not my sad refrain, A frozen statue of despair In winter's hard domain.
column2: 可嘆你雙耳已被冰雪封住，再也聽不見我哀傷的吟唱，你將化作一尊絕望的冰像，永立於這嚴酷的寒冬國度。

column1: I shall return you to Camelot!
column2: 我將送你返回肯萊特！

column1: I have freed Sir Launcelot and sent him back to Camelot, but your journey goes on.  Farewell, King Arthur, and may you overcome every obstacle with the same wit and courage you have shown here.
column2: 我已釋放蘭斯洛特爵士，送他回到肯萊特，但你的旅程仍要繼續。珍重了，亞瑟王，願你此後遭逢的每一道難關，都能以你在此展現的機智與勇氣一一克服。

column1: You may not pass that way, Pendragon, unless I lead you there.
column2: 除非由我引路，否則你不得從那條路過去，潘德拉貢。

column1: You may not pass that way.
column2: 你不得從那條路過去。

column1: I sense the presence of Merlin.  But I know that which he does not -- where to search for the Grail.  But to win my help, you must find and return an object of power that was stolen from me.
column2: 我感應到梅林的存在。但我知曉一件連他都不知道的事——該到何處尋找聖杯。然而要贏得我的相助，你必須尋得一件從我這裡被奪走的力量之物，並將它歸還。

column1: Go, and I will transport you safely across the ice.  Do not return unless you bring it to me!
column2: 去吧，我會護送你安然越過這片冰原。除非把它帶來給我，否則休得回來！

column1: Blessed be!  For this greatest of all gifts, I will give you the gift of knowledge in return.
column2: 願蒙祝福！為了這份至上的禮物，我將以知識的贈禮回報於你。

column1: To find the Grail, you must take ship to Gaza, then seek Jerusalem.  Somewhere in that city it lies hidden.
column2: 要尋得聖杯，你必須搭船前往加薩，再轉往耶路撒冷。聖杯就隱藏在那座城市之中的某處。

column1: Once you leave here, I will transport you safely across the ice to continue your search.  But Launcelot I will keep here, for he has spurned my love in favour of your queen. I will not release him, unless you ask it.
column2: 你一旦離開此地，我便會護送你安然越過這片冰原，讓你繼續尋覓。但蘭斯洛特，我要留在此處，因為他棄絕了我的愛，選擇了你的皇后。除非你開口求我，否則我不會放他自由。

column1: I can only tell you the name of each flower, if you ask about them.  Beyond that, you must consult your Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 你若問起，我只能告訴你每朵花的名字。除此之外，你得去查閱你的《Liber ex Doctrina》。

column1: It grows from a bed of soil locked in ice.
column2: 它從一片封鎖在冰中的土壤裡生長出來。

column1: Clearly, this Miraculous Bush of Flowers is the work of the Lady's sorcery, for it contains many different flowers upon the one bush.
column2: 這叢神奇花叢顯然出自女神的法術，因為同一株灌木上竟開著這麼多種花。

column1: Move to where you can best see all the flowers.
column2: 移動到能將所有花朵盡收眼底之處。

column1: Very well.  Let the test begin.
column2: 很好，考驗開始吧。

column1: Clearly, the bush grows here only by the Ice Maiden's magicks, yet it looks like an ordinary bush in an ordinary patch of soil.
column2: 這叢灌木顯然只是憑冰霜仙子的法術才得以在此生長，然而看上去，卻像是尋常土地裡一株尋常的灌木。
