column1: These are all the flowers on the Miraculous Bush of Flowers:   almond blossom, anemone, buttercup, chrysanthemum, cornflower, daffodil, forget-me-not, lilly, poppy, and sunflower.
column2: 以下是神奇花叢上所有的花：杏花、銀蓮花、毛茛花、菊花、矢車菊、水仙花、勿忘我、百合花、罌粟花，以及向日葵。

column1: In this glittering cave of ice, it is strange and wondrous to see a living thing.  Yet there stands the Miraculous Bush of Flowers.
column2: 在這座晶瑩剔透的冰穴之中，能見到一株活物，著實既奇異又奇妙。然而，神奇花叢就佇立在此。

column1: She looks expectant, in a frosty sort of way.
column2: 她一臉期待，帶著幾分冷冽的神情。

column1: He is in the pillar of ice and will remain there, unless you pass the Ice Maiden's test and free him.
column2: 他被困在冰柱之中，除非你通過冰霜仙子的考驗，否則他將永遠留在那裡。

column1: All but the Bush is ice, formed from the frozen body of the lake by the Ice Maiden's magicks.
column2: 除了那叢花，其餘一切皆是冰，是冰霜仙子以法術將湖水凍結而成。

column1: Please consult your Libera ex Doctrina.
column2: 請查閱你的《Liber ex Doctrina》。

column1: In every other respect, the bush is quite ordinary.
column2: 除此之外，這叢灌木再普通不過。

column1: There are no less than ten flowers upon this bush.
column2: 這叢灌木上，開著不下十種花。

column1: First, you must pass my test.
column2: 首先，你必須通過我的考驗。

column1: The different flowers fill the air with their mingled fragrances.
column2: 各色花朵的香氣交融，瀰漫在空氣之中。

column1: When you are ready for the test, we shall begin.
column2: 待你準備妥當，我們便開始考驗。

column1: Come, Pendragon.  My patience is not without limit.  If you will not look at the Bush and take this test, I will send you from here.
column2: 來吧，潘德拉貢。我的耐性並非無窮無盡。你若不肯細看這叢花、接受考驗，我便會把你送離此地。

column1: It would seem that your courage has failed you.  Farewell, then.
column2: 看來你的勇氣已經棄你而去。那麼，就此別過。

column1: You are worthy of the great legends that will live on in your name.  Come with me.
column2: 你當得起那些將以你之名流傳千古的偉大傳說。隨我來。

column1: Do not touch the Miraculous Bush of Flowers.  You may revel in the sight and scent of it, but it is mine alone to touch.
column2: 休得碰觸神奇花叢。你可以盡情欣賞它的姿色與香氣，但唯有我能觸碰它。

column1: I warn you most sternly, do not pursue this or I will punish you.
column2: 我嚴正警告你，休再堅持，否則我必懲罰你。

column1: To speak the Language of the Flowers means simply to know the special meaning that belongs to each flower, what thought or emotion is associated with it.
column2: 所謂通曉花語，不過是知曉每一朵花所蘊含的特殊意涵——它所代表的心思或情感。

column1: Nay, keep it.  I have no use for such a thing.
column2: 不必，留著吧。這種東西我用不上。

column1: You are here to free Launcelot.....if you dare.
column2: 你來到此地，是為了救出蘭斯洛特……若你敢的話。

column1: It is my Miraculous Bush of Flowers. Go look closely upon the one side that is in bloom.
column2: 這是我的神奇花叢。去仔細瞧瞧那一側正在綻放的花朵。

column1: That way is closed to you now, unless you can speak the Language of the Flowers and free Launcelot.
column2: 那條路如今已對你封閉，除非你能通曉花語、救出蘭斯洛特。

column1: You will hear me out first.
column2: 你得先聽我把話說完。

column1: To free Launcelot, you must speak the Language of the Flowers.  I will pose three riddles.  You must give me the name of the flower that solves each riddle.
column2: 要救出蘭斯洛特，你必須通曉花語。我將出三道謎題，你得答出能解開每道謎題的花名。

column1: The Language of the Flowers is the thought or emotion associated with each flower.  If you know this, you may be able to choose correctly.  If you fail even once, you will join Launcelot in a tomb of ice.
column2: 花語，便是與每一朵花相繫的心思或情感。你若通曉此道，或許便能選對答案。但凡失手一次，你便要與蘭斯洛特一同困於冰墓之中。

column1: But I will not force this upon you.  Recite the Message of the Rose and I will send you safely away, though Launcelot will not go free.
column2: 但我不會強迫你接受考驗。你若誦念玫瑰箴言，我便會送你安然離去，只是蘭斯洛特仍不得自由。

column1: But if you are determined to free your comrade in arms, look closely at the Miraculous Bush of Flowers.  And be warned: once you begin, you may not turn away from your fate.
column2: 但你若決意救出這位袍澤，便仔細看清神奇花叢。且要謹記：考驗一旦開始，你便再無法迴避自己的命運。

column1: Use cursor keys or mouse to choose a flower. Press "Enter" or mouse button to answer riddle with the flower you've chosen.
column2: 使用方向鍵或滑鼠選擇花朵，按下「Enter」鍵或滑鼠按鈕，以你所選的花朵回答謎題。

column1: Here is the first riddle. Remember, you must choose the flower that best answers it.
column2: 這是第一道謎題。切記，你得選出最能解答它的那朵花。

column1: Press F6 to see riddle again
column2: 按「F6」鍵可再次查看謎題。

column1: Your wisdom is great. Here is the next riddle.
column2: 你的智慧非凡，這是下一道謎題。

column1: Truly you are worthy to be king. The test is ended. Launcelot shall go free.
column2: 你確實無愧於王者之名。考驗至此結束，蘭斯洛特將重獲自由。

column1: You have failed. The price must be paid.
column2: 你已然失敗。這代價，終須償還。

column1: When light is dim and courage fails, When heart against adversity rails, When it seems you will never see the dawn, This alone can drive you on.
column2: 當光線黯淡、勇氣潰散之時，當心因逆境而痛楚難平之時，當你彷彿再難見到黎明之時，唯獨此物，能催你向前。

column1: If a dream is abandoned, Or a purpose dies, These are left with the dregs Of bitterness and sighs.
column2: 若夢想遭到棄置，或志向就此消亡，殘留下來的，唯有苦澀與嘆息的渣滓。

column1: It can be sweet on the tongue, Or vile as a curse, To hear it is evil, To believe it is worse.
column2: 它可以在舌尖上甘甜，也可以惡毒如詛咒，聽聞它是邪惡之事，相信它則更加不堪。

column1: In time of grief, It gives relief, It can lessen fears, Ease the pain of tears.
column2: 在悲傷之際，它帶來寬慰，能減輕恐懼，撫平淚水的傷痛。

column1: Oh, it is splendid, It has no peer, It scorns the lesser, And holds itself dear.
column2: 噢，它輝煌燦爛，舉世無雙，它蔑視卑微之物，唯獨珍視自身。

column1: Known to the priest And nun, Who natural pleasures Do shun.
column2: 為僧侶與修女所熟知，儘管他們棄絕世俗的歡愉。

column1: Surrounded by giants, Your worries were few, Wonders abounded, The world was new.
column2: 身邊環繞著巨人，你的煩憂寥寥無幾，奇蹟俯拾皆是，世界猶然嶄新。

column1: Wise are they who seek it, Fools are they who believe without it, Scorn those who claim To own it.
column2: 尋求它的人是智者，不憑它便輕信的人是愚者，聲稱擁有它的人，該受人鄙夷。

column1: It alleviates all pain and sorrows, The final end of all tomorrows, That to which we all must go, Rich or poor, high or low.
column2: 它能消解一切苦痛與哀傷，是所有明日終將抵達的盡頭，是無論貧富貴賤，眾人終須奔赴之處。

column1: For its sweet sake, You suffer in silence, What we both most desire, But will never possess.
column2: 為了它的甜美，你默默承受痛苦，那是我們彼此最渴望，卻永遠無法擁有之物。

column1: I need a bit more, m'lud, if you wish to go to the port you have chosen.
column2: 還需要再多一些，吾王，方能前往您所選定的港口。

column1: Beggin' m'lud's pardon, but this is not enough for the port you have chosen.  I will return your coins, so you may count them out again.
column2: 請吾王恕罪，這些銀錢不夠前往您所選的港口。容小人將錢幣奉還，請您重新點過。

column1: That is too much money, m'lud.  I cannot in all honesty accept more than is needed.
column2: 這錢太多了，吾王。憑良心，小人不能收下超出所需的部分。

column1: Thankee, m'lud.  You have booked passage to Gaza.
column2: 多謝，吾王。您已訂下前往加薩的船位。

column1: Thankee, m'lud.  You have booked passage to Thessalonica.
column2: 多謝，吾王。您已訂下前往帖撒羅尼迦的船位。

column1: Thankee, m'lud.  You have booked passage to Rome.
column2: 多謝，吾王。您已訂下前往羅馬的船位。

column1: Thankee, m'lud.  You have booked passage to Rennes.
column2: 多謝，吾王。您已訂下前往勒恩的船位。

column1: Thankee, m'lud.  You have booked passage to Dublin.
column2: 多謝，吾王。您已訂下前往都柏林的船位。

column1: He has the rolling gait of a retired sailor, and the portly bearing of a man who well enjoys his food and grog.
column2: 他走起路來步履搖晃，是退役水手的姿態，一身豐腴則透著愛好美食與烈酒之人的氣派。

column1: 'Tis a foreign ship, m'lud, recently sold to yet another foreigner.
column2: 這是一艘外國船，吾王，近日才又賣給了另一個外邦人。

column1: There are many ships that use this port, m'lud, like the foreign ship behind me that arrived a few days ago.
column2: 有許多船隻使用這個港口，吾王，就像我身後那艘幾天前才抵達的外國船。

column1: The "Conal Cearnach" sails for Dublin, m'lud, in the land of Eire. The "Frastrada" will dock somewhere along the coast of Brittany to deliver supplies for the scholars of Rennes in the Kingdom of the Franks.
column2: 「Conal Cearnach」號啟航前往愛爾蘭之地的都柏林，吾王。「Frastrada」號則會停靠布列塔尼沿岸某處，為法蘭克王國勒恩的學者們運送補給。

column1: The Captain of the "Remus" seeks to reach Rome, but will stop in two Muslim-held ports, Malaga and Tunis.  The "Athene" sails for Thessalonica, seeking also to trade in Malaga and Tunis.
column2: 「Remus」號的船長意欲抵達羅馬，但途中會停靠穆斯林治下的馬拉加與突尼斯兩港。「Athene」號則駛往帖撒羅尼迦，同樣打算在馬拉加與突尼斯進行貿易。

column1: A ship called "Al-Uzza" is bound for the Far East, by way of Malaga, Tunis, and Alexandria, and if God wills, coming at last to distant Gaza.
column2: 一艘名叫「Al-Uzza」的船正駛向遠東，途經馬拉加、突尼斯與亞歷山卓，若上天垂憐，終將抵達遙遠的加薩。

column1: If you care to book passage on any of these, m'lud, I will gladly help you.
column2: 若吾王有意訂下其中任一艘的船位，小人樂意效勞。

column1: I bid you to return later, m'lud, when the ships may be ready to sail.
column2: 還請吾王稍後再來，待船隻備妥啟航之時。

column1: No need to part with it, m'lud.  Being small, it should fit on a ship well enough.
column2: 不必捨棄它，吾王。它體積不大，船上盡夠容納。

column1: I know little about mules, m'lud.
column2: 小人對騾子所知不多，吾王。

column1: Beg pardon, m'lud?
column2: 您說什麼，吾王？

column1: There will not be enough room for your horse, m'lud.
column2: 空間不夠容納您的坐騎，吾王。

column1: Aye, 'tis a fine horse.
column2: 正是，這是匹良駒。

column1: Beg pardon, m'lud?
column2: 您說什麼，吾王？

column1: The fare to Dublin is one silver coin. The fare to Rennes is two silver coins. The fare to Rome is one gold coin. The fare to Thessalonica is two gold coins. The fare to Gaza is three gold coins.
column2: 前往都柏林的船費是一枚銀幣。前往勒恩的船費是兩枚銀幣。前往羅馬的船費是一枚金幣。前往帖撒羅尼迦的船費是兩枚金幣。前往加薩的船費是三枚金幣。

column1: I stand ready to accept your fare, m'lud, upon which I shall direct you to the proper ship.
column2: 小人已備妥收取吾王的船費，收訖之後便為您指引正確的船隻。

column1: Please return later, m'lud, when ships are ready to sail.  Then I will be able to help you book passage.
column2: 請吾王稍後再來，待船隻備妥啟航，屆時小人便能為您訂下船位。

column1: Jerusalem is a city in the desert near the easternmost end of the Mediterranean Sea.
column2: 耶路撒冷是一座位於沙漠中的城市，靠近地中海的最東端。

column1: Eh? Sounds like some foreign word to me.
column2: 嗯？聽起來像是某個外邦詞語。

column1: I know nothing of such things.
column2: 此事小人一概不知。

column1: Of these good knights, I have heard no tale.
column2: 這幾位騎士的事，小人未曾聽聞。

column1: Aye, he took ship from here to the Far East.  He said he had heard tales that made him believe he should seek the Grail in Jerusalem.
column2: 正是，他從此地搭船前往遠東。他說他聽聞的種種傳言，讓他相信該到耶路撒冷尋找聖杯。

column1: There be five ships in port today, m'lud.  They are called the Conal Cearnach, the Frastrada, the Al-Uzza, the Athene and the Remus.
column2: 今日港中共有五艘船，吾王。它們分別喚作 Conal Cearnach、Frastrada、Al-Uzza、Athene 與 Remus。

column1: My name is Rollin' Jack, m'lud.
column2: 小人名叫搖擺傑克，吾王。

column1: Aye, m'lud, it were a hard life what does it to a man.
column2: 正是，吾王，這行當著實艱苦，磨人得很。

column1: The "Conal Cearnach" sails for Dublin, m'lud, in the land of Eire.
column2: 「Conal Cearnach」號啟航前往愛爾蘭之地的都柏林，吾王。

column1: The "Frastrada" will dock somewhere along the coast of Brittany to deliver supplies for the scholars of Rennes in the Kingdom of the Franks.
column2: 「Frastrada」號會停靠布列塔尼沿岸某處，為法蘭克王國勒恩的學者們運送補給。

column1: The Captain of the "Remus" seeks to reach Rome, but will stop in two Muslim-held ports, Malaga and Tunis.
column2: 「Remus」號的船長意欲抵達羅馬，但途中會停靠穆斯林治下的馬拉加與突尼斯兩港。

column1: The "Athene" sails for Thessalonica, seeking also to trade in Malaga and Tunis.
column2: 「Athene」號駛往帖撒羅尼迦，同樣打算在馬拉加與突尼斯進行貿易。

column1: Aye, 'tis fair seas for sailing at this time of year.
column2: 正是，這個時節海象宜人，適合航行。

column1: I be guarding this gangplank, m'lud, while the Captain is ashore.
column2: 小人在此看守這條跳板，吾王，船長此刻正在岸上。

column1: There will be only enough room for you and your mule, m'lud.  I will see that your horse is delivered safely to Camelot, as I did for Sir Galahad when he departed from here some months ago.
column2: 船上只夠容納吾王與您的騾子。小人會確保您的坐騎安全送回肯萊特，正如數月前葛拉漢爵士自此地啟程時，小人為他所做的一樣。

column1: If that suits you, m'lud, you may book passage with me.
column2: 若這安排合吾王之意，便可向小人訂下船位。

column1: Aye, there should be enough room for you as a passenger.   If you seek to travel, you may book passage through me, m'lud.
column2: 正是，作為乘客，空間應是夠用的。吾王若有意遠行，可經由小人訂下船位。

column1: I cannot book a passage for you yet, m'lud.  Return later and I may be able to help you.
column2: 小人此刻還無法為吾王訂下船位。請稍後再來，屆時或能為您效勞。

column1: Aye, 'tis part of a ship, m'lud.
column2: 正是，這是船的一部分，吾王。

column1: Sail?  Did you say sail?  A ship will not get far without one, m'lud.
column2: 帆？您說的是帆嗎？沒有帆，船是走不遠的，吾王。

column1: There are five ships in the port ready to depart.  Their destinations are Dublin, Rennes, Rome, Thessalonica and Gaza.
column2: 港中有五艘船已備妥啟航，目的地分別是都柏林、勒恩、羅馬、帖撒羅尼迦與加薩。

column1: Several ships are in port, but none will be ready to sail again for some days.
column2: 港中雖有幾艘船，但短期內都不會再啟航。

column1: We have had some trouble at the docks.  Drunken brawls amongst the sailors, that sort of thing.
column2: 碼頭這邊出了些麻煩，水手們酗酒鬥毆，諸如此類的事。

column1: The crews will be unfit to sail for days yet.
column2: 船員們這幾天都還不宜出海。

column1: They be ashore in search of grog and women, m'lud.
column2: 他們上岸去找烈酒與女人了，吾王。

column1: You cannot deny the sailors a bit of fun while they are in port, not after months at sea.
column2: 在港停留期間，總不能不讓水手們稍作享樂，畢竟他們才在海上熬了數月。

column1: We have a number of foreign captains in port this day.  They are doing business with the port merchants.
column2: 今日港中有幾位外邦船長，他們正與港口商人洽談生意。

column1: We do a fair business here, m'lud.  Mostly we trade our tin, furs and some weapons, and receive trade goods of many kinds.
column2: 此地生意還算興隆，吾王。我們多以錫、毛皮與一些兵器進行交易，換得各式各樣的貨品。

column1: We commonly trade it to foreign lands, as m'lud surely knows.
column2: 我們常將它與外邦交易，這點吾王想必清楚。

column1: It is just some honey and tin waiting to be loaded onto the proper ship.
column2: 這不過是些等著裝上該去的船的蜂蜜與錫。

column1: The shore is green this time of year.
column2: 這個時節，岸邊一片翠綠。

column1: Aye, there are Vikings around Dublin and Saracen pirates in the Mediterranean.  They are the scourge of honest merchants, m'lord.
column2: 正是，都柏林一帶有維京人，地中海則有撒拉遜海盜，他們是誠實商人的禍害，吾王。

column1: Aye aye, an eye for an eye, say I.
column2: 正是正是，以眼還眼，小人向來這麼說。

column1: Awrr, they are the heathen worshippers of a foreign god, but they rule most of the Mediterranean now, so we must deal with them.
column2: 唉，他們是信奉外邦異神的異教徒，但如今地中海大半為其所據，我們也只得與之往來。

column1: Fearing? I be afeared of nothing but the sea, m'lud.
column2: 害怕？小人這輩子除了大海，什麼都不怕，吾王。

column1: My hearing? Aye, the roar of sea and wind has deafened me a trifle.
column2: 耳朵？正是，海浪與風聲的咆哮，把小人的耳朵震得有些背了。

column1: Pray pardon me, m'lud, but I cannot accept your fare now, until I have a ship on which to book you a passage.  I beg you to return later.
column2: 還請吾王見諒，小人此刻手邊尚無可訂位的船隻，暫不能收下船費。懇請您稍後再來。

column1: For this transaction, it would be better to dismount.
column2: 辦理此事，最好先下馬。

column1: Move closer to the Harbourmaster.
column2: 靠近港務司一些。

column1: Beg pardon, m'lud, but I did not hear you ask for a port of call yet.
column2: 請恕小人失禮，吾王，方才未曾聽見您說要去哪個港口。

column1: If you wish. I am sure the Harbourmaster can help you with that.
column2: 若您有意，港務司想必能幫上忙。

column1: Pardon, m'lud, but that is not a port and no ship sails there.
column2: 恕小人直言，吾王，那並非港口，沒有船隻駛往該處。

column1: Beggin' m'lud's pardon, but I be a trifle hard of hearing. I did not hear where you wished to go.
column2: 請吾王恕罪，小人耳朵有些背，方才沒聽清您想去哪裡。

column1: Eh? Never heard of it.  'Tis some piddling little foreign rathole, I suppose.
column2: 嗯？沒聽過這地方。想必是哪個不入流的外邦小地方吧。

column1: But m'lud has paid nothing that I might refund.
column2: 但吾王並未付過分毫，小人也就無從退還。

column1: As you command, m'lud.  I shall return what you have given me.
column2: 遵命，吾王。小人這便將您所付的奉還。

column1: Others might be surprised to see you here, m'lud, but not I.  Ever since Sir Galahad sailed from here and did not return, I felt another would follow in his steps.
column2: 旁人見您在此，或許會感到訝異，吾王，但小人不會。自葛拉漢爵士自此啟航、一去未歸之後，小人便料想會有人步上他的後塵。

column1: Though little did I suspect it would be our most noble knight and King himself.
column2: 只是小人萬萬沒料到，這人竟會是我們最尊貴的騎士、我們的王親自前來。

column1: If you wish to book passage upon one of them, m'lud, I will take your fare myself, for by your own law every man--even a king--must pay his way.
column2: 吾王若欲訂下其中一艘的船位，小人自當親自收取船費——依您自己所定的律法，人人皆須自付旅費，即便是王也不例外。

column1: If you have come to follow Galahad, m'lud, you have come at a bad time.  Several ships are in port, but none will be ready to sail again for some days.  I suggest you return later.
column2: 吾王若是為了追尋葛拉漢而來，此刻時機不巧。港中雖有幾艘船，但短期內都不會再啟航。小人建議您稍後再來。

column1: Ah, m'lud, your return is most timely.  I have five ships leaving port.  They are sailing for Dublin, Rennes, Rome, Thessalonica and Gaza.
column2: 啊，吾王，您回來得正是時候。小人這裡有五艘船即將啟航，分別駛往都柏林、勒恩、羅馬、帖撒羅尼迦與加薩。

column1: Would you care to book passage upon one of them? By your own law every man--even a king--must pay his way.   I would be pleased to answer any question you may ask about them.
column2: 您可願訂下其中一艘的船位？依您自己所定的律法，人人皆須自付旅費，即便是王也不例外。您若有任何疑問，小人樂意一一為您解答。

column1: Greetings, m'lud.  I fear you have returned too soon.  We have had some trouble at the docks.  Drunken brawls amongst the sailors, that sort of thing.
column2: 見過吾王。恐怕您回來得太早了些。碼頭這邊出了些麻煩，水手們酗酒鬥毆，諸如此類的事。

column1: The crews will be unfit to sail for days yet.  You had best return later.
column2: 船員們這幾天都還不宜出海，您最好稍後再來。

column1: Beggin' m'lud's pardon, but only coin may be collected for fare.
column2: 請吾王恕罪，船費只收錢幣。

column1: Sorry, m'lud, it is already sold.
column2: 抱歉，吾王，這東西已經賣出去了。

column1: I have five ships bound for different parts of the world on which you might book passage.  They sail for Dublin, Rennes, Rome, Thessalonica and Gaza.
column2: 小人這裡有五艘駛向世界各地的船，供您訂位。它們分別前往都柏林、勒恩、羅馬、帖撒羅尼迦與加薩。

column1: If you wish to book passage on one of them, m'lud, I will be most happy to tell you the fare for each.
column2: 吾王若欲訂下其中一艘的船位，小人樂意一一告知各船的船費。

column1: Beggin' m'lud's pardon, but I may accept only coin as the proper fare.
column2: 請吾王恕罪，船費只能以錢幣支付。

column1: No need to part with it, m'lud.  There will be just enough room on the ship for it.
column2: 不必捨棄它，吾王，船上剛好夠容納。

column1: I am not in the mule buying business, m'lud.
column2: 小人不做買騾子的生意，吾王。

column1: Methinks the man is hard of hearing, Arthur.
column2: 依我看，這人耳朵有些背，亞瑟。

column1: It would improper of you to break the seals on merchandise that does not belong to you.
column2: 拆封不屬於你的貨物，這是不妥當的。

column1: Did you not hear, Arthur?  Galahad went to Jerusalem.
column2: 你沒聽見嗎，亞瑟？葛拉漢去了耶路撒冷。

column1: If you want to know about ship destinations, booking passage or fares, you should ask the Harbourmaster about them.
column2: 若想知道船隻的目的地、如何訂位或船費，該去問港務司。

column1: It is fairly calm, indicating light wind.
column2: 海面相當平靜，顯示風勢不大。

column1: Beneath you is the dock.
column2: 你腳下便是碼頭。

column1: Ask the Harbourmaster.
column2: 去問港務司。

column1: It is fully loaded and ready to sail.
column2: 它已裝載完畢，隨時可以啟航。

column1: It has not yet finished with loading and unloading of cargo and supplies.  But the Harbourmaster would know more than I about such things.
column2: 貨物與補給尚未裝卸完畢。不過這類事情，港務司會比我清楚。

column1: A foreign ship is moored along one side of the dock.  Yonder portly fellow is the Harbourmaster, who has authority over all ships that enter and leave Southampton.   Some cargo has been off-loaded from the ship and awaits delivery.
column2: 碼頭一側停泊著一艘外國船。那邊那位體態豐腴的人便是港務司，凡出入南安普頓港的船隻都歸他管轄。船上已卸下一些貨物，正等候運送。

column1: My hearing is excellent, thank you.
column2: 我的耳朵好得很，多謝關心。

column1: It is Greek for "Kristi".
column2: 這是希臘語的「Kristi」。

column1: Peter loves Christy and Christy loves Peter and that is all you need to know.
column2: 彼得愛克莉絲蒂，克莉絲蒂也愛彼得，你只需知道這些就夠了。

column1: His whereabouts are yet unknown.
column2: 他的下落至今仍不明。

column1: Aye, 'tis a mast.   It holds the sail.
column2: 正是，這是桅杆，用來張帆。

column1: The gangplank is in place.  The ship must still be engaged in business.
column2: 跳板還架著，船想必仍在辦事。

column1: It is furled atop the mast.
column2: 它捲收在桅杆頂端。

column1: Perhaps the crews are having a final round of drinks at a local inn before departure.
column2: 船員們或許正在附近的客棧裡，趁啟航前再喝上最後一輪。

column1: He will surely appear once the Harbourmaster decrees the ship is cleared to leave.
column2: 一旦港務司宣布船隻獲准啟航，他必定會現身。

column1: The waves break on the shoreline of Southampton.
column2: 海浪拍打著南安普頓港的岸線。

column1: Aye, a ship has many ropes.
column2: 正是，一艘船上有許多繩索。

column1: Every ship has one.
column2: 每艘船都有一個。

column1: 'Tis not an uncommon practice among foreign seaman to paint an eye upon the prow so that the ship may better see where it is going.
column2: 外邦水手在船首畫上一隻眼睛，好讓船能看清前路，這並非罕見的習俗。

column1: It is a typical merchant ship bringing foreign cargo to trade for British goods such as tin.
column2: 這是一艘典型的商船，載著外邦貨物，前來交換不列顛的錫等物產。

column1: There is a small bit of shelter in the prow, but no cabins.  These ships are built for cargo, not comfort.
column2: 船首有一小塊遮蔽之處，但沒有艙房。這種船是為載貨而造，不是為了舒適。

column1: The ship's stern has a rudder, as might be expected.
column2: 船尾一如預期，裝有舵。

column1: It is, not surprisingly, the shoreline of Southampton.
column2: 不出所料，這正是南安普頓港的岸線。

column1: The clouds do not look threatening and should not delay the ship from sailing.
column2: 這些雲看來並無威脅，應不至於耽誤船隻啟航。

column1: The earthenware pots and jars might contain wax, oil, wine or honey.
column2: 這些陶罐與陶甕裡，或許裝著蠟、油、酒或蜂蜜。

column1: The packets are wrapped in oil cloth and could be any number of common trade items:  spices, furs, cloth, ivory, amber, glass beads, pottery.
column2: 這些包裹以油布包紮，裡頭可能是各式各樣常見的貿易貨品：香料、毛皮、布匹、象牙、琥珀、玻璃珠、陶器。

column1: There are many fish in the sea, Arthur, and seagulls to feast upon them.
column2: 海裡魚多得很，亞瑟，海鷗也樂得飽餐一頓。

column1: The cargo on the dock consists of earthenware pots and jars and some wrapped packets.
column2: 碼頭上的貨物，是些陶罐、陶甕與幾包用布包紮的東西。

column1: Since a goodly portion of your tax revenues come from shipping, I suppose it must be doing well enough.
column2: 既然您稅收有相當一部分來自航運，我想生意想必還算興隆。

column1: Ask the Harbourmaster about that.
column2: 這件事去問港務司吧。

column1: They are ports held by Muslim rulers.
column2: 那些是由穆斯林統治者掌控的港口。

column1: Brittany, or Bretagne, is held by wild and unruly Celtic tribes known as Gauls.
column2: 布列塔尼，法語稱作 Bretagne，是桀驁不馴的凱爾特部族「高盧人」的領地。

column1: Dublin is on the island of Eire.
column2: 都柏林位於愛爾蘭島上。

column1: Rennes is in the land of the Franks, across the channel.
column2: 勒恩位於海峽對岸的法蘭克人之地。

column1: Rome was once the center of the Roman Empire, but the power of this ancient city has much declined.
column2: 羅馬曾是羅馬帝國的中心，但這座古城如今國勢已大不如前。

column1: Thessalonica is in northern Greece, above Athens.
column2: 帖撒羅尼迦位於希臘北部，在雅典以北。

column1: Gaza is at the easternmost end of the Mediterranean Sea.
column2: 加薩位於地中海最東端。

column1: An Irish legend says Conal Cearnach was a prisoner of the Romans in Jerusalem and witnessed the crucifixion of Christ.
column2: 愛爾蘭傳說道，科納爾·柯納赫曾在耶路撒冷淪為羅馬人的階下囚，親眼目睹了基督被釘上十字架。

column1: Frastrada was a wife of Charlemagne, ruler of the Franks.  Rumour said she was a witch from the East.
column2: 芙拉斯特拉妲是法蘭克人統治者查理曼的妻子之一。傳聞她是來自東方的女巫。

column1: The legendary founders of Rome were twin brothers, Remus and Romulus, who were suckled by a she-wolf.
column2: 羅馬傳說中的建城者，是由母狼哺育長大的雙生兄弟——羅慕路斯與雷穆斯。

column1: The powerful Greek Goddess, Athene, is the patroness of sailors.  The city of Athens is named after her.
column2: 強大的希臘女神雅典娜，是水手的守護神。雅典城便是以她之名命名。

column1: The name Al-Uzza, means "Powerful One".  It was the title of an Arabic Goddess associated with the founding of Mohammed's tribe.
column2: Al-Uzza 之名意為「強大者」，是與穆罕默德所屬部族建立淵源的一位阿拉伯女神的稱號。

column1: That is a matter to discuss with the Harbourmaster.
column2: 這件事該找港務司商議。

column1: This is a foreign merchant's ship, not subject to your whim, King Arthur.
column2: 這是一艘外國商船，不受你隨心差遣，亞瑟王。

column1: That is work for sailors, not a warrior-king.
column2: 那是水手的活計，不是戰士之王該做的事。

column1: He is doing his duty and will move only when he should move.  As a king, you must set an example and respect him as master of this port.
column2: 他正在履行職責，該動身時自會動身。身為君王，你必須以身作則，尊重他作為此港之主的身分。

column1: Not a wise idea, Arthur.
column2: 這不是個明智的主意，亞瑟。

column1: Arthur! Do not disgrace yourself by threatening this good man.
column2: 亞瑟！休要威脅這位善良之人，那有失你的體面。

column1: I do not mean to anger you, m'lud, but it is my duty to collect fare before a passenger may board a ship.
column2: 老爺，我無意觸怒您，但收取船資本是我的職責所在，乘客得先付清才能登船。

column1: The purse itself is of no value to him.  And you may yet need it.
column2: 這錢囊本身對他並無用處，而你或許還用得上。

column1: You already did that during your ride here.  No need to do it again now.
column2: 你騎馬前來時已經做過此事，此刻無須再做一次。

column1: That would be absurd.
column2: 那未免太荒謬了。

column1: The sharp tang of salt water mingles with the pungent smell of fish.
column2: 海水的鹹澀氣息與魚腥的刺鼻味道交織在一起。

column1: The wooden ship creaks and bumps against the pier.  Water washes across wood and stone and waves dash upon the shore.  Seagulls cry raucously from above.
column2: 木船嘎吱作響，一次次撞上碼頭。潮水沖刷過木板與石塊，浪花拍打著岸邊。海鷗在頭頂上刺耳地鳴叫著。

column1: You must be on a horse to get off a horse.
column2: 你得先騎在馬上，才能從馬上下來。

column1: Enter destination:
column2: 輸入目的地：

column1: Weary days and nights march on. A storm catches the ship and you are forced to lend your strong back to the efforts of the crew to save themselves.
column2: 疲憊的晝夜一天天過去。一場暴風雨襲上船身，你被迫拿出強健的臂膀，協助船員們奮力自救。

column1: Huge waves crash across the decks. You barely save your mule, but your pack and nearly all your belongings are washed away.
column2: 巨浪不斷打上甲板。你好不容易保住了騾子，行囊與幾乎所有的隨身物品卻都被沖走了。

column1: The next day, the Captain thanks you by giving good advice, "You are not a king in these lands, so do not be quick to draw your sword for you will be surrounded by enemies. Be careful who you trust and never pay bribes with too much coin."
column2: 翌日，船長以一番忠告向你道謝：「在這片土地上，你並非君王，切莫輕易拔劍，否則將四面楚歌。慎選信任之人，行賄時也別出手太闊綽。」

column1: You join the crew in sharing several rounds of wine as they wait for the tide to change so they may enter Gaza port.
column2: 船員們等候潮水轉向以便駛入加薩港時，你也加入他們，一同暢飲了幾巡酒。

column1: The wine flows freely after such a long and arduous journey. Soon, you fall into a very deep, dreamless sleep.
column2: 歷經這段漫長艱辛的旅程，美酒暢流不絕。不久，你便沉入一場無夢的深眠。

column1: The skilled Captain beats past Celtic Brittany with all speed thanks to good winds.
column2: 憑藉著順風之助，經驗老到的船長全速繞過了凱爾特人的布列塔尼。

column1: At Malaga you get your first sight of those who worship Islam.  Their manners and dress are strange to you, yet they are hospitable to any man who worships the one god, no matter by what name he is called.
column2: 在馬拉加，你頭一回見到信奉伊斯蘭教的人。他們的舉止與衣著在你眼中十分陌生，但無論那唯一真神被稱作什麼名字，他們對敬奉祂的人都同樣好客。

column1: In Tunis the worshippers of Allah seem much the same but are ruled instead by the Aghlabid Emirate under the Abbasid Empire.
column2: 在突尼斯，敬奉阿拉的人看來大同小異，只是此地統治者換成了臣屬於阿拔斯帝國的阿格拉布王朝。

column1: As you approach Athens, a corsair filled with Saracen pirates overtakes your ship.
column2: 船隻將近雅典時，一艘滿載撒拉遜海盜的海盜船追上了你們。

column1: You fight like the great warrior you are, but the Saracens are many and merciless. You are finally cut down and thrown to the fish.
column2: 你如身經百戰的偉大戰士般奮力搏殺，但撒拉遜人人多勢眾又冷酷無情。你終究寡不敵眾，倒下後被拋屍餵魚。

column1: A quick voyage brings you to the northern coast of Brittany where you are tragically dashed to death upon jagged rocks.
column2: 一段短暫的航程將你帶到布列塔尼北岸，你卻在那裡不幸撞上嶙峋礁岩，慘遭滅頂。

column1: Many days and nights pass in cramped discomfort.  The coastline of Muslim-held Iberia glides past.
column2: 許多晝夜在侷促難耐中流逝。穆斯林治下的伊比利亞海岸線緩緩掠過眼前。

column1: You land briefly in Tunis, ruled by the Muslims of the Aghlabid Emirate under the Abbasid Empire.  Soon you will reach Rome.
column2: 你在突尼斯短暫靠岸，此地由臣屬阿拔斯帝國的阿格拉布王朝穆斯林統治。不久你便將抵達羅馬。

column1: Approaching Rome, your ship is caught in a powerful storm. You are washed overboard and your armour quickly drags you to the bottom of the sea.
column2: 船隻將近羅馬時，遭遇一場猛烈的暴風雨。你被捲落海中，一身盔甲迅速將你拖向海底。

column1: Captain beats his way expertly up St. George's Channel toward Dublin.
column2: 船長熟練地引領船隻，逆流而上駛過聖喬治海峽，朝都柏林前進。

column1: Alas, a longship of crazed Vikings falls upon the ship.  Excaliber sings from its sheath and does mighty work.  The decks run red, but you are overwhelmed and killed in combat with a berserker.
column2: 唉，一艘滿載瘋狂維京人的長船撲上船來。聖劍出鞘鏗鏘作響，大顯神威。甲板血染一片，但你終究寡不敵眾，命喪一名狂戰士之手。

column1: Oh, no, this mukhtar is an evil man and would make you a slave.  He must not find you.
column2: 噢，不好，這位村長是個惡人，會把你賣去為奴。絕不能讓他發現你。

column1: Oh, sir, I could not keep her.  And you will need her for your journey.
column2: 噢，大人，我不能留下牠。您這趟旅程還用得著牠呢。

column1: I am not allowed to accept gifts, sir, except from my Master.
column2: 大人，我不得收受餽贈，除非是我主人給的。

column1: I am not allowed to accept gifts for doing my duty, sir.
column2: 大人，我不得因盡本分而收受餽贈。

column1: You cannot seek it in Gaza, sir, or the mukhtar will imprison you.  Perhaps my Master can help you with this problem.
column2: 大人，您不能在加薩尋訪此事，否則村長會將您下獄。或許我主人能助您解決這個難題。

column1: I have never been anywhere but Gaza, but my Master can surely answer you.
column2: 我除了加薩之外哪裡都沒去過，但我主人必定能回答您。

column1: It is true my Master is poor, but he is a good man and he knows so many things.  And while you speak with Al-Sirat, I can care for your poor mule after her long sea journey.
column2: 我主人確實貧窮，但他是個好人，懂得的事情極多。您與 Al-Sirat 交談之時，我可以照料您那頭長途航行後疲憊的騾子。

column1: Please do not delay long, sir.  Gaza is no longer safe for foreigners and no man here will aid you in any way except my Master.
column2: 大人，請莫要耽擱太久。加薩對外地人來說已不再安全，此地除了我主人之外，沒有人會出手相助。

column1: Sa'alam aleikem.  Peace be unto you.
column2: Sa'alam aleikem，祝你平安。

column1: He is a young boy, poor but healthy, with an open, honest face and intelligence in his eyes.
column2: 他是個年幼的男孩，雖然窮困卻很健康，面容坦率誠懇，眼神透著聰慧。

column1: Please come and ask my Master.  He knows so much more than I.
column2: 請隨我去問問我主人，他懂得的遠比我多。

column1: Al-Sirat will know.  He is the most learned of men.
column2: Al-Sirat 必定知曉，他是天底下最有學問的人。

column1: He did not choose to visit my Master, but hurried off into the desert alone.
column2: 他沒有選擇去拜訪我主人，而是獨自匆匆奔進了沙漠。

column1: Sir, my Master is the wisest man in the whole world.  He can answer any question.  Please, let us go to him.
column2: 大人，我主人是全世界最有智慧的人，任何問題他都答得出來。請隨我去見他吧。

column1: Ignore the brat and let us do business.  The mukhtar could have spies about, so we should act quickly.  You have no pack, I see, and no waterskin.  You can buy nothing in Gaza without being arrested.
column2: 別理那小鬼，咱們談正事吧。村長恐怕布有眼線，我們得盡快行動。我瞧您沒有行囊，也沒有水袋。在加薩，您買什麼都會被逮捕。

column1: Therefore, you must surely hire me to take you through the desert and lead you from one waterhole to the next. That is the only way you will reach Jerusalem alive.
column2: 因此，您勢必得雇我帶您穿越沙漠，領您從一處水坑走到下一處水坑。唯有如此，您才能活著抵達耶路撒冷。

column1: You want to avoid the mukhtar.  I give you good advice.  Trust me in all things.
column2: 您想避開村長，我這是給您的良言。凡事都信我便是。

column1: No man in Gaza will deal with you because of the mukhtar's edicts.  If you are spotted by his men, you will be arrested.
column2: 因為村長的禁令，加薩沒有人敢與您打交道。若被他的人瞧見，您便會被逮捕。

column1: Most generous, habib.  She will make a fine payment for being your guide, if you let me take you to Jerusalem.
column2: 真慷慨啊，朋友。若您讓我帶您前往耶路撒冷，牠便是上好的嚮導酬勞。

column1: An odd looking trinket, but of no interest to me.
column2: 這件小玩意兒模樣古怪，但我沒興趣。

column1: I am content to wait until I bring you safely to Jerusalem to receive my reward.
column2: 我甘願等到平安帶您抵達耶路撒冷後，再收取酬勞。

column1: Trust me in all things.  Only I know the secret paths of the desert and where to find water.  Only I can guide you safely through.
column2: 凡事都信我便是。唯有我知曉沙漠中的密徑與水源何在，也唯有我能領您安然穿越。

column1: He looks a dry and hard man, as one might look from a lifetime in harsh deserts.
column2: 他看起來乾瘦而剛硬，正是在嚴酷沙漠中度過一生之人的模樣。

column1: Ignore the brat and let us do business.
column2: 別理那小鬼，咱們談正事吧。

column1: He is an impoverished old scholar.  Do not waste your time with him.
column2: 他不過是個窮困潦倒的老學究，別在他身上浪費時間。

column1: Never heard of it.
column2: 從未聽聞。

column1: Trust me in all things.  I can lead you safely to all waterholes and wadis.
column2: 凡事都信我便是。我能領您安然抵達每一處水坑與旱谷。

column1: There was another like you, but he was gone from here before I could offer my services.
column2: 之前也有個像您這樣的人來過，但我還沒來得及自薦，他就已經離開此地了。

column1: If you must ask questions, let us at least get started on the trip and talk later.
column2: 您若非問不可，咱們至少先上路，有話待會兒再說。

column1: It is an old tower on a spit of land.
column2: 那是一座建在沙嘴上的古塔。

column1: The sail was carefully repaired after the storm.
column2: 風暴過後，船帆已細心修補過了。

column1: By my beard, you must know every plank of the ship by now, having been aboard for weeks.
column2: 憑我這把鬍子起誓，您在船上待了數週，想必連每一塊船板都認熟了。

column1: Though the mule is here, she looks even more unhappy than when you started this trip.
column2: 騾子雖然在這兒，但牠看起來比啟程時還要更不高興。

column1: The rocks alongside the dock are slippery.  Avoid them.
column2: 碼頭邊的岩石很滑，須避開。

column1: This is one of the stone docks at Gaza port.
column2: 這是加薩港的一座石造碼頭。

column1: I would strongly advise you to heed this boy.
column2: 我強烈建議您聽從這孩子的話。

column1: I would advise you to remember the advice the Captain offered you during the voyage.
column2: 我建議您記住船長在航程中給您的忠告。

column1: It is not clear what you want.  Try to be more specific.
column2: 看不出你想要什麼，說得再明確些。

column1: I suspect that no matter how hard you look, you will not find Al-Sirat or Hazm again.
column2: 我猜想，無論你如何搜尋，都不會再找到 Al-Sirat 或哈慈了。

column1: You should have paid more attention to Hazm.  You would undoubtedly know a great deal more than you do now.
column2: 你當初該多留意哈慈的話。如此一來，你此刻懂得的必定遠比現在多。

column1: There is no guide here.  You are on your own.
column2: 這裡沒有嚮導，你只能靠自己了。

column1: From what we have heard, the mukhtar is the last man you wish to find.  Or to have find you.  You should dally here no longer.
column2: 據我們所聞，村長正是你最不想遇見的人——也最不想被他找到。你不該再在此逗留。

column1: You will have to make do with what you have or can find.
column2: 你只能將就手邊擁有或能找到的東西了。

column1: You should be well and truly sick of this ship by now.
column2: 此刻你想必早已對這艘船厭煩透頂了。

column1: It seems I must warn you often that such violent urges against those who have done you no wrong will stain your soul and make you unworthy of the Grail.
column2: 看來我得常常提醒你：對無辜之人動用如此暴戾的衝動，將玷污你的靈魂，使你不配獲得聖杯。

column1: Unfortunately, you lost nearly everything when the storm washed your pack overboard.
column2: 很不幸，那場暴風雨把你的行囊沖落海中，你幾乎失去了一切。

column1: All seaports share similar odors, mainly the tang of salt and fish.
column2: 所有海港氣味都大同小異，主要是海鹽與魚腥的味道。

column1: It has been emptied.  Do not waste your time.
column2: 裡頭已經空了，別浪費時間。

column1: Thank you, sir, but I cannot accept money.  My reward is serving my Master well.
column2: 謝謝您，大人，但我不能收下錢財。好好侍奉我主人，便是我的酬報。

column1: You have no business doing so.
column2: 你沒有理由這麼做。

column1: It would appear that you slept through the entire unloading of the ship.  Even the crew is gone.
column2: 看來你把整段卸貨的過程都睡過去了，如今連船員都已離去。

column1: Before you lies the sun-baked village of Gaza.  Beyond the town lie hills, and beyond them is the desert.
column2: 眼前是烈日曝曬下的加薩村落，村落之外是丘陵，丘陵之外便是沙漠。

column1: The land rises in rocky hills to the east.
column2: 東邊的地勢隆起，盡是嶙峋的丘陵。

column1: Only Hazm could have shown you the way.  You should have followed him when you had the chance.
column2: 唯有哈慈能為你指路。有機會時，你就該跟著他走。

column1: I presume he is with his Master.
column2: 我猜他是跟主人在一起。

column1: It is now quite empty.
column2: 如今已空無一物。

column1: It has been removed.
column2: 已被移走。

column1: It is made of stone, part of an old fortification.
column2: 這是石造的，屬於一座古老防禦工事的一部分。

column1: It is built of stone, solid and functional.
column2: 以石塊建成，堅固而實用。

column1: You have been looking at the waves for week upon weary week.  There is nothing new to see.
column2: 你已經望著這片波浪看了一個又一個疲憊的星期，沒什麼新鮮事可看了。

column1: At this moment, everything you possess is upon your person, except for your mule.
column2: 此刻，除了那頭騾子，你所擁有的一切都在你身上。

column1: Aye, 'tis a mast.  It holds the sail.
column2: 正是，那是桅杆，用來撐起船帆。

column1: Aye, it connects the ship to the dock.
column2: 正是，它將船與碼頭相連。

column1: It looks the same as it has for weeks.
column2: 看起來和這幾週以來一模一樣。

column1: They are gone.
column2: 他們已經離去。

column1: He is gone.
column2: 他已經離去。

column1: It has a rudder, as might be expected.
column2: 不出所料，它裝有一具船舵。

column1: There is a tower on a spit of land and other hills in the distance in one direction, and the town of Gaza in the other.
column2: 一邊是沙嘴上的塔樓與遠方隱約的丘陵，另一邊則是加薩鎮。

column1: It is not much to look at it.  Poor dwellings, empty streets, much dirt and an air of hostility.
column2: 這裡沒什麼好看的。破舊的屋舍、空盪的街道、遍地塵土，還瀰漫著一股敵意。

column1: Aye, they are pleasant enough, as clouds go.
column2: 是啊，就雲朵而言，它們看起來還算宜人。

column1: It is a valley cut into the earth by running water. Sometimes a wadi will still have water, but often they are dry.
column2: 那是一道被流水切鑿而成的谷地。旱谷有時仍存有水，但多半是乾涸的。

column1: I have much book knowledge, but I cannot guide you step by step to a place where I have never been.
column2: 我雖飽讀詩書，卻無法一步步引領你前往一個我從未去過的地方。

column1: You are the wisest of men, sir, except for my Master!  Please follow me.
column2: 大人，您是天下最有智慧的人——僅次於我主人！請隨我來。

column1: The desert lies ahead.  You will never cross it without my help.
column2: 沙漠就在前方。沒有我的幫助，你絕不可能穿越它。

column1: You need not pay now, but I could not insult your generosity by refusing.  Let us set out at once!
column2: 您現在無須付錢，但拒絕您的慷慨對我而言未免失禮。咱們這就啟程吧！

column1: Excellent!  Let us waste no time! Follow me.
column2: 太好了！咱們別浪費時間了，跟我來。

column1: Oh, sir!  I am so happy you have returned!
column2: 噢，大人！您回來了，我真是太高興了！

column1: Please, will you come with me now and accept the hospitality of my Master, Al-Sirat?
column2: 請問，您現在願意隨我同去，接受我主人 Al-Sirat 的款待嗎？

column1: Al-Sirat is only poor in worldly goods, but in knowledge and wisdom he is the richest man on earth!
column2: Al-Sirat 雖然家財微薄，但論知識與智慧，他卻是天底下最富有的人！

column1: If you change your mind, sir, I will still gladly lead you to him.  But I must return to him soon, either with or without you.
column2: 大人，您若改變心意，我仍樂意領您去見他。但無論您是否同行，我都得儘快回到他身邊。

column1: You are the wisest of men, sir, except for my Master!   Please follow me.
column2: 大人，您是天下最有智慧的人——僅次於我主人！請隨我來。

column1: Your armour and steel drag you to the bottom and there you will lie until you are rotten, soggy and pulpy and truly forgotten.
column2: 你的盔甲與鋼鐵把你拖向海底，你將長眠於此，直到腐朽、泡爛、化為一團爛泥，徹底被世人遺忘。

column1: You should not think of returning to Gaza, Arthur.  If the mukhtar's men find you, it will mean your life.
column2: 亞瑟，你不該考慮回加薩去。若被村長的人發現，你將性命不保。

column1: A pity.  You are so young to die.  Well, we may yet meet again, in case you change your mind.
column2: 可惜了，你這般年輕便要喪命。罷了，若你改變心意，咱們或許還能再見。

column1: He does not answer.
column2: 他沒有回應。

column1: He could never hear you from here.
column2: 他在這裡絕不可能聽見你的聲音。

column1: You should have returned directly to Jerusalem.  There is no hope for you now.
column2: 你早該直接返回耶路撒冷才是，如今已是回天乏術。

column1: Gaza is unsafe.  Jerusalem lies somewhere beyond the desert.  Your choices are limited and filled with danger at every step.  Go with caution.
column2: 加薩並不安全。耶路撒冷就在沙漠的另一端。你的選擇不多，且步步驚險，務必謹慎而行。

column1: You have safely left Gaza behind, but the desert lies ahead.  You will never cross it without my help.
column2: 你已安然離開加薩，但前方是茫茫沙漠。少了我的幫助，你絕無可能穿越它。

column1: I am a man of the desert, not of the sea.
column2: 我是沙漠之子，不是海上之人。

column1: Hire me, and I will lead you safely to water.  Trust me in all things.
column2: 雇用我，我必領你安然尋得水源。凡事都要信任我。

column1: I urge you once more to hire me as your guide through the desert.  Only I can show you where the hidden water lies.
column2: 我再次懇請你雇我為沙漠嚮導。唯有我知曉隱藏水源的所在。

column1: He is a useless pest.
column2: 他不過是個沒用的討厭鬼。

column1: He is an old fraud.
column2: 他是個老騙子。

column1: It is just an old tower.
column2: 那不過是座舊塔。

column1: If you must ask questions, you might at least hire me as your guide.
column2: 你若非問不可，倒不如先雇我當你的嚮導。

column1: I do not know what folly brought you back here to the hill above Gaza.  I fear you are doomed.
column2: 我不知是什麼糊塗念頭又把你帶回加薩上方這座山丘。恐怕你在劫難逃了。

column1: From this hard-earned height above Gaza you can see far across the sea and over the village.  But ahead of you lies a searing and treacherous desert to cross.
column2: 從加薩上方這座你辛苦爬上的高地望去，能遠眺大海與村落。但橫在你前方的，是一片酷熱而險惡、必須橫越的沙漠。

column1: I do not think you will see Hazm ever again.
column2: 我想你再也見不到哈慈了。

column1: Undoubtedly he hurried back to his master, as instructed.
column2: 他想必已依吩咐，匆匆趕回主人身邊。

column1: There is a slim chance he might be on the dock where you left him.
column2: 他仍有一絲可能留在你與他分別的碼頭。

column1: Al-Sirat's enclosure is hidden somewhere in the hillside below.  You would never find it again without Hazm.
column2: Al-Sirat 的居所就藏在下方的山坡某處。少了哈慈，你絕不可能再找到它。

column1: You had your chance when Hazm offered to take you to the scholar.  Now it may be too late.
column2: 哈慈曾提議帶你去見那位學者，你當時本有機會。如今恐怕為時已晚。

column1: You can barely make out the ship, let alone any other detail, from this distance.
column2: 從這個距離，你僅能勉強辨出那艘船的輪廓，更別提其他細節了。

column1: It may be the ship you came on still in port, or another ship entirely.  It matters not.
column2: 那或許是載你來的那艘船仍泊在港中，也或許是另一艘船。這都無關緊要。

column1: From this height above Gaza, the ship on which you spent so many weary weeks looks like a mere toy.
column2: 從加薩上方這處高地望去，那艘曾載你度過數週艱辛航程的船，看來不過像個玩具。

column1: You saw the stone tower when you disembarked.  It looked abandoned.
column2: 你下船時曾見過那座石塔，看來已遭棄置。

column1: The town of Gaza occupies the shoreline.
column2: 加薩城座落於這片海岸線上。

column1: From this hard-earned height above Gaza you can see far across the sea and over the village.
column2: 從加薩上方這座你辛苦爬上的高地望去，能遠眺大海與村落。

column1: The sea looks lovely from here.
column2: 從這裡望去，大海景色怡人。

column1: Aye, a most impressive looking bank of clouds.
column2: 正是，那片雲堤景象著實壯觀。

column1: You dare not look long at the glaring sun.
column2: 你不敢直視那刺目的驕陽太久。

column1: Cross?  Ah, you refer to the mast and furled sail of the ship down at the dock.
column2: 十字？啊，你說的是碼頭那艘船上的桅杆與收捲的船帆吧。

column1: Why do you refuse to listen to good advice?
column2: 你為何執意不聽良言？

column1: From here you can go either into the desert or back the way you came.
column2: 從這裡，你可以走入沙漠，也可以循原路折返。

column1: Follow me and I will lead you free of the cliffs.
column2: 跟著我，我會領你脫離這片峭壁。

column1: In this heat, you must waste no breath upon idle chatter.
column2: 在這等酷熱之中，你可耗不起力氣閒聊。

column1: Arthur, Arthur, why are you here?.  You should be back in Jerusalem by now.
column2: 亞瑟，亞瑟，你怎會在這裡？此刻你早該回到耶路撒冷了。

column1: This area is enclosed by cliffs.  There are but two openings...back to the ridge overlooking Gaza or into the desert.
column2: 這片區域四面為峭壁所困，僅有兩處出口……一是回到俯瞰加薩的山脊，一是通往沙漠。

column1: The cliffs are formidably high.
column2: 這片峭壁高聳得駭人。

column1: This way, habib.  Follow me.
column2: 這邊走，朋友，跟著我。

column1: Where are you going?  Follow me!
column2: 你要去哪裡？跟著我！

column1: It is too deeply buried.
column2: 它埋得太深了。

column1: The markings on the ancient pillar have been obliterated with the passage of time.
column2: 這根古柱上的刻痕，已被歲月磨蝕殆盡。

column1: Your way is blocked upon one side by cliffs.  The rest upon all sides is desert.
column2: 你的一側被峭壁擋住去路，其餘各面盡是沙漠。

column1: The high cliffs continue to one side of you.
column2: 高聳的峭壁在你一側延展而去。

column1: It appears to be a chunk of very ancient pillar, partially buried.
column2: 看來是一截極為古老的石柱殘塊，半埋於地下。

column1: Now that you have trudged far from the city walls, what have you to show for it?  Nothing.  You are lost in the blistering desert without water once again.
column2: 如今你已跋涉遠離城牆，可有什麼收穫？什麼也沒有。你再度迷失在這片酷熱的沙漠之中，滴水全無。

column1: Good, you are here.  But stay close behind me or you may get lost.
column2: 好，你來了。但要緊跟在我身後，否則你會迷路的。

column1: This way, habib.  We must go directly to the water.
column2: 這邊走，朋友，我們得直奔水源。

column1: Beware!  Ahead of you is only vast and open desert.  This is no time to get lost.
column2: 小心！你前方只有遼闊無垠的沙漠。此刻絕不是迷路的時候。

column1: There are rocks, barren ground and sand, and a vast array of desert stretching out in all directions, save for the way you came.
column2: 四周盡是岩石、荒地與黃沙，除了你來時的方向，沙漠向四面八方無盡延展。

column1: There are rocks, barren ground and sand, and a vast array of desert stretching out in all directions.
column2: 四周盡是岩石、荒地與黃沙，沙漠向四面八方無盡延展。

column1: Below you - and a lethal fall from here, I might add - is a long pool of fresh water.
column2: 你的下方——容我補一句，這一摔可是必死無疑——有一泓狹長的淡水池。

column1: I suspect I should know what this place is.  If you investigate further it may come to me.
column2: 我猜我該認得這個地方。你若再仔細查探，或許我就能想起來。

column1: The girl and her jug have vanished over the hill.
column2: 那女孩與她的水罐，已消失在山丘的另一頭。

column1: If you refer to Fatima, it would seem she had a lesson to teach you.  Next time, heed her words more closely.
column2: 你若說的是法提瑪，看來她是想教你一課。下回，把她的話聽得更仔細些。

column1: It appears dark and empty inside.
column2: 裡頭看來一片漆黑，空無一物。

column1: Below you is an enticing pool of water.
column2: 你的下方，有一泓誘人的水池。

column1: The platform around the pit is made of stone.
column2: 坑洞四周的平台以石塊砌成。

column1: You are babbling, Arthur.
column2: 你在胡言亂語了，亞瑟。

column1: He was so anxious for you to follow him, he did not wait to speak further with you.
column2: 他一心急著要你跟上，等不及再與你多說什麼。

column1: You swallowed a great deal of water when you landed in the aqueduct.  But if you want more, now is the time to do it.
column2: 你墜入水道時已嗆下不少水。但你若還想再喝，此刻正是時候。

column1: A fine idea, but you will not do it from up here.
column2: 好主意，但你在這上頭可辦不到。

column1: You will have to find it, first.
column2: 你得先找到它才行。

column1: I see nothing like that here.
column2: 此處我沒見著那樣的東西。

column1: The dates have all been harvested from the palm.
column2: 這棵椰棗樹上的果實已被採收殆盡。

column1: They will not soothe your thirst.  You should rather look for the source of their water.
column2: 它們解不了你的渴。你該去找的是它們水分的源頭。

column1: The aloe is not for eating and the dates have all been harvested from the palm.
column2: 蘆薈不能吃，椰棗樹上的果實也已被採收一空。

column1: The mule knows better than you what she should eat.
column2: 這頭騾子比你更清楚自己該吃什麼。

column1: You no longer have your mule.
column2: 你已不再有那頭騾子了。

column1: She has run away, Arthur.
column2: 牠跑掉了，亞瑟。

column1: Dear me.  The heat has affected you most severely.
column2: 天哪，這酷熱已把你折騰得不輕。

column1: You should remember the way back to Jerusalem from here.
column2: 從這裡，你應當記得回耶路撒冷的路。

column1: There is a building and a stone platform over a deep walled pit in the ground, and steps leading down into it.
column2: 地上有一座建築與一座石砌平台，架在一口以石壁圍砌的深坑之上，並有階梯通往坑底。

column1: There are some date palms, aloe vera and other plants nearby.
column2: 附近有幾株椰棗樹、蘆薈與其他植物。

column1: The building appears dark and empty inside.
column2: 這座建築內部看來一片漆黑，空無一物。

column1: It is a puzzling arch for it seems to serve no purpose.  It does not even span the pit next to it.
column2: 這座拱門令人費解，似乎毫無用處，甚至連旁邊的坑洞都跨不過去。

column1: It is very old and appears to be no longer in use.
column2: 它十分古老，看來早已棄置不用。

column1: The pit is lined with stone walls.
column2: 這口坑洞內壁以石塊砌成。

column1: It is deep and walled with stone.
column2: 它既深，四壁又以石塊砌成。

column1: Up the steep slope to the north lies Jerusalem, as you know now.
column2: 沿著北方的陡坡而上，便是耶路撒冷——這你現在已經知道了。

column1: There is a steep slope to the north which blocks any view down here of what lies in that direction, and a large hill rises above this walled pit.
column2: 北方有一道陡坡，擋住了那個方向的視野，一座大山丘則聳立於這口石壁深坑之上。

column1: Directly above and behind the walled pit there is a large hill.
column2: 就在這口石壁深坑的正上方與後方，有一座大山丘。

column1: Stairs lead down to the pool.
column2: 階梯通往水池底部。

column1: There are narrow stone stairs to the stone platform and stairs going down in one corner of the pit.
column2: 有一道狹窄的石階通往石砌平台，坑洞一角也有階梯往下延伸。

column1: As you know, you are at the Pool of Siloam.
column2: 如你所知，你正身處西羅亞池。

column1: It is a long, narrow pool filled with glorious, fresh water.
column2: 這是一泓狹長的水池，滿盈著清澈甘美的淡水。

column1: The presence of plants is a hopeful sign.
column2: 植物的存在，是個令人振奮的徵兆。

column1: The Pool in this walled pit is filled with fresh water, as good as any wadi or oasis.
column2: 這口石壁深坑中的水池滿是淡水，不遜於任何旱谷或綠洲。

column1: She found you most frightening and wanted nothing to do with you.
column2: 她被你嚇得不輕，再也不想跟你有任何瓜葛。

column1: There is no girl here.  You are suffering from delusions.
column2: 這裡沒有什麼女孩。你是在產生幻覺。

column1: He has not returned.  Perhaps he waits for you elsewhere.
column2: 他還沒回來。或許他正在別處等你。

column1: They are spirits, either good or bad, which can appear in either human or animal form.
column2: 牠們是精靈，有善有惡，能化作人形或獸形現身。

column1: The sweet water of the Pool of Siloam has quenched your thirst for now.
column2: 西羅亞池的甘美泉水，暫時解了你的渴。

column1: Only water will quench your burning thirst.
column2: 唯有清水，能解你那如火焚燒般的乾渴。

column1: There are some date palms whose dates have been harvested.
column2: 這裡有幾株椰棗樹，果實已被採收。

column1: There are some aloe vera plants and other plants that I do not know.
column2: 這裡有幾株蘆薈，還有些我不認得的植物。

column1: There are narrow stone stairs between the stone platform and the desert.
column2: 石砌平台與沙漠之間，有一道狹窄的石階相連。

column1: Steps lead down to an enticing pool of water.
column2: 階梯向下通往一泓誘人的水池。

column1: Steps lead down into a deep walled pit in the ground.
column2: 階梯向下通往地面上一口石壁深坑。

column1: There is a deep walled pit in the ground, and steps leading down into it.
column2: 地上有一口石壁深坑，並有階梯通往坑底。

column1: You have seen enough of this tunnel for now.
column2: 這條隧道，你此刻已看得夠多了。

column1: The tunnel is quite small and soon becomes pitch black inside.
column2: 這條隧道相當狹小，往裡走沒多久便是一片漆黑。

column1: The water is not very deep.
column2: 這裡的水不算深。

column1: The ground is paved with stone.
column2: 地面以石塊鋪成。

column1: You are once more at the Pool of Siloam.  The hike back to Jerusalem awaits you.
column2: 你又再度回到了西羅亞池。回耶路撒冷的路途，還等著你去走。

column1: The walls and ground are paved with stone.  The water flows from a tunnel carved into the rock of the hill above it.
column2: 四壁與地面皆以石塊鋪成。池水源自上方山壁鑿出的一條隧道。

column1: Wait!  At last I know where you are.  This is the Pool of Siloam.
column2: 等等！我終於認出你身在何處了。這裡是西羅亞池。

column1: The pool is enclosed upon four sides by stone walls.  In one wall there is a tunnel opening.
column2: 這座水池四面皆為石壁環繞，其中一面石壁上有隧道開口。

column1: There are some aloe plants around the outside of the Pool's upper platform.
column2: 水池上方平台的外緣，長著幾株蘆薈。

column1: There are sections of old tumbled-down wall on the platform above the Pool.
column2: 水池上方的平台上，散落著幾段傾頹的舊牆殘壁。

column1: There is a large hill through which the aqueduct is carved.
column2: 這條水道正是穿鑿一座大山丘而成。

column1: The tunnel is known as Hezekiah's Aqueduct.
column2: 這條隧道名為希西家水道。

column1: I doubt your mule would have attempted those narrow stone stairs had she not been so desperate for water.
column2: 我懷疑，若非渴水渴得走投無路，你那頭騾子絕不會嘗試走上那道狹窄的石階。

column1: There is one set of narrow stone stairs.
column2: 這裡有一道狹窄的石階。

column1: The niche is empty.
column2: 這處壁龕空無一物。

column1: Your mule delights in the fresh water and is ready to go on.
column2: 你的騾子暢飲清水，樂不可支，已準備好繼續上路。

column1: It is pure and cold, flowing through the aqueduct from the Spring of Gihon.
column2: 池水純淨清冽，經水道從基訓泉流淌而來。

column1: Your mule certainly seems to enjoy it.
column2: 你的騾子看來確實喝得暢快。

column1: The sun burns no less fiercely overhead, though this cool pit provides some relief.
column2: 頭頂驕陽依舊灼人，不過這口陰涼的深坑倒能稍解暑氣。

column1: Upon one side are tall cliffs.  Upon the other side, open desert.
column2: 一側是高聳的峭壁，另一側則是遼闊的沙漠。

column1: Tall cliffs block you on one side.
column2: 高聳的峭壁擋住了你一側的去路。

column1: Come, the water is not much farther.
column2: 來吧，水源已經不遠了。

column1: The cliffs end and a huge, flat expanse of searing desert opens out before you.
column2: 峭壁到此為止，一片廣袤平坦、酷熱難當的沙漠在你眼前展開。

column1: The water looks and smells most inviting.  I am surprised your mule has not drunk from it yet.
column2: 這水看來、聞來都十分誘人。你那頭騾子居然還沒喝，倒教我意外。

column1: It is a naturally formed pool, fed by a small stream flowing down a wadi to the east.
column2: 這是一處天然形成的水池，由東邊一道旱谷流下的小溪注入。

column1: Worry not about me, habib.  But please, you need water.  I beg you to have a drink.
column2: 別擔心我，朋友。但求求你，你需要水，懇請你喝上一口。

column1: This is neither the time nor place.
column2: 此時此地都不合適。

column1: You certainly could use a drink.  And the closest water is that pool.
column2: 你確實需要喝點水。而最近的水源，就是那座水池。

column1: Nonsense.  You can barely carry what you have in this heat.
column2: 胡說。這等酷熱之下，你連身上帶的東西都快扛不住了。

column1: Nay, I do not advise it.  They are unknown and could be dangerous.
column2: 不可，我不建議這麼做。這些東西來歷不明，可能有危險。

column1: There is nothing but sand.
column2: 這裡除了黃沙，什麼也沒有。

column1: You sound parched.  Wet your throat and ease your burning thirst.  Please, drink your fill.
column2: 聽你的聲音已乾渴難耐。潤潤喉，解解你這如焚的乾渴吧。請盡情暢飲。

column1: As you see, there is water in this wadi.  Drink your fill.
column2: 如你所見，這道旱谷中有水。盡情暢飲吧。

column1: It is a perfectly good pool.  Drink your fill.
column2: 這是一泓上好的水池。盡情暢飲吧。

column1: Your mule is a stupid animal.  It does not even have the sense to drink when there is water.
column2: 你的騾子是頭蠢貨。連有水可喝都不懂得喝。

column1: you have no mule, habib, and neither do I.
column2: 你沒有騾子，朋友，我也沒有。

column1: Eh?  It is nothing.  A camel I once owned, that is all.
column2: 嗯？沒什麼。不過是我曾養過的一頭駱駝罷了。

column1: See how beautifully the pool reflects all around it.  Surely you will wait no longer to drink from it.
column2: 瞧這水池映著四周景致，多麼美。你想必不會再猶豫，這就喝上一口吧。

column1: Jabir is very eager for you to drink, yet insists you drink first.  What do your own instincts tell you?
column2: 賈比耳一心盼你喝下這水，卻堅持要你先喝。你自己的直覺告訴你什麼？

column1: Perhaps your mule is merely too stupefied to drink.  Perhaps the camel died of old age or injury.
column2: 或許你的騾子只是呆得不懂得喝水。又或許那駱駝是因年邁或傷病而死。

column1: Perhaps the camel died of old age or injury.
column2: 或許那駱駝是因年邁或傷病而死。

column1: You have a choice between this naturally formed pool and the other pool nearby.  Your own instincts must guide you.
column2: 你可以在這座天然水池與附近的另一座水池之間選擇。你得憑自己的直覺判斷。

column1: You need water, but you must rely upon your own instincts to make a decision.
column2: 你需要水，但這決定得靠你自己的直覺。

column1: If you wish to use your sword, Arthur, stand on dry land.
column2: 亞瑟，你若要拔劍，得先站上乾地。

column1: There is a natural pool of water, surrounded by cliffs and flowing down through a ravine.  Some plants grow here.
column2: 這是一座天然水池，四周崖壁環繞，水順著一道溝壑流下。這裡長著些植物。

column1: There is also a camel's skeleton.
column2: 這裡還有一具駱駝的骸骨。

column1: Cliffs hide this wadi quite well, and the water flows down from a deep cleft in the ground.
column2: 崖壁把這條乾谷藏得極隱密，水便是從地面一道深裂縫中流下來的。

column1: They are strange plants.  I cannot identify them.  Nor do I like the look of them.  They have an odd colour.
column2: 這些是些怪異的植物，我認不出是什麼，也不喜歡它們的模樣。顏色透著古怪。

column1: The reflections are almost entrancing.
column2: 這倒影幾乎令人看得出神。

column1: Aye, 'tis odd that your mule shows no desire for this water when she is clearly quite thirsty.
column2: 正是，你的騾子明明渴得很，卻對這水毫無興致，著實古怪。

column1: The skeleton could be nothing else save a camel.  It must have died here some time ago.
column2: 這副骸骨除了駱駝不作他想。想必是很久以前死在此地的。

column1: There are fleas and lice, drying blood and a ripe smell.  There is nothing of any worth.
column2: 這裡有跳蚤與蝨子、乾涸的血跡與陣陣腥臭，沒有一樣值得留意的東西。

column1: We are very close to the pool where this water collects.  Follow me.
column2: 我們離水匯聚成池的地方不遠了，跟我來。

column1: This trickle of water in the wadi flows into a pool further down.  That is where we wish to go.
column2: 這條乾谷裡的細流會匯入下游的一座水池，那正是我們要去的地方。

column1: There is a pool at the end of this wadi.  Follow me.
column2: 這條乾谷的盡頭有座水池，跟我來。

column1: We must not waste time with idle chatter, habib.  You must come with me.
column2: 我們不能把時間浪費在閒話上，朋友，你得跟我來。

column1: Do not fall into this wadi.  It looks treacherous.
column2: 別掉進這條乾谷裡，看來十分凶險。

column1: Not here!  Follow me to the pool.
column2: 不是這裡！跟我到水池去。

column1: The side of the wadi is steep and unsafe.  This is not a good place to try to reach the water, but it must flow down to an easier place.
column2: 乾谷的側壁陡峭而危險，這裡不是取水的好地方，不過水勢應當會流向更容易抵達之處。

column1: No, no, that is trickier than you think.  Follow me to where you can easily drink from this water.
column2: 不、不，這比你想的棘手得多。跟我到能輕易取水的地方去。

column1: Do not try it!  The ground may give way, or you may find yourself unable to climb out.
column2: 別輕舉妄動！地面隨時可能塌陷，你也可能爬不出來。

column1: The wadi drops off steeply.  Do not fall into it.
column2: 這條乾谷陡然下切，別掉進去。

column1: Water bubbles from the ground and flows down from this wadi.  Be careful you do not fall into it.  You might not be able to climb out again.
column2: 水從地下湧出，順著這條乾谷流下。小心別掉進去，你可能爬不出來。

column1: The fissures are not deep, and there is nothing in them.
column2: 這些裂縫不深，裡頭什麼也沒有。

column1: You have seen the Pool of Siloam and Hezekiah's aqueduct.  This stream must come from the same source.
column2: 你見過西羅亞池與希西家水道，這道水流想必來自同一源頭。

column1: What odd things you babble about.  Clearly, the heat is affecting your brain.
column2: 你在胡言亂語些什麼古怪話。想必是這酷熱燒壞了你的腦子。

column1: This seems to be what the Arabs call a wadi, but you are not in a safe place to reach the water.  If you follow it, it should lead to more level ground.
column2: 這似乎是阿拉伯人稱作「乾谷」的地形，但你所在之處並不安全，無法取水。若順著它走，應當能通往較平坦的地面。

column1: You have managed to stumble off the crumbling edge and crack open your head upon a rock.                   Wadi shame.
column2: 你踩空了崩落的邊緣，一頭撞上岩石，就此喪命。          谷中憾事。

column1: You must follow me this way.  There is a pool of fresh water over here.
column2: 你得跟我走這條路，這邊有一池清水。

column1: Ah, your mule lacked the energy to run far.  She waited for you in the small relief offered by the shadow of the cliffs.
column2: 啊，你的騾子沒有力氣跑遠，她就在崖壁投下的一小片陰涼裡等你。

column1: Cliffs block your way upon one side and draw close to other cliffs ahead.
column2: 崖壁擋住了你一側的去路，前方又與另一片崖壁漸漸逼近。

column1: The tall ridge of cliffs continues unbroken toward some kind of pass or valley ahead.
column2: 這道高聳的崖脊連綿不絕，直通向前方某處隘口或山谷。

column1: Aye, there is something sticking out of the ground that looks like the remains of a very ancient wall.
column2: 正是，地面上有東西突起，看來像是一道極古老城牆的遺跡。

column1: Your mule has no intention of getting close to a desert cobra.
column2: 你的騾子絲毫不想靠近沙漠眼鏡蛇。

column1: Your mule is ready to follow you anywhere except into the valley of the cobras.
column2: 你的騾子什麼地方都願意跟你去，唯獨不肯進眼鏡蛇的山谷。

column1: This valley is filled with cobras!   Turn back, Arthur.  You will never pass through here alive.
column2: 這山谷裡滿是眼鏡蛇！亞瑟，快回頭，你絕不可能活著穿過這裡。

column1: There are too many cobras to do that without being fatally bitten.
column2: 眼鏡蛇太多了，這麼做免不了被咬中要害。

column1: To do that, you would have to get through the cobras.  I can think of no earthly reason to take such a risk.
column2: 那樣做，你就得穿過這群眼鏡蛇。我實在想不出有什麼理由值得冒這種險。

column1: Do not trifle with cobras.
column2: 別拿眼鏡蛇開玩笑。

column1: The cliffs converge into a narrow valley, but this portion of it is filled with cobras.  And they have no intention of letting you pass.
column2: 崖壁在此收攏成一道狹窄的山谷，這一段卻滿是眼鏡蛇，牠們絲毫無意讓你通過。

column1: Your mule is smarter than you.  She refuses to come near the cobras.
column2: 你的騾子比你聰明，她拒絕靠近那些眼鏡蛇。

column1: The snake lies where you killed it.
column2: 那條蛇倒在你殺死牠的地方。

column1: Beware, Arthur.  This cobra watches you with malign intent.
column2: 亞瑟，當心。這條眼鏡蛇正不懷好意地盯著你。

column1: There are some aloe vera plants growing here.
column2: 這裡長著幾株蘆薈。

column1: You dare not look long at the glaring sky, unbroken by any cloud, where the sun burns as mercilessly as a demon's eye.
column2: 你不敢久望這片無雲的刺目天空，烈日在其中燃燒，猶如惡魔的眼睛般毫不留情。

column1: The cliffs have drawn together to form this narrow valley, but it is impossible to tell whether the valley continues or closes up ahead.
column2: 崖壁在此靠攏，形成這道狹窄的山谷，但看不出前方山谷是延續下去，還是就此封閉。

column1: Aye, it is dead and not pleasant to look upon.
column2: 正是，牠已經死了，模樣並不好看。

column1: The snakes are alive and well, which you will not be if you get too close to them.
column2: 這些蛇活得好好的，你要是靠得太近，可就活不成了。

column1: These snakes are desert cobras and are utterly lethal.  Stay well clear of them.
column2: 這些蛇是沙漠眼鏡蛇，致命無比，務必遠遠避開。

column1: A rather novel idea, Arthur, but entirely foolish.
column2: 亞瑟，這主意倒是新奇，卻愚蠢至極。

column1: Arthur, beware!  The cobra prepares to strike.
column2: 亞瑟，小心！那條眼鏡蛇正準備發動攻擊。

column1: With quick reflexes, you were able to kill the lone cobra, but there are many more.  One of them is bound to strike you.
column2: 憑著敏捷的反應，你殺了那條落單的眼鏡蛇，但還有更多蛇在，其中必有一條會咬中你。

column1: Did I not warn you?  This valley may truly be called a dead end, especially for you.
column2: 我不是警告過你了嗎？這山谷當真稱得上是條死路，尤其對你而言。

column1: The cliffs reduce to a few boulders as the desert opens up to a trackless expanse.
column2: 崖壁漸漸化為幾塊巨石，沙漠隨即展開成一片無路可循的荒野。

column1: As you approach Jerusalem bear in mind that you are one lone foreigner surrounded by dangerous and hostile natives.
column2: 你即將接近耶路撒冷，切記你不過是孤身一名異鄉客，身處危險而充滿敵意的當地人之中。

column1: You may, if you wish to return to the Pool of Siloam.
column2: 你可以這麼做，若你想回到西羅亞池的話。

column1: At last, after your arduous journey the walls of Jerusalem rise before you.  At this corner you can see the golden mosque called the Dome of the Rock.
column2: 歷經艱辛跋涉，耶路撒冷的城牆終於矗立在你眼前。從這個角落，你能望見那座金色的清真寺，人稱「圓頂清真寺」。

column1: Once more you approach the walls of Jerusalem.
column2: 你再度接近耶路撒冷的城牆。

column1: This pass brings you to the hill where Jerusalem is built.
column2: 這道隘口通向耶路撒冷所在的山丘。

column1: The golden Dome of the Rock is one of the holiest mosques in Islam.  It houses a rock from which the Muslims believe that Mohammed ascended to Heaven.
column2: 這座金色的圓頂清真寺，是伊斯蘭教最神聖的清真寺之一。寺內供奉著一塊岩石，穆斯林相信穆罕默德便是由此升天。

column1: I know nothing about it.  Perhaps it is a tower from which the muslims are called to prayer.
column2: 我對此一無所知，或許那是穆斯林被召喚禮拜的高塔。

column1: Since you can see the golden mosque, that must be the southeastern corner of Jerusalem.
column2: 既然你能望見那座金色清真寺，這裡想必是耶路撒冷的東南角。

column1: As you know, this pass becomes a road which leads you inevitably to the Zion Gate.
column2: 如你所知，這道隘口會接上一條路，終將把你引向錫安城門。

column1: There are a number of gates.  It depends on where this pass will lead.
column2: 城門不只一座，得看這道隘口通往何處而定。

column1: Let us hope that the mercenaries at the Zion Gate are better disposed toward you this time.
column2: 但願這回錫安城門的傭兵們，對你能和善一些。

column1: In addition to Saracens and city soldiers, you may encounter some mercenaries acting as guards.
column2: 除了撒拉遜人與城中的士兵之外，你也可能遇上充當守衛的傭兵。

column1: There are some aloe vera plants around.
column2: 附近長著幾株蘆薈。

column1: I hope you will pay more attention to Fatima's warnings when you return to pass her Test, as you must yet do.
column2: 但願你日後回來接受法提瑪的考驗時，能多留心她的警告——那考驗你終究還得去面對。

column1: By my beard!  This is a cold lesson to learn.  Next time, you must deal more carefully with Fatima before you attempt to leave.
column2: 憑我這把鬍子起誓！這教訓可真夠慘痛。下回你想離開之前，得更謹慎地應付法提瑪才是。

column1: It is too dark to see anything.
column2: 這裡黑得什麼都看不見。

column1: The water is dark, but not deep.
column2: 水色幽暗，但並不深。

column1: It is too dark to see anything above you.
column2: 太暗了，看不清你頭頂上方有什麼。

column1: Above you it is solid rock.
column2: 你頭頂上方是堅實的岩石。

column1: I see nothing dangerous in here other than the dark.
column2: 這裡除了黑暗之外，我看不出還有什麼危險。

column1: The tunnel is small and carved from solid rock, as you can see in the light reflected from the tunnel's mouth.
column2: 這條隧道狹小，是從堅實的岩石中鑿出來的——從洞口反射進來的光線便能看清這一點。

column1: The light of the entrance is but a distant point that can barely illuminate this gloom.
column2: 入口的光只剩遠處一個小點，幾乎照不亮這片幽暗。

column1: The tunnel is quite dark here.  If you go any further into it, it will be pitch black and dangerous to stumble about in.
column2: 這裡的隧道相當昏暗，若再往裡走，便會漆黑一片，在其中摸索行走十分危險。

column1: You cannot see a thing, and you are stumbling dangerously on the roughly hewn rock.
column2: 你什麼也看不見，在這粗糙鑿成的岩地上跌跌撞撞，十分危險。

column1: It is pitch black here.
column2: 這裡漆黑一片。

column1: It is pure and cold, flowing through this aqueduct from the Spring of Gihon.
column2: 這水清澈冰涼，順著這條水道，從基訓泉流淌而來。

column1: The walls of the tunnel are carved from solid rock.
column2: 隧道的牆壁是從堅實的岩石中鑿出來的。

column1: It is too dark to think of doing anything.
column2: 太暗了，什麼都無從做起。

column1: The tunnel walls offer no grip and the way back up to Fatima is nearly vertical.
column2: 隧道牆壁無處可攀，通往法提瑪那邊的回頭路幾乎垂直而上。

column1: You are in a tunnel carved of rock.  There is nothing to climb.
column2: 你身處一條鑿於岩石中的隧道，沒有什麼可以攀爬的東西。

column1: Your mule prudently waits for you at the Pool of Siloam.
column2: 你的騾子明智地在西羅亞池等你。

column1: That is simple.  The further into the tunnel you go, the darker it will get.
column2: 這很簡單。你越往隧道深處走，就會越黑暗。

column1: After a long and dizzying slide you have landed in the cold waters of Hezekiah's Aqueduct.
column2: 經過一段漫長而令人暈眩的滑落，你落進了希西家水道冰冷的水中。

column1: It is now pitch black, deep inside the aqueduct.  You are stumbling about dangerously on the roughly hewn floor.
column2: 此刻水道深處漆黑一片，你在這粗糙鑿成的地面上跌跌撞撞，十分危險。

column1: Arthur!  What was that sound?
column2: 亞瑟！那是什麼聲音？

column1: Ah.  As I feared.  You have struck your head upon a low spot in the tunnel, knocked yourself out, fallen forward into the water and drowned.  Not a very glorious end for the King of all the Britons.
column2: 啊，正如我所擔心的。你的頭撞上了隧道裡低矮的一處，昏了過去，往前跌進水中溺斃。對於不列顛眾王之王而言，這算不上什麼光榮的結局。

column1: A fool and his money are soon parted.  Heh, heh, heh!
column2: 傻子和他的錢財，總是很快就要分家。嘿嘿嘿！

column1: This is not enough.  All my men must be paid as well.
column2: 這還不夠。我手下的人也都得付錢才行。

column1: You may pass, infidel.
column2: 你可以過去了，異教徒。

column1: A rich man!!
column2: 好個有錢人！！

column1: Now we shall see how well an infidel dies.
column2: 這下便讓我們瞧瞧，異教徒是怎麼個死法。

column1: Leaving, heathen?  Good.  We do not like infidels.
column2: 要走了嗎，異教之徒？很好，我們不喜歡異教徒。

column1: Come closer, coward!  Our swords thirst for your blood!
column2: 靠近點，懦夫！我們的劍渴求你的鮮血！

column1: We do not want your greetings, dog.
column2: 我們不需要你的問候，狗東西。

column1: You want me to move, heathen dog?  Give me money and I will consider it.
column2: 你要我讓路，異教徒狗？給我錢，我便考慮考慮。

column1: I am not in your way now, but by Allah I will GET in your way if you provoke me.
column2: 此刻我沒擋你的路，但憑阿拉起誓，你要是惹惱了我，我便存心擋你的路。

column1: Hah!  Come closer and try that, dog.
column2: 哈！有種就靠近點試試看，狗東西。

column1: I do not answer questions, infidel.  Move along.
column2: 我不回答問題，異教徒。走開。

column1: You get nothing back from me, unbeliever.  Be on your way.
column2: 你從我這裡什麼也得不到，不信者。上路吧。

column1: You will get nothing but trouble if you bother me, heathen dog.
column2: 你要是來惹我，異教徒狗，得到的只有麻煩。

column1: We do not buy, we take.
column2: 我們不買，我們搶。

column1: What is this?  Some kind of filthy heathen talisman?  Keep it away from me, by Allah.
column2: 這是什麼？某種骯髒的異教護符？憑阿拉起誓，離我遠一點。

column1: How can you offer that which you do not have?
column2: 你自己都沒有的東西，怎麼拿來給人？

column1: I do not want your wretched mule.
column2: 我才不要你那頭可憐的騾子。

column1: Do you fool with me, unbeliever?  I am not amused.
column2: 你在耍我嗎，不信者？我可笑不出來。

column1: This is empty, dog!  Give me money or be gone!
column2: 這是空的，狗東西！拿錢來，不然就滾！

column1: Do you mock us, infidel?  We are not amused.
column2: 你在嘲弄我們嗎，異教徒？我們可笑不出來。

column1: You had better pay in coin, infidel, or you will pay in blood.
column2: 你最好用錢來付，異教徒，不然就得用血來償。

column1: If you want to pass, you will come here and pay me.
column2: 你若想通過，就過來付錢給我。

column1: I do not waste speech with heathens. Move along, unless you wish to give us more money, heh heh.
column2: 我不跟異教之徒多費唇舌。走開，除非你想再多給我們一些錢，嘿嘿。

column1: The Zion Gate is closed.  You cannot enter here.  You must go to the Jaffa Gate.
column2: 錫安城門已經關閉，你無法從這裡進去，得走賈法城門才行。

column1: You look like a stinking infidel.  If you want to pass to the Jaffa Gate, you had better make it worth my while.
column2: 你看著就是個臭異教徒。想去賈法城門的話，最好讓我覺得值得放你過去。

column1: I do not waste speech with infidels. I would as soon talk to a cur in the street.
column2: 我不跟異教徒多費唇舌，跟街上的野狗說話我還更樂意些。

column1: Be on your way, infidel, before we tire of your ugly face.
column2: 走開吧，異教徒，趁我們還沒看膩你那張醜臉。

column1: You were warned, infidel!
column2: 你已經被警告過了，異教徒！

column1: By Allah! Look, men, our infidel returns as bedraggled as an old sow that has been rolling in dust and muck.
column2: 憑阿拉起誓！弟兄們瞧瞧，我們這位異教徒又回來了，狼狽得像頭在塵土泥濘裡打過滾的老母豬。

column1: Hah!  They must raise some clumsy fools where you come from.
column2: 哈！你老家想必淨養些笨手笨腳的蠢貨。

column1: Fool of a heathen.  Can you not even find the right gate?
column2: 蠢貨異教徒，連該走哪座城門都找不對？

column1: Sheathe your sword, infidel, or we will chop you to pieces.
column2: 收起你的劍，異教徒，不然我們把你剁成碎塊。

column1: Be warned, infidel!  Keep your sword sheathed or we will chop you to pieces.
column2: 警告你，異教徒！把劍收好，否則我們把你剁成碎塊。

column1: The Zion Gate is closed.  Move along, infidel, and I mean NOW!
column2: 錫安城門已經關閉。滾開，異教徒，我說的是現在！

column1: The Zion gate is closed.  You should consider yourself fortunate if we allow you to leave with your skin intact.
column2: 錫安城門已經關閉。若我們容你毫髮無傷地離開，你便該心懷感激。

column1: It is a long way to the bottom of the hill!
column2: 到山腳還有好長一段路！

column1: The wall is too thick and the opening too narrow to see anything inside.
column2: 牆壁太厚，開口太窄，看不見裡頭的情形。

column1: Why would you insult an armed group of men?  Are you feeling exceptionally suicidal today?
column2: 你為何要出言侮辱一群全副武裝的人？難道你今天特別想尋死？

column1: We have moved as far as we will move.  Do not push your luck, dog of an infidel.
column2: 我們已經讓到頭了，不會再退。休得得寸進尺，異教狗。

column1: There is a dangerous looking Mercenary guard and his thugs guarding a small, closed gate.  They outnumber you, Arthur, and they are well armed.
column2: 一名面露凶光的傭兵守衛與他的爪牙，看守著一道緊閉的小門。亞瑟，他們人數多於你，而且裝備精良。

column1: These thugs have the look of violence about them.
column2: 這些爪牙渾身透著一股凶悍之氣。

column1: The mercenary's evil eyes are filled with a savage bloodlust.  He enjoys killing as much as he enjoys taking money
column2: 這名傭兵的雙眼透著凶殘嗜血之色，殺人取樂與圖財害命，於他而言不相上下

column1: Now that he has been paid, the mercenary eyes you with contempt.
column2: 如今傭兵已經拿到了錢，只以輕蔑的眼神看你。

column1: The large Mercenary in the pale blue robe is obviously the leader of this little band of thugs.
column2: 那個身披淺藍長袍的高大傭兵，顯然是這群爪牙的頭目。

column1: These men carry scimitars, a most lethal Arab weapon.
column2: 這些人佩帶彎刀，是阿拉伯人最致命的武器。

column1: Do not be fooled by the look of cloth.  They could well have a helmet beneath the turban.
column2: 別被那身布料的外表騙了，頭巾底下很可能藏著頭盔。

column1: Their robes may look strange to us, but they are perfectly suited to this climate.
column2: 他們的長袍在我們眼中或許顯得古怪，卻十分適合這裡的氣候。

column1: You may have to pay them again.   Let us hope not.
column2: 你或許還得再付他們一次錢，但願不必如此。

column1: Let us hope that they will not wish payment to let you leave Jerusalem.
column2: 但願他們不會要你付錢才肯放你離開耶路撒冷。

column1: You were very wise to avoid a fight with four heavily armed and dangerous men.
column2: 避開與四名全副武裝的凶悍男子交手，是明智之舉。

column1: You are a lone foreigner against four dangerous mercenaries.  Your life is worth far more than a few coins.
column2: 你孤身一人，對上四名凶悍的傭兵。你的性命遠比幾枚錢幣更加珍貴。

column1: I do hope you can talk your way out of this, Arthur, but I fear the only language they speak is that of money.
column2: 亞瑟，我衷心希望你能靠三言兩語脫身，但恐怕他們只聽得懂金錢這種語言。

column1: The discs seem to be a part of the walls, but I cannot say what their purpose may be.
column2: 這些圓盤似乎是城牆的一部分，但我說不出它們的用途。

column1: It is an archiere, from which arrows can be fired in time of war.
column2: 那是一處箭孔，戰時可從中射箭。

column1: The door handles are made of iron.
column2: 門把是鐵製的。

column1: You cannot see it from here.  It is in the western wall.
column2: 從這裡看不見，它在西邊的城牆上。

column1: If I read my maps of Jerusalem correctly, this is called the Zion Gate and is a minor gate in the south wall.
column2: 若我沒看錯耶路撒冷的地圖，此處喚作錫安城門，是南面城牆上的一道小門。

column1: The arch is part of the structure of the Gate.
column2: 這道拱門是城門結構的一部分。

column1: These spiny plants are Aloe Vera.
column2: 這些帶刺的植物是蘆薈。

column1: The walls of Jerusalem are made of huge blocks of a buff-colored stone.
column2: 耶路撒冷的城牆由巨大的淺黃色石塊砌成。

column1: Aye, they are rocks.  There is a lot of rock in this country.
column2: 正是，這些是岩石。這片土地上岩石多得很。

column1: Arthur, are you mad?!
column2: 亞瑟，你瘋了嗎？！

column1: The walls of Jerusalem continue on as far as you can see.
column2: 耶路撒冷的城牆一路延伸，望不到盡頭。

column1: It is a long way to the bottom of the hill.
column2: 到山腳還有好長一段路。

column1: You have reached one corner of the walls of Jerusalem.  The mercenaries back at the Zion Gate watch you warily.
column2: 你來到了耶路撒冷城牆的一角。錫安城門那邊的傭兵正警戒地盯著你。

column1: Another stretch of ancient wall awaits you.
column2: 眼前又是一段古老的城牆。

column1: To the north is the Jaffa Gate.
column2: 北邊是賈法城門。

column1: There is something ahead that may be the Jaffa Gate.
column2: 前方似乎有什麼東西，可能是賈法城門。

column1: To the south is the southwest corner of the walls of Jerusalem.
column2: 南邊是耶路撒冷城牆的西南角。

column1: Aye, 'tis a scrubby tree of no great interest.
column2: 正是，這是一株矮小的灌木，沒什麼看頭。

column1: He smells as though he has been sleeping in a pen of goats.  It is a good thing that you are standing upwind.
column2: 他身上的氣味，彷彿睡在羊圈裡似的。幸好你站在上風處。

column1: I warn you, I am an official of the city!  Pay me an entrance fee or go away.
column2: 我警告你，我是本城的官吏！付入城費，不然就滾開。

column1: Come, come, I do not have all day.  You must pay me a fee to enter the Jaffa Gate.  Whatever you can afford.
column2: 來吧來吧，我可沒空耗一整天。你得付費才能進賈法城門，多少都行，隨你的能力。

column1: He did not seem to hear you. Perhaps you are too far away.
column2: 他似乎沒聽見你的話，或許你離得太遠了。

column1: If you lay hands upon me, I will call for the city guards and they will chop you into little pieces.
column2: 你若敢對我動手，我便叫城衛來，他們會把你剁成碎片。

column1: May the fleas of a thousand camels infest your tent!
column2: 願千頭駱駝的跳蚤，都鑽進你的帳篷！

column1: He does not seem to hear you.
column2: 他似乎沒聽見你的話。

column1: He is dirty, has a disreputable look, and his clothes are old, threadbare, and smell of goats.
column2: 他一身骯髒，模樣不端，衣衫破舊，還帶著羊臊味。

column1: A thicket of bushes blocks the path to the north.
column2: 一叢灌木擋住了通往北方的路。

column1: He is gone, good riddance.
column2: 他走了，走了也好。

column1: He will know the escape routes of this city.  I doubt that you will have a chance to catch up with him.
column2: 他必然熟知這座城的脫身路線，我不認為你追得上他。

column1: Arthur!  Will you PLEASE show some caution with the few possessions you have left.
column2: 亞瑟！你剩下沒幾件家當了，拜託小心一點好嗎！

column1: Ridiculous!  The last thing on earth you need is a brainless sheep.
column2: 荒唐！你這輩子最不需要的，就是一頭沒腦子的羊。

column1: Perhaps one of the merchants inside would be interested.
column2: 或許裡頭有哪位商人會感興趣。

column1: This is the Jaffa Gate.  What are you waiting for?  Enter.
column2: 這是賈法城門，你還在等什麼？進去吧。

column1: I suppose there are plenty of merchants in the bazaar.
column2: 我想市集裡商人多得是。

column1: Aye, he was a fraud if I ever saw one.
column2: 正是，他要不是騙子，我這輩子就沒見過騙子。

column1: Aye, Arthur, you must be wary of thieves.
column2: 正是，亞瑟，你得提防竊賊。

column1: There is a shop selling cloth inside the bazaar.
column2: 市集裡有間賣布的鋪子。

column1: He is gone, and good riddance.
column2: 他走了，走了也好。

column1: The woman and her sheep are gone.
column2: 那婦人與她的羊都不見了。

column1: This must be the Jaffa Gate.  There is a glimpse of the local bazaar inside, with an open gutter that runs down the center of the street.
column2: 這想必就是賈法城門了。門內可以窺見當地的市集，一條露天水溝沿著街道中央流淌。

column1: Not to mention this bothersome man who is determined to have words with you.
column2: 更別提這個死纏著要跟你搭話的討厭傢伙了。

column1: It is the Jaffa Gate and the way is open.
column2: 這是賈法城門，門是開著的。

column1: You must pay me a fee to enter the Jaffa Gate.  Whatever you can afford, but you must pay.
column2: 你得付費才能進賈法城門，多少隨你，但一定得付。

column1: Hey, you!
column2: 喂，你！

column1: Yes, yes, welcome to Jerusalem.  Now pay me the fee to enter and let us be done with it.
column2: 好好，歡迎來到耶路撒冷。現在付入城費吧，咱們好把這事了結。

column1: There is a rather interesting smell of frying food drifting out of the Jaffa Gate.
column2: 賈法城門飄出一股頗誘人的煎炸食物香氣。

column1: Without the smell of goat interfering, there is a rather interesting smell of frying food drifting out of the Jaffa Gate.
column2: 少了那股羊臊味的干擾，賈法城門飄出的煎炸食物香氣顯得格外誘人。

column1: Ah, uh, no, a mule is too difficult to deal with.  Just money will do.
column2: 啊，呃，不了，騾子太麻煩了，給錢就行。

column1: No, no, YOU must pay ME to enter the gate.
column2: 不，不，是「你」得付錢給「我」才能進這城門。

column1: No, no, you must give me money, not sell me something.
column2: 不不，你得給我錢，不是要賣我東西。

column1: We are reasonable here.  Whatever you can afford.  Come on, I do not have all day.
column2: 我們這裡通情達理，多少隨你的能力。來吧，我可沒空耗一整天。

column1: Ahm...uhmm...I know nothing of any thief!
column2: 呃……嗯……我對什麼竊賊一無所知！

column1: Yasser likes not the flash of your steel.
column2: 亞西爾不喜歡看見你亮出鋼刃。

column1: That has set the fraud to his heels.  But you had best put up your sword for now.  There may be more guards like those at the Zion gate.
column2: 這下讓那騙子拔腿就跑了。但你此刻最好還是收起劍——這附近說不定還有像錫安城門那樣的守衛。

column1: By my beard, Arthur, I believe he was a fraud.
column2: 憑我這把鬍子起誓，亞瑟，我看他就是個騙子。

column1: The road leads back into the desert.
column2: 這條路通回沙漠。

column1: My advice is simple and obvious.  Enter Jerusalem and search for the Grail!
column2: 我的建議簡單明瞭：進入耶路撒冷，尋找聖杯！

column1: There's no one here to attack.
column2: 這裡沒有人可以攻擊。

column1: The road seems to stretch on forever.
column2: 這條路彷彿沒有盡頭。

column1: It is a scrubby and uninteresting tree.
column2: 這是一株矮小平凡的樹，沒什麼看頭。

column1: In the distance is the searing desert and arid hills through which you have journeyed.
column2: 遠方是你一路走過的灼熱沙漠與乾旱丘陵。

column1: It cannot be seen from here.
column2: 從這裡看不見。

column1: The walls of Jerusalem are but a few paces away.
column2: 耶路撒冷的城牆只在幾步之遙。

column1: Behind you, the Jaffa Gate is open and Jerusalem awaits you.
column2: 你身後，賈法城門敞開著，耶路撒冷正等著你。

column1: Concern yourself with your sacred mission.  That is all that matters.
column2: 把心思放在你神聖的使命上，那才是唯一要緊的事。

column1: Arthur, halt!  At great cost to myself, I send this vision of warning.  You must not turn away from your mission now.
column2: 亞瑟，止步！我耗費莫大的心力，才將這個警示的異象傳給你。此刻，你絕不能背離你的使命。

column1: Months of weary labor and travel have brought you here.  There is nothing this way but the desert whose hardship you have already suffered.
column2: 數月的艱辛跋涉，才將你帶到此地。這條路上除了你已經受過的沙漠苦難，再無他物。

column1: Turn back to Jerusalem, King Arthur, and seek your destiny within.
column2: 回頭吧，亞瑟王，回耶路撒冷去，在城中尋得你的命運。

column1: So, in spite of my best efforts and advice, you insist on heading back into the desert like an utter fool.
column2: 看來，不顧我竭盡全力的勸告，你仍執意像個十足的傻子那樣，一頭栽回沙漠裡去。

column1: And to think that men once hailed you as King and praised your ability.
column2: 想想看，曾經有人尊你為王，讚頌你的才能。

column1: The guards remain and will not let you leave. Do not annoy them, Arthur. There are many more of them and they are all well armed.
column2: 守衛仍守在那裡，不會放你離開。亞瑟，別去招惹他們，他們人數眾多，而且裝備精良。

column1: In Latin, the sign reads "Arma" meaning weaponry or armour. Mohammed is the name of the merchant.
column2: 以拉丁文寫著「Arma」，意為武器或盔甲。商人的名字是穆罕默德。

column1: The Islamic symbols above his name are the crescent moon and a scimitar. The rest is in Arabic.
column2: 他名字上方的伊斯蘭符號是一彎新月與一把彎刀，其餘部分則是阿拉伯文。

column1: It is difficult to see through the shutters.
column2: 百葉窗擋著，很難看清裡頭。

column1: My, quite a view.
column2: 哎呀，好一片景致。

column1: The second floor of this building has a window and a balcony.
column2: 這棟建築的二樓有一扇窗與一座陽台。

column1: Across the street are more merchants.
column2: 街道對面還有更多商人。

column1: The weapons shop is closed.
column2: 武器店關著門。

column1: There is nothing more to be gained here. Do as she instructs.
column2: 這裡已經沒有更多可得的了，照她說的做吧。

column1: There is now a girl crying in front of Mohammed's shop. And see, her doves have escaped.
column2: 此刻有個女孩在穆罕默德的店前哭泣，你看，她的鴿子都逃走了。

column1: Mohammed's shop may be closed, but it appears Mari is open for business.
column2: 穆罕默德的店雖然關著，但瑪麗似乎正在營業。

column1: The weapon merchant's shop is closed.
column2: 武器商人的店關著門。

column1: Your mule is being held safely by the weapons merchant. You are fortunate he is an honest man.
column2: 你的騾子安然由武器商人代為看管，幸好他是個誠實的人。

column1: The weapons merchant looks sympathetic. I suspect this is not the first time he has seen this thief in action.
column2: 武器商人一臉同情的神色，我猜這已不是他第一次見識那竊賊的手法。

column1: The scimitar is a common Islamic emblem.
column2: 彎刀是常見的伊斯蘭象徵。

column1: The crescent moon is a symbol of the Goddess.
column2: 新月是女神的象徵。

column1: It is dark inside and you can see nothing.
column2: 裡頭一片漆黑，你什麼也看不見。

column1: The windows downstairs are closed. One of the windows upstairs is closed.
column2: 樓下的窗戶關著，樓上也有一扇窗戶關著。

column1: It is closed.
column2: 它關著。

column1: There is no way up to it from here.
column2: 從這裡沒有路可以上去。

column1: There are no stairs.
column2: 這裡沒有樓梯。

column1: Aye, they are rocks.
column2: 正是，這些是岩石。

column1: Watch for him if you like, but I doubt he will come near you again.
column2: 你若想留意他也行，但我不認為他還敢靠近你。

column1: He is gone, as you can see.
column2: 如你所見，他已經走了。

column1: A dubious tactic at best.
column2: 這頂多算是個可疑的招數。

column1: First you must get her attention.
column2: 你得先引起她的注意。

column1: She is not here.
column2: 她不在這裡。

column1: She is gone.
column2: 她已經離開了。

column1: These rocks are too heavy for any practical use.
column2: 這些石頭太重，派不上什麼實際用場。

column1: The door is locked.
column2: 門鎖著。

column1: No one answers.
column2: 沒有人應門。

column1: You would not need to, even if the weapons merchant were here.
column2: 就算武器商人在這裡，你也用不著這麼做。

column1: And be mistaken for a thief?! Do not be a fool. Besides, you could find nothing better than Excaliber, even in this shop.
column2: 還被人誤認成竊賊？！別犯傻了。再說，就算在這間店裡，你也找不到比聖劍更好的東西。

column1: Totally impractical with all your gear, not to mention how it might excite the city guards.
column2: 帶著你這一身裝備，那根本不切實際，更別提會引來城衛的注意了。
