column1: You should have paid more attention to the scroll in my room before you left Camelot.
column2: 你離開肯萊特之前，該多留心我房裡那卷卷軸才是。

column1: Why do you waste time here?
column2: 你何必在這裡浪費時間？

column1: Remember, you are dealing with Arab money now. A fals is a copper coin. 4 fals are worth a dirham which is silver. 4 dirhams equal a dinar, which is gold.
column2: 記住，如今你打交道的是阿拉伯貨幣。法爾斯（fals）是銅幣，四枚法爾斯抵一枚銀幣迪爾罕（dirham）；四枚迪爾罕則等於一枚金幣第納爾（dinar）。

column1: No answer. Perhaps she is not home.
column2: 沒有回應，或許她不在家。

column1: She does not answer.
column2: 她沒有回應。

column1: Across the street is a weapons shop.
column2: 街道對面是一間武器店。

column1: The felafel seller does business as usual. Ibrahim has still not returned, however.
column2: 賣法拉費的攤販一如往常做著生意，然而易布拉興依舊沒有回來。

column1: There is a textile merchant and a woman selling felafels.
column2: 這裡有一位布商，還有一名賣法拉費的婦人。

column1: The woman sells her felafels, but as I suspected, Ibrahim has forsaken his business for the pleasure of his wife's company. And who can blame him?
column2: 那婦人一如往常做著生意，但正如我所料，易布拉興撇下了鋪子，只顧著陪伴愛妻。這又能怪他嗎？

column1: It is golden fried and hot from oil. You must either eat it or give it to someone, Arthur. It will crumble to bits if you carry it about.
column2: 它炸得金黃，帶著油鍋的熱氣。你得立刻吃掉，或轉手給人，亞瑟。若一直帶在身上，它會碎成渣。

column1: You were warned they are delicate. It has crumbled away to nothing.
column2: 早提醒過你這東西易碎。它已經碎成渣，什麼都不剩了。

column1: There is a basket of crisp, golden brown felafels, fresh from the oil on the woman's table.
column2: 婦人的攤桌上，有一籃酥脆金黃、剛出油鍋的法拉費。

column1: It is dark and empty.
column2: 裡頭又暗又空。

column1: He has quite a lot of it.
column2: 他這東西可不少。

column1: There is a basket of raw felafel balls and a basket of fried felafels.
column2: 這裡有一籃生的法拉費丸子，還有一籃炸好的法拉費。

column1: It looks uninviting.
column2: 看起來讓人提不起食慾。

column1: Your mule is across the street with the weapons merchant.
column2: 你的騾子在街對面，跟武器商在一起。

column1: How?
column2: 怎麼做？

column1: The felafels do smell especially good.
column2: 這些法拉費聞起來確實格外香。

column1: Nay, do not disturb Ibrahim and his wife at such a moment.
column2: 不可，此刻不該打擾易布拉興夫婦。

column1: If Ibrahim wanted you to enter, he would invite you.
column2: 若易布拉興想讓你進去，他自會邀你入內。

column1: Ibrahim has not returned.
column2: 易布拉興還沒回來。

column1: I do not think you will see Ibrahim any time soon.
column2: 我想你一時半刻是見不著易布拉興了。

column1: No need to stand there drooling. Help yourself, I said.
column2: 用不著站在那裡流口水。我說了，自己拿去吃吧。

column1: He has rather a taste for bright colours, I note.
column2: 我注意到，他挺偏愛鮮豔的色彩。

column1: The textile merchant has quite an array of cloth.
column2: 這位布商陳列著各式各樣的布料。

column1: You cannot see through the door.
column2: 你透過門看不進去。

column1: Observe, if you will, the quality of my fabrics. You will find none finer even if you journeyed to Constantinople, and indeed, some have come from twice as far.
column2: 且請細看，我這些布料的品質。縱使你遠赴君士坦丁堡，也找不到更好的了——其中有些，來歷還遠上一倍不止。

column1: See the exquisite colors, the glowing patterns, the perfect weave of these silks from the Orient.
column2: 瞧瞧這些東方絲綢，色澤精緻、紋樣鮮亮、織工完美無瑕。

column1: And these magnificent linens that will keep you cool when the sun scorches the earth, and by its virtue of absorbing moisture, will keep you dry.
column2: 還有這些上等亞麻布，烈日炙烤大地時能為你消暑，又因其吸濕之性，能讓你保持乾爽。

column1: Then perhaps you come from a colder clime, as indeed your armor would hint. See my beautifully dyed woolens and feel the perfection of their natural oils.
column2: 那麼，你或許來自較寒冷之地——你這身盔甲確實透著這樣的訊息。瞧瞧我這染色精美的羊毛織品，感受一下它天然油脂的極致觸感。

column1: You are undoubtedly awed by the selection. Take your time.
column2: 你想必是被這些選擇給看呆了。慢慢挑吧。

column1: My anguish overwhelms me. I cannot speak.
column2: 我痛苦難當，說不出話來。

column1: But you are not buying anything.
column2: 但你什麼都沒買。

column1: Keep it away! I once had a mule who ate cloth. I will never keep one again.
column2: 拿開！我曾養過一頭吃布的騾子，此後再也不敢養了。

column1: Ahh! You have it, habibi! If only I could have it, I would be the happiest man in the world!
column2: 啊！你竟然有這個，朋友！我若能擁有它，便是世上最快樂的人了！

column1: No thank you. I do not eat meat.
column2: 不用了，謝謝。我不吃肉。

column1: Forgive my ingratitude, but I have eaten more of Sarah's felafels than the sky has stars.
column2: 恕我失禮，莎拉的法拉費，我吃過的怕是比天上的星星還多。

column1: You wish me to accept this gift? I cannot imagine why. I must respectfully decline.
column2: 你要我收下這份禮？我實在想不出理由。恕我不能領受。

column1: No, I do not eat meat.
column2: 不，我不吃肉。

column1: I think not today, thank you. May Allah guide you elsewhere.
column2: 今日就不必了，多謝。願阿拉指引你前往別處。

column1: Rather ostentatious for you, I deem, and not of much use without the skills of a tailor.
column2: 依我看，這對你來說未免太招搖，何況沒有裁縫的手藝，也派不上什麼用場。

column1: If you wish, here it is.
column2: 你若想要，這就給你。

column1: Do not mention the word veil to me! It is a word of misery.
column2: 休再提「面紗」這個詞！那是個令人痛苦的字眼。

column1: She is beautiful and trusting. I fear I do not deserve such a good wife.
column2: 她美麗又信任於我。我恐怕配不上這樣一位賢妻。

column1: I do not have rugs for sale.
column2: 我這裡沒有地毯可賣。

column1: Perhaps Ismail the relic merchant can help you.
column2: 或許聖物商艾思美能幫上你。

column1: I do not know him.
column2: 我不認識他。

column1: Just feel the marvelous fabric, habib. They can make a pauper look like a prince!
column2: 摸摸這絕妙的布料吧，朋友。它能讓乞丐看起來像王子！

column1: My woolens are the finest in Jerusalem.
column2: 我這羊毛織品，是耶路撒冷最上乘的。

column1: The silks come from the Orient, very rare and very beautiful.
column2: 這些絲綢來自東方，極為稀有，也極為美麗。

column1: Yes, they plague and the city guards seldom catch them. For this, I pay taxes?
column2: 是啊，他們四處為害，城衛卻鮮少抓到他們。我繳稅就是為了這個？

column1: That alley goes nowhere and is most unpleasant.
column2: 那條巷子哪裡都通不了，而且十分不宜久留。

column1: Do not speak her cursed name! I wish I had never seen her!
column2: 休提她那受詛咒的名字！我真希望自己從未見過她！

column1: My neighbor, Sarah, sells excellent felafels.
column2: 我的鄰居莎拉，賣的法拉費十分出色。

column1: Her felafels are the best in Jerusalem.
column2: 她的法拉費是耶路撒冷最好的。

column1: It means cloth, of course.
column2: 那當然是指布料。

column1: The thieves are a dreadful nuisance.
column2: 那些竊賊實在是個大麻煩。

column1: Even if you travelled there, you would find no finer fabrics than mine.
column2: 縱使你親自遠行至彼處，也找不到比我這裡更好的布料。

column1: What can I say about that, habibi.
column2: 這事我還能說什麼呢，朋友。

column1: It appears she partakes liberally of her own food.
column2: 看來她自己也毫不吝於享用自家的食物。

column1: It is a heavy metal cauldron filled with bubbling hot oil.
column2: 這是口沉重的金屬大鍋，裝滿了滾沸的熱油。

column1: One basket of raw felafels and one basket of cooked felafels sits on the table.
column2: 桌上擺著一籃生的法拉費，還有一籃煮熟的法拉費。

column1: Stop that, Arthur. You have been away from Gwenhyver for too long.
column2: 住手，亞瑟。你離開昆海兒身邊太久了。

column1: I see no girl, only the matronly felafel seller.
column2: 我沒看見什麼姑娘，只有那位賣法拉費的婦人。

column1: 'Tis no more than a little stall with a canopy to keep out the rain and sun, a cauldron of bubbling oil and the felafels, raw and cooked.
column2: 不過是個小攤子，撐著遮風擋雨的棚子，一口滾油的大鍋，還有生的、熟的法拉費。

column1: Ah, it is you! How good to see your face again. If you want a felafel, just speak up.
column2: 啊，是你！能再見到你，真是高興。想要法拉費，儘管開口。

column1: Fresh, hot felafels for a hungry man. Made from the finest ground chick peas and ground sesame seed. Flavored with parsley, onion and garlic.
column2: 新鮮熱騰的法拉費，正合飢腸轆轆的漢子。用最上等的鷹嘴豆磨粉、芝麻磨粉製成，佐以荷蘭芹、洋蔥與大蒜調味。

column1: Golden fried felafels cooked in pure sesame oil. If you are hungry, a felafel would work wonders for your belly. See what it has done for mine!
column2: 用純芝麻油炸得金黃的法拉費。你若餓了，一份法拉費會讓你的肚子大為滿足。瞧瞧它把我的肚子養成什麼樣子！

column1: Well, I should not be telling you this, but all day long I cook felafels. Every day I eat felafels. Not that they are not delicious!
column2: 唉，我實在不該說這個，但我整天都在煮法拉費，天天也都在吃法拉費。倒不是它不好吃！

column1: But even I am tired of felafels. I dream of lamb! A nice, fresh cut of lamb. Lamb and felafel! Oi, that would be Paradise.
column2: 但就連我，也吃膩了法拉費。我夢想著羊肉！一塊上好新鮮的羊肉。羊肉配法拉費！啊，那簡直是天堂。

column1: I do not mind paying his prices, but I am terrified of the meat merchant, that evil-tempered ox! That is why I go without lamb.
column2: 他的價錢我倒不介意，可我怕透了那賣肉的，那頭脾氣暴躁的蠻牛！所以我才一直沒吃上羊肉。

column1: Do not try to cheat me now! No coin, no felafel.
column2: 休想耍花招！沒錢就沒法拉費。

column1: You can carry no more felafels without making a mess of yourself.
column2: 你身上帶的法拉費已經夠多了，再拿只會弄得一團糟。

column1: They are not very good uncooked.
column2: 沒煮熟的可不怎麼好吃。

column1: Only 1 fals for one of my delicious felafels.
column2: 我這美味的法拉費，一份只要一枚銅幣。

column1: Gluttony is what the Christians call one of the Seven Deadly Sins, you know. That is quite enough with the felafels already.
column2: 你知道嗎，貪食是基督徒口中的七宗罪之一。法拉費就吃到這裡吧，夠了。

column1: I rather doubt she would wish to part with that.
column2: 我很懷疑她會捨得割捨那個。

column1: I have been craving a bit of lamb. Thank you for bringing it.
column2: 我一直饞著想吃點羊肉呢。多謝你帶來。

column1: Why are you asking ME?
column2: 你為何問我？

column1: That would be like giving wool to the sheep, do you not think?
column2: 那豈不是像把羊毛送給羊，你不覺得嗎？

column1: I have no room for it, thank you all the same.
column2: 我沒地方放這個，但還是謝謝你。

column1: Really, you are too kind, but I could not take it.
column2: 真的，你太客氣了，但我不能收下。

column1: Very pretty. Maybe my neighbor, Ibrahim, would be interested.
column2: 真漂亮。或許我的鄰居易布拉興會有興趣。

column1: What, do I look rich?
column2: 怎麼，我看起來像是有錢人嗎？

column1: Buy another one, if you please.
column2: 勞煩再買一份吧。

column1: You mean like a cup? Farabi across the street sells cups.
column2: 你是說像杯子那樣的東西？街對面的法拉比有賣杯子。

column1: Galahad? What a strange name.
column2: 葛拉漢？好奇怪的名字。

column1: I am cooking felafels, of course.
column2: 我當然是在煮法拉費。

column1: He simply appeared days ago and never says a word. An orphan, no doubt.
column2: 他就這麼幾天前冒出來的，一句話也不說。想必是個孤兒。

column1: I use very fine ingredients in my felafels.
column2: 我的法拉費用的都是上等食材。

column1: I cook the felafels in my cauldron, until they are just right.
column2: 我在鍋裡煮法拉費，煮到恰到好處為止。

column1: He knows cloth well, but he has much to learn about women.
column2: 他對布料很懂，但論起女人，他還有得學。

column1: I cannot help you with that.
column2: 這事我幫不上忙。

column1: Help yourself.
column2: 自己拿去吧。

column1: But you must eat it quickly or it will crumble. My felafels are as delicate as they are delicious.
column2: 但你得快點吃，不然它會碎掉。我的法拉費，好吃歸好吃，卻也一樣易碎。

column1: I can sense how much you enjoyed that crisp, hot felafel.
column2: 我看得出來，你有多喜歡那份酥脆熱燙的法拉費。

column1: I fail to see how you could have enjoyed that with the eyes of that poor hungry urchin upon you.
column2: 那可憐飢餓的流浪孩子盯著你看，我實在不懂你怎麼吃得下去。

column1: Under Sarah's care, he will be happy and healthy. Right you are to feel proud of this deed.
column2: 在莎拉的照料下，他會過得快樂又健康。你為此感到自豪，是應該的。

column1: He is only a young boy, a half-starved, ragged urchin who is surely alone in the world. What a pathetic sight!
column2: 他不過是個小男孩，半飢半飽、衣衫襤褸，想必在這世上孤苦無依。多麼可憐的景象！

column1: You will need to move closer to the boy, but gently! He is alone and afraid.
column2: 你得再靠近那孩子一些，但要輕柔！他孤單又害怕。

column1: One of your felafels is reduced to crumbs from too much handling.
column2: 你有一份法拉費，因為拿太久，已經碎成渣了。

column1: Your only felafel is reduced to crumbs from too much handling.
column2: 你僅剩的那份法拉費，因為拿太久，已經碎成渣了。

column1: Of the Arab and Hebrew writing, I can tell you nothing, but the Latin is easy: "fictilia" refers to pottery, "cetarius" means fishmonger, and "horreum" is a granary.
column2: 阿拉伯文與希伯來文的部分，我一無所知，但拉丁文倒是簡單：「fictilia」指陶器，「cetarius」指魚販，「horreum」則是穀倉。

column1: Across the street are three merchants.
column2: 街對面有三位商人。

column1: There is a merchant selling pottery, a fishmonger and a grain merchant.
column2: 這裡有一位賣陶器的商人、一位魚販，還有一位穀物商。

column1: The birds are perched upon the arch.
column2: 鳥兒棲在拱門上。

column1: Aye, there are birds pecking at dropped grain. Nothing unusual about that.
column2: 正是，有幾隻鳥在啄食掉落的穀粒，沒什麼稀奇的。

column1: You have startled the birds and sent them flying.
column2: 你驚動了那些鳥，牠們都飛走了。

column1: It is a pottery shop, though he undoubtedly deals in more than mere ceramics.
column2: 這是間陶器店，不過他做的生意想必不只陶器。

column1: It is a fishmonger's shop.
column2: 這是間魚舖。

column1: It is a granary.
column2: 這是座穀倉。

column1: The only symbol I see is a stalk of grain on the horreum.
column2: 我只看得出一個符號——穀倉上的一株麥穗。

column1: Looks like a sleek, well-fed cat with a taste for fish.
column2: 看起來是隻毛色油亮、養得肥胖的貓，愛吃魚。

column1: I cannot say what fish they are, but they smell bad enough.
column2: 我說不出那是什麼魚，但氣味已經夠難聞了。

column1: The fragrant herbs have certainly improved this part of the bazaar.
column2: 這些香草，確實讓市集這一帶好聞了不少。

column1: The restless grain merchant has huge jars presumably filled with grain.
column2: 那位坐立難安的穀物商，擺著幾個大罐子，想必裝的都是穀物。

column1: The huge clay jars are filled with grain.
column2: 這些大陶罐裡裝滿了穀物。

column1: He is a most agitated man.
column2: 他是個十分焦躁不安的人。

column1: The birds are happy as they are. Leave them alone.
column2: 鳥兒就這樣挺自在的，別去打擾牠們。

column1: The scents from the fishmonger's stall are vastly improved.
column2: 魚販攤子傳來的氣味，已經好聞許多。

column1: The smell of the fishmonger's wares is an assault to the nose.
column2: 魚販貨品的氣味，簡直是對鼻子的一種侵犯。

column1: The grain merchant will not stop pacing. He is a most agitated man.
column2: 那位穀物商踱步不停，是個十分焦躁不安的人。

column1: He is the fattest merchant I have ever seen.
column2: 他是我見過最胖的商人。

column1: The pottery he has on display outside his shop is really quite plain, more for function than pleasure, I would say.
column2: 他店外陳列的陶器相當樸素，依我看，重實用而不重美觀。

column1: He has a number of earthenware jars on display.
column2: 他陳列著不少陶罐。

column1: His shelves display plain, but well-made pieces of pottery. Probably only his least valuable wares, considering the problem with thieves.
column2: 他架上擺的陶器樸素卻做工紮實。考慮到竊賊猖獗，這些想必只是他最不值錢的貨色。

column1: Welcome back. Let me know if I may serve you.
column2: 歡迎回來。若有什麼能為你效勞的，儘管開口。

column1: I have but two wishes in the world. One is that the wind which blows down this street will not change, so that the smell of fish stays away from my shop.
column2: 我在這世上只有兩個願望。其一，是這街上吹的風永遠別變向，好讓魚腥味遠離我的鋪子。

column1: And the other? Why, to sell you something. A mug or bowl of earthenware perhaps. Inside, under lock and key, I have fine silver plates and goblets. I have a few other items, probably of no interest to you, such as mirrors.
column2: 另一個？當然是賣你點東西。或許一只陶杯或陶碗？我店裡上鎖收著的，還有上好的銀盤與高腳杯。此外也有些別的物件，你大概不感興趣，比如鏡子。

column1: Please speak if there is anything I might sell you.
column2: 若有什麼想買的，儘管開口。

column1: Be not misled by my sign, habib. True, I deal in earthenware -- bowls and plates and jugs and vases for everyday use, but I have richer wares which are not safe to display on this street.
column2: 莫被我的招牌給誤導了，朋友。沒錯，我是賣陶器——日常用的碗、盤、罐、瓶，但我還有更貴重的貨色，在這條街上可不敢公然陳列。

column1: I have silver plates, bowls, goblets. Plain or worked with design. Shined to glimmering perfection. I sell mirrors as well.
column2: 我有銀盤、銀碗、高腳杯，素面的或雕花的都有，擦得光亮閃耀。我也賣鏡子。

column1: Even gold plates and goblets I can make to order, if your wealth is great enough. Plain or patterned or encrusted with jewels.
column2: 就連金盤與金杯，我也能訂製——只要你財力夠雄厚。素面的、雕花的，或鑲滿寶石的，皆可。

column1: I am at your service when you know what you want...and can show the coin for it.
column2: 等你想清楚要買什麼……又拿得出錢來，我隨時恭候。

column1: No coin, no sale.
column2: 沒錢就沒生意。

column1: I am not sure what you wish to buy.
column2: 我不確定你想買什麼。

column1: Come, come. That is not enough.
column2: 來吧，來吧，這樣可不夠。

column1: I am most sorry. The mirrors I have left are all promised to ladies of the Sultan's harem.
column2: 深感抱歉，我剩下的鏡子都已許給蘇丹後宮的女眷了。

column1: Certainly! I have a nice mirror for only 2 dirhams.
column2: 當然！我這兒有一面上好的鏡子，只要兩枚銀幣。

column1: I have the finest pottery in the city. Nowhere else will you find such quality.
column2: 我這裡有全城最好的陶器，別處絕找不到這等品質。

column1: I have the finest pottery anywhere.
column2: 我這裡的陶器，天下無雙。

column1: I deal in earthenware -- bowls and plates and jugs and vases for everyday use, but I have richer wares which are not safe to display on this street.
column2: 我經營陶器——日常用的碗、盤、罐、瓶，但我還有更貴重的貨品，不便擺在這條街上展示。

column1: It is strange, is it not, that fish taste fair but smell foul.
column2: 說來也奇怪，魚吃起來鮮美，聞起來卻臭。

column1: Ali will always find something to complain about.
column2: 阿里總能找到抱怨的理由。

column1: It is latin for pottery, more or less.
column2: 這大致上是拉丁文，意思是陶器。

column1: A curse upon all thieves!
column2: 願詛咒降臨在所有竊賊身上！

column1: I have little to say about that.
column2: 這事我沒什麼好說的。

column1: You joke with me. I would not sully my hands with fish.
column2: 你在跟我開玩笑吧。我才不會弄髒了手去碰魚。

column1: Two doors down you will find grain.
column2: 往前兩間店，就能找到賣穀物的。

column1: Why would you want to carry around expensive table wares? Concentrate on what you truly need.
column2: 你何必帶著昂貴的餐具到處走？把心思放在真正需要的東西上吧。

column1: It would be a bulky thing to carry about and of no great use. Concentrate on what you truly need.
column2: 這東西又笨重又沒什麼用處。把心思放在真正需要的東西上吧。

column1: I sell only plates, jars, vases, jugs, bowls, goblets, mirrors, and such items.
column2: 我只賣盤子、罈子、花瓶、罐子、碗、高腳杯、鏡子這類東西。

column1: Ummm...of what use are these to me?
column2: 嗯……這些東西對我有什麼用？

column1: If you wish to buy, I am at your service. If not, go away.
column2: 你若要買，我隨時效勞。不買的話，就請離開。

column1: One moment, habibi.
column2: 稍候片刻，朋友。

column1: Here you are, a very fine mirror.
column2: 給您，這是一面上好的鏡子。

column1: He is bent from a lifetime of toil at sea, and burdened with an injury.
column2: 他因一輩子在海上勞碌而佝僂著背，還帶著一身舊傷。

column1: The two baskets on his counter are full of fish.
column2: 他櫃檯上的兩個籃子裡裝滿了魚。

column1: The fishmonger is selling fish, of course.
column2: 這魚販自然是在賣魚。

column1: I see no jars in the fishmonger's shop.
column2: 魚販的攤子上沒有罈子。

column1: The cat, in typical cat fashion, ignores you.
column2: 這隻貓一如貓的習性，對你不理不睬。

column1: It is so well fed by the fishmonger that it utterly ignores you.
column2: 魚販把牠餵得肥肥胖胖，牠對你完全不屑一顧。

column1: That is not the behaviour of a king.
column2: 這可不是身為君王該有的舉止。

column1: Forget the cat. You have things to do.
column2: 別管那隻貓了，你還有正事要辦。

column1: Fish for sale! St. Peter's Fish and carp.
column2: 賣魚囉！聖彼得魚與鯉魚！

column1: I want only to sell my fish in peace without the snarls and threats of my neighbors, Ali and Fawaz. They complain that my fish stink, that the wind blows the smell into their shops.
column2: 我只想安安穩穩地賣我的魚，不必聽鄰居阿里和法瓦茲的咆哮與威脅。他們老抱怨我的魚臭，說風把味道吹進了他們的店裡。

column1: What can I do?! Fish smell like fish. Am I to change the very nature of life itself, or command the wind not to blow?
column2: 我能怎麼辦？！魚聞起來就是有魚味。難道要我改變生命本身的天性，或是命令風不要吹嗎？

column1: I will be a happy man only when they leave me in peace.
column2: 只有他們不再來煩我，我才能快活。

column1: Thank you for the herbs, habibi. You are not bad, for a foreigner.
column2: 謝謝你送的藥草，朋友。以一個外邦人來說，你人還不錯。

column1: I can see you are not truly interested in buying fish.
column2: 看得出來，你並非真心想買魚。

column1: Why on earth would you want to carry about a raw, smelly fish?
column2: 你到底為什麼想帶著一條生腥的魚到處走？

column1: Try Farabi next door.
column2: 去試試隔壁的法拉比。

column1: Did you not notice Ali next door?
column2: 你沒注意到隔壁的阿里嗎？

column1: I would direct you next door to Ali, but he is upset over the smell of my fish filling his shop, that he has virtually ceased to do business.
column2: 我本該叫你去隔壁找阿里，但他為了我魚攤的臭味瀰漫他店裡而動怒，生意都快做不下去了。

column1: No, no, my cat is not for sale.
column2: 不、不，我的貓不賣。

column1: He is useful enough and I always have scraps he can eat.
column2: 牠挺有用的，而且我總有些魚雜碎能餵牠。

column1: I have sold fish here all my life, and my father and his fathers before him.
column2: 我一輩子都在這裡賣魚，我父親和他的父輩也都是如此。

column1: Ah, it happened long ago. I wrestled with a shark and lost.
column2: 啊，那是很久以前的事了。我跟一條鯊魚搏鬥，輸了。

column1: He sells good pots and is honest enough, as merchants go.
column2: 他賣的陶器不錯，以商人來說也算誠實。

column1: As you can see, he sells grain.
column2: 你也看到了，他賣的是穀物。

column1: Ali refuses to sell me grain any more! He does nothing but complain about the smell of my fish.
column2: 阿里再也不肯賣穀物給我了！他成天只會抱怨我魚的臭味。

column1: They make my neighbors more friendly and will surely improve my business.
column2: 這些東西能讓我的鄰居們友善些，想必也會讓我的生意好轉。

column1: The word has always been there above my door. It has something to do with fish, I suppose.
column2: 那個字一直掛在我門上。我想大概是跟魚有關吧。

column1: I hate thieves. They prey upon me because of my injured leg.
column2: 我痛恨竊賊。他們就因為我腿有傷，才敢欺負我。

column1: I am sorry, habibi, but I cannot help you.
column2: 抱歉，朋友，這事我幫不了你。

column1: So? What does this mean to me? They do smell fragrant, I must admit.
column2: 那又如何？這跟我有什麼關係？不過我得承認，它們聞起來確實芬芳。

column1: No, no, I do not want it.
column2: 不、不，我不要這個。

column1: He looks like an ordinary Arab merchant.
column2: 他看起來像個尋常的阿拉伯商人。

column1: I am most grateful to you for giving Hayyam the herbs. That smell of fish was driving me mad!
column2: 多謝你把藥草送給哈耶姆。那股魚腥味都快把我逼瘋了！

column1: I have the best grain in all of Jerusalem. How may I serve you?
column2: 我這裡有全耶路撒冷最好的穀物。有什麼能為您效勞的？

column1: This man is so agitated, he will not stand still long enough to talk to you.
column2: 這人焦躁不安，一刻也靜不下來跟你說話。

column1: You cannot even speak to him, let alone give him money.
column2: 你連跟他說話都辦不到，更別提給他錢了。

column1: Return when you know what you want.
column2: 想清楚要買什麼再回來吧。

column1: You are carrying around quite enough as it is.
column2: 你身上帶的東西已經夠多了。

column1: I must have at least 3 fals, since the bag alone is worth 2 coins. The grain is 1 fals for 1 scoop.
column2: 我至少得收三枚銅幣，光是袋子就值兩枚錢幣了。穀物是一勺一枚銅幣。

column1: He will not stop to talk.
column2: 他不肯停下來說話。

column1: You will have no luck with him.
column2: 跟他打交道，你不會有什麼運氣。

column1: If he would ever stand still, you might be able to do business with him.
column2: 若他哪天肯站定不動，你或許就能跟他做成生意。

column1: One scoop of grain for 1 fals.
column2: 一勺穀物，一枚銅幣。

column1: One scoop of grain for 1 fals, 2 fals for the bag to carry it in, since I see you have not brought a bag for grain.
column2: 一勺穀物一枚銅幣，裝穀物的袋子再加兩枚銅幣——我看你沒帶裝穀物的袋子來。

column1: I only sell the bags with the grain. Grain is my business, not bags.
column2: 我只在買穀物時才附袋子。我做的是穀物生意，不是賣袋子。

column1: I bought these grain jars from the pottery merchant. Paid too much for them, that is what I think.
column2: 這些裝穀物的罈子，是我跟陶器商買的。我看是買貴了。

column1: Those herbs had better work for a long time. I will go mad if I have to smell his fish again.
column2: 這些藥草最好能撐久一點，若再讓我聞到他那魚腥味，我會發瘋的。

column1: Eh? Why do you ask me this?
column2: 嗯？你為何這麼問我？

column1: You are a most strange man. I have all these jars full of grain, why should I want grain from you?
column2: 你這人真是奇怪。我這裡的罈子都裝滿了穀物，我何必跟你要穀物？

column1: No, thank you.
column2: 不用了，謝謝。

column1: Here is your grain.
column2: 這是你的穀物。

column1: Lucernae means "lamps". As for the Greek underneath, I cannot translate it. My Greek is too long out of use.
column2: 「Lucernae」的意思是「燈」。至於下面那行希臘文，我譯不出來，我的希臘文荒廢太久了。

column1: Across the street are several merchants.
column2: 街對面有幾位商人。

column1: You should know the lamp shop well enough and the Seeress is still with her apples.
column2: 你對這間燈鋪應該已經很熟了，那位女預言家也還在賣她的蘋果。

column1: There is the lamp shop. And you now know that the old woman is far more than she appears to be.
column2: 那是燈鋪。而你如今也知道，那位老婦人絕非表面看來那麼簡單。

column1: Upon the left is a lamp shop. The old woman on the right is selling apples.
column2: 左邊是一間燈鋪，右邊的老婦人在賣蘋果。

column1: Lucernae means that he sells lamps.
column2: 「Lucernae」意思是他賣燈。

column1: They are ceramic, made in the yoni style. When filled with oil, a flame will burn in the lamp's spout.
column2: 這些是陶製的，做成陰形的樣式。注滿油後，燈嘴便會燃起火焰。

column1: The yoni style is...ahem...well, shaped after a certain part of a woman.
column2: 這陰形樣式……咳……嗯，是仿照女子身上某個部位做成的。

column1: It looks like an ordinary, well-made broom.
column2: 這看起來是把做工精良、卻很尋常的掃帚。

column1: He has a bundle of sweetly pungent herbs hanging in the doorway.
column2: 他門口掛著一束氣味濃郁香甜的藥草。

column1: Aye, he has charcoal for sale.
column2: 是的，他有炭在賣。

column1: I suppose some of these jars contain various scented oils for the lamps, though some of the vases seem to be purely decorative.
column2: 我想這些罈子裡有些裝著供燈用的各式香油，不過有些花瓶似乎純粹是擺設。

column1: On the lamp merchant's shelves are jars, bottles, and vases.
column2: 燈鋪商人的架上擺著罈子、瓶子與花瓶。

column1: They are finely made, perhaps designed to hold ground herbs or spices or perfumed oils.
column2: 它們做工精細，或許是用來盛裝磨碎的藥草、香料或是香油。

column1: It looks quite ordinary.
column2: 看起來相當尋常。

column1: The old woman's basket is filled with the small green apples common to this area.
column2: 老婦人的籃子裡裝滿了這一帶常見的小青蘋果。

column1: Do as she instructs. That is the best advice I can give you.
column2: 照她的指示去做。這是我能給你最好的建議。

column1: You are meant to find her by your own devices.
column2: 你得靠自己找到她。

column1: You surely do not refer to the old woman selling apples? It has been many decades since she was a girl.
column2: 你該不會是指那位賣蘋果的老婦人吧？她做姑娘的時候，都已是幾十年前的事了。

column1: Your wisdom and character are being tested. Act wisely.
column2: 你的智慧與品格正受到考驗，行事務必明智。

column1: He appears to be a typical, prosperous Arab merchant.
column2: 他看起來是個典型、生意興隆的阿拉伯商人。

column1: The lamp shop appears to carry quite a few other items besides oil lamps.
column2: 這間燈鋪除了油燈之外，似乎還賣不少別的東西。

column1: I am most pleased to see such a fine customer return. I am at your service.
column2: 很高興見到您這樣的貴客再度光臨，我隨時為您效勞。

column1: 'Tis odd. I feel I must tell you that although I am content with my lot, for I am an honest man, I would be happier still if my cousin, Achmed, had not broken his oath to me and thus ruined our friendship.
column2: 說來奇怪，我覺得該告訴您——雖然我這人誠實，也安於自己的境況，但若我表弟阿賀密德當初沒有背棄誓言、毀了我們的情誼，我會更快活些。

column1: Let us not dwell on Achmed the Oathbreaker. My wares include lamps, oil, vases, jars, bottles, herbs and charcoal. How may I serve you?
column2: 別再提那背信的阿賀密德了。我的貨品有燈、油、花瓶、罈子、瓶子、藥草和炭。有什麼能為您效勞的？

column1: Please do not hesitate to ask for something.
column2: 您若想要什麼，請儘管開口。

column1: A thousand apologies, but I have no use for a mule.
column2: 萬分抱歉，但我用不上騾子。

column1: Have you changed your mind? Well, no matter. Come back any time.
column2: 您改變主意了嗎？沒關係，歡迎隨時再來。

column1: I am sorry, I must not have been listening properly. What did you wish to purchase?
column2: 抱歉，我方才想必沒聽仔細。您想買什麼？

column1: Forgive a humble merchant, habib, but this is not enough for what you wish to buy.
column2: 請恕小商人失禮，朋友，但這些錢不夠買您想要的東西。

column1: But, habib, I sold it to you. What sort of merchant would I be to take it back?
column2: 可是，朋友，這東西我已經賣給您了。若又收回，我還算什麼商人？

column1: Surely you need it more than I.
column2: 您想必比我更需要它。

column1: Some of these herbs are quite rare, but for you only 1 dirham.
column2: 這些藥草有些相當珍稀，不過看在您的份上，只要一枚銀幣。

column1: I sold you the last bundle.
column2: 最後一束，我已經賣給您了。

column1: A good-sized bag of charcoal is only 2 fals.
column2: 一大袋炭，只要兩枚銅幣。

column1: It is messy stuff to carry about. Once is enough.
column2: 這東西帶著到處走挺髒的，一次就夠了。

column1: But you took the only broom, habibi.
column2: 但那把唯一的掃帚，您已經拿走了，朋友。

column1: I am not fooled. I saw you speaking with my cousin, Achmed the Oathbreaker, and I can guess what he has sent you here to do.
column2: 我可沒被騙。我見您和我那背信的表弟阿賀密德說過話，猜得出他派您來此有何用意。

column1: You see, Achmed went on a pilgrimage. I could not come with him, which grieved me, so I made him swear he would bring me a holy relic.
column2: 是這樣的，阿賀密德去朝聖時，我沒能同行，這事讓我十分傷心，於是我要他發誓會替我帶回一件聖物。

column1: But he did not. He said nothing of it and why should I go begging? Nay, I have not spoken to him since and no broom will he get from me!
column2: 可是他沒有做到。他隻字未提，我又何必去乞求？不，自那以後我便再沒跟他說過話，他休想從我這兒拿到一把掃帚！

column1: It is not for sale. I keep it here in plain sight and refuse to sell it because it annoys my cousin, Achmed, against whom I have a grudge.
column2: 這東西不賣。我故意把它擺在顯眼處、不肯賣掉，就是要氣氣我那心懷怨懟的表弟阿賀密德。

column1: I had rope, but it was all stolen by a miserable little thief who preys upon this bazaar.
column2: 我原有繩子，卻全被一個在這市集裡橫行的可惡小賊偷光了。

column1: Do not overburden yourself with something you do not truly need.
column2: 別為了不真正需要的東西而讓自己負擔過重。

column1: They are of the finest quality.
column2: 這些都是上等的品質。

column1: Thanks to you, habibi, my cousin and I will be friends again. I admit, I have missed visiting his inn.
column2: 多虧了您，朋友，我和表弟又能重修舊好了。我得承認，我挺懷念去他客棧作客的日子。

column1: Achmed promised me that he would bring back a holy relic from his pilgrimage, but he did not, so I curse him as an oathbreaker.
column2: 阿賀密德答應過我，朝聖歸來時會帶回一件聖物，他卻沒做到，所以我咒他是個背信之人。

column1: He broke a solemn oath to me for which I cannot forgive him.
column2: 他對我背棄了莊嚴的誓言，這事我無法原諒。

column1: She is a strange old woman, but her apples are marvelous.
column2: 她是個古怪的老婦人，但她的蘋果著實美味。

column1: Any relic would satisfy me, though a relic of the holy Elzer would make me truly joyous.
column2: 任何聖物都能讓我滿足，不過若是聖艾爾澤的聖物，我會真正欣喜若狂。

column1: Why, surely you can guess that it means lamps.
column2: 哎呀，您想必猜得出，那意思是燈。

column1: I would do much to get my hands on the thief who keeps stealing all my rope!
column2: 我願不惜代價，抓住那個老是偷我繩子的賊！

column1: Perhaps I can interest you in something else, habib. I have many fine wares.
column2: 或許您對別的東西有興趣，朋友。我這裡好貨不少。

column1: Of what interest is that?
column2: 那跟我有什麼關係？

column1: I am sorry, but I am not interested.
column2: 抱歉，我沒有興趣。

column1: Why should I buy back what I am selling?
column2: 我自己在賣的東西，何必買回來？

column1: A genuine relic! It is not as pleasurable as receiving it from my cousin, Achmed, but....I will give you 1 dirham.
column2: 真正的聖物！雖不如親手從我表弟阿賀密德那兒收到來得暢快，但……我給您一枚銀幣。

column1: No, keep it. I have no need for it.
column2: 不用了，您留著吧，我用不上。

column1: Sa'alam aleikem, good sir. You look like a man of taste. Notice the fine craftsmanship of my lamps. My lamp oils are of the purest quality.
column2: Sa'alam aleikem，貴客。您看來是位識貨之人。請看我這些燈精湛的做工，我的燈油也是最純淨的品質。

column1: If lamps are not to your taste, I carry good, long- burning charcoal for your brazier.
column2: 若燈不合您的心意，我這裡還有耐燒的好炭，供您火盆之用。

column1: Are not these herbs sublimely fragrant? They sweeten the air and lend freshness to even the foulest room.
column2: 難道這些藥草不是芳香無比嗎？它們能使空氣芬芳，即便是最污穢的房間也能為之一新。

column1: For sweetness of the body I have scented oils that will moisten the skin and inflame passions.
column2: 若要滋養肌膚，我這裡備有香油，能潤澤肌膚，撩動情慾。

column1: My vases and bottles are made by the finest artisans. Feast your eyes upon the delicate colors.
column2: 我的花瓶與瓶罐皆出自名匠之手，且盡情飽覽這些精緻的色澤。

column1: If you desire to buy, I am ready to serve you.
column2: 你若有意購買，我隨時為你效勞。

column1: Here are the herbs, habibi. A pleasure to do business with you.
column2: 藥草在此，朋友。與你交易，是我的榮幸。

column1: Here is the charcoal. Return any time I may be of further service.
column2: 炭在此。若還有需要，歡迎隨時再來。

column1: Good sir, I am speechless! Surely my cousin, Achmed, has sent this through you as an offering of peace between us.
column2: 好心的先生，我真是說不出話來！這想必是我表兄阿賀密德託你送來，作為我倆和解的表示。

column1: Now I am ashamed that I behaved in such a petty way. Please, I beg you, take this broom and give it to Achmed and he will know that this is my apology.
column2: 如今我為自己那般小器的行徑感到羞愧。求你把這把掃帚帶給阿賀密德，他自會明白這是我的歉意。

column1: I detect an unusual look of wisdom in this old woman's eyes.
column2: 你察覺這位老婦人的眼中，透著一股不尋常的智慧。

column1: The small green apples in her basket are native to this region and rather tart, I believe.
column2: 她籃裡的小青蘋果是本地土產，想來滋味相當酸澀。

column1: That would be most unwise.
column2: 那實在不是明智之舉。

column1: I hope you find what you seek, but I have no further help to give you.
column2: 但願你能尋得所求之物，只是我已無力再助你了。

column1: Seek Fatima now! You have no time to waste.
column2: 速去尋找法提瑪！你已沒有時間可以浪費。

column1: Your greed has betrayed you. You chose to sell what you should have given freely. You are not worthy. Be gone from my sight.
column2: 你的貪婪出賣了你。本該無私贈與之物，你卻選擇了販售。你不配得此殊榮，速從我眼前退下。

column1: Nothing more will I say or give until you have completed every task.
column2: 在你完成每一項考驗之前，我不會再多說一句、多給一物。

column1: You have made your choice. Now you must live with it.
column2: 你已做出抉擇，如今便須承受這抉擇的後果。

column1: King Arthur, I know your purpose here. It is given to me to know such things, for I am a seeress.
column2: 亞瑟王，我知曉你此行的目的。這等事物我自能洞悉，因我是位女先知。

column1: Another came from your land and his name was Galahad. He spoke of you, for if he failed, he knew only you might follow and succeed.
column2: 曾有一人從你的國度而來，名叫葛拉漢。他提起過你，因為他深知，若自己失敗，唯有你能繼之而成。

column1: But as a servant of the Goddess, I must know you are worthy. I bid you to buy an apple, for this fruit is sacred to Aphrodite.
column2: 但身為女神的僕人，我必須確認你當得起此殊榮。我命你買下一顆蘋果，因這果實是阿芙羅黛蒂的聖物。

column1: Buying the apple is but the first test I shall place before you, if you are ready.
column2: 買下這顆蘋果，不過是我為你設下的第一道考驗，如果你已準備好的話。

column1: You have the apple that ends hunger, slakes thirst, and eases weariness. May it comfort you in time of greatest need.
column2: 你已得到這顆能止饑、解渴、消除疲憊的蘋果。願它在你最需要之時，予你慰藉。

column1: You have purchased the only apple I will sell you.
column2: 你已買下我唯一願意賣給你的蘋果。

column1: One apple, and one only, I will sell you. Here are your choices.
column2: 我只會賣給你一顆蘋果，僅此一顆。以下是你的選擇。

column1: If you give me 1 fals, I will give you an apple that is only an apple and nothing more. Eat, and it will taste good.
column2: 若你給我一枚銅幣，我會給你一顆平凡無奇的蘋果。吃下去，滋味不錯。

column1: If you give me 1 dirham, I will give you an apple that will satisfy all your hunger, slake all your thirst and ease your weariness.
column2: 若你給我一枚銀幣，我會給你一顆能止盡你的饑餓、解盡你的乾渴、消除你疲憊的蘋果。

column1: If you give me 1 dinar, I will give you an apple that is bitter to the tongue, yet you will know the taste of Truth.
column2: 若你給我一枚金幣，我會給你一顆入口苦澀，卻能讓你嚐到真理滋味的蘋果。

column1: It is obvious what I have and do not have.
column2: 我有什麼、沒有什麼，一目瞭然。

column1: Give me nothing and you gain nothing.
column2: 你若什麼都不給，便什麼也得不到。

column1: You have already bought the only apple I will sell you.
column2: 你已買下我唯一願意賣給你的蘋果了。

column1: If you wish to buy an apple, please say so.
column2: 你若想買蘋果，儘管開口。

column1: Nay, I need it not.
column2: 不，我不需要它。

column1: Such things are not sacred to the Goddess.
column2: 這類東西並非女神的聖物。

column1: I am a lesser servant of the Goddess and do not know where it is to be found. Only Fatima can provide the guidance you need.
column2: 我不過是女神座下的一名小小僕人，不知此物何處可尋。唯有法提瑪能給你所需的指引。

column1: She is the great mother of all, whom we call Aphrodite
column2: 她是萬物的偉大母親，我們稱她為阿芙羅黛蒂

column1: She is the Great Goddess, mother of the universe, creator of gods.
column2: 她是偉大的女神，宇宙之母，眾神的創造者。

column1: I serve Aphrodite.
column2: 我侍奉阿芙羅黛蒂。

column1: You have seen her. What more is there to say?
column2: 你已見過她了，還有什麼好說的？

column1: You will learn about Fatima if you are found worthy.
column2: 若你被判定為當得起此殊榮，自會知曉法提瑪之事。

column1: You will find her with the symbols of the Goddess, the star and crescent.
column2: 你能在女神的標識——星與新月——之處尋得她。

column1: He came here only recently, after long weeks of search in other places. But I have not seen him for many days.
column2: 他是近日才到此地，之前在別處尋訪了數週之久。但我已有多日未曾見過他了。

column1: I know nothing of them.
column2: 我對他們一無所知。

column1: You must be a wise man to find a wise man.
column2: 唯有智者，方能尋得智者。

column1: Whosoever you speak with in this bazaar will be compelled to speak the truth about what he or she most deeply needs or wants.
column2: 在這市集中，凡與你交談之人，皆會不由自主地道出內心最深切的渴求。

column1: Your task is to do as your soul and heart dictate. Only you can decide what that means.
column2: 你的職責，是依循自己的靈魂與內心行事。這意味著什麼，唯有你自己能夠決定。

column1: Speak with him and judge his character for yourself.
column2: 與他交談，親自評斷他的品格。

column1: Only by seeking it will you be able to attain it.
column2: 唯有透過尋求，你才能有所得。

column1: There are six Guardians whose tests you must pass. I am one of them.
column2: 共有六位守護者，你必須通過她們的考驗，而我便是其中之一。

column1: It was not planned as a part of your test, if that is what you wonder.
column2: 你若在納悶，那並非我考驗你的一環。

column1: A seeress knows which questions are worth answering and which should be ignored.
column2: 女先知自知哪些提問值得回答，哪些該置之不理。

column1: Take this, and by my command, eat of it.
column2: 拿去，並依我之命，吃下它。

column1: You have chosen wisely, for the apple has conferred upon you a Truth Spell. Whoever you speak with in this bazaar from this moment on will confide to you his or her most secret and urgent need.
column2: 你選得明智，這顆蘋果已賦予你真言術。從此刻起，在這市集中與你交談之人，皆會向你吐露內心最隱密、最迫切的需求。

column1: To prove your full worthiness to me, and thus be led ever closer to your goal, you must fulfill these tasks revealed for you by the Truth Spell. Your heart and mind must guide you.
column2: 為了向我證明你完全當得起此殊榮，並藉此更接近你的目標，你必須完成真言術為你揭示的這些任務。你的心與意志必須引領著你。

column1: You have eaten, but gained nothing. You failed my test and you will never possess the Grail. Your hopes die here.
column2: 你已吃下蘋果，卻一無所獲。你未能通過我的考驗，永遠也不會擁有聖杯。你的希望，就此終結。

column1: She spoke true. The apple has eased all your hunger and thirst. New strength flows into your limbs.
column2: 她所言不虛。這顆蘋果已消除了你所有的饑渴，一股新的力量注入你的四肢。

column1: You feel refreshed, yet you have failed miserably to pass my test. Your quest ends here. The Grail is denied to you.
column2: 你感到神清氣爽，然而你卻慘遭我的考驗所淘汰。你的探尋就此終止，聖杯與你無緣。

column1: I greet you with reverence, King Arthur, for you are indeed worthy. Knowledge is your reward.
column2: 我以敬意迎接你，亞瑟王，因你確實當得起此殊榮。知識，便是你的獎賞。

column1: Seek the star and crescent where Fatima dwells. Now that you are ready, she will admit you. She is the most powerful, though not the last, of the Guardians of the Sacred Cup.
column2: 尋著星與新月，前往法提瑪所居之處。如今你已準備就緒，她將接見你。她是聖杯守護者之中最有力者，卻並非最後一位。

column1: So you have suffered a misfortune? Very well, I will help you again.
column2: 你竟遭逢此等不幸？也罷，我再助你一次。

column1: Take also this gift.
column2: 再收下這件禮物吧。

column1: It is the apple that ends hunger, slakes thirst, and eases weariness. May it comfort you in time of greatest need. The Goddess be with you.
column2: 這是能止饑、解渴、消除疲憊的蘋果。願它在你最需要之時，予你慰藉。願女神與你同在。

column1: Here is an apple that will relieve all hunger and thirst and renew your strength.
column2: 這顆蘋果能消解一切饑渴，重振你的氣力。

column1: Do not lose THIS one.
column2: 這一顆，你千萬別再弄丟了。

column1: Let us say simply that it is someone's crude idea of a joke.
column2: 就這麼說吧，這不過是某人拙劣的惡作劇。

column1: It is only graffiti.
column2: 這不過是塗鴉。

column1: It is completely dark and deserted.
column2: 這裡一片漆黑，杳無人跡。

column1: The walls are far too high to jump over.
column2: 這牆太高了，跳不過去。

column1: The alley is paved with stone, solidly set. The thief could not have escaped through the ground.
column2: 這條巷子鋪著石板，結結實實。竊賊不可能從地面脫逃。

column1: The bars are made of heavy iron.
column2: 這些欄杆是以厚重的鐵條打造。

column1: It is a dead end alley with no doors and only two windows, one of which is bricked up and the other blocked by a heavy iron bar.
column2: 這是條死巷，沒有門，只有兩扇窗——一扇已被磚封死，另一扇則被厚重的鐵條擋住。

column1: The thief quickly pulls up his rope so you cannot follow!
column2: 竊賊迅速將繩子收起，教你無法跟上！

column1: The thief has escaped.
column2: 竊賊已然逃脫。

column1: There is no sign of him at all.
column2: 完全不見他的蹤影。

column1: The thief must have left behind a rope and climbed up it to escape.
column2: 竊賊想必是留下一條繩子，攀繩而上脫逃了。

column1: The lower window is bricked up. Only a skinny man could squeeze into the upper window, if he had the means to reach it.
column2: 下方的窗戶已被磚封死。唯有瘦小之人，若有辦法搆得到，方能擠進上方的窗戶。

column1: The walls are old and deteriorating on the surface, but solid underneath. No doors, no sign of hidden openings, no way to scale or climb them.
column2: 這些牆面古舊，表層已剝落，內裡卻依然堅實。沒有門，也不見任何暗藏的開口，無法攀爬翻越。

column1: They are very old, but quite solid.
column2: 它們雖已老舊，卻十分堅固。

column1: Judging from the smell, it is not something you want to step in.
column2: 從氣味判斷，那不是你會想踩上去的東西。

column1: A dog carcass is busily rotting.
column2: 一具狗屍正腐爛著。

column1: They swarm over the remains of the dog.
column2: 牠們群聚在狗的殘骸上。

column1: I would prefer not to guess as to what that is.
column2: 那究竟是什麼，我寧可不去猜測。

column1: The outer surface is crumbling. As for using the lower window as a foothold, you would not get far enough to do any good.
column2: 外層表面正在剝落。至於想拿下方的窗戶當立足點，你也搆不到什麼有用的地方。

column1: Powerful though Excaliber is, it still has its limits. These bars would destroy the blade.
column2: 聖劍雖然威力強大，仍有其極限。這些鐵條會毀了劍身。

column1: Had you followed him immediately, you might have at least had a chance to catch him. Now he could be anywhere.
column2: 你若立刻追上前去，至少還有機會逮住他。如今他已不知去向何方。

column1: This thief was cunning enough to climb down a rope from the barred window, leave the rope hanging, then scurry back up the rope and escape.
column2: 這竊賊夠狡猾，先順著繩子從有欄杆的窗戶爬下，留下繩子懸著，再匆匆攀繩而上逃走。

column1: Even Excaliber could not stop this quick and elusive thief.
column2: 即便是聖劍，也攔不住這身手敏捷、飄忽不定的竊賊。

column1: The thief has escaped. And you would blunt your fine blade by hacking uselessly at these heavy iron bars.
column2: 竊賊已然逃脫。而你若徒勞劈砍這些厚重的鐵條，只會鈍了你那把好劍。

column1: The combination of rotting dog and human excreta leaves much to be desired. Such as getting as far away from it as you can.
column2: 腐爛的狗屍混著人類排泄物，實在令人不敢恭維——比如，儘可能離它遠一點。

column1: The dog is dead, putrid and full of disease, Arthur. Leave it be.
column2: 這狗已死，腐臭不堪，滿身病菌，亞瑟，別去碰它。

column1: They are busy with the rotting dog.
column2: 牠們正忙著啃食那具腐爛的狗屍。

column1: The thief is too quick for you.
column2: 竊賊的身手比你快得多。

column1: The thief is gone.
column2: 竊賊已經走了。

column1: The thief is too busy escaping.
column2: 竊賊正忙著逃命。

column1: Caupona is the Latin for "inn" or "tavern". If I interpret the symbol below correctly, this is the "Star of Allah Inn".
column2: 「Caupona」在拉丁文中意為「客棧」或「酒館」。如果我沒解讀錯下方的符號，這裡便是「真主之星客棧」。

column1: The grain merchant's agitation is so great, he will not stand still long enough to speak or do business.
column2: 這穀物商人心浮氣躁，連好好站著說話做生意的耐性都沒有。

column1: Across the street are two merchants.
column2: 街道對面有兩名商人。

column1: Next to the grain merchant's shop, there is an inn.
column2: 穀物商人的店鋪旁，有一間客棧。

column1: It is a rather rundown place.
column2: 那是個相當破敗的地方。

column1: You cannot see inside with Achmed blocking the door.
column2: 阿賀密德擋在門口，你看不見裡頭的情形。

column1: Dare I say it? The inside does not look like an improvement on the outside. Still, he is offering his hospitality.
column2: 這話我也不知該不該說：裡頭似乎並不比外頭好上多少。不過，他仍盛情款待。

column1: My Arabic is not quite good enough to translate that.
column2: 我的阿拉伯語還沒好到能翻譯這個。

column1: The door is shut, to state the obvious.
column2: 這扇門是關著的，這是明擺著的事。

column1: The door is partway open.
column2: 這扇門半掩著。

column1: The door is open. You should either enter or move on.
column2: 這扇門開著。你該不進去，就得繼續前行。

column1: Nothing can be seen through these windows.
column2: 透過這些窗戶，什麼也看不見。

column1: It is too dim inside to make out much more than some crude tables and chairs.
column2: 裡頭光線昏暗，只能勉強看出幾張粗陋的桌椅。

column1: The shutters are closed.
column2: 百葉窗是關著的。

column1: It is not so much an alley as a gap between the buildings that is walled off. You can glimpse more back streets of Jerusalem, but nothing that is of use to you.
column2: 與其說是條巷子，不如說是建築之間被牆封住的一道縫隙。你能瞥見耶路撒冷更多的後街，但沒什麼對你有用的東西。

column1: There is no one here to ask.
column2: 這裡沒有人可問。

column1: The birds peck at grain spilt over from the merchant's pots.
column2: 鳥兒啄食著從商人罐子裡灑出的穀粒。

column1: You startled the birds into flight.
column2: 你驚起了那群鳥，牠們飛走了。

column1: The birds perch on the ledge, waiting for you to leave.
column2: 鳥兒棲在窗臺上，等著你離開。

column1: He stands on the other side of his shop.
column2: 他站在自己店鋪的另一側。

column1: Are you confused? There is no one here.
column2: 你糊塗了嗎？這裡沒有人。

column1: It does not smell particularly inviting inside.
column2: 裡頭的氣味可稱不上誘人。

column1: Achmed looks as rundown as his inn.
column2: 阿賀密德看起來和他的客棧一樣破敗。

column1: I do not see him.
column2: 我沒看見他。

column1: Achmed would let you in if he so desired.
column2: 阿賀密德若有意，自會讓你進去。

column1: Well? Will you enter or not?
column2: 怎麼樣？你到底進不進去？

column1: These windows cannot be opened from the outside.
column2: 這些窗戶無法從外面打開。

column1: The door is already open.
column2: 這扇門已經開著了。

column1: Talking to the door will not help.
column2: 對著門說話也無濟於事。

column1: Believe me, I regret I cannot serve you. If only I had a broom.
column2: 相信我，我很遺憾無法招待你。要是我有把掃帚就好了。

column1: Please enter, habibi. Allow me to show my gratitude by giving you food and drink while I clean up.
column2: 請進，朋友。且讓我以食物和飲水略表謝意，我這就去打掃。

column1: Perhaps he cannot hear you call.
column2: 或許他聽不見你的呼喚。

column1: Ah, I am in desperate need of a broom!
column2: 唉，我真是迫切需要一把掃帚！

column1: Thank you so very much for the broom, habibi!
column2: 太感謝你送的這把掃帚了，朋友！

column1: My cousin Tariq is angry with me and will not sell me a broom!
column2: 我表弟泰利克在生我的氣，不肯賣我掃帚！

column1: I never believed my cousin would give me the broom. Allah be praised!
column2: 我從沒想過表弟會把掃帚送給我。讚美真主！

column1: My inn is filthy. Only with a broom can I properly clean it.
column2: 我的客棧髒亂不堪，唯有一把掃帚才能將它徹底清理乾淨。

column1: Come in! Come in! I am still cleaning, but you are welcome.
column2: 進來吧！進來吧！我還在打掃，但歡迎你進來。

column1: It is the name of my inn, the 'Star of Allah.'
column2: 這是我旅店的名字，「阿拉之星」。

column1: The name of my inn is 'The Star of Allah.' Caupona means inn, habib.
column2: 我旅店的名字是「阿拉之星」。Caupona 的意思就是旅店，朋友。

column1: I do my best to keep them out of my inn.
column2: 我盡力不讓牠們靠近我的旅店。

column1: If I only had a broom, I would help you.
column2: 若我有把掃帚，我便會幫你。

column1: I cannot help you with that, but you can surely stay at my inn.
column2: 那件事我幫不上忙，但你儘管留宿在我的旅店。

column1: As much as I would like to take your money, I cannot think of serving you until I can clean my inn.
column2: 我雖然很想收你的錢，但旅店未清理乾淨之前，我實在無法招待你。

column1: I could never take your money, habibi. I am in your debt.
column2: 我絕不能收你的錢，朋友。我還欠著你的情。

column1: But he has the broom.
column2: 但掃帚在他手上。

column1: I will never part with this broom!
column2: 這把掃帚，我絕不會放手！

column1: Would that I HAD a broom!
column2: 但願我真的有把掃帚！

column1: Your generosity does you credit, but if I could have anything, I would only desire a broom.
column2: 你的慷慨令人敬佩，但若要我說想要什麼，我只求一把掃帚。

column1: I could not take another gift. I am in your debt already.
column2: 我不能再收你的禮物了，我已經欠你人情。

column1: Perhaps later, when I recover my losses from being closed for so long.
column2: 或許等日後吧，等我把歇業許久的損失彌補回來再說。

column1: One of the merchants on this street could doubtless sell you that.
column2: 這條街上的商人，想必有人能賣你那個。

column1: Odd that the inn should be locked.
column2: 旅店竟然上了鎖，真是奇怪。

column1: It is still locked.
column2: 依然上著鎖。

column1: Achmed is surely busy sweeping his floor. I doubt he will answer you.
column2: 阿賀密德想必正忙著掃地，我看他不會理你。

column1: I am not open for business. Go away.
column2: 我沒有營業，走開。

column1: I cannot open my shop. For weeks I have been without a broom and now I am overcome with filth. All because my cousin, Tariq, is angry with me and will not sell me a broom for any amount of coin. And I offered good money just for a broom!
column2: 我沒法開店。這幾個星期我都沒有掃帚，如今店裡髒亂不堪，全是因為我表弟泰利克在生我的氣，無論出多少錢都不肯賣我一把掃帚。我可是出了好價錢，就只為求一把掃帚啊！

column1: Do not blame me that I cannot offer you rest and food. Talk to Tariq, who has the stubbornness of a goat. He certainly will not talk to me!
column2: 我沒法供你歇腳用膳，這可不能怪我。去找泰利克談吧，那人跟山羊一樣倔強。他肯定是不會跟我說話的！

column1: I am sorry, but without a broom, I cannot open for business.
column2: 很抱歉，沒有掃帚，我沒法開店營業。

column1: Did you want something else? I thought you did.
column2: 你還想要別的嗎？我還以為你有事。

column1: Welcome, habibi, welcome! Come in!
column2: 歡迎，朋友，歡迎！請進！

column1: Until then, may I offer you the hospitality of my humble inn. Excuse the mess on the floor. I will clean it while you eat and drink at no charge.
column2: 在那之前，且容我以寒舍略盡地主之誼。地上凌亂，還請見諒，你儘管吃喝，我這就分文不收，一邊替你打掃。

column1: You have eaten well and spent a restless night being bitten by bedbugs and dreaming about Camelot, Gwenhyver, and the Grail.
column2: 你飽餐一頓，卻在床蝨叮咬與夢見肯萊特、昆海兒與聖杯之中，度過了一夜輾轉難眠。

column1: A new sense of urgency fills you. The land and the people will not survive much longer unless you can find the Grail!
column2: 一股新的迫切感湧上心頭。除非你能尋得聖杯，否則這片土地與人民撐不了多久了！

column1: Good, I am glad you have the sense not to dally at an inn when your entire kingdom is at stake.
column2: 很好，你的王國正處存亡之際，你懂得不在旅店裡蹉跎，這讓我甚感欣慰。

column1: I can see why you did not remain. You have gotten more flea bites from this brief visit than in all your years in Camelot.
column2: 我明白你為何沒有留下。這趟短暫停留，你被跳蚤咬的次數，竟比你在肯萊特這些年加起來還多。

column1: Do you think you could possibly stop blundering around terrifying the natives long enough to do what you are supposed to be doing?
column2: 你能不能別再橫衝直撞驚嚇當地百姓，好好去做你該做的事？

column1: How clever of you to somehow convince Tariq to sell the broom. Here, I gladly give you a dirham for it.
column2: 你竟有辦法說服泰利克賣出掃帚，真是聰明。來，我樂意付你一枚銀幣。

column1: Ya'Allah! You have managed to part Tariq from his broom. And you give this to me? But surely...why, this can only mean it is an offering of peace from my cousin through you. He has forgiven me!
column2: 阿拉在上！你竟讓泰利克交出了他的掃帚。而你把它給了我？這……這只能說明一件事，這是我表弟藉你之手送來的和解之禮。他原諒我了！

column1: Allah bless you, habibi! You have brought my cousin and me together in kinship again. Even though I see you are an infidel, I pray you shall one day know the ecstasy of Paradise!
column2: 願阿拉保佑你，朋友！你讓我與表弟重修舊好。雖然我看得出你是異教徒，我仍祈願你有朝一日能得知天堂的至樂！

column1: There is nothing to see.
column2: 此處無物可看。

column1: Across the street is an inn.
column2: 街對面是一間旅店。

column1: There is some sort of antiquities shop and a butcher's shop.
column2: 這裡有間古物店和一間肉舖。

column1: I have the most profound suspicion that Ismail will not return.
column2: 我深深懷疑艾思美不會再回來了。

column1: He has vanished into his back room.
column2: 他已躲進裡屋去了。

column1: The dog looks like it is well fed from the butcher's scraps.
column2: 這隻狗看來吃肉舖的剩肉吃得很好。

column1: Nice try, but I do not think that being nice to Fawaz's dog will do anything to improve Fawaz's temper.
column2: 想得美，但我看討好法瓦茲的狗，對法瓦茲的脾氣是不會有什麼幫助的。

column1: Do not bother the dog, he may bite.
column2: 別招惹那條狗，牠會咬人。

column1: Would you buy a used chariot from this man?
column2: 你會向這種人買二手戰車嗎？

column1: It loosely translates as "Ismail, King of Antiquities". The rest is Arabic and Hebrew graffiti.
column2: 大略譯來是「古物之王艾思美」。其餘則是阿拉伯文與希伯來文的塗鴉。

column1: Alas, I have let my Greek fade with disuse and cannot translate.
column2: 可惜我的希臘文久未使用，早已生疏，譯不出來。

column1: You should recognize the countenance of the greatest of Roman generals, Julius Caesar.
column2: 你應當認得出這副面容，那是羅馬最偉大的將領，儒略·凱撒。

column1: It is pitch black inside.
column2: 裡頭一片漆黑。

column1: He has nothing displayed except a Roman bust. Behind that is only a short, empty hall leading to a door. He must keep his antiquities locked in another room.
column2: 他店裡除了一尊羅馬胸像外，什麼也沒陳列。胸像後方只是一條通往門口的短短空廊。他的古物想必都鎖在另一間房裡。

column1: Ismail's shop is closed.
column2: 艾思美的店關著門。

column1: There are no symbols on the antiquities shop.
column2: 古物店上沒有任何符號。

column1: There are no wares in sight. He must keep them in a back room.
column2: 不見任何貨物，想必都收在裡屋。

column1: Truly if I could have anything in the world, I would have your money. Yes, that is what I most desire. Your money.
column2: 說真的，若這世上能任我挑一物，我要的就是你的錢。是的，那正是我最渴望的——你的錢。

column1: Chas V'Chalila! What possessed me to say such a thing?! Forgive me, habibi. I meant to say that I have a special on saint's relics today. Reasonable prices!
column2: 天哪，萬萬不可！我這是鬼迷心竅，怎麼會說出這種話？！原諒我，朋友。我是想說，今天聖徒聖物特價，價錢公道！

column1: My storehouse of relics is a miracle unto itself! If it is holy, I will have it.
column2: 我的聖物庫本身便是一則奇蹟！只要是神聖之物，我這裡應有盡有。

column1: Ahalan, habibi. I am Ismail and within my vaults I have wonders, I have miracles, I have relics of the holy saints and prophets.
column2: 你好，朋友。我是艾思美，我的寶庫裡有奇珍、有奇蹟，還有聖徒與先知的聖物。

column1: I have blood of the prophet Mohammed! Hairs from the beard of Guruka Singh! Fingerbones of the saints! A sliver from what the Christians call the True Cross!
column2: 我有先知穆罕默德的血！有古魯卡·辛格鬍鬚上的毛髮！有聖徒的指骨！還有一片基督徒稱為真十字架的碎片！

column1: A relic for you today, perhaps? I have a special on saint's fingerbones.
column2: 今天要不要來件聖物？聖徒指骨正在特價。

column1: No need to yell, habibi. I am right here.
column2: 不必喊叫，朋友，我就在這兒。

column1: Habibi, you accidentally closed your purse without giving me money.
column2: 朋友，你不小心把錢囊闔上了，卻沒給我錢。

column1: Buying one relic from this fraud is more than enough.
column2: 跟這個騙子買一件聖物就已經夠了。

column1: Keep counting, habibi, keep counting.
column2: 繼續數吧，朋友，繼續數。

column1: What do you wish to buy, habibi?
column2: 你想買什麼，朋友？

column1: Sorry, I am all out of grails today. Try me again in a few weeks. Something is bound to turn up.
column2: 抱歉，聖杯今天賣完了。過幾週再來看看，總會有貨進來的。

column1: Ah, well, the truth is I am forbidden by law to sell relics of the Great Prophet Mohammed. But I have a special on saints' relics.
column2: 啊，其實吧，律法禁止我販售大先知穆罕默德的聖物。不過聖徒聖物正在特價。

column1: That is rare and valuable. Have you ever tried to shave a Sikh? It is most dangerous. Normally, I would ask no less than 10 dinars! But for you, only 4 dinars.
column2: 那件可是稀世珍寶。你可曾試過替錫克教徒剃鬚？那是極其危險之事。照理我開價絕不會低於十枚金幣！但看在你的份上，只要四枚金幣。

column1: I sell holy fingerbones! Not fingernails. Of course, for the right price, it could be arranged.
column2: 我賣的是神聖的指骨！不是指甲。當然，價錢談得攏的話，指甲也不是不能安排。

column1: Do I look like a pig-headed Nubian? Go next door.
column2: 我看起來像個跟豬一樣倔強的努比亞人嗎？去隔壁吧。

column1: He is a bad-tempered, pig-headed Nubian? Ah, but you should see his daughter!
column2: 他是個脾氣壞、跟豬一樣倔強的努比亞人？啊，但你真該見見他的女兒！

column1: Saint Galahad? Did you wish a relic of Saint Galahad? I can sell you one, only 2 dirhams.
column2: 聖葛拉漢？你想要聖葛拉漢的聖物嗎？我可以賣你一件，只要兩枚銀幣。

column1: Ahhh, this is an authentic bust of the great Julius Caesar. Pure marble. Only 5 dinars.
column2: 啊，這可是偉大的儒略·凱撒的真品胸像，純大理石打造，只要五枚金幣。

column1: I doubt that it is worth any price that this crook asks for it.
column2: 我看這騙子開的價錢，那東西根本不值。

column1: I sell antiquities from the holy land. Holy relics and holy fingerbones!
column2: 我賣的是聖地古物。神聖聖物與神聖指骨！

column1: I am the king of antiquities! No one can beat my selection or prices!
column2: 我是古物之王！我的貨色與價錢，無人能及！

column1: Thief? Heh-heh, that is a harsh word. I am an honest merchant, that I can assure you.
column2: 小偷？呵呵，這話說得太重了。我是個誠實的商人，這點我敢保證。

column1: You are in the wrong place. I deal in antiquities only.
column2: 你找錯地方了，我只做古物買賣。

column1: Do not worry about that, habib. My relics, though, are something to talk about!
column2: 那件事不必擔心，朋友。不過我的聖物，倒是值得一談！

column1: Please keep it, habibi. I do not get along well with animals.
column2: 留著吧，朋友，我跟動物向來合不來。

column1: That is like selling bricks to the Bedouin. I have a room full of relics. Want to buy another?
column2: 這就像賣磚頭給貝都因人一樣。我這一屋子都是聖物，還想再買一件嗎？

column1: I cannot say that what you offer is entirely without interest, but it does not fit my speciality.
column2: 我不能說你這東西全無價值，但它不合我的專門。

column1: What? You want nothing in return? Is this a trick? Nobody gives away something for nothing. No, I will not take it.
column2: 什麼？你什麼都不要？這是什麼把戲？天下沒有白白送人東西的事。不，我不會收下。

column1: Please do. I hate that dog.
column2: 請便，我討厭那條狗。

column1: This man is unfamiliar with the concept of cleanliness. He has the aroma of a billy goat.
column2: 這人似乎不懂什麼叫乾淨，身上一股公山羊的氣味。

column1: Brilliant move, Arthur. The sight of your sword has sent him into hiding in his back room.
column2: 好一招，亞瑟。你亮出劍來，把他嚇得躲進裡屋去了。

column1: He is an extraordinarily mean-looking Nubian.
column2: 他是個相貌異常兇惡的努比亞人。

column1: Tabulae Lanius is a term meaning "butcher", though more literally from the Latin it is "butcher's block". I cannot read the Hebrew graffiti above the door.
column2: 「Tabulae Lanius」意為「屠夫」，但按拉丁文直譯則是「屠案」。門上方的希伯來文塗鴉，我讀不懂。

column1: It is a symbol unknown to me. It looks like a flying eye.
column2: 這是個我不認得的符號，看起來像一隻長了翅膀的眼睛。

column1: That is quite a large goat.
column2: 那是頭相當大的山羊。

column1: There are three chickens hung upon hooks.
column2: 鉤子上掛著三隻雞。

column1: There is one leg of lamb hanging on a hook.
column2: 鉤子上掛著一條羊腿。

column1: He has sold all of his lamb.
column2: 他的羊肉已經賣完了。

column1: Beware of that cleaver, Arthur. I fear the Nubian may use it on more than animal flesh.
column2: 小心那把剁肉刀，亞瑟。我擔心那努比亞人動起刀來，恐怕不只對付牲畜的肉。

column1: It is dark inside. You can see nothing.
column2: 裡頭一片昏暗，什麼也看不見。

column1: You already are.
column2: 你已經是了。

column1: The butcher has sold his stock of meat for the day.
column2: 屠夫今天的存貨已經賣完了。

column1: He has a goat, a leg of lamb and chickens hanging in his shop.
column2: 他店裡掛著一頭山羊、一條羊腿和幾隻雞。

column1: If you have come back for more meat, you are out of luck. I have sold it all.
column2: 你若是回來買肉，那可不巧，我已經賣光了。

column1: Be gone, heathen. I do not like the look of you and I serve only who I please and today it does not please me to serve anyone.
column2: 走開，異教徒。我不喜歡你這副模樣，我只招待我樂意招待的人，而今天我誰都不樂意招待。

column1: Do you wonder why I am angry? It is the stink of fish I must endure every day. The foul, damnable stink of fish would drive any man to fury!
column2: 你想知道我為何動怒？那是因為我天天得忍受那股魚腥味。這惡臭該死的魚腥味，換作誰都會被逼瘋！

column1: No-one will ever know a day's peace from me for as long as I smell that stinking fish! A curse upon that fishmonger!
column2: 只要我還聞得到那股腥臭的魚味，誰都休想從我這兒得半日安寧！詛咒那個賣魚的！

column1: Ya'Allah! The wind blows sweet today. As for you, you look like a foreign heathen, but if you have good coin I will sell to you.
column2: 阿拉在上！今天風吹得挺舒暢。至於你，看起來像個外邦異教徒，但你若有好錢，我照樣賣你。

column1: Put up your weapon, infidel dog, or I will call the city guard. And I will chop up whatever pieces of you they leave behind.
column2: 收起你的武器，異教狗，否則我便叫城中衛兵來。他們留下的殘軀，我還會拿去剁碎。

column1: He is not for sale.
column2: 他不賣。

column1: Touch my dog and you die, infidel.
column2: 敢碰我的狗，你就死定了，異教徒。

column1: GUARDS!
column2: 衛兵！

column1: Mercenaries chop you up here.
column2: 傭兵們就在這裡把你剁成碎塊。

column1: I told you to be gone! I do not want your money or your business.
column2: 我叫你走開！我不要你的錢，也不做你的生意。

column1: I am not amused, stranger. Either do business or get lost.
column2: 我可沒興致陪你玩，陌生人。要嘛做生意，要嘛滾開。

column1: You are beginning to annoy me again, little man. Go away.
column2: 你又開始惹我不耐了，小子。走開。

column1: I do not bargain. Pay my price or be gone.
column2: 我不還價。照我的價錢付，不然就走人。

column1: So, do you want to buy something? Speak up!
column2: 那麼，你到底要不要買東西？說話啊！

column1: Stop bothering me!
column2: 別煩我了！

column1: Are you trying to insult me, infidel?! How dare you suggest I would touch an unclean meat!
column2: 你是想羞辱我嗎，異教徒？！你竟敢暗示我會碰不潔的肉！

column1: They are already spoken for by regular customers.
column2: 那些已經被老主顧訂走了。

column1: That was only brought to me for butchering by a customer. It is not mine to sell.
column2: 那只是有位客人送來讓我宰殺的，不是我的東西，不能賣你。

column1: In Jerusalem?!
column2: 在耶路撒冷？！

column1: What would you do with an entire large leg of lamb, Arthur?
column2: 你要一整條大羊腿做什麼，亞瑟？

column1: The whole leg is 5 dinars, but I will sell a single cut for 6 fals.
column2: 整條羊腿要五枚金幣，但單獨一塊肉我可以賣你六枚銅幣。

column1: I have goat, lamb, and chicken.
column2: 我這裡有山羊肉、羊肉和雞肉。

column1: I feed him scraps and he guards my shop. Dogs are far more trustworthy than men.
column2: 我拿剩肉餵牠，牠替我看店。狗可比人可靠多了。

column1: Do not even think about my daughter, you foreign swine!
column2: 別打我女兒的主意，你這外邦畜生！

column1: Bah, he is crook. All merchants are crooks. I am the only honest man here.
column2: 哼，他是個騙子。這裡的商人個個都是騙子，只有我是誠實人。

column1: Pretty dumb you are, if you do not know the sign of a butcher's shop.
column2: 連肉舖的招牌都認不出來，你還真是遲鈍。

column1: Bah, no thief dares to rob me!
column2: 哼，沒有哪個小偷敢來搶我！

column1: Can you not read? I am a butcher.
column2: 你不識字嗎？我是個屠夫。

column1: You annoy me, little man. Go away.
column2: 你惹我不耐了，小子。走開。

column1: If you have money, fine. If you do not have money, go somewhere else. I do not buy or trade.
column2: 你若有錢，好說。沒錢的話，去別處吧。我不買東西，也不以物易物。

column1: Have you ever tried to eat mule meat? Very tough. But I hear Mohammed is looking for a pack mule, if he has not already left on his trip.
column2: 你吃過騾肉嗎？肉硬得很。不過我聽說穆罕默德正在找一頭馱騾，前提是他還沒動身上路。

column1: Is that some piece of Ismail's junk? You bought that? You infidels are dumber than I thought.
column2: 那是艾思美賣的破爛玩意兒嗎？你居然買了？你們這些異教徒，比我想的還蠢。

column1: I do not take gifts from strangers.
column2: 我不收陌生人的禮物。

column1: I am not sure which smell is stronger: Fawaz or the meat.
column2: 我分不清是法瓦茲身上，還是那些肉，味道比較重。

column1: The building is but one floor with no other entrances.
column2: 這棟建築只有一層樓，沒有其他入口。

column1: This house sits at the end of the street, abutting an ancient wall. There is but one door.
column2: 這棟房子坐落在街道盡頭，緊鄰一道古牆，只有一扇門。

column1: It is the remnant of some even older part of the city, as best I can tell.
column2: 依我看，這是這座城市更古老一部分的遺跡。

column1: It is of colored glass through which you can see nothing.
column2: 這是彩色玻璃，你什麼也看不透。

column1: They look like ordinary bushes of some Eastern variety.
column2: 這些看起來像是某種東方常見的普通灌木。

column1: Over the door are two symbols, a crescent moon and a star.
column2: 門上方有兩個符號：一彎新月與一顆星。

column1: The crescent and star are both symbols associated with the Goddess.
column2: 新月與星辰都是與女神相關的符號。

column1: Bits of plaster have fallen away revealing bricks underneath, a common enough sight in Jerusalem.
column2: 部分灰泥已經剝落，露出底下的磚塊，這在耶路撒冷是常見的景象。

column1: The tiles are beautifully decorated, but of no consequence to you.
column2: 這些磁磚裝飾精美，但與你無關緊要。

column1: It is a heavy wooden door framed by beautifully glazed tiles.
column2: 這是一扇厚重的木門，四周鑲著裝飾精美的釉磚。

column1: She is nowhere in sight, if she is around here at all.
column2: 就算她在附近，此刻也不見蹤影。

column1: I see no-one here with whom to speak.
column2: 此處不見任何可交談之人。

column1: It is already open.
column2: 它已經是開著的。

column1: Such poetic language will never get you through this door.
column2: 這般詩意的言語，斷不能讓你通過此門。

column1: A powerful enchantment keeps this door shut. It will not open unless the owner is ready to open it.
column2: 一道強大的咒法將此門封鎖。除非主人有意開啟，否則此門絕不會開。

column1: Ahem...it IS closed.
column2: 呃……它確實是關著的。

column1: First, you must confront her. Then we shall see what will be.
column2: 你得先與她正面相對，之後才知分曉。

column1: You are alone in a hostile city. Do try to avoid rash and foolish actions.
column2: 你孤身一人置身於敵意四伏的城中，切莫輕舉妄動。

column1: There is no merchant here.
column2: 此處並無商販。

column1: It is too high.
column2: 太高了。

column1: Enter. Then we shall speak.
column2: 進來吧，我們再談。

column1: I will not tolerate such filth.
column2: 這等污穢之語，我絕不容忍。

column1: I warned you once. Now you will never step across my threshold.
column2: 我警告過你一次。如今，你休想再跨過我的門檻。

column1: Enter, if you would speak with me.
column2: 若想與我交談，便進來吧。

column1: What are you waiting for, Arthur? It is open.
column2: 你還在等什麼，亞瑟？門開著呢。

column1: There is no need. Fatima controls this door.
column2: 沒有這個必要，這扇門由法提瑪掌控。

column1: There is no answer.
column2: 沒有回應。

column1: Fatima has finished with you. She will not answer.
column2: 法提瑪已經與你了結，她不會再回應了。

column1: You were warned. This door will never open for you again.
column2: 你已被警告過。這扇門再也不會為你開啟。

column1: Enter.
column2: 進來。

column1: You may try, but I do not think you will succeed.
column2: 你儘管一試，但我不認為你會成功。

column1: I really think you are better off keeping your eyes on Fatima.
column2: 我認為你最好把目光放在法提瑪身上。

column1: This is no girl, Arthur!
column2: 這可不是個尋常女子，亞瑟！

column1: I can tell you nothing.
column2: 我什麼也不能告訴你。

column1: Above you is an unadorned ceiling.
column2: 你頭頂上是一片素淨無飾的天花板。

column1: Fatima awaits you upon the other side of a tiled pool. Water splashes from a bronze dolphin fountain. At the other end is a couch amply decorated with pillows. There is only one other door from the room.
column2: 法提瑪在磁磚砌成的水池另一端等著你。青銅海豚噴泉濺灑著水花，池的另一端擺著一張堆滿抱枕的長榻。這房間只有另一扇門可通行。

column1: Nothing has changed, except perhaps your level of caution.
column2: 一切如舊，變的或許只有你的戒心。

column1: There is no bench, but there is a couch.
column2: 這裡沒有長椅，但有一張長榻。

column1: There is the front door, through which you entered, and a side door which seems to be the only other exit.
column2: 這裡有你進來時走的前門，以及一扇側門，看來是唯一的另一個出口。

column1: That is the front door, through which you entered.
column2: 那是你進來時走的前門。

column1: That side door is the only other door in this room besides the front door.
column2: 除了前門，那扇側門是這房間裡唯一的另一扇門。

column1: It is a piece of dark slate with a painted edge.
column2: 這是一塊深色石板，邊緣繪有彩紋。

column1: The crescent over the side door is a lunar symbol associated with the Goddess.
column2: 側門上方的新月，是與女神相關的月亮符號。

column1: It is a beautifully sculpted bronze dolphin.
column2: 這是一尊雕工精美的青銅海豚。

column1: I do not recognize her plants, but I doubt they are important.
column2: 我認不出她種的這些植物，但我想它們並不重要。

column1: The utterly clear water ripples in a most mesmerizing way.
column2: 這池澄澈見底的水，泛起令人目眩神迷的漣漪。

column1: The couch with its wealth of lush pillows suggests the pursuit of physical pleasures.
column2: 這張長榻堆滿了華美的抱枕，透著追求肉體歡愉的意味。

column1: Everything in this room, including Fatima, should be considered a possible trap.
column2: 這房間裡的一切，包括法提瑪在內，都該視為可能的陷阱。

column1: Aye, you had best avoid it unless you have reason to think it is safe.
column2: 正是，除非你有理由相信它是安全的，否則最好避開。

column1: It is paved with squares of terra cotta.
column2: 地面鋪著一塊塊赤陶磚。

column1: The room has no windows. The alcoves are filled with tiles glazed with complex Arabian patterns.
column2: 這房間沒有窗戶，壁龕裡鑲滿了繪有繁複阿拉伯紋樣的釉磚。

column1: The walls have arches and recessed tiled alcoves.
column2: 牆上有拱門，以及嵌入牆內、鋪著磁磚的壁龕。

column1: The alcoves look primarily decorative, covered with brightly glazed, patterned tiles.
column2: 這些壁龕看來主要作裝飾之用，覆滿色澤鮮亮、紋樣繁複的釉磚。

column1: The glazed tiles are bright and dazzle the eye.
column2: 這些釉磚色澤鮮豔，令人目眩。

column1: Really, Arthur, that would be most unwise here.
column2: 說真的，亞瑟，在此處這麼做極不明智。

column1: It is good that you have returned for you have yet to pass the Test of Symbols.
column2: 你能回來是件好事，畢竟你尚未通過符號考驗。

column1: Welcome back, seeker. You have learned a difficult lesson. There is but one way to walk through my outer door in safety and that is when I will it.
column2: 歡迎歸來，求道者。你已學到了艱難的一課。要安然走過我的外門，唯有一法——待我有意讓你通過之時。

column1: She is so exquisite, that even I am moved by her beauty. And she is no ordinary woman. I feel a power here that rivals my own.
column2: 她如此絕美，連我也為之動容。她絕非尋常女子，我在此處感受到一股足以與我匹敵的力量。

column1: You have earned the right to question me.  Ask of me what you will.
column2: 你已贏得向我提問的資格。有話儘管問。

column1: When I want something of you, seeker, I will ask it.
column2: 求道者，若我有所求於你，自會開口。

column1: I care not what amount of coin you have. I ask for the entire purse, be it empty or full, for the purse represents attachment to material wealth.
column2: 你錢囊裡有多少錢，我並不在意。我要的是整個錢囊，無論空滿，因為錢囊象徵著對物質財富的執著。

column1: What I have to offer you is greater than any sum of money.
column2: 我所能給你的，遠勝過任何一筆錢財。

column1: Your lips will not reach that far.  And I do NOT advise getting closer.
column2: 你的嘴唇夠不著那麼遠。我也奉勸你別再靠近。

column1: By refusing my seductions, you have proven yourself to be a man of moral worth. But beware that you do not undo it all with a passing moment of weakness.
column2: 拒絕我的誘惑，證明了你是個有德之人。但要當心，莫讓一時的軟弱，毀了這一切。

column1: You would look like a fool.
column2: 你這樣看起來會像個傻子。

column1: For that, you must find the hierophant.
column2: 為此，你必須找到祭司。

column1: I cannot see what good that would do you.
column2: 我看不出這對你有什麼好處。

column1: There is no key to be gotten.
column2: 沒有鑰匙可拿。

column1: There is but one way out, through the front door.
column2: 只有一條出路，經由前門。

column1: Would you expect anyone to answer?
column2: 你以為會有人回應嗎？

column1: You may leave by the front door at any time, though I advise you not to do so unless I give you my blessing. The inner door opens only at my command.
column2: 你隨時可從前門離去，不過我勸你除非得到我的祝福，否則莫要如此。內門唯有依我之命方能開啟。

column1: You may leave by the front door at any time, though I advise you not to do so unless I give you my blessing. The inner door is open. The Test awaits you.
column2: 你隨時可從前門離去，不過我勸你除非得到我的祝福，否則莫要如此。內門已經開啟，考驗正等著你。

column1: It is good that you have brought this. Keep it close to you.
column2: 你能帶著這個來是件好事，將它貼身留著。

column1: I should think you have had more than your share of merchants this day.
column2: 我想你今日打交道的商販已經夠多了。

column1: No, do not eat it now. You may have need for it later.
column2: 不，現在別吃它，日後或許用得著。

column1: My sacred waters are protected by a spell to keep them clean of any defilement, though I will allow you to drink of it.
column2: 我這聖水受一道咒法守護，不受任何污染，但我允許你飲用。

column1: My sacred waters are not for such mundane uses.
column2: 我這聖水，不作這等世俗用途。

column1: Fatima's heady perfume and musky incense overwhelms your senses with sensual pleasure.
column2: 法提瑪馥郁的香氣與濃烈的麝香薰香，讓你的感官沉浸在肉慾的愉悅之中。

column1: You cannot draw your sword and if you turn to violence against me, I will punish you.
column2: 你拔不出劍。若你對我動用武力，我必懲罰你。

column1: You are far from the enchantress who gave you this sword and my power is supreme here. Your sword will not leave its scabbard in my presence.
column2: 賜你這把劍的女法師遠在天邊，此地是我的力量至高無上。在我面前，你的劍絕不會出鞘。

column1: Do not seek to lose the good favor you have won from me.
column2: 莫要親手斷送你在我這裡贏得的恩寵。

column1: Soon enough, my handsome one.
column2: 快了，我的美男子。

column1: Knowledge must be earned before it will be given.
column2: 知識須先贏得，方能授予。

column1: You have passed my Test and are truly you are the most worthy of all men who have passed my door. Go with my blessings and find the hierophant.
column2: 你已通過我的考驗，確實是所有踏過我門檻的人之中最堪當之人。帶著我的祝福去吧，找到祭司。

column1: Enter the door and take my test.
column2: 進門，接受我的考驗。

column1: You are acquainted with my front door.  This inner door leads to my Test of Symbols.
column2: 我的前門你已熟悉。這扇內門通往我的符號考驗。

column1: If you persevere, you will find the Grail.  Now, you must seek out the hierophant and gain entrance to the catacombs, as did Galahad before you.
column2: 若你堅持到底，終將尋得聖杯。如今，你必須尋出祭司，設法進入地下墓窖，如同在你之前的葛拉漢一般。

column1: You have trials of body, spirit and heart yet to face if you are to wrest the Cup of Regeneration from the Goddess and take it with you as the Grail.
column2: 若要從女神手中奪得重生之杯、將它當作聖杯帶走，你還有肉身、心靈與意志的試煉要面對。

column1: From here, your path must lie through the deadly catacombs, as it did for the man who came here before you, the one called Galahad.
column2: 從此處起，你的路必須穿過那致命的地下墓窖，正如在你之前來到此地、名叫葛拉漢的那人一樣。

column1: But to walk safely in the catacombs, you must pass my Test of Symbols.
column2: 但要在地下墓窖中安然而行，你必須先通過我的符號考驗。

column1: He, too, resisted my seductions. I have learned from the hierophant that Galahad entered the catacombs to continue his search.
column2: 他也曾抵擋住我的誘惑。我從祭司那裡得知，葛拉漢已進入地下墓窖，繼續他的尋索。

column1: But he did not pass the Test of Symbols that I placed before him, and so I fear he has suffered by entering the catacombs without the gift of the hierophant.
column2: 但他未能通過我為他設下的符號考驗，因此我擔心，他未帶祭司的贈禮便進入墓窖，恐已遭逢不幸。

column1: I judge from your words that these men also sought the Grail. But I know them not. They have not come to me.
column2: 從你的話中，我判斷這些人也在尋找聖杯。但我不識得他們，他們並未來過我這裡。

column1: Hezekiah's Aqueduct feeds the Pool of Siloam by bringing it waters from the Spring of Gihon, the same waters I draw upon for my own pool.
column2: 希西家水道將基訓泉的水引入西羅亞池，我這池中所用的，正是同一水源。

column1: The catacombs lie beneath the city. You must find the hierophant if you wish to enter them.
column2: 地下墓窖就在城市之下。你若想進入，必須先找到祭司。

column1: The hierophant will guide you to the catacombs, when you are ready. But first I entreat you to pass my Test of Symbols.
column2: 待你準備就緒，祭司會引你前往地下墓窖。但在此之前，我懇請你先通過我的符號考驗。

column1: Unless you pass this test, you will enter the catacombs without the gift of the hierophant.
column2: 除非你通過此考驗，否則你進入墓窖時，將沒有祭司的贈禮相伴。

column1: Ancient he is, and he is wise, yet shunned by fools who fear his guise.
column2: 他年邁而智慧，卻遭懼其外貌的愚人所棄。

column1: You have seen the leprous beggar. Look to your own knowledge.
column2: 你已見過那染上痲瘋的乞丐。回想你自己所知便是。

column1: The crescent above my inner door signifies that behind it lies the Test of Symbols.
column2: 我內門上方的新月，標誌著門後便是符號考驗。

column1: You will learn about that from the hierophant, if ever you meet him.
column2: 若你有幸遇見祭司，自會從他那裡得知此事。

column1: She who I serve has infinite names. Yet in all times and in all places she is known by her three natures.
column2: 我所侍奉的她擁有無數的名字。然而不論何時何地，她皆以三種神性為人所知。

column1: As the White Virgin she renews and generates life, as the Red Mother she nurtures and protects life, as the Black Crone she is death and the forces of destruction.
column2: 化身白色處女時，她更新並創造生命；化身紅色聖母時，她滋養並守護生命；化身黑色老太婆時，她便是死亡與毀滅之力。

column1: You have three more Guardians to face.
column2: 你還有三位守護者要面對。

column1: Some questions are more worthy of my answers than others. This one is less worthy.
column2: 有些問題比其他問題更值得我回答，這一個不值得。

column1: You shall not move until my dance is through. No other words but a yes or a no will do.
column2: 在我的舞蹈結束之前，你不得挪動半步。除了「是」與「否」，其餘言語一概無用。

column1: O' handsome stranger from a distant land, this is my dance of love. I offer you pleasures such as you have never known.
column2: 喔，來自遠方的俊美陌生人，這是我的愛之舞。我要獻給你前所未有的歡愉。

column1: I offer you my body and soul and sensual delights beyond imagining. In this enchanted place, we will take our endless fill of one another.
column2: 我獻上我的肉身與靈魂，以及超乎想像的感官歡愉。在這方施了魔法的所在，你我將無盡地享受彼此。

column1: I offer you the sweetest wine and the most succulent fruits and meats. I offer you complete freedom from all weariness and care.
column2: 我獻上最甘美的酒、最鮮美的果肉，並讓你從一切疲憊與憂慮中徹底解脫。

column1: Kiss me and I will give you forgetfulness and bliss in an earthly paradise. All the pains of your heart and soul will be cured.
column2: 吻我，我便賜你忘卻與極樂，如置身人間樂園。你心靈與靈魂的一切傷痛，都將痊癒。

column1: Will you kiss me and be my cherished lover?
column2: 你願吻我，做我珍愛的戀人嗎？

column1: Then if the delights of the flesh are not enough for you, I can offer more powerful gifts, for I serve the Goddess herself and I have drunk from her sacred cup.
column2: 那麼，若肉體的歡愉還不足以打動你，我能獻上更強大的贈禮——因為我侍奉的正是女神本身，我曾親飲她的聖杯。

column1: Behold!  A vision of the Holy Grail!
column2: 且看！聖杯的異象！

column1: I have the power to give you immortality! With but one kiss, you will become invincible. No man, woman or beast will ever overcome you.
column2: 我有能力賜你不朽！只消一吻，你便無敵於天下，無論男女或野獸都再也無法勝過你。

column1: You will stride the earth, powerful and invincible, for all time. Think of the deeds of valor you could perform!
column2: 你將以無敵之力縱橫天下，直到永遠。想想你能成就多少英勇的偉業！

column1: Will you kiss me and become a god in human form?
column2: 你願吻我，化身為人形之神嗎？

column1: Then I find you worthy, King Arthur, and will help you to find what you seek.
column2: 那麼，我認定你堪當此任，亞瑟王，我將助你尋得所求之物。

column1: Ask of me what you will.
column2: 有話儘管問。

column1: The Street of David ends here against this sacred wall. A beggar sits, coaxing what warmth he can from a brazier filled with burning charcoal.
column2: 大衛街到此為止，抵著這面聖牆。一名乞丐坐在此處，就著一只燒著炭火的火盆，勉強取暖。

column1: Though this wall looks to be made of similar stone to the rest of Jerusalem, it is a remnant of a very ancient temple built by King David many hundreds of years ago and is held sacred by the Jewish people.
column2: 這面牆的石材看似與耶路撒冷其他建築相仿，實則是數百年前大衛王所建古老聖殿的遺跡，猶太人視之為聖物。

column1: What is this mindless violence that inflicts you? Even a leper has a right to live.
column2: 這般不明所以的暴行，是誰加諸於你？即便是痲瘋病人，也有活下去的權利。

column1: Touch a man with leprosy? Do not be a fool!
column2: 觸碰一個染上痲瘋的人？別犯傻了！

column1: That would be extraordinarily cruel, Arthur.
column2: 那樣做未免太過殘忍了，亞瑟。

column1: A small pile of charcoal burns inside a simple bronze brazier.
column2: 一只簡樸的青銅火盆裡，燃著一小堆炭火。

column1: The beggar is a pathetic sight for his limbs are rotting with the disease of leprosy.
column2: 這乞丐景況淒慘，四肢正因痲瘋病而腐爛。

column1: The beggar holds a staff in one hand.
column2: 這乞丐一手拄著一根拐杖。

column1: A thousand blessings upon for bringing me this charcoal.
column2: 承蒙你送來這些炭火，願千般祝福降臨於你。

column1: At night, I suffer from the cold. I have only this brazier in which to burn charcoal, my only source of warmth. Men fear to come near me and I can no longer walk upon my rotted limbs.
column2: 入夜之後，我飽受寒冷之苦。我只有這只火盆能燒炭取暖，是我僅有的暖源。人們懼怕靠近我，我這雙腐爛的腿，也再也無法行走。

column1: I must rely upon the goodness of strangers, such as yourself, to bring me charcoal so I will not suffer in the night.
column2: 我只能仰賴像你這樣的陌生人心懷善意，為我送來炭火，好讓我夜裡不致受苦。

column1: A small bag of charcoal would be a gift greater than silver or gold to this poor leper.
column2: 對這可憐的痲瘋病人而言，一小袋炭火，勝過金銀之贈。

column1: Alms for a poor leper. Look upon the wretched with mercy. Alms for a poor leper.
column2: 可憐可憐這痲瘋病人吧。求你以慈悲眼光看待這不幸之人。可憐可憐這痲瘋病人吧。

column1: Sa'alam aleikem, King Arthur. You have passed many trials, yet more Guardians of the Sacred Cup wait to test you.
column2: Sa'alam aleikem，亞瑟王。你已通過重重考驗，但更多聖杯的守護者仍等著試煉你。

column1: Through the catacombs you must pass. Not long ago, the one called Galahad entered the catacombs and has not returned. If you are ready to follow him, ask of me "open the catacombs", and I will do so.
column2: 你必須穿過地下墓窖。不久前，那位喚作葛拉漢的騎士已進入地下墓窖，至今未歸。你若已準備好追隨他而去，便向我說「open the catacombs」，我自當為你開啟通路。

column1: I am the hierophant you seek, King Arthur. Though I may admit you to face the next Guardian of the Sacred Cup, you have not yet passed the Test of Symbols.
column2: 我便是你所尋的祭司，亞瑟王。雖然我可讓你去面對下一位聖杯守護者，但你尚未通過符號考驗。

column1: Unless you do, you face almost certain death in the catacombs. This may be the fate of Galahad, who entered without heeding my warning. He has not been seen again.
column2: 若不如此，你在地下墓窖中幾乎必死無疑。葛拉漢或許正是如此下場——他無視我的警告便逕自進入，此後再無人見過他。

column1: Return to Fatima and complete the Test. But if you choose to ignore this warning, say to me "Open the catacombs" and I will let you pass.
column2: 回到法提瑪那裡完成考驗吧。但你若執意無視這個警告，便向我說「Open the catacombs」，我便放你通行。

column1: You would ask a gift from a poor leprous beggar?
column2: 你竟向一個貧苦的痲瘋乞丐討要禮物？

column1: Return to Fatima and pass the Test of Symbols, if you desire greater help from me.
column2: 你若盼望從我這裡得到更多的援助，就回到法提瑪那裡通過符號考驗吧。

column1: Your reward for such a mean-spirited action would be to burn your hands.
column2: 如此刻薄的行徑，換來的報應就是燒傷你的雙手。

column1: Usually an alm can be money, though sometimes it may be some other gift. You must decide what would be best to give this beggar.
column2: 施捨通常是錢財，但有時也可以是別的餽贈。你得自行判斷，什麼才是給這位乞丐最好的東西。

column1: Bless you! May you always walk the path of righteousness.
column2: 願上天保佑你！願你永遠行走在正義之路上。

column1: Bless you, good sir, bless you!
column2: 願上天保佑你，善心的大人，願上天保佑你！

column1: May you be richly blessed for your kindness!
column2: 願你的善心得到豐厚的福報！

column1: Best to leave it to the beggar to decide when and how to burn the charcoal once you give it to him.
column2: 木炭一旦交給了這位乞丐，何時、如何燃燒，最好還是留給他自己決定。

column1: Great is your charity, yet I would only ask for one thing -- a bag of charcoal.
column2: 你的仁慈可謂深厚，但我只求一件事——一袋木炭。

column1: I am content with what I have.
column2: 我對現有的一切已心滿意足。

column1: I am but a poor, leprous beggar, not a merchant.
column2: 我不過是個貧苦的痲瘋乞丐，並非商人。

column1: It is not mine to give.
column2: 此物並非我所能給予。

column1: There are many merchants in the bazaar who may help you, though they will not help me.
column2: 市集裡有許多商人或許能幫得上你，只是他們不會幫我。

column1: My task it to guide you toward the Grail, nothing more.
column2: 我的任務只是指引你尋向聖杯，僅此而已。

column1: What answer can you expect from a leprous beggar?
column2: 你能從一個痲瘋乞丐那裡得到什麼答案呢？

column1: He chose to enter the catacombs without passing the Test of Symbols. He has not been seen since.
column2: 他未通過符號考驗便執意進入地下墓窖，自此再無人見過他。

column1: If you ask me to open the catacombs, then I will tell you more. If you choose not to enter, there is no point in my telling you anything.
column2: 你若要我開啟地下墓窖，我便會告訴你更多。你若不打算進入，那我說再多也是枉然。

column1: Wisdom and knowledge must always be sought. With them you will be rewarded, but without them you will be doomed.
column2: 智慧與知識永遠值得追求。擁有它們，你將得到回報；缺了它們，你便注定沉淪。

column1: She is extremely powerful for she has the highest favor of the goddess.
column2: 她法力極為強大，因為她最受女神的眷顧。

column1: Once in this city she was greatly worshipped under the name of Aphrodite. By that name still we call her.
column2: 昔日在這座城裡，她曾以阿芙羅黛蒂之名備受敬奉，至今我們仍如此稱呼她。

column1: Tamra serves Aphrodite, as do I.
column2: 泰姆拉侍奉阿芙羅黛蒂，我也是。

column1: I sit with by back to the north, my face to the south, half in shadow, half in light.
column2: 我坐著，背朝北方，面向南方，半身隱於陰影，半身沐於光中。

column1: Thanks to your generosity, the charcoal will keep me warm during the cold nights.
column2: 多虧你的慷慨，這些木炭能讓我在寒夜裡保持溫暖。

column1: The burning charcoal heats my brazier which in turn warms my poor diseased body.
column2: 燃燒的木炭溫暖了我的火盆，火盆又溫暖了我這副可憐病弱的身軀。

column1: My brazier needs charcoal to keep me warm during the cold nights.
column2: 我的火盆需要木炭，才能讓我在寒夜裡保持溫暖。

column1: It causes my body to rot, my fingers and toes to fall off. Do not come near me, I beg you.
column2: 這病使我的身軀腐爛，手指與腳趾一根根脫落。求你別靠近我。

column1: I guard the way to the catacombs and admit only those who are found worthy.
column2: 我看守著通往地下墓窖的道路，只放行被認定為夠格之人。

column1: No thief dares to rob from a leper.
column2: 沒有哪個竊賊敢向痲瘋病人下手。

column1: Bless you a thousand times, good sir! May your charity win you a place in Paradise.
column2: 千謝萬謝，善心的大人！願你的慈悲為你換得天國的一席之地。

column1: Because you have passed the Test of Symbols, I will give you a gift that could save your life. Within the catacombs are cursed rats whose bite is poison.
column2: 既然你已通過符號考驗，我便贈你一件能救你性命之物。地下墓窖裡棲居著受詛咒的老鼠，牠們的咬傷帶有劇毒。

column1: One bite from these rats and you will die slowly. Even the slightest bite means certain death. If bitten again, the end comes more quickly and with great agony.
column2: 被這些老鼠咬上一口，你便會緩緩死去。哪怕只是輕輕一咬，也必死無疑。若再遭二次咬傷，死期便會加速降臨，且痛苦萬分。

column1: Take this vial of elixir.
column2: 收下這瓶解藥吧。
