column1: As you wish it. Listen carefully. Within the catacombs are hordes of rats with a deadly poison in their bite. Once you are bitten, nothing can save you.
column2: 既然你堅持，那就仔細聽好。地下墓窖裡群聚著帶有致命毒性的老鼠。一旦被咬，便再無法可救。

column1: If you are bitten, drink it and you will be cured. There is but one dosage, so waste it not.
column2: 你若被咬，飲下此物便能痊癒。這只有一劑份量，切莫浪費。

column1: Go now. There is no turning back.
column2: 去吧，此去再無回頭路。

column1: The way is open. Go.
column2: 通路已開，去吧。

column1: There are three doorways.
column2: 這裡有三道門。

column1: There are two doorways, mummies, urns and symbols upon one wall.
column2: 這裡有兩道門，其中一面牆上有木乃伊、甕與符號。

column1: There are two doorways, a mummy, urns and symbols upon one wall.
column2: 這裡有兩道門，其中一面牆上有一具木乃伊、幾個甕與符號。

column1: There is a round copper medallion around the neck of what may be the mummy of a child.
column2: 那具看似孩童的木乃伊頸間，掛著一枚圓形的銅製六角星項鍊。

column1: There is nothing left but a pile of dust.
column2: 只剩下一堆塵土，別無他物。

column1: The mummy in this niche is unremarkable.
column2: 這個壁龕裡的木乃伊平平無奇。

column1: The mummy beneath the pentacle is quite small and has a medallion hanging around its neck.
column2: 五芒星下方的木乃伊體型頗小，頸間掛著一枚六角星項鍊。

column1: The child's mummy has disintegrated, leaving only a pile of dust.
column2: 那具孩童的木乃伊已然崩解，只剩下一堆塵土。

column1: Three of the walls are barren, but upon one wall there are two symbols painted.
column2: 三面牆空無一物，唯有一面牆上繪著兩個符號。

column1: Two of the niches hold mummies, and two smaller niches are empty.
column2: 兩個壁龕裡供著木乃伊，另外兩個較小的壁龕則是空的。

column1: One niche holds a mummy, and three others are empty.
column2: 一個壁龕裡供著木乃伊，其餘三個都是空的。

column1: One symbol is a pentacle. The other is a labarum.
column2: 其中一個符號是五芒星，另一個是拉巴倫。

column1: The pentacle, apples and the Goddess are often associated together because if one cuts an apple open lengthwise, he can find a five-pointed star hidden within.
column2: 五芒星、蘋果與女神常被相提並論，因為若把蘋果縱切剖開，便能發現裡頭藏著一顆五角星。

column1: It is the symbol of Mithras, so we might assume that Roman soldiers once used these catacombs.
column2: 這是米夏拉的標識，由此可以推想，羅馬士兵或許曾使用過這處地下墓窖。

column1: There are a great many bones around, as might be expected in catacombs.
column2: 四周散落著大量骸骨，在地下墓窖裡倒也不足為奇。

column1: The funereal urns within these sepulchers are designed to hold the ashes of the deceased, or their mummified organs.
column2: 這些墓穴中的喪葬甕，是用來盛裝逝者的骨灰，或是他們製成木乃伊的臟器。

column1: It is round, made of copper as best I can tell, and seems to have engraving upon it, but it is heavily coated with dust which obscures it.
column2: 據我判斷，它是圓形的，以銅製成，上頭似乎刻有花紋，但積滿厚厚的灰塵，看不真切。

column1: I can tell you little about it until it can be clearly and closely seen.
column2: 在能仔細看清楚之前，我對它所知不多。

column1: It is engraved with a pentacle and is imbued with a warding spell.
column2: 上頭刻著五芒星，並被賦予了辟邪的法術。

column1: The medallion hangs around your neck beneath your tunic.
column2: 這枚六角星項鍊掛在你的頸間，藏於外衣之下。

column1: There is no medallion here.
column2: 這裡沒有六角星項鍊。

column1: Aye, but how, without risking a rat bite?
column2: 正是，但該如何取得，才不會冒著被老鼠咬傷的風險？

column1: But you already took it.
column2: 但你已經拿到手了。

column1: The trick is how to lift the medallion without risking a poisonous rat bite.
column2: 關鍵在於如何取下這枚六角星項鍊，同時不冒被毒鼠咬傷的風險。

column1: What ARE you blathering about?
column2: 你到底在胡扯些什麼？

column1: It is painted upon the wall.
column2: 它就畫在牆上。

column1: It is too short and too blunt to do what you need.
column2: 它太短又太鈍，做不了你需要的事。

column1: Very clever, Arthur! You have safely taken possession of the medallion.
column2: 真聰明，亞瑟！你已安全取得了這枚六角星項鍊。

column1: Once more you are forced into a pitch black tunnel that leads in but one direction.
column2: 你再度被逼入一條漆黑的甬道，唯有一個方向可走。

column1: It seems an eternity before the tunnel takes a turning and brings you to yet another hidden door.
column2: 彷彿過了永恆般漫長，甬道才終於轉了個彎，將你帶到另一扇隱藏的門前。

column1: Push harder, Arthur! Aye, it opens as did the other one and returns you to the catacombs.
column2: 再用力推，亞瑟！沒錯，它如同先前那扇門一樣開啟了，將你帶回地下墓窖。

column1: There are three doorways, mummies, urns and some symbols.
column2: 這裡有三道門、木乃伊、甕，以及一些符號。

column1: Two walls contain niches of mummies and the two painted symbols. The other two walls are barren.
column2: 兩面牆上有供著木乃伊的壁龕與那兩個繪製的符號，另外兩面牆則空無一物。

column1: Over one doorway is a small mushroom. Over the other doorway is the Gnostic symbol of the eight rayed sun.
column2: 其中一道門上方畫著一朵小蘑菇，另一道門上方則是諾斯替教的八芒太陽符號。

column1: It is simply a small mushroom painted over one doorway. There are many mushroom cults in the Far East.
column2: 那不過是門上方畫的一朵小蘑菇。遠東有許多崇拜蘑菇的教派。

column1: To the Gnostics, the eight rayed sun represents the universe with the dome of heaven in the center.
column2: 對諾斯替教徒而言，八芒太陽象徵著宇宙，中央則代表著蒼穹的圓頂。

column1: Most of these mummies must be quite old, for they look dry and brittle, and smell of dust and decay.
column2: 這些木乃伊多半年代久遠，看來乾枯易碎，散發著塵土與腐朽的氣味。

column1: This room now has three doors from which to choose.
column2: 這個房間現在有三道門可供選擇。

column1: Now that the secret entrance is shut, there remain two doorways to choose from. The entire wall through which you entered is covered with a mural.
column2: 如今密道已經關閉，只剩兩道門可供選擇。你進來時經過的那整面牆上，都覆著一幅壁畫。

column1: The air is stale and musty. Everything around you is covered with the dust of centuries. The mummies in their niches are ancient, untouched for ages.
column2: 空氣沉悶又帶著霉味。四周一切都覆著數百年的塵埃。壁龕裡的木乃伊古老不堪，多年來無人碰觸。

column1: Would that Galahad had left some sign to guide us. He may be trapped in this foul place. Let us pray he is still alive.
column2: 但願葛拉漢曾留下什麼記號指引我們。他或許正受困於這污穢之地。讓我們祈禱他仍然在世。

column1: But you must be extremely careful. I hear the skittering of the poisonous rats everywhere within the walls. Their evil eyes glint from behind and around the mummies. Avoid them at all costs!
column2: 但你必須萬分小心。我聽見毒鼠在牆壁四處竄動的聲響，牠們邪惡的雙眼在木乃伊四周與後方閃著光。無論如何都要避開牠們！

column1: I can tell you this much, when you came down the stairs from the bazaar, you were facing north. Therefore the wall with the mural is facing south.
column2: 我能告訴你的是，當你從市集走下樓梯時，你面朝北方。因此那面有壁畫的牆，是朝南的。

column1: There are two doorways from this room.
column2: 這個房間有兩道門。

column1: There are now three doorways to choose from in this room. But the third one is not the same as the one through which you first entered.
column2: 這個房間現在有三道門可供選擇，但第三道並非你最初進來時經過的那道。

column1: The secret entrance closed behind you. Your task, it would seem, is to discover a way out of here.
column2: 密道在你身後關閉了。看來，你的任務便是找出離開這裡的路。

column1: Let us hope you will also discover some sign of Galahad.
column2: 但願你也能找到葛拉漢留下的什麼線索。

column1: The tunnel and door which led you here are now irrevocably closed. Your choices are before you.
column2: 帶你來到這裡的甬道與門，如今已徹底封閉，再也回不去了。眼前的選擇就在你面前。

column1: It shows the death of Adonis, one of Aphrodite's lovers. The legend is written in the Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 畫中描繪的是阿度尼斯之死，他是阿芙羅黛蒂眾多情人之一。這段傳說記載於《Liber ex Doctrina》之中。

column1: Interestingly, there is also a tree filled with golden apples in this mural.
column2: 有趣的是，這幅壁畫裡還畫著一棵結滿金蘋果的樹。

column1: To learn more about the legend of Adonis, as shown in this mural, consult your Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 若想多了解這幅壁畫所描繪的阿度尼斯傳說，可查閱你的《Liber ex Doctrina》。

column1: The tree in the mural bears golden apples, a reminder of Aphrodite.
column2: 壁畫中的樹結著金蘋果，讓人聯想起阿芙羅黛蒂。

column1: There are colourful, but meaningless patterns painted upon one of the doorways.
column2: 其中一道門上畫著色彩繽紛卻毫無意義的圖案。

column1: He also would have entered here. Indeed, the dust on the floor looked a bit disturbed, but not enough to show which way he went.
column2: 他想必也是從這裡進來的。地上的灰塵確實看似有些被擾動過，但還不足以看出他往哪個方向去了。

column1: That door closed securely behind you, leaving no trace that it was ever there.
column2: 那扇門在你身後牢牢關上，不留一絲曾經存在過的痕跡。

column1: You cannot. A more powerful will than yours commands these doors.
column2: 你辦不到。掌管這些門的，是比你更強大的意志。

column1: As before, the hidden door shuts as though it had never been there.
column2: 如同先前一樣，那扇隱藏的門闔上了，彷彿它從未存在過。

column1: Nay, you have chosen wrongly! The door has shut behind you, trapping you within a pitch black hole scarcely larger than a coffin.
column2: 不，你選錯了！門在你身後關上，將你困在一個幾乎只有棺材大小的漆黑洞穴之中。

column1: And a stone coffin it is, for here you shall die all too soon. Farewell, King Arthur.
column2: 而這確實是一具石棺，因為你不消多久便會死在此處。永別了，亞瑟王。

column1: There is nothing worth seeing there.
column2: 那裡沒有什麼值得一看的東西。

column1: Galahad's body lies upon the bier in what is now his own tomb as well.
column2: 葛拉漢的遺體躺在棺架上，此處如今也成了他自己的墓穴。

column1: Galahad lies upon a bier within this chamber, surrounded by those long dead.
column2: 葛拉漢躺在這密室中的棺架上，四周環繞著早已作古之人。

column1: He is in a healing trance
column2: 他正陷入療癒的恍惚之中

column1: He is still alive, but deep in a fevered coma. He has been bitten and could die at any moment.
column2: 他還活著，但陷入了高燒導致的昏迷之中。他已遭咬傷，隨時都可能喪命。

column1: Galahad has died because you failed to save him, though you had the means. His death is a black stain upon your soul.
column2: 葛拉漢已經死了，只因你明明有能力救他，卻未能出手。他的死是你靈魂上一道抹不去的污點。

column1: Galahad is dead. Had you heeded the warnings of Fatima and the heirophant, this may have been averted.
column2: 葛拉漢死了。你若當初聽從法提瑪與祭司的警告，或許便能避免這場悲劇。

column1: The low stone bier is covered by an old lion skin.
column2: 低矮的石製棺架上覆著一張老舊的獅皮。

column1: Galahad's shield rests where he dropped it at the foot of the bier.
column2: 葛拉漢的盾牌就擱在他失手掉落之處，棺架的腳邊。

column1: It is Galahad's sword.
column2: 這是葛拉漢的劍。

column1: I do not know what gift Galahad wanted you to bring to Aphrodite, nor how you would do this. You will have to search for the answer to this riddle yourself.
column2: 我不知道葛拉漢想要你帶給阿芙羅黛蒂的禮物是什麼，也不知道你該如何辦到。這個謎題的答案，你得自己去尋找。

column1: I do not know what "gift" you mean.
column2: 我不明白你所說的「禮物」是指什麼。

column1: He will not answer. He is dead.
column2: 他不會回答了。他已經死了。

column1: He is in a healing trance and cannot answer.
column2: 他正陷入療癒的恍惚之中，無法回答。

column1: He is in no condition to answer you.
column2: 他此刻的狀態，無法回答你。

column1: You have Excaliber. It is the only weapon you need.
column2: 你已有聖劍在身，那是你唯一需要的武器。

column1: You have your own fine shield. It would be absurd to carry two.
column2: 你自己就有一面精良的盾牌，帶兩面實在荒謬。

column1: It is made of stone and not going anywhere.
column2: 它是石頭做的，哪裡都去不了。

column1: It is old and deteriorating and of no use to you.
column2: 它老舊又逐漸腐朽，對你毫無用處。

column1: As the hierophant warned you, there is only enough for one use.
column2: 正如祭司警告過你的，這只夠使用一次。

column1: If only you had not been such a fool and done as Fatima and the hierophant advised. Galahad is dead and you must bear the responsibility.
column2: 若你當初不曾如此愚蠢，聽從法提瑪與祭司的忠告該有多好。葛拉漢已死，你必須承擔這份責任。

column1: It is too late. Had you acted in time, he would have lived. His death weighs heavily upon your soul.
column2: 為時已晚。你若及時採取行動，他本可存活。他的死，沉沉壓在你的靈魂之上。

column1: This will serve as his tomb. Let him lie.
column2: 這裡便作他的墓穴吧，讓他安息。

column1: He is just as well off here as anywhere. Better not to move him.
column2: 他留在這裡，並不比別處差。最好別移動他。

column1: All hope is gone. Galahad is dead.
column2: 一切希望都已破滅，葛拉漢死了。

column1: You have the means to save his life, if you have the courage to make the sacrifice.
column2: 你有能力救他一命，只要你有勇氣做出這份犧牲。

column1: Galahad will live and revive eventually. Now you must go on. Your own life is at stake.
column2: 葛拉漢終將活下來、甦醒過來。如今你必須繼續前行，你自己的性命同樣攸關。

column1: Alas, if you had but heeded the warnings of Fatima and the hierophant, perhaps you would have had a chance.
column2: 唉，你若聽從了法提瑪與祭司的警告，或許還有一線機會。

column1: The rat's poison must be affecting your mind. You are babbling nonsense.
column2: 想必是鼠毒侵擾了你的心智，你正語無倫次地胡言亂語。

column1: That is utter madness, to even think such a thing.
column2: 光是有這種念頭，便是徹底的瘋狂。

column1: Ahem...do try to restrain yourself.
column2: 咳……還請你克制一下自己。

column1: The elixir burns like fire through your veins. You are healed. The poison is gone, but at the cost of Galahad's life.
column2: 解藥如烈火般燒遍你的血脈。你痊癒了。毒素已經清除，但代價是葛拉漢的性命。

column1: Wait! Here lies Sir Galahad, purest of your knights. He has also been bitten and is at death's very door.
column2: 且慢！葛拉漢爵士就躺在此處，他是你麾下最純潔的騎士。他也遭到咬傷，已是命懸一線。

column1: If you do not give him the elixir, he will die. He could die at any moment! A terrible choice is before you.
column2: 若不將解藥給他，他必死無疑。他隨時都可能斷氣！一個可怕的抉擇擺在你面前。

column1: If you drink the elixir, you let Galahad die. If you give Galahad the elixir, your one chance is to find the Grail before your own time runs out.
column2: 若你飲下解藥，便是任由葛拉漢死去。若你把解藥給了葛拉漢，你唯一的生機，便是趕在自己時限用盡前尋得聖杯。

column1: Only the healing powers of the Grail may be able to save you. If not, at least Galahad would remain alive to carry on the mission.
column2: 唯有聖杯的療癒之力或許能救你一命。若不成，至少葛拉漢仍能存活，繼續完成這項使命。

column1: He is in a healing trance, unable to hear, speak or move.
column2: 他正處於療癒的昏迷之中，無法聽聞、言語或動彈。

column1: He cannot use it now. You had best keep it.
column2: 他此刻無法使用它，你最好還是留著。

column1: He is unable to eat it and you may yet have need of it.
column2: 他無法食用它，而你或許還用得上。

column1: I would not part with it just yet. You may well need it.
column2: 我勸你先別捨棄它，你很可能還會用到。

column1: That would not help him.
column2: 那對他毫無幫助。

column1: Truly, you are noble. But you must make the clear the nature of the sacrifice you intend.
column2: 你確實高潔。但你必須先弄清楚自己打算做出的犧牲，究竟是什麼性質。

column1: Arthur....my king. I knew....you would....come.
column2: 亞瑟……吾王。我早知……你會……前來。

column1: Only way out....the gift....for Aphrodite....you must....bring her....bring her the.....
column2: 唯一的出路……那份獻禮……獻給阿芙羅黛蒂……你必須……帶給她……帶給她那……

column1: He has lapsed into a healing coma. By the time he is healed, you will be dead of the rat's poison.
column2: 他已陷入療癒性昏迷。等他痊癒之時，你早已因鼠毒而喪命。

column1: You have but one chance--to find the Grail! Only its healing powers may yet save you....if you can find it in time.
column2: 你只剩一個機會——尋得聖杯！唯有它的療癒之力或許還能救你……前提是你能及時尋得。

column1: Do not despair or regret your choice. You have done the good and noble deed and saved Galahad, who served you so faithfully.
column2: 莫要絕望，也莫要懊悔你的抉擇。你做了良善而高潔的事，救了對你忠心耿耿的葛拉漢。

column1: Alas! A rat has bitten you! There was nothing you could do to avoid it.
column2: 唉！一隻老鼠咬傷了你！這是你避無可避之事。

column1: The hierophant warned that even one bite was lethal and death inevitable, though it may be slow in coming.
column2: 祭司曾警告，即便只是一口咬傷也是致命的，死亡無可避免，只是來得或許緩慢。

column1: And it appears that Galahad has fallen prey to the rats, for there he lies upon a bier, unaware even of your presence.
column2: 看來葛拉漢也已成為鼠群的獵物，此刻他躺在靈架上，甚至渾然不覺你在此處。

column1: Nay, you chose wrongly! Now you are trapped within this room. By the time Galahad recovers, he will find you dead.
column2: 不，你選錯了！如今你被困在這房間裡。等葛拉漢康復之時，見到的將是你的屍身。

column1: I cannot bear to remain and watch. At least you die knowing that Galahad will live to carry on the mission, for the Goddess has sworn to release him. Farewell, Arthur.
column2: 我不忍留下來看著。至少你臨死之際能知曉，葛拉漢將活下去繼續這項使命，因為女神已立誓要釋放他。永別了，亞瑟。

column1: Never have I felt such contempt for you as I do at this moment. You have chosen your own life over that of Galahad and now he is dead.
column2: 我從未如此刻這般鄙夷你。你選擇了保全自己的性命而非葛拉漢，如今他已死去。

column1: The elixir burns through your body, purging the poison. You are healed in body, but your soul is forever tainted.
column2: 解藥燒遍你的全身，滌淨了毒素。你的肉身痊癒了，靈魂卻永遠蒙上污點。

column1: Galahad is dead. You have failed to save one of your greatest and purest knights. This is a grievous failure on your part.
column2: 葛拉漢死了。你未能救下麾下最偉大、最純潔的騎士之一，這是你莫大的失職。

column1: Arthur, Galahad grows much worse! I fear he is about to die!
column2: 亞瑟，葛拉漢的情況急轉直下！我恐怕他就要死了！

column1: Do not go too close, Arthur, I beg you! a ghoul is not to be trusted.
column2: 亞瑟，求你別靠得太近！食屍鬼不可信任。

column1: You will learn nothing from this long-dead fiend in the sarcophagus.
column2: 從石棺裡這具早已作古的邪物身上，你什麼也問不出來。

column1: Below the pentacle are carved these words...
column2: 五芒星下方刻著這些文字……

column1: Cursed is the priest who lies here. He betrayed the Goddess and stole her treasures. Sacred objects of gold he has stolen.
column2: 長眠於此的祭司受了詛咒。他背叛女神，竊取她的寶物，偷走了聖潔的黃金聖物。

column1: By the sign of the pentacle, he is imprisoned. The star of the Goddess rules him. Take heed, you who read these words of warning.
column2: 憑五芒星的印記，他被囚禁於此。女神之星統御著他。讀到這則警語的人啊，務必當心。

column1: The light is too dim to make out the inscription from here.
column2: 光線太暗，從這裡看不清銘文。

column1: The lid of the sarcophagus is closed.
column2: 石棺的蓋子是闔上的。

column1: You cannot look inside it from here and I do not advise getting closer.
column2: 你從這裡看不進去，我也不建議你靠得更近。

column1: That is quite impossible. It is solid stone.
column2: 那絕無可能，它是實心的石頭。

column1: There is nothing upon the other side of the sarcophagus but a blank wall.
column2: 石棺的另一側除了一面空牆，什麼也沒有。

column1: There are three doorways and colorful patterns upon the walls. There are no mummies or funeral urns here, only the one large, stone sarcophagus.
column2: 這裡有三道門，牆上繪著色彩繽紛的圖案。此處沒有木乃伊或骨灰甕，只有一具巨大的石棺。

column1: What ARE you babbling about?
column2: 你究竟在胡言亂語些什麼？

column1: Nay, Arthur! Let your curiosity rest. Draw no closer, I beg you!
column2: 不，亞瑟！按捺你的好奇心吧。求你別再靠近了！

column1: It crouches in the dark end of the sarcophagus, gibbering, grinding its hideous teeth and smelling of putrefaction, a vile and demented creature.
column2: 牠蜷伏在石棺陰暗的一端，喃喃自語，磨著猙獰的牙齒，散發腐爛的氣味，是個邪惡而瘋狂的生物。

column1: Whatever its origins, it is clearly evil and hungers for that which is still alive.
column2: 不論牠的來歷為何，牠顯然邪惡，渴求著仍有生氣之物。

column1: It is solid stone, carved with geometric designs on the sides. There is something different upon the lid, however.
column2: 它是實心石材，側面刻著幾何圖案。不過蓋子上頭有些不同的東西。

column1: There is a pentacle carved upon it and an inscription in Latin below that.
column2: 上面刻著一枚五芒星，下方還有一段拉丁文銘文。

column1: The light is too dim to make it out from here.
column2: 光線太暗，從這裡看不清楚。

column1: It is the five-pointed star or pentacle that is associated with the Goddess.
column2: 那是與女神相關聯的五芒星，即五角星形。

column1: And because it is formed of one unbroken line, it is used to keep out harmful spirits. Or to lock them in.
column2: 由於它是由一筆不間斷的線畫成，因此可用來擋住有害的鬼靈，或是將牠們封鎖在內。

column1: There are many colourful geometric patterns painted upon the walls and doorways.
column2: 牆上與門邊繪著許多色彩繽紛的幾何圖案。

column1: One wall has geometric designs painted upon it and a pentacle over one door. The other three walls are barren.
column2: 一面牆上繪有幾何圖案，其中一道門上方有一枚五芒星，其餘三面牆則空無一物。

column1: It is...well, frankly, Arthur, I do not know what it is. I do not know EVERYTHING.
column2: 那是……嗯，老實說，亞瑟，我也不知道那是什麼。我並非無所不知。

column1: There are some support beams sticking out of the wall over one door.
column2: 有幾根支撐橫樑從一道門上方的牆裡凸出。

column1: The lid is under the control of the Thing inside. I guarantee you could not move it.
column2: 蓋子受裡頭那東西所掌控，我敢保證你根本移不動它。

column1: It IS shut.
column2: 它確實是關著的。

column1: The stone lid is heavy and undoubtedly better left in place.
column2: 石蓋十分沉重，無疑最好別去動它。

column1: The thing in the sarcophagus wants nothing further to do with you, fortunately.
column2: 所幸，石棺裡的那東西不想再與你有任何瓜葛。

column1: Merely possessing the medallion is protection enough. The fiend will know it is there.
column2: 光是持有這條六角星項鍊便足以自保，那邪物會知曉它的存在。

column1: It is more likely to get you, were you to attempt such folly.
column2: 你若貿然做出這等蠢事，牠反倒更可能捉住你。

column1: The sarcophagus is closed.
column2: 石棺是闔上的。

column1: If what you seek is in the sarcophagus, it is guarded by the Thing.
column2: 你若尋找的東西在石棺裡，那便有那東西看守著。

column1: There was but one and you took it.
column2: 那裡原本只有一個，已被你取走。

column1: Impractical, not to mention impossible.
column2: 不切實際，更別說根本不可能。

column1: You cannot kill that which is already dead.
column2: 你殺不死早已死去之物。

column1: Yes, come closer. I will show you my golden treasure. Do not be afraid.
column2: 是啊，再靠近些。我會讓你瞧瞧我的黃金寶藏，不必害怕。

column1: I wish only to smell more of your warm blood, to hear the rhythm of living breath in your lungs. That is all. Come closer.
column2: 我只想再多嗅幾分你溫熱的血氣，聽一聽你肺裡活人呼吸的節奏。僅此而已，再靠近些。

column1: Sssssst! Begone! The accursed Goddess protects you. Begone!
column2: 嘶嘶嘶！滾開！那該死的女神在庇護著你。滾開！

column1: Your source of protection? Are you mad!?
column2: 你的護身之物？你瘋了嗎！？

column1: How could I have raised you to be such a fool?
column2: 我怎會把你養育成這般愚笨之人？

column1: Arthur, do not tempt fate by trifling with this ghoul.
column2: 亞瑟，別拿這隻食屍鬼來試探命運。

column1: There is nothing left to get.
column2: 已經沒有東西可拿了。

column1: The Thing drank it then ate the glass vial.
column2: 那東西喝下了它，接著連玻璃瓶一起吞下。

column1: Without the medallion around your neck, you are no longer protected from the Thing. You were a fool to part with it.
column2: 沒了掛在頸間的六角星項鍊，你便不再受那東西的庇護。捨棄它實在愚蠢。

column1: Screeeeeaaaagh! The accursed pentacle!
column2: 嘎啊啊啊啊！那該死的五芒星！

column1: The Thing has retreated from the warding spell of the medallion. There is a glint of gold at this end of the sarcophagus.
column2: 那東西已被六角星項鍊的護符之力逼退。石棺這一端閃著一絲金光。

column1: I believe....aye, it is a golden apple.
column2: 我想……沒錯，那是一顆金蘋果。

column1: An apple of solid gold! I wonder how often the fiend has used it as a lure.
column2: 一顆純金打造的蘋果！不知那邪物用它當誘餌，騙過了多少次。

column1: Hang onto it this time, Arthur.
column2: 這次好好留著它，亞瑟。

column1: Alas, curiosity killed the King. Even the worms will go hungry by the time the ghoul is finished with you.
column2: 唉，好奇心害死了國王。等那食屍鬼把你解決掉時，連蛆蟲都要餓肚子了。

column1: I smell warm blood and live flesh. Come closer. I have golden treasure. Come closer and see.
column2: 我嗅到了溫熱的血與活人的肉。再靠近些。我有黃金寶藏，靠近來瞧瞧。

column1: The sound of the Thing gnashing at your apple is truly revolting. And what a waste of the Seeress' gift!
column2: 那東西啃咬你那顆蘋果的聲音，實在令人作嘔。這下白白浪費了女預言家的贈禮！

column1: The Thing devours the elixir, vial and all. That was truly a foolilsh move. It does the creature no good, but leaves you with no protection from rat bite.
column2: 那東西把解藥連瓶子一併吞下。這一步實在愚蠢，對那生物毫無益處，卻讓你失去了對抗鼠咬的防護。

column1: I cannot imagine what possessed you to do such a mindless thing.
column2: 我實在想不透，是什麼鬼迷心竅讓你做出這種蠢事。

column1: From the sound of the ghoul's gnashing teeth, I would say it enjoyed even that old bone. Imagine how much more he would enjoy your own, fresh bones.
column2: 聽那食屍鬼磨牙的聲音，我猜牠連那根舊骨頭都吃得津津有味。可以想見，牠會有多麼享用你那新鮮的骨頭。

column1: The Thing in the sarcophagus wants nothing further to do with you, fortunately.
column2: 所幸，石棺裡的那東西不想再與你有任何瓜葛。

column1: The stairs lead upward.
column2: 這道階梯通往上方。

column1: There are two doorways to this room.
column2: 這房間有兩道門。

column1: A mural covers one entire wall. There are two doorways, mummies and painted designs, including many spirals.
column2: 一整面牆繪滿了壁畫。這裡有兩道門、數具木乃伊，以及包括許多螺形紋飾在內的彩繪圖案。

column1: There are lunar and solar spirals here. A solar spiral goes in the sunwise direction. Sunwise is the direction that the shadow of the sun moves around a sundial.
column2: 這裡有太陽螺紋與月亮螺紋。太陽螺紋依順日方向盤繞，順日方向即是日晷上日影移動的方向。

column1: A lunar spiral moves to the left, in the opposite or counter-sunwise direction.
column2: 月亮螺紋則向左盤繞，與順日方向相反，即逆日方向。

column1: Solar spirals are signs of a God, while lunar spirals are signs of a Goddess.
column2: 太陽螺紋是男神的標識，月亮螺紋則是女神的標識。

column1: This mural shows the death of Hippolytus, as brought about by Aphrodite. The full story is told in your Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 這幅壁畫描繪的是希波萊特斯之死，正是阿芙羅黛蒂一手造成。完整故事記載於你的《Liber ex Doctrina》之中。

column1: This poor warrior had his head split in two.   He must have lain there for centuries. We shall never know his story.
column2: 這名可憐的戰士頭顱被劈成兩半，想必已在此躺了數個世紀，他的故事我們永遠無從得知。

column1: The skeletons of the mummies remain well wrapped.
column2: 這些木乃伊的骸骨依舊包裹得完好。

column1: It was split in half by some powerful blow from a large sword. A helmet would have saved him.
column2: 它是被某柄大劍的一記重擊劈成兩半的，若有頭盔或許能保住他一命。

column1: All the skulls in this room are well-wrapped... which is sometimes more than I can say for yours.
column2: 這房裡所有的頭骨都包裹得很好……有時候，我對你的腦袋可就沒把握這麼說了。

column1: To learn more about what the mural shows, read the Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 想多了解這幅壁畫描繪的內容，去讀《Liber ex Doctrina》吧。

column1: It is quite old, but intact, though not as good as what you have.
column2: 它相當古老，卻依然完整，只是比不上你手上那件。

column1: The only armour here is upon your person.
column2: 這裡唯一的甲冑，就穿在你自己身上。

column1: A secret exit has opened in the mural. This is now the only way out.
column2: 壁畫中開啟了一道密門，如今這是唯一的出路。

column1: One wall is covered with the mural, with four spirals in the corners. There are more spirals upon another wall, and some geometric designs on the other doorway.
column2: 一面牆被壁畫覆蓋，四個角落各有一枚螺形紋飾。另一面牆上還有更多螺形紋飾，另一道門邊則繪有幾何圖案。

column1: Other than the spirals and mural, the other decorations are simply painted geometric designs.
column2: 除了螺形紋飾與壁畫之外，其餘裝飾都只是彩繪的幾何圖案。

column1: The way is open. Surely the end of your mission draws nigh.
column2: 通路已開。你此行的終點，想必已經不遠了。

column1: Nay, let it lie undisturbed any further. The way is open. Press onward.
column2: 不，就讓它繼續安眠吧。通路已開，繼續前行。

column1: It is old and far inferior to your own.
column2: 它十分老舊，遠遠比不上你自己那件。

column1: The tunnel has brought you to this room. In the wall behind you, the hidden door seals. You cannot even see where it was.
column2: 甬道將你帶到了這房間。你身後的牆上，那道密門已經封閉，你甚至看不出它原本在哪裡。

column1: Heavy stone doors have sealed the room! Has the Goddess trapped you or---nay. Look!
column2: 沉重的石門已將這房間封死！難道是女神把你困在此處，還是——不，你看！

column1: Secret stairs leading upward have been revealed....along with the skeleton of a warrior.
column2: 一道通往上方的密梯顯露出來……旁邊還有一具戰士的骸骨。

column1: You should not be trapped in 73
column2: 你不該被困在 73 裡

column1: This room is smaller and more barren, except for the mural upon one wall. The opposite wall has partially collapsed. There are no mummies or urns here.
column2: 這房間較小也更為空蕩，除了一面牆上的壁畫之外別無他物。對面的牆壁已部分崩塌，這裡沒有木乃伊或骨灰甕。

column1: It shows the story of Pygmalion, which is written in your Liber ex Doctrina. This version is rather fancifully embellished with doves and piping satyrs.
column2: 它描繪的是皮格梅里恩的故事，記載於你的《Liber ex Doctrina》之中。這個版本添了不少幻想的點綴，畫著鴿子與吹笛的森林之神。

column1: Except for the one mural, the other walls are bare. Part of the wall opposite the mural has crumbled away.
column2: 除了那幅壁畫之外，其餘牆面都光禿禿的。壁畫對面的牆壁有一部分已經崩落。

column1: I suppose the satyr figures in the mural represent the nature god, Pan, playing upon his pipes.
column2: 我猜壁畫裡吹著笛子的森林之神形象，代表的是自然之神潘恩。

column1: There are doves shown in the mural, representing the power of Aphrodite.
column2: 壁畫中畫著幾隻鴿子，代表阿芙羅黛蒂的力量。

column1: The stone dove you now carry is much like the doves painted in the mural.
column2: 你此刻攜帶的石鴿，與壁畫中所繪的鴿子十分相似。

column1: It is merely a decorative element in the mural.
column2: 那不過是壁畫中的裝飾元素罷了。

column1: To learn more of this legend, read the Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 想多了解這則傳說，去讀《Liber ex Doctrina》吧。

column1: There is an inverted cross above one door. The Christians call it St. Peter's Cross, for they believe the apostle Peter was crucified upside-down.
column2: 一道門上方有一個倒十字。基督徒稱之為聖彼得十字，因為他們相信使徒彼得是被倒釘十字架而死。

column1: There are some geometric designs painted in one doorway.
column2: 一道門邊繪著幾個幾何圖案。

column1: There is nothing there.
column2: 那裡什麼也沒有。

column1: Behind and to each side of the statue, hidden doors have opened.
column2: 雕像的背後與兩側，都出現了敞開的密門。

column1: It is utterly empty except for a statue of Aphrodite.
column2: 這裡空無一物，只有一尊阿芙羅黛蒂的雕像。

column1: This room holds only the statue of Aphrodite and now has a total of four doors from which to choose.
column2: 這房間只有阿芙羅黛蒂的雕像，如今共有四道門可供選擇。

column1: There is a stone statue of Aphrodite in the center of the room. Upon one hand rests a carved dove, but the other hand, though held out with palm open, is empty.
column2: 房間正中央立著一尊阿芙羅黛蒂的石像。一手擱著一隻雕鑿的鴿子，另一手雖攤開手掌伸出，卻空無一物。

column1: The statue of Aphrodite now holds the apple which has turned to stone in its hand.
column2: 阿芙羅黛蒂的雕像手中，如今握著那顆已化為石頭的蘋果。

column1: The walls are completely blank.
column2: 牆壁完全是空白的。

column1: What seemed to be blank walls have revealed three hidden doors.
column2: 原本看似空白的牆壁，如今顯露出三道密門。

column1: Only half of the doorway into the room is left for part of the wall has crumbled away.
column2: 通往這房間的門洞只剩一半，因為牆壁有一部分已經崩塌。

column1: With the exception of the doorway through which you entered, the other doorways are utterly black inside and it is impossible to tell what might lie within.
column2: 除了你進來時經過的那道門之外，其餘門內一片漆黑，完全看不出裡頭有什麼。

column1: I cannot imagine why you think the Goddess herself would answer you.
column2: 我實在想不透，你為何認為女神本尊會親自回應你。

column1: The statue shows no sign of answering.
column2: 雕像沒有任何回應的跡象。

column1: The statue of Aphrodite has a dove upon her hand. Doves are considered one of her fertility symbols.
column2: 阿芙羅黛蒂的雕像手上停著一隻鴿子。鴿子被視為她的生育象徵之一。

column1: The statue's instructions were to use the dove after you had proven yourself with sword and shield.
column2: 雕像的指示是：待你以劍與盾證明自己之後，再使用那隻鴿子。

column1: I shall attempt to recall the directions: six doors must be entered in this order: west, east, south, east, south, north.
column2: 我試著回想那些方向：六道門必須依此順序進入：西、東、南、東、南、北。

column1: It encompasses all things that are considered plants.
column2: 凡屬植物之類，皆涵蓋於此。

column1: It refers to anything that is an animal.
column2: 凡屬動物之類，皆涵蓋在內。

column1: In this place, it would not surprise me to hear a statue talk, but this one shows no interest in speech as yet.
column2: 在這種地方，就算聽見石像開口說話，我也不會意外，但這一尊至今尚無開口的跡象。

column1: You have passed this test and the statue is silent.
column2: 你已通過此試煉，石像陷入沉默。

column1: You are not making sense, Arthur.
column2: 你這話毫無道理，亞瑟。

column1: It has turned to stone and become part of the statue.
column2: 它已化為石頭，成了石像的一部分。

column1: It is part of the statue.
column2: 它是石像的一部分。

column1: What nonsense is this? You were given the dove.
column2: 這是什麼胡言亂語？你已得到了那隻鴿子。

column1: That is quite beyond your ability.
column2: 這遠超出你的能力。

column1: You have given the statue the only apple it required.
column2: 你已把石像所需的唯一一顆蘋果交給了它。

column1: You have both a green apple and a golden apple.
column2: 你身上同時有一顆青蘋果與一顆金蘋果。

column1: The apple fit perfectly in the statue's hand, but caused nothing to happen.
column2: 蘋果恰好嵌入石像的手中，卻沒有任何動靜。

column1: You have brought the gift by which I am made complete. For this, I will tell you what you must do to escape the catacombs.
column2: 你帶來了使我完整的禮物。為此，我將告訴你該如何逃出這地下墓窖。

column1: First, be warned. From this moment on, every door within the catacombs is a possible trap. If you leave the safety of this room too soon, you may be trapped forever within a tomb.
column2: 首先，容我提醒你：自此刻起，這地下墓窖裡的每一扇門都可能是陷阱。若你過早離開這房間的庇護，你或許將永遠困死於某座墓穴之中。

column1: It is Aphrodite's will that you should know something of her history. I will pose you six questions to test your knowledge of her.
column2: 阿芙羅黛蒂的旨意，是要你知曉她的一些過往。我將提出六個問題，考驗你對她的認識。

column1: Each question requires but one word in answer. When you have answered all six, I shall reveal to you how you may escape the catacombs.
column2: 每個問題只需一個字作答。待你答完全部六題，我便會告訴你如何逃出這地下墓窖。

column1: As for the sacred cup, it lies beyond the catacombs. You will not find it here. The test now begins.
column2: 至於那神聖之杯，它在地下墓窖之外，你在此處是找不到的。試煉現在開始。

column1: That is not the answer. The test continues.
column2: 這不是答案。試煉繼續。

column1: The answer requires but a single word. The test continues.
column2: 答案只需一個字。試煉繼續。

column1: That is the answer. The test continues.
column2: 這正是答案。試煉繼續。

column1: You have given the six answers I require and earned your chance at freedom. First, accept this gift.
column2: 你已答出我所要求的六個答案，贏得了重獲自由的機會。且先收下這件禮物。

column1: When you have proven yourself by sword and shield, the time will be right to use the dove.
column2: 待你以劍與盾證明自己之時，便是使用那隻鴿子的時機。

column1: To escape from the catacombs, you must enter six doors exactly as I tell you. If you choose a door that is wrong, you will find yourself trapped forever.
column2: 要逃出這地下墓窖，你必須依我所言，一絲不差地走過六扇門。若你選錯了門，你將永遠受困於此。

column1: You begin here by choosing the first door you must enter.
column2: 你要從此處開始，選出你該走的第一扇門。

column1: The doors you choose must face the direction I give you and you must ENTER them in exactly this order....
column2: 你所選的門，必須朝向我告訴你的方向，且必須依照這個順序逐一進入……

column1: West, east, south, east, south, north.
column2: 西、東、南、東、南、北。

column1: Have no fear for Galahad. When he is healed, I shall set him free. You have earned that boon.
column2: 無須為葛拉漢憂心。待他傷勢痊癒，我便會釋放他。你已贏得這份恩典。

column1: I shall not speak again. Your escape relies now upon your own ingenuity.
column2: 我不會再開口了。你能否脫身，如今全憑你自己的機智。

column1: You are enclosed in a narrow tunnel within the wall. Inch forward carefully and test the floor as you go.
column2: 你被困在牆內一條狹窄的通道中。小心翼翼地一寸寸前進，邊走邊試探地面。

column1: It takes you in one direction. Let us hope you find an exit soon, for it is as cold as the grave and the stone walls covered with something slick and unpleasant.
column2: 它只通往一個方向。但願你能盡快找到出口，這裡冷得如同墳墓，石牆上還覆著一層濕滑黏膩的東西。

column1: The tunnel stops at a wall. Push, Arthur! Aye, it gives way into one of the rooms of the catacombs through a hidden doorway.
column2: 通道盡頭是一堵牆。用力推，亞瑟！沒錯，它讓開了一道路，通向地下墓窖裡的一間密室，門就藏在其中。

column1: Catch him, Arthur! He must not escape!
column2: 抓住他，亞瑟！絕不能讓他逃了！

column1: Hurry! You must not let him out of your sight for an instant!
column2: 快！你片刻都不能讓他離開你的視線！

column1: You will never see it again unless you catch that Thief!
column2: 除非你抓住那個小偷，否則你再也見不到它了！

column1: Arthur, nothing else matters except that you catch that thief and retrieve the Grail at once!
column2: 亞瑟，此刻別無他事要緊，你只須立刻抓住那個小偷，奪回聖杯！

column1: First, you must catch him!
column2: 你得先抓住他！

column1: Do not stand there then! Chase him!
column2: 那就別杵在那裡！追上去！

column1: First you must catch him and quickly!
column2: 你得先抓住他，快！

column1: Aye, you must, but only if you catch the Thief!
column2: 正是，但前提是你得先抓住那小偷！

column1: First catch the Thief, then decide how to deal with him.
column2: 先抓住那小偷，再來決定如何處置他。

column1: I can hardly blame you for being upset, but it will take more than foul language to catch the thief.
column2: 你心煩意亂，我不怪你，但光靠粗言穢語可抓不住那小偷。

column1: Each broken pillar looks much the same as its neighbor. You must find the right one by your wits.
column2: 每根斷裂的柱子看起來都與鄰旁的相差無幾。你得憑自己的智慧找出正確的那一根。

column1: The elegant marble pillars which once held a roof have all been broken and thrown down, the work of those who would destroy the worship of Aphrodite.
column2: 這些昔日支撐屋頂的華美大理石柱，如今已全數斷裂倒塌，正是那些意圖摧毀阿芙羅黛蒂信仰之人所為。

column1: They are common weeds, of no interest.
column2: 那些只是尋常的雜草，沒什麼好留意的。

column1: The round pedestal in the center of the temple's ruins must have once held an altar or statue, but is empty now.
column2: 神殿廢墟中央的圓形底座，想必昔日曾立有祭壇或雕像，如今卻已空無一物。

column1: The walls which encompass these ruins have deliberately been build without windows or doors, to enclose and hide this ruin.
column2: 圍繞這片廢墟的牆壁，是刻意建成沒有窗戶或門的模樣，為的是封閉並隱藏這座遺跡。

column1: It closed solidly behind you. Only the Goddess herself could reopen it.
column2: 它在你身後牢牢闔上了。唯有女神本人才能將它重新開啟。

column1: The stairs bring you to the surface and into blessed light and fresh air.
column2: 這階梯將你帶回地面，重見祝福般的光明與新鮮空氣。

column1: Around you is the ruin of a circular temple. Once there was a famous Temple of Aphrodite in Jerusalem. Perhaps this was it.
column2: 你身處一座圓形神殿的廢墟之中。耶路撒冷曾有一座著名的阿芙羅黛蒂神殿，或許眼前這座正是。

column1: The marble stones are ancient and weather-worn. The marble pillars are toppled and an empty round pedestal in the middle may have once held a statue or altar.
column2: 這些大理石早已古老斑駁，飽經風霜。大理石柱已然傾倒，中央那座空的圓形底座，想必昔日曾立有雕像或祭壇。

column1: Walls without doors or windows have been built entirely around the temple, right up to the very edge of the ruins.
column2: 沒有門窗的牆壁將神殿團團圍住，一路築到廢墟的邊緣。

column1: The indentation once held a pillar.
column2: 這處凹痕，昔日曾立著一根柱子。

column1: The spiral carved into the threshold is lunar. That is, it turns to the left and denotes feminine power and influence.
column2: 門檻上刻著的螺形紋飾屬於月相，也就是說，它向左旋繞，象徵女性的力量與影響。

column1: The steps lead down into a narrow alley.
column2: 階梯向下通往一條狹窄的巷弄。

column1: The Thief ran this way. Catch him!
column2: 那小偷是往這個方向逃的。抓住他！

column1: Stop babbling and catch the Thief!
column2: 別再喋喋不休了，快去抓住那小偷！

column1: He is dead, you fool! Catch the Thief!
column2: 他已經死了，你這個傻子！去抓那小偷！

column1: She is gone, you fool! Catch the thief!
column2: 她已經走了，你這個傻子！去抓那小偷！

column1: Forget that! Catch the Thief!
column2: 別管那個了！去抓那小偷！

column1: The alley is bounded by tall buildings without windows or doors. It takes a sharp turn not far from the Temple stairs.
column2: 這條巷弄兩側是沒有窗戶或門的高聳建築。離神殿階梯不遠處，巷弄陡然一轉。

column1: Just around the bend in the alley, there is a tiny grate in the bottom of the wall. Otherwise, there seem to be no windows or doors in these walls.
column2: 就在巷弄轉角過去不遠處，牆根有一個小小的柵格。除此之外，這些牆上似乎再無窗戶或門。

column1: The fallen pillars are too heavy to look under.
column2: 倒塌的柱子太過沉重，無法翻看底下。

column1: Why do you waste time here? The Temple awaits you but a few steps away.
column2: 你何必在此浪費時間？神殿只在幾步之外等著你。

column1: This appears to be the only way in or out of the Temple.
column2: 這似乎是進出神殿唯一的通道。

column1: They are the fallen marble pillars that once formed the Temple of Aphrodite.
column2: 那些是倒塌的大理石柱，昔日曾構成阿芙羅黛蒂神殿的一部分。

column1: There is none here.
column2: 此處並無此物。

column1: There is a tiny grate or barred opening of some sort at the base of this wall.
column2: 牆根處有一個小小的柵格，或說某種帶柵欄的開口。

column1: There are a few trees rising above the high walls that encircle the Temple.
column2: 幾株樹木高過圍繞神殿的高牆，探出頭來。

column1: A few roofs can be glimpsed in the distance, for all the good it does you.
column2: 遠處隱約可見幾片屋頂，但對你也沒什麼用處。

column1: The stairs and only entrance to the Temple face the alley where once they must have faced a major street.
column2: 神殿的階梯，也是唯一的入口，如今面向這條巷弄——想必昔日曾面向一條大街。

column1: It is one of the walls which enclose the temple.
column2: 這是圍住神殿的其中一面牆。

column1: Aye, that IS your mission. Do get on with it.
column2: 正是，這正是你的使命。快去做吧。

column1: He grovels before you, pleading for mercy. You have two choices--take up the Grail and show him mercy, or draw your sword and strike him down.
column2: 他在你面前匍匐哀求，乞求饒恕。你有兩個選擇——拿起聖杯，饒他一命，或是拔劍將他斬殺。

column1: She is no longer concerned with these affairs. You must decide whether or not to show mercy to this man.
column2: 她已不再過問這些俗事。你必須自行決定是否饒恕此人。

column1: The Thief offers it to you. You must decide whether to slay him, or take it and show him mercy.
column2: 那小偷將它奉還於你。你必須決定，是要殺了他，還是收下它、饒他一命。

column1: Arthur, this man is begging for mercy. You must deal with him. Nothing else matters.
column2: 亞瑟，這人正在乞求饒恕。你必須處置他，此刻別無他事要緊。

column1: Are you blind? He grovels in front of you.
column2: 你瞎了嗎？他就匍匐在你面前。

column1: He deserves nothing from you except possibly your mercy. Either take the Grail or slay him.
column2: 他不配從你這裡得到什麼，或許唯有你的憐憫例外。拿起聖杯，或是殺了他，二者擇一。

column1: Do not be absurd. Either take the Grail and show him mercy, or draw your sword and slay him.
column2: 休得荒唐。拿起聖杯饒他一命，或是拔劍將他殺了。

column1: The alley ends here, going nowhere. All the other walls around you are featureless.
column2: 巷弄到此為止，再無去路。四周其餘的牆面皆平淡無奇。

column1: But to one side there is an alcove in which rests the weathered head of an ancient stone statue. And there is a window at the top of the alcove and another tiny grate at the bottom.
column2: 但一側有個壁龕，裡頭安放著一顆風化的古代石像頭。壁龕頂部有一扇窗，底部則另有一個小柵格。

column1: Why do you waste time here? Return to the Temple.
column2: 你何必在此浪費時間？回神殿去吧。

column1: Since this is a dead end, you seem to have no choice but to return to the Temple.
column2: 既然此處已是死路，你似乎除了回神殿之外別無選擇。

column1: There is a tiny grate or barred opening of some sort at the base of this wall. I believe it may even be the top of a buried window.
column2: 這面牆根處有一個小小的柵格，或說某種帶柵欄的開口。我猜這或許正是一扇被掩埋的窗戶的上緣。

column1: And there is a small window high in this alcove, with a single metal bar across it.
column2: 壁龕高處還有一扇小窗，橫著一根鐵條。

column1: There is a small window high in this alcove, with a single metal bar across it.
column2: 壁龕高處有一扇小窗，橫著一根鐵條。

column1: The stairs and only entrance to the Temple are at the other end of this alley which ends here.
column2: 神殿的階梯，也是唯一的入口，位於這條巷弄的另一端，而巷弄到此為止。

column1: It could be the head of a god, a king, a warrior. Who can say? Perhaps the entire statue is buried. We shall never know its strange story.
column2: 那或許是神祇之首，或是君王，或是戰士，誰能說得準？也許整尊石像都埋在地底。它的離奇來歷，我們終究無從得知。

column1: That would be wonderful, if it were here.
column2: 若真在此處，那就太好了。

column1: That is quite impossible for it is partially buried and would weigh far more than you could manage to move.
column2: 這絕無可能，它有一部分埋在地底，重量遠非你所能搬動。

column1: I hardly think such barbaric behaviour is called for.
column2: 我實在不認為有必要做出如此野蠻的舉動。

column1: The window is too high to reach.
column2: 那扇窗太高，搆不著。

column1: Nay, your god smiles upon you! His rope has broken!
column2: 不，你的神明正對你微笑！他的繩子斷了！

column1: By all that is holy, you have dallied shamelessly and the Thief has escaped. There is no hope for you, Arthur. You may as well fall upon your sword.
column2: 憑一切神聖之名，你竟如此無恥地虛耗光陰，讓那小偷逃了。你已無望可言，亞瑟。你不如伏劍自盡算了。

column1: By all the gods, he will escape!
column2: 憑諸神之名，他要逃了！

column1: Mercy, master, mercy! I am only a poor, miserable wretch! Have mercy!
column2: 饒命啊，主人，饒命！我只是個可憐悲慘的窮鬼！求你饒命！

column1: Here is your treasure, untouched! Take it and let me live, I beg you! Have mercy!
column2: 這是你的寶物，分毫未動！收下它，饒我一命，我求你了！求你饒命！

column1: He is a pathetic creature. You must choose, Arthur. Either take up the Grail now in an act of mercy....or draw your sword and slay him.
column2: 他是個可悲的傢伙。你必須做出抉擇，亞瑟。此刻，或是拿起聖杯，展現憐憫……或是拔劍將他斬殺。

column1: By the gods, he dared to stab you in the back! If not for your mail tunic, you would be dead at the hands of this foul dog.
column2: 憑諸神之名，他竟敢從背後刺你一劍！若非你身上這件鎖甲，你早已死在這條惡狗手裡。

column1: It is time to let the Grail decide his fate.
column2: 是時候讓聖杯來決定他的命運了。

column1: And so, he comes to the end he deserves.
column2: 於是，他迎來了自己應得的結局。

column1: Now you must move quickly to find Galahad and return to Camelot.
column2: 如今你必須盡快找到葛拉漢，返回肯萊特。

column1: I do not blame you for slaying him after all the grief he has caused you. The merchants of Jerusalem would no doubt thank you.
column2: 他帶給你的苦楚如此之多，我不怪你殺了他。耶路撒冷的商人們必定會感謝你。

column1: At least the Grail is unharmed. Now you must move quickly to find Galahad and return to Camelot.
column2: 至少聖杯毫髮無損。如今你必須盡快找到葛拉漢，返回肯萊特。

column1: Mercy, I beg you, show mercy!
column2: 饒命，我求你，饒了我吧！

column1: The scholar may know more about symbols than you.
column2: 這位學者對符號的了解，或許比你更多。

column1: There are no olives.
column2: 沒有橄欖了。

column1: Hazm is not here.
column2: 哈慈不在這裡。

column1: Perhaps you should stay and seek knowledge from the old scholar.
column2: 或許你該留下，向這位老學者請益。

column1: His clothing and bearing are simple, yet his words reveal wisdom and complexity.  There is no doubt that he is what he says he is.
column2: 他的衣著與舉止都樸素無華，言語間卻透著智慧與深意。毫無疑問，他確如自己所言。

column1: Even his name, Al-Sirat, is a clue.  It is a name for the knife-edged path of truth that one must tread to reach paradise or heaven.
column2: 就連他的名字 Al-Sirat 也是條線索。那是真理之路的名字——一條刃薄如鋒的道路，人須踏過它才能抵達樂園或天堂。

column1: Which means, Arthur, that he invited you here for a specific purpose, one which you must unravel for yourself.
column2: 這意味著，亞瑟，他邀你前來自有特定用意，而那用意，你得自己解開。

column1: You must unravel his purpose for yourself.
column2: 他的用意，你得自己解開。

column1: The walls are a bit too high for that.
column2: 那些牆太高了，做不到。

column1: Overhead, it is open sky.
column2: 頭頂上是一片開闊的天空。

column1: Beneath the colourful mats there is pale, sandy earth.
column2: 這些色彩繽紛的墊子底下，是淡色的沙質地面。

column1: I suspect this is a place of meditation and that Al-Sirat's home is elsewhere.
column2: 我猜這裡是個沉思冥想之處，Al-Sirat 的住所應在別處。

column1: There is nothing here save four bare walls, plants, the two rugs and a small table with a carafe, cups and a bowl of figs.
column2: 此處空無一物，只有四面光禿的牆、幾株植物、兩張地毯，還有一張小桌，上頭擺著一個玻璃瓶、幾只杯子與一碗無花果。

column1: Through the open doorway one can see the hills and the high desert.
column2: 透過敞開的門，可以望見丘陵與高地沙漠。

column1: The serenity of the scholar's courtyard make the port and town of Gaza seem far away.
column2: 這學者庭院裡的靜謐，讓加薩的港口與城鎮彷彿遙不可及。

column1: A tree branch gives some scant shade to this open yard.
column2: 一根樹枝為這片開闊的庭院投下些許稀疏的樹蔭。

column1: It is a small cup.  The carafe must contain a strong drink.
column2: 這是個小杯子。玻璃瓶裡裝的想必是烈性的飲品。

column1: There is no more qahwah in the carafe.
column2: 玻璃瓶裡已沒有 qahwah 了。

column1: The elegant carafe holds the brew, qahwah, that he prepared for you.  From the small size of the cups, it must be quite potent.
column2: 這只精緻的玻璃瓶裡，裝著他為你準備的飲品 qahwah。從杯子的小巧看來，這飲品想必後勁十足。

column1: There are no more ripe figs in the bowl.
column2: 碗裡已沒有熟透的無花果了。

column1: There are ripe figs in the bowl.
column2: 碗裡有熟透的無花果。

column1: Aye, he has aloe vera growing here.  It is a desert plant with a bitter, astringent sap.
column2: 沒錯，他在這裡種著蘆薈。這是一種沙漠植物，汁液又苦又澀。

column1: It is a low, round, wooden table just large enough to hold the carafe, cups and one bowl.
column2: 這是一張低矮的圓形木桌，大小恰好能擺下玻璃瓶、杯子與一只碗。

column1: It could be a young olive tree in the planter.  Another tree gives some scant shade to this open yard.
column2: 花盆裡種的或許是一株幼橄欖樹。另一棵樹則為這片開闊的庭院投下些許稀疏的樹蔭。

column1: They seem to be quite ordinary bushes. I believe that is a young tree in the planter.
column2: 這些看起來只是尋常的灌木。我想花盆裡那株是幼樹。

column1: The rugs are brightly decorated in abstract patterns.
column2: 這些地毯以鮮豔的抽象花紋裝飾著。

column1: There are four, plain walls forming this enclosed yard.
column2: 四面樸素的牆，圍成這座封閉的庭院。

column1: The ground is bone dry and covered with a pale sandy soil.
column2: 地面乾涸龜裂，覆著一層淺色的沙土。

column1: The most powerful smell here is that of the qahwah, which is both bitter and oddly pleasant.
column2: 此處最濃烈的氣味來自qahwah，苦澀卻又帶著一股奇異的怡人香氣。

column1: Can you not tell when you are on your own two feet?
column2: 你難道連自己是不是站著都分不清？

column1: It would be better to pay attention, Arthur.
column2: 你最好專心點，亞瑟。

column1: That would be a silly thing to carry about with you in the desert.
column2: 帶著這東西走進沙漠，未免太蠢。

column1: Al-Sirat has informed you that your mule is being cared for by Hazm.  When you leave, she will be there, as usual.
column2: Al-Sirat 已告訴你，你的騾子由哈慈照料著。你離去時，她一如往常會在那裡等你。

column1: It should be obvious that this scholar has no money.
column2: 顯而易見，這位學者身無分文。

column1: Only by passing the tests of the Six Guardians will you eventually find the Grail.
column2: 唯有通過六位守護者的試煉，你才能終得聖杯。

column1: Are you sure, Arthur?  The qahwah is a bit TOO invigorating.  I fear you may never sleep again.
column2: 你確定嗎，亞瑟？這qahwah提神得有點過頭，我擔心你恐怕從此再也睡不著了。

column1: I am sorry, my friend, there is no more.
column2: 抱歉，朋友，已經沒有了。

column1: Thank you, I have had my fill.
column2: 多謝，我已經喝夠了。

column1: Your cup is full, Arthur.
column2: 你的杯子已經滿了，亞瑟。

column1: You ARE sitting, Arthur.
column2: 你已經坐著了，亞瑟。

column1: Jerusalem lies northeast of Gaza, but you must pass through the desert to reach it.  And you cannot survive the heat of this desert unless you find water upon the way.
column2: 耶路撒冷位於加薩東北方，但你必須穿越沙漠才能抵達。若不能在途中尋得水源，你撐不過這片沙漠的酷熱。

column1: Farewell.
column2: 珍重。

column1: You must stand up before you can take your leave.
column2: 你得先起身，才能告辭離去。

column1: My pardons, I have only qahwah for you.
column2: 恕我招待不周，我只有qahwah能奉上。

column1: In the name of the Goddess, I bid you welcome.
column2: 以女神之名，歡迎你的到來。

column1: I am ready to answer what inquiries you put to me.  Think carefully and neglect nothing, for you will not see me again once you leave here.
column2: 我已備妥回答你的一切詢問。仔細思量，不要遺漏任何事，因為你一旦離開此處，便不會再見到我了。

column1: When you leave here, he will lead you by secret paths away from Gaza to the edge of the desert that you must cross.
column2: 你離開此處時，他會引你走隱密的小徑，穿出加薩，直抵你必須橫越的那片沙漠邊緣。

column1: To walk the path that leads to truth and knowledge is all that I desire.
column2: 行走在通往真理與知識的道路上，便是我唯一的心願。

column1: I cannot accept such a gift, nor do I desire it.
column2: 這樣的餽贈，我既不能收下，也毫無所求。

column1: I have no money, but there are merchants aplenty in Jerusalem.
column2: 我身無分文，但耶路撒冷不乏商賈。

column1: I have little, and nothing I choose to sell.
column2: 我所有無多，也沒有什麼願意出售。

column1: No words, however crude or foul, can affect me unless I allow it, which I shall not.
column2: 無論多麼粗鄙污穢的言語，都動搖不了我，除非我自己允許，而我絕不會如此。

column1: I do not travel in the desert and cannot give you any directions, save that Jerusalem lies northeast of Gaza.  But beware, the way through the desert is devious.
column2: 我不曾涉足沙漠，無法為你指路，只知耶路撒冷位於加薩東北方。但要當心，穿越沙漠的路途詭譎多變。

column1: Hazm will pass a well as he leads you from Gaza and there you may drink.  Beyond that, I cannot help you.
column2: 哈慈引你離開加薩時，會經過一口水井，你可在那裡飲水。除此之外，我便幫不上你了。

column1: I have no waterskin to give you, I regret.
column2: 很遺憾，我沒有水袋可以給你。

column1: I will not part with my carafe, nor would it serve your purpose.
column2: 我的水瓶我不會割捨，況且它也派不上你的用場。

column1: I will not part with my qahwah cups and, delicate as they are, they would not endure your journey.
column2: 我的qahwah杯我不會割捨，況且它們精巧易碎，禁不起你這趟旅程的顛簸。

column1: I will not part with my bowl.  It is the only one I have.
column2: 我的碗我不會割捨，那是我僅有的一只。

column1: I will not part with my rugs.  Indeed, what you see here is nearly all I possess.
column2: 我的地毯我不會割捨。說實話，你眼前所見，幾乎就是我的全部家當了。

column1: Although many Muslims are tolerant of Christians, the mukhtar of Gaza delights in killing them, or anyone like them.
column2: 儘管許多穆斯林對基督徒相當包容，加薩的村長卻樂於殺害基督徒，或任何與他們相似之人。

column1: There is no more qahwah.  You seem to have aquired a taste for it quite readily.
column2: qahwah已經沒有了。看來你很快便對它上了癮。

column1: The carafe and the cups are for my qahwah.  Please help yourself.
column2: 這水瓶與杯子是用來盛我的qahwah，請自行取用。

column1: Qahwah is a hot drink made from brewing the roasted, crushed beans of the qahwah tree.
column2: qahwah是一種熱飲，以qahwah樹烘焙、搗碎的豆子沖煮而成。

column1: You may find it bitter, but it is most invigorating.
column2: 你或許會覺得它苦澀，但提神效果極佳。

column1: You have eaten all the figs.
column2: 你已把無花果吃個精光。

column1: In the bowl on the table are sweet figs that Hazm picked for me.  Please eat them, if you wish.
column2: 桌上碗裡是哈慈替我摘來的甜無花果，你若想吃，儘管取用。

column1: I will show you the symbol again, if you will name the goddess whose symbol you wish to see.
column2: 你若說出想看哪位女神的標識，我便再展示給你看。

column1: There is no symbol to see......yet.
column2: 眼下……還沒有標識可看。

column1: He is a good boy and will be a fine scholar one day.
column2: 他是個好孩子，日後必成一位傑出的學者。

column1: You need not fear for your mule.  Hazm loves animals and will take good care of her until you are ready to depart.
column2: 你不必為你的騾子擔心。哈慈喜愛動物，會妥善照顧她，直到你準備啟程為止。

column1: Six Guardians stand between you and this sacred cup.  Six times you will be judged, weighed and tested.  They will be tests of mind, spirit and body.
column2: 六位守護者橫亙在你與這只聖杯之間。你將受六次評斷、衡量與試煉，考驗你的心智、心靈與體魄。

column1: If you prevail, the Goddess will relinquish her guardianship of the sacred cup.  What you call the Holy Grail will pass into your hands and its powers of regeneration will be yours.
column2: 你若得勝，女神便會放下對這只聖杯的守護。你所稱的聖杯將落入你手中，其重生之力亦將歸你所有。

column1: There are six you must pass.  I am the first.
column2: 你必須通過六位守護者，我是第一位。

column1: There are always bandits, for there are always men of greed.
column2: 盜匪永遠都在，因為貪婪之人永遠都在。

column1: To reach paradise, one must walk the razor-edged path of truth and purity.
column2: 欲達天堂，須行走於真理與純潔那條如刀鋒般的道路。

column1: He who came before you searched long and far, yet he did not come here, though I sent Hazm with an invitation.
column2: 在你之前來尋訪的那位，找了許久、走了很遠，卻始終沒有來到此處，儘管我已派哈慈送去邀請。

column1: I know nothing more of him save that he reached Jerusalem, but has not succeeded in his quest.
column2: 關於他，我只知他已抵達耶路撒冷，但尚未完成他的探尋。

column1: He did not come to this land.
column2: 他並未來到這片土地。

column1: The Goddess gave birth to the universe.  By many names and faces she is known.  As Virgin, Mother and Crone.  As Birth, Growth and Death.
column2: 女神孕育了宇宙。世人以諸多名號與面貌認識她：作為處女、母親與老太婆；作為誕生、成長與死亡。

column1: I serve her in her form of Aphrodite, but she has six other manifestations which must concern you.  You will not reach the Grail unless you learn of these Six Goddesses.
column2: 我以阿芙羅黛蒂之相侍奉她，但她另有六種化身，是你必須留心的。除非你認識這六位女神，否則你到不了聖杯面前。

column1: Six is the sacred number of Aphrodite.
column2: 六，是阿芙羅黛蒂的聖數。

column1: It is not safe for you. You will be wise to avoid it.
column2: 那對你並不安全，避開它才是明智之舉。

column1: There are men who know the desert and where precious water may be found, but there are men who will guide you astray so they may kill and rob you.  Be careful who you trust.
column2: 有人熟知這片沙漠、知道珍貴水源何在，但也有人會故意引你走偏，好殺你劫你。信任誰，要謹慎選擇。

column1: It is barren, treacherous and hot as a furnace. I have known of men who cooked eggs upon the rocks at midday.
column2: 那裡荒蕪、險惡，酷熱如爐。我聽聞有人曾在正午的岩石上把雞蛋煮熟。

column1: The Zion gate is in the southern wall of Jerusalem.
column2: 錫安城門位於耶路撒冷的南面城牆。

column1: The Jaffa gate is in the western wall of Jerusalem and there is no fee to enter it.
column2: 賈法城門位於耶路撒冷的西面城牆，由此入城不需付費。

column1: He is the official who runs Gaza.  He has just come to power and he hates foreigners, especially Christians.  You have escaped his notice for now, but Gaza is very dangerous for you.
column2: 他是治理加薩的官員，才剛掌權，痛恨外邦人，尤其是基督徒。目前你還沒引起他的注意，但加薩對你而言十分危險。

column1: There is water between here and Jerusalem, but I cannot help you to find it.
column2: 此處與耶路撒冷之間確有水源，但我無法助你尋得。

column1: Certainly, as Hazm leads you from Gaza, he will see you have a drink at a well, but that will not take you far in the desert.
column2: 當然，哈慈引你離開加薩時，會讓你在一口井邊飲水，但那點水撐不了你在沙漠裡走太遠。

column1: The path to truth is as narrow and dangerous as a razor's edge.
column2: 通往真理之路，如刀鋒般狹窄而危險。

column1: Though I am more than willing to answer questions, I will answer only those questions which I deem significant.
column2: 我雖十分樂意回答問題，但只會回答我認為重要的問題。

column1: None for me, thank you.
column2: 我不用了，謝謝。

column1: I am so glad you enjoyed my figs. What a shame there are no more.
column2: 很高興你喜歡我的無花果，可惜已經沒有了。

column1: These are the names of the Six Goddesses: Athene, Vesta, Isis, Astarte, Ceres, Venus.
column2: 這便是六女神的名號：雅典娜、維斯塔、艾西斯、阿斯塔特、席瑞絲、維納斯。

column1: And these are their symbols.
column2: 而這些便是她們的標識。

column1: This is the symbol of Athene.
column2: 這是雅典娜的標識。

column1: This is the symbol of Vesta.
column2: 這是維斯塔的標識。

column1: This is the symbol of Isis.
column2: 這是艾西斯的標識。

column1: This is the symbol of Astarte.
column2: 這是阿斯塔特的標識。

column1: This is the symbol of Ceres.
column2: 這是席瑞絲的標識。

column1: This is the symbol of Venus.
column2: 這是維納斯的標識。

column1: There was nothing terribly interesting about that other wall.
column2: 另一面牆並沒有什麼特別值得一看的東西。

column1: It is good that you have come.  The Captain sent word to me that you were here, though in truth I have been expecting you for some time.
column2: 你能前來，甚好。隊長已捎信告訴我你到了，其實我等候你已有些時日了。

column1: I am Al-Sirat, the first of Six Guardians who serve the Goddess, she who gives the power of life and regeneration through her sacred cup, which you know as the Grail.
column2: 我是 Al-Sirat，六位守護女神聖杯者中的第一位。她藉由她那只聖杯——也就是你所知的聖杯——賜予生命與重生之力。

column1: We who are the Six Guardians will test you in different ways.  We will test your mind, spirit and body.  You must pass each one of us before the Goddess will relinquish her sacred cup to you.
column2: 我們六位守護者，將以不同方式試煉你，考驗你的心智、心靈與體魄。你必須通過我們每一位，女神才會將她的聖杯交到你手中。

column1: Excuse me, Master.  I have fed and watered the mule for your guest, as you said.
column2: 稟告主人，我已依吩咐替貴客的騾子餵食飲水了。

column1: Thank you, Hazm.  Wait with the mule until our guest is ready to leave.  Then you will guide him in secret away from Gaza.
column2: 多謝，哈慈。你且守著騾子，等貴客準備啟程，再悄悄引他離開加薩。

column1: I am a scholar.  I have spent my life in study and meditation.  I am at your disposal, to share what knowledge I may.
column2: 我是個學者，畢生鑽研學問、潛心冥想。但憑差遣，我所知所學，皆願與你分享。

column1: And please, allow me to offer you qahwah to drink and figs to eat.  It is simple fare, but all that I have.
column2: 也請容我奉上qahwah與無花果。粗茶淡飯，卻已是我所能給予的一切。

column1: PRESS F6 WHEN FINISHED
column2: 完成後請按 F6

column1: Here is the challenge placed before you. There are six Tablets engraved with a symbol, one for each of the Six Goddesses.
column2: 眼前便是擺在你面前的考驗。這裡有六塊刻著標識的石板，各代表六女神之一。

column1: There are six Niches for the tablets. Choose a Niche and I will pose a question, one question for each of the Six Goddesses.
column2: 這裡有六個安放石板的壁龕。選一個壁龕，我便會提出一道問題，每位女神各有一題。

column1: You must know which Goddess answers the question, then move the Tablet with her symbol into the Niche.
column2: 你必須判斷是哪位女神能回答這道問題，再把刻著她標識的石板移進那個壁龕。

column1: When you have answered all six questions, only then will I tell you whether you have passed or failed.
column2: 待你答完全部六道問題，我才會告訴你，你是通過了，還是失敗了。

column1: I bid you to begin and may Aphrodite smile upon you.
column2: 我請你開始吧，願阿芙羅黛蒂對你展露微笑。

column1: Click on an empty Niche to see the clue.  Click on a Tablet to select it. Click on a destination to move the selected Tablet.  PRESS F6 WHEN ALL TABLETS HAVE BEEN PLACED.
column2: 點選空壁龕以查看線索。點選石板以選取它。點選目的地以移動選取的石板。所有石板都放妥後請按 F6。

column1: USE ARROW KEYS TO POSITION CURSOR BOX.  On an empty Niche: press "Enter" to see clue.  On a Tablet: press "Enter" to select. Position cursor box on destination, and press "Enter" again to move the selected Tablet.  PRESS F6 WHEN ALL TABLETS HAVE BEEN PLACED.
column2: 用方向鍵移動游標框。停在空壁龕上：按「Enter」查看線索。停在石板上：按「Enter」選取。將游標框移至目的地，再按一次「Enter」以移動選取的石板。所有石板都放妥後請按 F6。

column1: Your wisdom is great.  You have passed my test.
column2: 你的智慧非凡，你已通過我的試煉。

column1: You have not passed my test. Will you try again?
column2: 你未能通過我的試煉。要再試一次嗎？

column1: My King! You have won the Grail!
column2: 吾王！您已贏得聖杯！

column1: Aye, but rise, Sir Galahad, and draw near to your King at once! A great power is at work!
column2: 正是，但快起身，葛拉漢爵士，速速上前見你的王！一股偉大的力量正在運作！

column1: The Grail has chosen to bring you home in your hour of desperate need!
column2: 在你危急存亡之際，聖杯選擇帶你回家！

column1: The Grail has brought you here, Arthur. Only one god may rule in thy kingdom now. The altar of the Christ god awaits its vessel.
column2: 聖杯帶你來到此處，亞瑟。如今你的王國只能容一位神祇為主。基督之神的祭壇，正等候著承接它的聖器。

column1: Cast down your eyes! The radiance of the Grail is too great for any man to see.
column2: 垂下你的雙眼！聖杯的光輝太過耀眼，凡人不可直視。

column1: Behold, Mithra has been driven away! And the Grail is gone!
column2: 看啊，米夏拉已被驅逐！聖杯也已消失無蹤！

column1: It has become a healing force that spreads outward, touching every corner of your kingdom!
column2: 它已化作一股治癒之力向外擴散，觸及你王國的每一個角落！

column1: The land returns to life. The lakes and rivers and wells fill once more with clean, fresh water.
column2: 這片土地重獲新生。湖泊、河流與水井再度盈滿潔淨甘美的水。

column1: Camelot is healed!
column2: 肯萊特痊癒了！

column1: You receive Gwenhyver's praise and adoration, as you have well earned.
column2: 你得到了昆海兒的讚美與愛慕，這是你應得的。

column1: Your knights salute you and the joyous cries of the love and      gratitude of your people fills          the air.
column2: 你的騎士向你致敬，人民滿懷愛戴與      感恩的歡呼聲，迴盪在          空中。

column1: And so you have won, through purity of spirit and heart, through skill and strength. No praise is too great.
column2: 如此，你已然勝利——憑藉心靈與靈魂的純淨，憑藉技藝與力量。任何讚譽，都不足以言表。

column1: With peace and prosperity returned to your kingdom, you have the time to rest and enjoy the land you have saved.
column2: 隨著和平與繁榮重返你的王國，你終於有時間歇息，享受你所拯救的這片土地。

column1: But though your land is healed, your heart is not. Perhaps it never shall be.
column2: 然而，縱使你的國土已然痊癒，你的心卻未曾痊癒。或許，永遠也不會痊癒。

column1: Would you like to:
column2: 你希望：

column1: My lord King, look upon your stronghold, Camelot. By strength of spirit, skill of sword and quickness of mind, you have built a kingdom that could live in legends.
column2: 吾王，且看你的要塞——肯萊特城堡。你以堅毅的心志、精湛的劍術與敏捷的智謀，締造了一個足以名留傳奇的王國。

column1: Beneath your firm and wise hand, the warring tribes of Celts, Saxons, Jutes, and Angles have been brought under control and foreign marauders driven from the shores.
column2: 在你堅定睿智的治理之下，凱爾特人、撒克遜人、朱特人與盎格魯人這些征戰不休的部族俱已臣服，外敵劫掠者也已被逐出海岸。

column1: Your queen is the beautiful Gwenhyver, who loves you and whom you love dearly. Yet you know that her deepest and most passionate love is reserved for your greatest knight, Sir Launcelot.
column2: 你的王后，美麗的昆海兒，愛著你，你也深愛著她。然而你心知，她最深沉、最熱切的愛，卻留給了你麾下最傑出的騎士——蘭斯洛特爵士。

column1: And because Launcelot is chivalrous, brave and a true friend, you do nothing to bring harm to him or your queen. Instead, you suffer in silence.
column2: 而蘭斯洛特為人豪俠、驍勇，又是你真摯的朋友，你不忍加害於他或你的王后，只能獨自默默承受這份苦楚。

column1: Sharing the Round Table with you are noble warriors of the realm: Launcelot, Kai, Ector, Gareth, Percival, Gawaine, Galahad and many others.
column2: 與你同坐圓桌的，是這王國裡的高貴武士：蘭斯洛特、凱伊、艾克特、加雷斯、帕西法爾、高文、葛拉漢，以及其他許多人。

column1: And I? I am Merlin. Advisor, mentor and, as some would have it, wizard, though my true nature remains a secret known only to the ancient gods and me.
column2: 至於我？我是梅林。你的顧問、導師，也有人稱我是巫師，但我真正的本相，唯有古老諸神與我自己知曉。

column1: I must speak to you now of dark truths: the forbidden love of Gwenhyver and Launcelot has cast a blight upon your soul. And in so doing, has put a curse upon your kingdom.
column2: 此刻，我必須向你道出一則黑暗的真相：昆海兒與蘭斯洛特之間那段禁忌之愛，已在你的靈魂上投下陰影，也因此為你的王國招來了詛咒。

column1: The fruit has withered on the vine, grain dies of disease, while springs and wells turn foul. Your people cry out to you for a miracle.
column2: 果實在藤上枯萎，穀物染病而死，泉水與井水俱已腐臭。你的子民正向你哭求奇蹟。

column1: A vision of the Holy Grail covered in a white cloth appeared to you in your time of need. Three of your greatest knights went forth to seek it...
column2: 就在你最需要指引之時，一幅覆著白布的聖杯異象，在你眼前顯現。你麾下三位最傑出的騎士，隨即啟程尋找它……

column1: ...Sir Gawaine...
column2: ……高文爵士……

column1: ...Sir Launcelot...
column2: ……蘭斯洛特爵士……

column1: ...and Sir Galahad.
column2: ……以及葛拉漢爵士。

column1: Gawaine, Launcelot and Galahad have not returned. The search must now fall to you and during this search you will be sorely tested in physical, moral and spiritual strength.
column2: 高文、蘭斯洛特與葛拉漢至今未歸。如今，這場尋找必須落到你的肩上，而在尋找途中，你的體魄、道德與心靈之力都將受到嚴酷的考驗。

column1: If you are found wanting in any of these virtues, the Grail will be denied to you and your kingdom will turn to ashes and dust.
column2: 若你在這些德行中有任何一項有所欠缺，聖杯將棄你而去，你的王國也將化為灰燼與塵土。

column1: I will watch over you and speak to you, though I will be with you only in spirit, not body.
column2: 我將守護著你、與你交談，儘管伴隨你的只有我的心神，而非我的軀體。

column1: Prepare well, Arthur, for once you begin, you dare not turn back. Seek the Holy Grail! Search with all speed and dedication. Time is running out.
column2: 亞瑟，做好萬全準備，因為此行一旦啟程，便再無回頭之路。去尋找聖杯！以最快的速度、最堅定的心意去尋找。時間所剩無多。

column1: The forest and undergrowth are too thick to go that way.
column2: 林木與灌叢過於濃密，無法從那個方向通行。

column1: I do not have the ability to look inside a solid tree.  I doubt that you have.
column2: 我沒有透視實心樹木的能力，我想你也沒有。

column1: The forest grows thicker and darker.  It is impossible to see very far.
column2: 森林愈發濃密昏暗，視線難及遠方。

column1: There are roots under the trees.
column2: 樹下有盤結的樹根。

column1: Most of them are too tall for that.
column2: 多數樹木對此而言都太高了。

column1: Aye, 'tis a forest and therefore filled with trees.
column2: 正是，此地乃森林，自然林木遍布。

column1: Overhead is a thick canopy of leaves and interwoven branches filled with dappled light.
column2: 頭頂是濃密交織的枝葉華蓋，篩落點點斑駁的光影。

column1: Trees are generally adorned with leaves.  Indeed, the trees here are quite thick with them.
column2: 樹木本就綴滿枝葉，此地的樹木更是枝葉茂密。

column1: Most trees of my acquaintance have roots.  They are no threat to you, unless you are particularly clumsy.
column2: 依我所知，樹木大多都有根。它們對你並無威脅，除非你格外笨拙。

column1: It is too thick to see through.
column2: 過於濃密，無法看穿。

column1: The undergrowth of this forest protects many animals, but is the bane of travelers.
column2: 此地的灌木叢庇護著眾多野獸，卻是旅人的剋星。

column1: The rich forest floor is covered with centuries of fallen leaves and thick grasses which muffle the sound of your passage.
column2: 肥沃的林地覆滿數百年堆積的落葉與濃密的野草，讓你行走的腳步聲悄然無聲。

column1: It is a thick, hardy type of wild grass.
column2: 這是一種濃密而耐生的野草。

column1: The only thing you would find under these stones is forest soil and a few worms perhaps.
column2: 在這些石頭底下，你只會找到林地的泥土，或許還有幾條蟲子。

column1: There is much good stone in the forest, though some stones are more dangerous than others.
column2: 森林裡有不少好石頭，不過有些石頭比其他的更為危險。

column1: There are only glimpses of the sky through the thick canopy of leaves overhead.
column2: 透過頭頂濃密的枝葉華蓋，只能瞥見片片天光。

column1: It should not surprise you to see your knees, saddle and horse.
column2: 看見自己的膝蓋、馬鞍與坐騎，應該不會讓你感到意外。

column1: There is nothing more exciting to see than your own booted feet.
column2: 沒有什麼比看著自己那雙穿靴的腳更令人興奮的了。

column1: Aside from some very ordinary beetles, there is nothing of interest there.
column2: 除了幾隻極為普通的甲蟲，那裡沒有什麼值得留意的。

column1: Once it was a tree, now it is a log.  Someday, it will be peat.  Such is the cycle of life.
column2: 它曾是一棵樹，如今成了朽木。終有一日，它將化為泥炭。生命的循環，便是如此。

column1: Forget the beetles.  Think about your sacred mission.
column2: 別管那些甲蟲了，想想你神聖的使命吧。

column1: There are no berries in the Forest Perilous.  Or certainly none you would dare to eat.
column2: 派瑞樂斯森林裡沒有漿果，至少沒有你敢吃的那種。

column1: There are none here, but avoid the forest mushrooms at all costs.
column2: 這裡沒有，但無論如何都要避開林中的蕈菇。

column1: They hear you and smell you and stay well away.
column2: 牠們聽見你、嗅到你的氣味，便遠遠避開了。

column1: The birds are all but invisible in the dense trees.
column2: 鳥兒隱身在濃密的林木間，幾乎難見蹤影。

column1: He looks much the same as he did a moment ago.
column2: 他看起來和方才並無二致。

column1: What horse?
column2: 什麼馬？

column1: He is part of the spirit of the forest and dwells in the heart of it.  You will not see him here.
column2: 他是森林精魄的一部分，棲居於林心之中，你在此處是見不到他的。

column1: There are prints of your horse heading toward Camelot.  You may assume he is safe.
column2: 地上有你坐騎的蹄印，朝著肯萊特的方向而去。你可以斷定牠平安無事。

column1: Gawaine will never be seen upon this earth again.
column2: 高文再也不會出現在這世間了。

column1: Have you not seen enough boars for one quest?
column2: 難道這一趟任務裡，你見到的野豬還不夠多嗎？

column1: The giant boars of the Forest Perilous are particularly dangerous.  How fortunate there are none around at the moment.
column2: 派瑞樂斯森林裡的巨型野豬格外危險。所幸此刻附近一頭也沒有。

column1: You would need chisels for that.  You do not have time to play at being a stonemason.
column2: 那需要鑿子才行。你沒有閒工夫扮演石匠。

column1: Your mule does not answer.
column2: 你的騾子沒有回應。

column1: It is not edible.  Nor does it look appetizing.
column2: 它不能吃，看起來也毫無食欲。

column1: It smells of green growing things, of musty mouldering things beneath the earth, of ash and oak, the passage of wolf and bear, squirrel and hare -- a thousand mingled scents of life and decay.
column2: 空氣中瀰漫著青翠草木的氣息，混著地底腐朽發霉之物，還有梣木與橡木、狼與熊、松鼠與野兔行過的痕跡——生與滅的萬千氣味交織在一起。

column1: Almost impossible to do unless you have a net and many helpers.  Which you do not.
column2: 除非你有網子與眾多幫手，否則幾乎不可能辦到。而你兩者皆無。

column1: There is no-one here to help.
column2: 這裡沒有人可以幫忙。

column1: There is the rush of wind through the leaves, the scurry and scitter of the squirrels and small creatures, the bell-like notes of the birds.  The creaking of your leather and metallic jingle of your gear sets you apart from this forest world.
column2: 風穿過枝葉發出陣陣呼嘯，松鼠與小獸窸窸窣窣地竄動，鳥鳴清脆如鈴。而你身上皮革的吱嘎聲與裝備的金屬叮噹聲，卻讓你與這片森林的世界格格不入。

column1: You could spend the rest of your life trying to cut your way through this forest.  Use your head and find the easiest path.
column2: 你就算耗盡餘生，也未必能砍出一條穿越這片森林的路。動動腦筋，找出最容易的那條路。

column1: For that you want an axe and you have none.
column2: 要做那件事，你需要一把斧頭，而你並沒有。

column1: You don't feel particularly inclined to climb trees.  Anyway, what do you expect if you did? A golden egg or a magick bird or something?
column2: 你並不特別想爬樹。再說，就算爬了，你又能指望什麼？一顆金蛋，還是一隻魔法鳥？

column1: Rather like trying to ride the air, I would think.
column2: 我想，那大概就像試圖騎乘空氣一樣吧。

column1: Is this some strange delusion you have that you are riding a horse, O' Arthur, King of all the Britons?
column2: 亞瑟，不列顛諸民之王啊，你莫非有種奇怪的錯覺，以為自己正騎著馬？

column1: You have no time to spare for hunting.
column2: 你沒有時間可以耗在狩獵上。

column1: The surviving boars have retreated far from this part of the forest.  They fear you now.
column2: 倖存的野豬已退到這片森林的遠處，牠們如今對你心生畏懼。

column1: Face the giant boars only if you must.  They are the most deadly of the wild creatures here.
column2: 除非萬不得已，否則別去招惹那些巨型野豬。牠們是此地最致命的野獸。

column1: I am sure you will find a likely tree when the need is great enough.
column2: 我相信，當真有必要時，你自會找到合適的樹。

column1: From the deafening silence, I would say there are no talking stones here.
column2: 從這震耳欲聾的寂靜看來，此處應該沒有會說話的石頭。

column1: This is not a talking tree.
column2: 這不是一棵會說話的樹。

column1: I am already speaking.
column2: 我已經在說話了。

column1: St. Leonard is long gone from his Forest and of no use to you.
column2: 聖倫納德早已離開他的森林，對你毫無用處。

column1: The joys of hunting Windsor must wait for another time.
column2: 在溫莎狩獵的樂趣，得留待日後再說了。

column1: There is nothing in ancient Avebury to help your search.
column2: 古老的埃夫伯里裡沒有任何東西能幫上你的尋找。

column1: These silent stones of Mottistone have no tale to tell.
column2: 莫蒂斯通這些沉默的石頭，並無故事可說。

column1: Let us hope you never have need of the healing waters of Bath.
column2: 但願你永遠用不上巴斯的療癒之泉。

column1: St. Keyne of Keynsham has no connection with the Grail.
column2: 凱恩夏姆的聖凱恩，與聖杯毫無關聯。

column1: The bishop of Winchester may be a miracle worker, but not even he knows where the Grail may be.
column2: 溫徹斯特的主教或許能行奇蹟，但就連他也不知道聖杯身在何處。

column1: The martyrs of Shapwick provide no clue.
column2: 沙普維克的殉道者提供不了任何線索。

column1: Avoid Halstock, where St. Juthware could not keep her head.
column2: 避開哈斯托克，聖朱斯瓦在那裡連自己的頭顱都保不住。

column1: There is nothing of worth to milk from Braunton.
column2: 布朗頓沒有什麼值得你去汲取的東西。

column1: Neither Hercules nor Hartland Point will lead to the Grail.
column2: 海克力斯與哈特蘭角，都不會指引你找到聖杯。

column1: St. Sidwell's waters in Exeter will reveal nothing of use.
column2: 艾克希特的聖西德威爾之泉，不會透露任何有用的訊息。

column1: Neither Brutus, his giants nor clue of the Grail are to be found in Totnes.
column2: 布魯特斯、他的巨人們，或是聖杯的線索，在托特尼斯都找不到。

column1: It is made of the purest crystal, as best I can tell, and it contains enormous power such as only a wizard or enchantress could control.
column2: 依我看，它是以最純淨的水晶製成，蘊藏著巨大的力量，唯有巫師或女巫方能駕馭。

column1: Such beings tend to manifest near some spot where they were once worshipped.
column2: 這類存在往往會在昔日受人崇拜之處現身。

column1: They will not answer you now.
column2: 牠們此刻不會回應你。

column1: You must find a place where they will answer you.
column2: 你必須找到一個牠們願意回應你的地方。

column1: These walls are ancient and most likely would collapse beneath you.
column2: 這些牆垣年代久遠，你一踩上去多半會塌陷。

column1: What a useless idea.
column2: 這主意毫無用處。

column1: She is undoubtedly grazing at the bottom of the hill.
column2: 她想必正在山腳下吃草。

column1: Not a trace of the Monk is left.  The Old Ones have taken him, body and soul.
column2: 僧侶已無蹤影可尋，古代幽靈已將他連同肉身與靈魂一併帶走。

column1: If he is in these ruins, you will surely find him.
column2: 他若在這片廢墟之中，你必能找到他。

column1: Are YOU mad?!  He is here!
column2: 你瘋了嗎？！他就在這裡！

column1: You have the air of a man who is searching for someone, but I assure you I am the only other soul upon this Tor.
column2: 你身上帶著尋人的神情，但我向你保證，這座山丘上除了我，再無旁人。

column1: He appears to be just on the other side of the wall.
column2: 他似乎就在牆的另一側。

column1: There is little to be found but rubble.
column2: 這裡除了瓦礫，幾乎一無所有。

column1: Inside the rubble is....nothing.
column2: 瓦礫之中……什麼也沒有。

column1: It is only debris from the collapsed walls and roof of whatever once stood here.
column2: 這不過是此處昔日建物倒塌的牆垣與屋頂殘骸。

column1: The sky is open overhead.  Not a bit of the original roof remains.
column2: 頭頂天空一片開闊，原本的屋頂已蕩然無存。

column1: These could possibly be the ruins of the shrine built by Joseph of Arimathea, but no one, not even I, can be sure of that.
column2: 這裡或許就是亞利馬太的約瑟所建聖堂的遺跡，但無人能夠斷定——即便是我，也不敢肯定。

column1: You have more important things to do.
column2: 你還有更重要的事得做。

column1: It has been a sacred hill for centuries.
column2: 數百年來，這一直是座聖丘。

column1: The Old Ones took his body and soul away.
column2: 古代幽靈把他的肉身與靈魂一併帶走了。

column1: Perhaps the Monk no longer dwells here.  As yet, there is no sign of him.
column2: 或許那僧侶已不再住在此處，至今仍不見他的蹤影。

column1: There is no monk in sight here.
column2: 這裡不見任何僧侶的蹤影。

column1: Those glazed, fanatical eyes filled with hatred, those snarling lips flecked with foam!  The Monk truly is a madman!
column2: 那雙充滿仇恨、目光呆滯而狂熱的眼睛，那咆哮著、沾滿唾沫的雙唇！這僧侶果真是個瘋子！

column1: Ah, so THIS is why he is called the Mad Monk of Glastonbury.
column2: 啊，原來這便是他被稱為格列斯登伯利瘋僧侶的緣由。

column1: This Monk seems calm enough.  Perhaps he is not the one they call the Mad Monk.  We shall see.
column2: 這位僧侶看起來相當平靜。或許他並非人稱瘋僧侶的那一位。且看下去便知。

column1: The spell of Circular Entrapment is broken now that you possess this crystal heart, for this was the object of power which held the spell in place.
column2: 如今你已擁有這顆水晶心，環困之咒已然破除，因為正是這件靈物維繫著這道咒語。

column1: There is a spell of Circular Entrapment cast over Glastonbury Tor.  You cannot leave here unless you break it.
column2: 格列斯登伯利山上籠罩著一道環困之咒，除非破除它，否則你無法離開此地。

column1: I sense only minor sorcerous ability in the monk, so there must be some other source of extraordinary power to hold the spell in place.
column2: 我只感應到這僧侶身上有些許微弱的法力，想必另有非凡的力量之源，維繫著這道咒語。

column1: There are many illusions.  Some say life itself is an illusion.  But this is no time for philosophical discourse.
column2: 幻象有很多種。有人說生命本身便是一場幻象。但此刻並非高談哲理之時。

column1: This monk has minor sorcerous powers, enough to generate two illusions of himself to confuse you.
column2: 這僧侶身懷些許法力，足以幻化出兩個自己的分身來迷惑你。

column1: The illusions are harmless, but the monk is armed with a deadly club and can do you great harm indeed.
column2: 那些幻象並無害處，但僧侶手持一根致命的棍棒，確實能對你造成重創。

column1: I do not know of any key.
column2: 我不知道有什麼鑰匙。

column1: I know nothing of a crystal heart.  What a peculiar thing to ask about.
column2: 我對水晶心一無所知，你問這個還真是奇怪。

column1: My heart is fine, thank you.
column2: 我的心很好，多謝關心。

column1: Joseph of Arimathea is a legendary figure, supposedly a man who helped to bury Christ and who then brought the Grail to our island and established a shrine upon this Tor.
column2: 亞利馬太的約瑟是一位傳說人物，據說他曾協助安葬基督，其後將聖杯帶到我們這座島上，並在此山丘建立了一座聖堂。

column1: Any doors this building once had are long gone.
column2: 這棟建築昔日或許有過門，但如今早已蕩然無存。

column1: Grass, rubble, some bushes....not much to see, really.
column2: 草地、瓦礫，還有幾叢灌木……其實沒什麼好看的。

column1: The ghost of the Mad Monk is here, but cannot be seen, heard or felt.  He can do you no harm.
column2: 瘋僧侶的鬼魂就在此處，但看不見、聽不到，也感覺不到。他傷不了你。

column1: There are no ghosts here.
column2: 此處並無鬼魂。

column1: There is no body to see here.
column2: 此處並無屍首可看。

column1: He is a stout man with powerful arms.
column2: 他是個體格壯碩、雙臂強而有力的男子。

column1: The Monk's garb is very old, very worn and very smelly.
column2: 這僧侶的衣袍十分老舊，破爛不堪，還臭氣沖天。

column1: You cannot see what is not here.
column2: 不在此處之物，你看不見。

column1: The Old Ones took the club along with the Monk's body.
column2: 古代幽靈把棍棒連同僧侶的屍身一併取走了。

column1: It is a crude but lethal weapon.
column2: 這是件粗陋卻致命的武器。

column1: What club?
column2: 什麼棍棒？

column1: There are no true trees on Glastonbury Tor.  There are only some common bushes.
column2: 格列斯登伯利山上並無真正的樹木，只有些尋常的灌木。

column1: They are common bushes.
column2: 這些是尋常的灌木。

column1: Most of the rocks on this hill are fallen from the ancient walls.
column2: 這座山丘上的石塊，多半是從古老城牆崩落下來的。

column1: You will not hear from these spirits again.   They have taken their silver and gone elsewhere.
column2: 這些幽靈，你不會再聽見牠們的動靜了。牠們已帶著銀兩，離去他方。

column1: You will have to find a way to appease these Old Ones, Arthur, if you are ever to leave this Tor.
column2: 亞瑟，你必須想辦法安撫這些古代幽靈，否則休想離開這座山丘。

column1: Such beings tend to manifest in some spot where they were once worshipped.
column2: 這類存在，往往會在昔日受人祭拜之處現身。

column1: The "Old Ones" is a name sometimes given to ancient, elemental spirits.  Often our ancestors worshipped them as gods, but they are not, though they can be powerful.
column2: 「古代幽靈」，是人們有時用來稱呼上古元素精靈的名字。我們的祖先常將牠們奉為神明祭拜，其實牠們並非神，儘管力量確實不容小覷。

column1: The Old Ones cannot be seen unless they will it.
column2: 古代幽靈除非自願現身，否則無法被看見。

column1: It would be more advisable to go around.  In times of danger, it is best to keep both feet on the ground.
column2: 繞道而行才是明智之舉。身處險境時，雙腳踏實在地為上策。

column1: The confusing swish of his robes does nothing to help you.
column2: 他袍衫窸窣紛亂的聲響，對你毫無助益。

column1: There is an eerie quality to the wind as it blows through these ruins.  Almost like voices chanting.
column2: 風穿過這片廢墟時，帶著一股詭異的氣息，幾乎像是有人在低聲吟唱。

column1: You will get it the hard way if you do not defend yourself!
column2: 你若不自我防衛，就準備吃苦頭吧！

column1: Why should you want a club?  You have Excaliber.
column2: 你何必要棍棒？你已擁有聖劍。

column1: He no longer exists on this earth.
column2: 他已不在人世。

column1: He is not even here.
column2: 他根本不在此處。

column1: Do something, Arthur, before HE gets YOU!
column2: 亞瑟，快做點什麼，別讓他搶先一步抓住你！

column1: Frankly, I think you would be better off without him.
column2: 老實說，我認為沒有他，你反倒更好過。

column1: Personally, I would touch the Monk's garb as little as possible.
column2: 依我看，那僧袍你還是少碰為妙。

column1: You should feel no need for anything as common as a rock when you have Excaliber and your shield.
column2: 你既有聖劍與盾牌在身，何須用得著石頭這種尋常之物。

column1: You already have it.
column2: 你已經擁有此物。

column1: Key? What key?
column2: 鑰匙？什麼鑰匙？

column1: You must know something I do not know.
column2: 你必定知道些我所不知道的事。

column1: Only they can tell you what will appease them.
column2: 唯有牠們自己，才能告訴你如何安撫牠們。

column1: Merely possessing the crystal heart has broken the Spell of Circular Entrapment that has kept you trapped upon this Tor.
column2: 光是持有水晶心，便已破除了那困你於此山丘的循環禁錮咒。

column1: But it is an object of great power.  Keep it safe.
column2: 但此物力量非凡，務必妥善保管。

column1: You waste your time. The monk truly IS mad!
column2: 你這是在浪費時間。這僧侶當真是瘋了！

column1: A lot of good that will do you.
column2: 那對你毫無用處。

column1: He is too busy ranting and raving to talk to you.
column2: 他忙著胡言亂語、瘋狂咆哮，無暇搭理你。

column1: There is no monk here.
column2: 此處並無僧侶。

column1: I do not think the Monk cares very much who you are.
column2: 我看這僧侶根本不在乎你是誰。

column1: He is a pungent fellow.
column2: 他身上的氣味相當刺鼻。

column1: The Tor smells of crushed grass and misty air.
column2: 這座山丘瀰漫著碎草與霧氣的氣息。

column1: The well is elsewhere on the Tor.
column2: 水井在這座山丘的另一處。

column1: There is nothing left to search.
column2: 已無他物可供搜尋。

column1: It would help to find the monk first.
column2: 你若先找到這僧侶，會有幫助。

column1: You will never be able to do that while he is alive, I fear.
column2: 恐怕只要他還活著，你便永遠辦不到此事。

column1: What can you hope to hear from a madman?  But you may try it when you find him.
column2: 從一個瘋子口中，你還能指望聽到什麼？不過待你找到他，倒不妨一試。

column1: But there is no Monk here.
column2: 但此處並無僧侶。

column1: He has nothing to say now that he is dead.  Just as well.  His conversation was a bit limited.
column2: 他已死，如今再無話可說。也好，反正他的談吐本就乏善可陳。

column1: Kill! Kill! Kill!
column2: 殺！殺！殺！

column1: The dead have no use for money.
column2: 死人用不著錢財。

column1: He does not want money.  He wants your life.
column2: 他要的不是錢財，是你的性命。

column1: You must keep your money.  I have taken a monk's vows of poverty.
column2: 你的錢財還是自己留著吧，我已立下僧侶的清貧誓言。

column1: Come, come.  Have a drink.
column2: 來吧，來吧，喝一杯。

column1: Why do you hesitate?  Trust me in all things.
column2: 你何必猶豫？凡事都該信任我。

column1: So, you will not drink, foreign dog?
column2: 這麼說，你這外邦野狗，不肯喝這一杯？

column1: There is but one explanation for this unnatural siege of winter upon the lake -- the mood of the Lady of the Lake has turned cold, and her power affects all that is around her.
column2: 這湖泊反常地陷入寒冬圍困，只有一個解釋——湖中女神的心境轉冷，而她的力量牽動著周遭的一切。

column1: Though the Lady now has her heart and has turned once more to warmth and the natural seasons, it will take some time for the deep cold she laid upon this lake to pass away.
column2: 雖然女神已尋回她的心，重新轉向溫暖，回歸自然時序，但她加諸於此湖的深沉寒意，仍需一段時日才能消退。

column1: There would be no purpose in that.
column2: 那麼做並無意義。

column1: She is beyond your voice, Arthur.
column2: 亞瑟，她聽不見你的呼喚。

column1: All is quiet here, as though nature itself is frozen into silence.
column2: 此處萬籟俱寂，彷彿連大自然本身都凍結於沉默之中。

column1: The glare and sparkle of the ice dazzles your eyes.
column2: 冰面的耀眼光芒與閃爍令你目眩。

column1: No such thing can be seen.
column2: 未見此物。

column1: A glittering palace of ice rises from the center of the lake.
column2: 一座晶瑩剔透的冰宮，自湖心聳然而立。

column1: The heart glows with colour as power flows through it.  Study it carefully.
column2: 力量流轉其中時，這顆心便綻放出色澤。仔細端詳它。

column1: You are surrounded by what looks like solid ice, but it could break beneath your feet at any moment.  Ridges of ice have been thrust up in places.
column2: 你周圍看似堅實的冰面，隨時都可能在你腳下裂開。有些地方的冰層被擠壓隆起成脊。

column1: As an elemental enchantress, she can have more than one form.  In her usual watery form, she is known as the Lady of the Lake.
column2: 身為元素女巫，她能化作不只一種形貌。以她慣常的水之形貌現身時，人稱湖中女神。

column1: And since her form usually reflects her mood, I would say that something is seriously wrong.
column2: 而她的形貌通常映照著她的心境，依我看，此刻必是出了嚴重的差錯。

column1: He has always had the special favour of the Lady of the Lake.  Yet she is possessive and surely is not pleased with his love for Gwenhyver.
column2: 他向來深受湖中女神的特別眷顧。然而她生性佔有欲強，對他鍾情於昆海兒一事，想必極為不悅。

column1: The lake which forms Ot Moor is frozen over.
column2: 形成奧特摩爾的這片湖水，已徹底結凍。
