column1: The spires and peaks of this cold palace have grown from the ice by the power of the Lady of the Lake.  It lies north and slightly west of the shore in the center of the lake.
column2: 這座寒冰宮殿的尖塔與峰頂，是湖中女神以其力量自冰中孕育而成，座落於湖心，偏北偏西處。

column1: A glittering Palace made of ice has been created from the lake itself.
column2: 一座以冰築成的晶瑩宮殿，已由這片湖泊本身孕育而生。

column1: There is naught but glaring ice and bitter cold.
column2: 此處除了刺眼的寒冰與徹骨的嚴寒，別無他物。

column1: It is made of frozen water.  I thought you knew that.
column2: 這是凍結的水所造。我還以為你早就知曉。

column1: It is simply ice pushed upward into a ridge by the pressure of freezing too quickly.
column2: 這不過是冰層因驟然凍結的壓力，被推擠隆起而成的一道冰脊。

column1: The area immediately around Ot Moor is blanketed with snow, which is quite unusual, considering that it is summer.
column2: 奧特摩爾周遭一帶白雪覆蓋，時值夏季，此景著實反常。

column1: Everything is covered with snow and ice.
column2: 萬物皆為冰雪所覆蓋。

column1: None can be seen with all this snow and ice.
column2: 這片冰雪之中，什麼也看不見。

column1: Aye, I sense a spell of guidance upon the rose, but it was placed there by Gwenhyver.  You must speak the Message of the Rose to invoke its spell.
column2: 正是，我感應到這朵玫瑰上有一道指引之咒，但那是昆海兒施加上去的。你必須誦念玫瑰箴言，方能喚醒此咒。

column1: Perhaps you should consult your Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 或許你該查閱你的《Liber ex Doctrina》。

column1: Only the Message of the Rose can invoke the spell placed upon this flower.  Perhaps you should consult your Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 唯有玫瑰箴言，能喚醒施加於這朵花上的咒語。或許你該查閱你的《Liber ex Doctrina》。

column1: I have no spells to offer you, Arthur, nothing save advice.  This is your task alone.
column2: 亞瑟，我沒有咒語能給你，能給的只有忠告。此事終須你獨自承擔。

column1: The spell is in effect! Stay within the whirlwind of petals or you will lose its protection.
column2: 咒語已然生效！留在花瓣旋風之中，否則你將失去它的護佑。

column1: The rose trembles with the spell of the incantation, but the place is not quite right for it to work.
column2: 這朵玫瑰隨著咒語的吟誦而顫動，但此地並非它施展效力的正確場所。

column1: It is cold as ice, clear as crystal in your hand. It pulls you toward the Ice Palace, as though eager to go within.
column2: 它在你手中冰冷如寒霜，澄澈如水晶，彷彿急欲進入冰宮一般，牽引著你朝那方向而去。

column1: There are faint stirrings of color within the heart, flashes of golden and purple light. I sense it is caused by the nearness of the frozen lake. The ice calls to it.
column2: 這顆心之中隱隱浮動著色彩，閃現金光與紫光。我感應到這是因為靠近了這片冰封的湖泊——寒冰在召喚著它。

column1: You ARE using it.
column2: 你正在使用它。

column1: Fortunately, you had time on the journey here to eat, drink, rest, and don your warmer clothing as it grew colder.
column2: 所幸來此的路上，你有時間進食、飲水、歇息，並在天氣轉冷時添上禦寒的衣物。

column1: It is so cold, your nose aches too much to smell anything.
column2: 天寒地凍，你的鼻子凍得生疼，什麼氣味都聞不出來。

column1: Nothing here will burn.  Better to do what you must as quickly as possible and be gone.
column2: 此處無一物可燃。你該儘快辦完該辦之事，速速離去。

column1: Across thin ice you dared to tread, 'tis no surprise that you are dead.
column2: 你竟敢踏上這薄冰之上，喪命於此，又何足詫異。

column1: There are countless rocks in this desert.  This is yet another one.
column2: 這片沙漠裡石頭多不勝數，這不過又是其中一顆。

column1: Aye, 'tis a rock.  A very hot rock.
column2: 正是，是顆石頭。一顆滾燙的石頭。

column1: One rock is much like any other in this merciless terrain.
column2: 在這片無情的地域裡，石頭與石頭之間，並無太大分別。

column1: This treacherous false guide has claimed yet another victim!  Would that you had been a bit quicker with your sword on this occasion.
column2: 這奸詐的惡嚮導，又奪走了一條性命！此番若你出劍再快一些，便不致如此。

column1: Do not swing your sword so close to your mule, Arthur. You might hurt the poor beast.
column2: 亞瑟，別把劍舞得離你的騾子這麼近，你會傷了這可憐的畜生。

column1: Arthur, you must find water soon or you will perish!
column2: 亞瑟，你須儘快找到水源，否則性命難保！

column1: Your mule is suffering from lack of water!
column2: 你的騾子正因缺水而受苦！

column1: Arthur, holding your sword constantly at the ready only serves to tire you more quickly.
column2: 亞瑟，時時刻刻持劍戒備，只會讓你更快疲憊。

column1: Your mule suffers and needs water as urgently as you do.
column2: 你的騾子與你一樣，急需水源解渴。

column1: You sold her to Mohammed, as you should remember.
column2: 你該記得，你已將牠賣給了穆罕默德。

column1: There is no reason to draw your sword here.
column2: 此處沒有拔劍的理由。

column1: That is rather difficult, since you do not have your sword.
column2: 這可有些難辦，畢竟你此刻並未佩劍。

column1: Pay attention, Arthur. Your sword is sheathed.
column2: 亞瑟，留神些。你的劍還在鞘中。

column1: You could, if you but had your sword.
column2: 若你佩著劍，倒是可以。

column1: The incantation works no magick upon the rose. It awaits a time when its spell of guiding will be of the most use.
column2: 這咒語此刻對玫瑰不起作用。它等待的，是指引之咒最能派上用場的時機。

column1: Most poetic, Arthur. And if you had Gwenhyver's rose, the incantation might even have been useful.
column2: 說得真有詩意，亞瑟。若你身上帶著昆海兒的玫瑰，這咒語或許還真能派上用場。

column1: You are a warrior-king, not a discus thrower.
column2: 你是位征戰的王者，不是擲鐵餅的選手。

column1: That is not how one uses a sword, as if I needed to tell you that.
column2: 劍可不是這麼用的——這種事還用得著我提醒你嗎。

column1: The shield could be vital to your continued existence.  Which may not continue much longer with foolish notions like these.
column2: 這面盾牌，可能攸關你的存續。若總懷著這等愚蠢的念頭，你的存續怕是撐不了多久。

column1: Life is dangerous enough without tempting fate by rampant stupidity.
column2: 人生已夠凶險，何必再以荒唐愚行去挑戰命運。

column1: Excaliber is an extension of your very soul.  To abandon it is unthinkable.
column2: 聖劍是你靈魂的延伸，捨棄它，簡直不可思議。

column1: What a truly mindless idea.
column2: 真是個毫無腦子的念頭。

column1: What a foolish notion.
column2: 真是個愚蠢的念頭。

column1: That is not only stupid, it is impossible since you do not have it.
column2: 這不僅愚蠢，而且根本不可能——你並未持有此物。

column1: There is no need to greet me, Arthur. I am here.
column2: 亞瑟，不必向我問候，我一直都在。

column1: This is no time to be sitting around.
column2: 此刻不是閒坐的時候。

column1: Is that some sort of odd Gaelic word?
column2: 那是某種古怪的蓋爾語詞彙嗎？

column1: Deeds of mindless violence will make you unworthy of the Grail.
column2: 盲目的暴行，將使你不配獲得聖杯。

column1: This is hardly the time or place.
column2: 此時此地，都不合適。

column1: Some other time, mayhaps.
column2: 或許改日再說吧。

column1: There is no need for that here.
column2: 此處無需如此。

column1: Please do.
column2: 請便。

column1: That has gone with the mule.  A serious setback, but one which must not deter you from your mission.
column2: 那東西已隨騾子一併失去了。此乃嚴重的挫折，但不可因此讓你的使命受阻。

column1: That is in the pack which is with the mule.....wherever she is.
column2: 那東西在騾子身上的行囊裡……不論牠此刻身在何處。

column1: Only your deeds can determine your fate and it shall not be Merlin that renders the final judgment.
column2: 唯有你的所作所為，能決定你的命運，而最終的裁斷，也絕非出自梅林之手。

column1: No need to thank me. My service is its own reward.
column2: 不必言謝。為你效力，本身便是回報。

column1: Very well.
column2: 很好。

column1: It IS a problem with armour. I am sure you will manage somehow.
column2: 甲冑一事，確實是個難題。我相信你總會設法應付過去。

column1: The knight who wins the Grail must be pure of heart, mind, spirit and body. You seem determined to fail.
column2: 贏得聖杯的騎士，必須心、意、靈、身俱皆純淨。看來你是鐵了心要失敗。

column1: Here? In front of god and everybody?
column2: 在這裡？當著眾人與神明之前？

column1: It is ready upon your arm.
column2: 它已備妥，就在你臂上。

column1: The sweet heady smell of the rose reminds you, inevitably, of Gwenhyver.
column2: 玫瑰那濃郁香甜的氣息，讓你不由自主地想起昆海兒。

column1: What is it you wish to do instead?
column2: 那麼你想改做什麼？

column1: This is not the Chapel of the Two Gods. Here, you can only hope that whatever god or goddess is listening will heed your prayers.
column2: 此處並非雙神神殿。在這裡，你只能盼望，不論是哪位神祇正聽著，都願垂聽你的禱告。

column1: A mysterious request. Try to rephrase it more clearly.
column2: 這是個令人費解的要求，試著換個更清楚的說法。

column1: That is rather vague.  Which animal?
column2: 這話說得太籠統了。是哪種動物？

column1: There are many knights in the world. You must name the one for which you seek.
column2: 世上騎士眾多，你得說出你所尋之人的姓名。

column1: What difficulty:
column2: 難度：

column1: The joust will continue until either you or I have been unhorsed three times. Let it begin!
column2: 這場馬上長槍比武，將持續到你我任一方被擊落馬下三次為止。開始吧！

column1: You have vanquished the Black Knight, King Arthur!
column2: 你已擊敗黑武士，亞瑟王！

column1: You have struck your first successful blow against the Black Knight!
column2: 你已首次成功擊中黑武士！

column1: You have unhorsed the Black Knight for the second time! Once more and you have won!
column2: 你已第二次將黑武士擊落馬下！再一次，你便獲勝了！

column1: Alas! All Camelot will grieve to hear that valiant King Arthur was slain by the Black Knight.
column2: 唉！全肯萊特聞知驍勇的亞瑟王死於黑武士之手，無不哀慟。

column1: The Black Knight has unhorsed you for the first time, Arthur. Make it the last!
column2: 黑武士已首次將你擊落馬下，亞瑟。務必讓這是最後一次！

column1: Beware! The Black Knight has struck a second telling blow against you.
column2: 當心！黑武士已對你造成第二次重擊。

column1: OW!
column2: 哎唷！

column1: Deal with the Mad Monk and his illusions! Then you will have time to look around.
column2: 先解決瘋僧侶與他的幻術！之後你才有時間四處查看。

column1: Like a mad dog, he has been destroyed.  Tragic, but necessary.
column2: 他如瘋狗一般，已遭剷除。可悲，卻是不得不然。

column1: Arthur, beware!  Two of these monks are illusions, but one is deadly!
column2: 亞瑟，當心！這些僧侶中有兩個是幻影，但有一個是致命的！

column1: Kill!  Kill!  Kill!
column2: 殺！殺！殺！

column1: One must be off a horse to get on a horse.
column2: 人得先下馬，才能上馬。

column1: Your warhorse is trained to be mounted from the left side.
column2: 你的戰馬受過訓練，習慣從左側上馬。

column1: You have only begun your journey. You can surely stay in your saddle longer than this.
column2: 你的旅程才剛開始。你當然能在馬鞍上撐得比這更久。

column1: There are very few places in the forest where that would be either safe or advisable.  This is not one of them.
column2: 這片森林裡，既安全又適宜這麼做的地方少之又少。此處並非其中之一。

column1: This is no time to wander about on foot. Do get on with your mission.
column2: 此刻不是徒步閒晃的時候。快去完成你的使命。

column1: Being a superb rider, you do not carry one.
column2: 身為出色的騎手，你並未攜帶這東西。

column1: Not now.  You have places to go.
column2: 現在不行，你還有地方要去。

column1: Your horse is not cold, Arthur.
column2: 你的坐騎並不冷，亞瑟。

column1: You already have the reins.
column2: 韁繩已經在你手上了。

column1: Mount your horse first, Arthur.
column2: 先上馬吧，亞瑟。

column1: You need not tie a trained warhorse.
column2: 訓練有素的戰馬，不必拴繫。

column1: He looks much the same as last time you looked at him.
column2: 他的模樣，和你上次看他時沒什麼兩樣。

column1: Your horse is built for power, stamina and solidity to carry you with armor and weaponry into battle.  This does not make him a very good jumper.
column2: 你的坐騎生來力大、耐久、體格堅實，足以馱著全副武裝的你上陣殺敵，卻不擅長跳躍。

column1: Do you suffer from the delusion that you are on a horse?
column2: 你是不是有種錯覺，以為自己正騎在馬上？

column1: One must generally be on a horse to do that.
column2: 一般來說，得先騎在馬上才能這麼做。

column1: It would be best to go at a pace the mule can match.
column2: 最好放慢腳步，配合騾子能跟上的速度。

column1: Trust the instincts of your well-trained steed.  He knows when to hurry and when to tread with care.
column2: 相信你那匹訓練有素的坐騎的本能，牠明白何時該加快腳步、何時該小心慢行。

column1: There will be time enough for that later.
column2: 之後有的是時間做這件事。

column1: Jabir likes not the flash of your steel.
column2: 賈比耳不喜你鋼刃出鞘的寒光。

column1: Jabir likes not the sound of your steel being drawn.
column2: 賈比耳不喜你拔劍出鞘的聲響。

column1: You have set Jabir to his heels.  Let us hope that will be the last of him.  You have no strength to spare for chasing him.
column2: 你已把賈比耳嚇得拔腿逃竄。但願此後不會再見到他。你已無餘力去追捕他。

column1: Your mule carries your pack containing extra clothes, water and provisions.
column2: 你的騾子馱著行囊，裡頭裝著替換衣物、飲水與糧食。

column1: That is best left where it is.
column2: 那東西還是留在原處的好。

column1: For what purpose?
column2: 為了什麼目的？

column1: What you are wearing will do for now.
column2: 你目前身上穿的，暫時夠用了。

column1: The frost and ice chill the soul more than the body.
column2: 霜雪凍的不只是身軀，更是靈魂。

column1: It is not THAT cold.
column2: 還沒冷到那個地步。

column1: You are carrying quite enough as it is.  That is why you have a pack mule.
column2: 你身上背的已經夠多了，這正是你有一頭馱騾的緣故。

column1: The mule does not need the blanket, nor do you need a blanket that smells like a mule.
column2: 騾子不需要這條毯子，你也不需要一條滿是騾子氣味的毯子。

column1: You may talk to your mule all you like, Arthur, as long as you do not expect her to talk back.
column2: 你儘管對著騾子說話，亞瑟，只要別指望她會回話就好。

column1: She already carries the pack and you have your horse.
column2: 她已經馱著行囊了，而你有自己的坐騎。

column1: The weight of the pack is enough.  Your own two feet will serve to carry you.
column2: 行囊的重量已經夠了，靠你自己的雙腳走就行。

column1: You must be on your guard here.  Best to wait until you are free of the forest to take your ease.
column2: 此處你必須保持戒備。最好等離開這片森林後，再放鬆歇息。

column1: You did that during your journey here.
column2: 你在來此的路上已經做過這件事了。

column1: Time enough for that later.  135 For now, think only of your mission.
column2: 之後有的是時間做這件事。135 眼下，你只需想著你的使命。

column1: The pack washed overboard in the storm, remember?
column2: 還記得嗎？那個行囊在風暴中被沖落海裡了。

column1: No need.  She will follow you as usual.
column2: 不必，她會照常跟著你。

column1: A mule is not for riding.  Your own two feet will serve to carry you.
column2: 騾子不是用來騎的，靠你自己的雙腳走就行。

column1: Arthur! The mule is an innocent animal and should be valued. Do try to show some sense.
column2: 亞瑟！騾子是無辜的牲畜，理應受到珍視。拿出點分寸來。

column1: Your mule does not need to be tied.
column2: 你的騾子不需要拴繫。

column1: It is a book of knowledge which should be in your possession already. It looks like this and it is vital that you have it.
column2: 這是一本你早該持有的知識之書，模樣便是如此，你務必要隨身攜帶。

column1: The Message of the Rose is written in your liber ex doctrina.
column2: 玫瑰箴言，寫在你的《Liber ex Doctrina》裡。

column1: Clearly he is not here.
column2: 他顯然不在此處。

column1: The Liber ex Doctrina looks like this. I sincerely hope you have it with you.
column2: 《Liber ex Doctrina》模樣便是如此，衷心盼望你有隨身攜帶。

column1: You have worn these sturdy leather boots on many journeys. They will last quite a while yet.
column2: 這雙結實的皮靴，你已穿著走過許多路程，還能再撐上一段時日。

column1: It's nice armor, isn't it?
column2: 這副鎧甲不錯吧？

column1: I am only with you in spirit, but that should be enough.
column2: 我只能以心神與你同在，但那應該就夠了。

column1: That is on the mule, wherever she is.
column2: 那東西在騾子身上，不論她此刻在哪裡。

column1: I see nothing that is significant to your mission.
column2: 我看不出這與你的使命有何干係。

column1: That would solve nothing.
column2: 那樣做無濟於事。

column1: What an abysmally foolish idea.
column2: 這主意愚蠢至極。

column1: Unnecessary violence is a stain upon the soul.
column2: 不必要的暴力，是靈魂上的污點。

column1: You had better don sword and armour first.
column2: 你最好先佩劍披甲。

column1: I have nothing special to tell you now.
column2: 此刻我沒有什麼特別的話要告訴你。

column1: I have no special knowledge to help you here.
column2: 在這件事上，我沒有特別的見識能幫上你。

column1: I am unable to help more at this time.
column2: 此刻我無法再多幫你什麼了。

column1: That would avail you nothing.
column2: 那對你毫無助益。

column1: At the moment, I know no more than you of his fate.
column2: 此刻，他的命運我所知並不比你多。

column1: I would gladly tell you more if I had the knowledge.
column2: 若我知道得更多，必然樂意告訴你。

column1: I can tell you nothing relevant at the moment.
column2: 此刻我沒有任何相關的事能告訴你。

column1: Aye, that is the purpose of your mission.
column2: 正是，那正是你此行的目的。

column1: I do not see how you can, unless you know something I do not.
column2: 我看不出你能如何辦到，除非你知道某些我不知道的事。

column1: Obtain only what you need. Your burdens are already great.
column2: 只取你所需之物，你肩上的負擔已經夠重了。

column1: This is no time for the vulgar pursuit of money.
column2: 此刻不是追逐俗世錢財的時候。

column1: That is not for sale.
column2: 那東西不賣。

column1: Search what?
column2: 搜什麼？

column1: There is nothing of interest.
column2: 沒有什麼值得注意的東西。

column1: I would not look up into the blindingly bright sky too often, if I were you.
column2: 換作是我，不會太常抬頭直視那刺目的天空。

column1: In your armour?  Without ladder or scaling gear?  Do not be absurd.
column2: 穿著這身鎧甲？又沒有梯子或攀爬用具？休得荒唐。

column1: The walls are far too high for that.
column2: 這牆太高了，辦不到。

column1: I can see no purpose in that.
column2: 我看不出這麼做有什麼意義。

column1: You would not enjoy that.  Trust me.
column2: 你不會喜歡那種滋味的，相信我。

column1: Draw your sword only when absolutely necessary, or you may attract attention you do not want.  Remember the captain's warning.
column2: 非到萬不得已，切莫拔劍，否則恐招來你不樂見的注目。記住那位船長的警告。

column1: Let us pray that the end of your mission will lie within these walls.
column2: 讓我們祈禱，你此行的終點就在這城牆之內。

column1: You cannot actually see much of the city from outside the walls.
column2: 站在城牆之外，你其實看不清這座城市多少樣貌。

column1: At least you know what to expect this time.
column2: 至少這一回，你已知道會遇到什麼。

column1: Let us hope that other gates will not be as inhospitable as the one you passed.
column2: 但願其他城門不會像你剛經過的那道一樣難以親近。

column1: The narrow path around the walls of Jerusalem is hard packed soil.  It drops off quite steeply, so be careful.
column2: 耶路撒冷城牆外那條窄路，是踩得結實的泥土地，坡度頗陡，務必小心。

column1: The Zion Gate is a small gate in the south wall of Jerusalem.
column2: 錫安城門是耶路撒冷南牆上的一道小城門。

column1: The Jaffa Gate is the main gate in the western wall of Jerusalem.
column2: 賈法城門是耶路撒冷西牆上的主城門。

column1: Some of the spiny plants are Aloe Vera.  The others are some Eastern desert varieties unknown to me.
column2: 這些帶刺的植物，有些是蘆薈，其餘則是我所不識的東方沙漠品種。

column1: Trees do not seem to fare well around here.  I see nothing but shrubs.
column2: 這一帶樹木似乎長得不好，我看到的盡是灌木叢。

column1: Aloe Vera is originally from Africa.  The leaves have a bitter, astringent juice within.
column2: 蘆薈原產自非洲，葉片中含有苦澀的汁液。

column1: My that IS a steep drop.
column2: 哎呀，這坡可真陡。

column1: There is no cause to swear at me, Arthur.  It was your own clumsiness that caused it.
column2: 沒理由衝著我咒罵，亞瑟，這是你自己笨手笨腳造成的。

column1: Now pick yourself up, dust yourself off, and we shall start all over again.
column2: 現在起身，拍拍身上塵土，我們從頭再來一次。

column1: The whirlwind of rose petals will guide and protect you, but only if you stay within it.
column2: 玫瑰花瓣的旋風會指引並護佑你，但唯有你留在其中方能生效。

column1: The petals disperse in an icy wind. You are no longer protected by its spell of guidance.
column2: 花瓣在寒風中四散消逝。你已不再受那指引法術的護佑。

column1: Rather than waste your time in fruitless endeavors, I advise you to simply avoid the mummies and the urns and concentrate upon your task -- finding a way out of here.
column2: 與其把時間浪費在徒勞無功之事上，我勸你乾脆避開木乃伊與陶甕，專心於你的任務——找到離開此處的路。

column1: The rats are too quick and can hide too easily from your sword. You are wasting precious time, Arthur.
column2: 這些老鼠動作太快，輕易便能躲過你的劍。你在浪費寶貴的時間，亞瑟。

column1: The elixir is gone and I did not keep track of where you dropped the empty vial.
column2: 解藥已經用盡，你把空瓶丟在哪裡，我也沒留意。

column1: I am quite disoriented in these catacombs. You could be facing in any direction, for all I can tell.
column2: 在這地下墓窖裡，我完全辨不清方向。就我所知，你此刻可能面朝任何一方。

column1: The red eyes of a poisonous rat glare back at you.
column2: 一隻毒鼠赤紅的雙眼，正回瞪著你。

column1: There is a plenty of dust and rat droppings.
column2: 這裡滿是塵土與鼠糞。

column1: The lethal rats of the catacombs lurk behind these mummies.
column2: 墓窖裡致命的老鼠，就潛伏在這些木乃伊後方。

column1: There is a vaulted stone ceiling.
column2: 這裡有一座拱形的石頂。

column1: The floor is made of cold, cold stone.
column2: 地板是由冰冷、冰冷的石頭鋪成的。

column1: The poisonous rats are everywhere, but seem to favor the mummies and urns. Best to stay clear of them.
column2: 毒鼠四處都是，但似乎特別偏好木乃伊與陶甕一帶。最好離牠們遠一點。

column1: Remember the hierophant's warning: one bite means a slow but certain death. To be bitten more than once, will hasten that terrible fate.
column2: 記住祭司的警告：被咬一口，便是緩慢卻必然的死亡；若不止一次被咬，那可怕的命運將提前降臨。

column1: The niches hold the mummies, as you can clearly see.
column2: 壁龕裡安放著木乃伊，這你看得很清楚。

column1: The doorways are quite low and show how thick the walls are between the rooms.
column2: 這些門道相當低矮，正顯出房間之間牆壁的厚實。

column1: A spell of warding is one which repels evil spirits or creatures.
column2: 防護法術，是能驅退邪靈或邪祟生物的法術。

column1: I suppose it could be hidden in these catacombs. You must be alert to any possibility.
column2: 我猜想它或許就藏在這片墓窖之中，你得對任何可能保持警覺。

column1: You let him die, Arthur. Your soul will never be cleansed of this sin.
column2: 你任由他死去，亞瑟。你的靈魂將永遠洗刷不去這樁罪孽。

column1: So close was he to death, that it may take some time for the elixir to work. Your only chance is to find the Grail so that it may heal you.
column2: 他已如此接近死亡，解藥恐怕得花上一段時間才能見效。你唯一的機會，是尋得聖杯，讓聖杯治癒你。

column1: Though you have not found him, he may yet be in some undiscovered chamber.
column2: 雖然你尚未尋獲他，他或許仍在某個未被發現的密室之中。

column1: If you seek such knowledge, consult your Liber ex Doctrina.
column2: 若你尋求這樣的知識，請查閱你的《Liber ex Doctrina》。

column1: There is no mural here.
column2: 此處沒有壁畫。

column1: Gnostic means "knowledge." It refers to secretive Christian cults who seek after heavenly knowledge, disdain all matters of the flesh, and worship Sophia, the Great Mother of all wisdom.
column2: 「諾斯替」（Gnostic）意為「知識」，指的是那些追求天啟知識、鄙棄一切肉身之事、崇奉索菲亞──萬智之大母的秘密基督教教派。

column1: For the past four centuries they have been heavily persecuted by the Christian sect ruling from Rome and may have met here to worship in secret.
column2: 四個世紀以來，他們始終受到羅馬治下基督教派的嚴酷迫害，或許正因如此，才選擇在此秘密聚會禮拜。

column1: To the Gnostics, she is the Great Mother of wisdom, creator of the universe, mother and wife to the god who came after her.
column2: 對諾斯替教徒而言，她是智慧的偉大之母，宇宙的創造者，也是繼她而生之神的母親兼妻子。

column1: Because of this belief, the Gnostics also allow women to be priests. And for this reason, the Christians in Rome particularly hate them.
column2: 正因這樣的信仰，諾斯替教也容許女性擔任祭司。也正因如此，羅馬的基督徒對他們恨之入骨。

column1: The only statue present in the catacombs is that of Aphrodite.
column2: 地下墓窖中僅存的雕像，是阿芙羅黛蒂的雕像。

column1: What statue? I see no statue.
column2: 什麼雕像？我沒看見任何雕像。

column1: It is quite dusty.
column2: 上頭積了不少塵土。

column1: The apple made of solid gold was probably once a sacred object in a temple of the Goddess.
column2: 這顆純金打造的蘋果，昔日想必曾是女神神殿中的聖物。

column1: The Seeress gave you the green apple, do you not remember?
column2: 女預言家給了你那顆青蘋果，你不記得了嗎？

column1: She said that eating it would relieve all your hunger and thirst and give you renewed strength.
column2: 她說吃下它能解除你一切飢渴，並讓你重新恢復氣力。

column1: Doves are a fertility symbol sacred to Aphrodite. But also it is widely believed that the soul becomes a dove at death and flies to heaven.
column2: 鴿子是阿芙羅黛蒂神聖的生育象徵。但也有人普遍相信，人死後靈魂會化為鴿子，飛往天堂。

column1: The best I can tell you at the moment is that the stone dove you carry seems to be a stone dove.
column2: 此刻我能告訴你的，也不過是你身上那隻石鴿，看起來就是一隻石鴿。

column1: These solid, musty rooms absorb your voice. You will have to search room by room.
column2: 這些厚實而霉味瀰漫的房間會吞沒你的聲音，你得一間一間地搜索。

column1: Like the other dead souls in this place, he can no longer answer you.
column2: 如同此地其他亡魂一般，他已無法回應你了。

column1: Do not expect him to answer. Even if he could hear you, he will not yet be healed and conscious.
column2: 別指望他會回應。就算他聽得見你，此刻也還未痊癒清醒。

column1: There are poisonous.
column2: 牠們有毒。

column1: No need. If you do not find a way out of these catacombs, you will BE dust.
column2: 不必如此。你若找不到走出這地下墓窖的路，終將化為塵土。

column1: One disgusting old bone is quite enough.
column2: 一根噁心的老骨頭就已經夠了。

column1: There are no loose bones here to pick up, Arthur, and there are rats lurking around the mummies.
column2: 此處並無散落的骨頭可拾取，亞瑟，木乃伊四周還潛伏著老鼠。

column1: You don't have one.
column2: 你並未持有此物。

column1: Not now. Keep your mind on what you are doing.
column2: 現在不行。專心在你正在做的事情上。

column1: I cannot imagine a use for it....except for rats to gnaw upon.
column2: 我想不出它有什麼用處……除了讓老鼠啃食之外。

column1: Disgusting. You are a king, not a ghoul.
column2: 噁心。你是一位國王，不是食屍鬼。

column1: Nothing happens.
column2: 沒有任何反應。

column1: Treat the dead with respect and caution. Especially in this place. And beware the rats.
column2: 對待亡者要心懷敬意，謹慎行事。在此地尤其如此。並且要提防老鼠。

column1: It is a mummy. It has been dead for perhaps hundreds of years. Do try to show some sense.
column2: 那是一具木乃伊，死去恐怕已有數百年之久。還請你拿出點見識來。

column1: Mummies are not known for their witty conversation.
column2: 木乃伊向來不以妙語如珠聞名。

column1: It is good that no-one else is here to see you having a one-sided conversation with a poisonous rat.
column2: 幸好沒有旁人在此，看見你正對著一隻毒鼠自說自話。

column1: Considering the danger of their bite, you are best to avoid these rats at all costs.
column2: 考量到牠們咬人的危險，你最好無論如何都避開這些老鼠。

column1: They have plenty of bones to gnaw on.
column2: 牠們有大量的骨頭可以啃食。

column1: That would be exceedingly foolish.
column2: 那將是極其愚蠢之舉。

column1: You are already wearing it.
column2: 你已經戴著它了。

column1: You do not have a medallion.
column2: 你並未持有六角星項鍊。

column1: That would not be wise. It has a powerful warding spell upon it.
column2: 那並非明智之舉。它身上附有強力的護身法術。

column1: Even King Midas could not eat a golden apple.
column2: 就連邁達斯王也無法吃下一顆金蘋果。

column1: You have two apples to choose from. The green apple and the golden apple.
column2: 你有兩顆蘋果可以選擇：青蘋果與金蘋果。

column1: Aye, but how?
column2: 正是，但該如何做到？

column1: Clearly your challenge is to escape these catacombs. You must use your wits to discover the means.
column2: 顯然你面臨的難題，便是逃出這座地下墓窖。你必須運用機智，找出脫身之法。

column1: There is no-one here who still desires mortal things.
column2: 此地已無人仍貪戀塵世之物。

column1: That is the purpose of your mission. I pray you will succeed.
column2: 那正是你此行使命的目的。我祈求你能成功。

column1: Arthur! Beware the rats! Any closer and you will be bitten!
column2: 亞瑟！當心那些老鼠！再靠近一步就會被咬傷！

column1: Your strength is fading. The remorseless hand of Death draws near.
column2: 你的氣力正逐漸消逝。死神無情的手正步步逼近。

column1: Another quest turned to dust, Another feast for the worms.
column2: 又一場任務化為塵土，又一頓供蛆蟲享用的盛宴。

column1: I thank you, habib, but you need not pay me until we reach Jerusalem.
column2: 多謝你，朋友，但你不必現在付錢，等我們抵達耶路撒冷再說。

column1: Do not lay hands upon me, foreigner!
column2: 休得對我動手，異鄉人！

column1: Eh?  Dagger?  I have no dagger, habib.
column2: 嗯？匕首？我沒有匕首，朋友。

column1: I did not bring one for this trip.  The desert is no threat to me.
column2: 這趟旅程我沒帶。沙漠對我構不成什麼威脅。

column1: An odd trinket, of no use to me.  I would prefer money.
column2: 一件古怪的小玩意兒，對我毫無用處。我寧可要錢。

column1: I would prefer money in exchange for my services.  We will discuss it at Jerusalem.
column2: 我提供服務，寧願換取金錢作為報酬。這事我們到耶路撒冷再談。

column1: You have no waterskin?  A pity.  I need none, for I can well endure the desert.  You had best follow me closely to reach the water you need.
column2: 你沒有水袋？真可惜。我倒是不需要，畢竟我很能在沙漠裡耐得住。你最好緊跟著我，才能找到你需要的水。

column1: Jabir means to kill you, Arthur!
column2: 賈比耳存心要殺你，亞瑟！

column1: This name means nothing to me.
column2: 這個名字對我毫無意義。

column1: You will see the walls of Jerusalem soon enough, but first you must have water.
column2: 你很快就能看見耶路撒冷的城牆，但在那之前，你得先有水才行。

column1: Only one such as I knows the unmarked paths of the desert.
column2: 唯有像我這樣的人，才熟知沙漠裡那些不見標記的路徑。

column1: Beware of mirages.  They will only lead you astray to your death.
column2: 當心海市蜃樓。它們只會將你引入歧途，步向死亡。

column1: Your mule will last no longer than you without water.
column2: 沒有水，你的騾子撐不了比你更久。

column1: Follow me.  I will lead you directly to water.
column2: 跟著我，我會直接帶你到水源那裡。

column1: I know where every wadi is hidden.  Follow me.
column2: 每一處旱谷藏在哪裡，我都一清二楚。跟著我走。

column1: Thief!  Robber!  You come seeking treasure, but you will find only death!
column2: 賊子！強盜！你前來尋找財寶，卻只會找到死亡！

column1: Thief!  Dog of a bandit!  I should have known at once from your evil face!
column2: 賊子！強盜狗賊！看你那張凶惡的臉，我早該一眼看穿！

column1: So! You have revealed yourself, enemy, as I knew you would!
column2: 哼！你終於露出真面目了，敵人，我早知道你會如此！

column1: The power is mine!  Mine!  I will never share it!
column2: 這力量是我的！是我的！我絕不與人分享！

column1: But you will never rob me, you devil!
column2: 但你休想搶得了我，你這惡魔！

column1: Thief!  Robber!  You will never leave here alive!
column2: 賊子！強盜！你休想活著離開此地！

column1: Greetings, stranger.  Welcome to Glastonbury Tor.
column2: 陌生人，你好。歡迎來到格列斯登伯利山。

column1: Arthur.  The monk IS mad!
column2: 亞瑟，這僧侶果真是瘋了！

column1: He does not answer yet. Try getting a bit closer.
column2: 他還沒有回應。試著再靠近一些。

column1: I have made you welcome, though I wonder what your purpose may be, you with armour, shield and sword.
column2: 我已表明歡迎之意，只是好奇你此來所為何事——身披盔甲、手持盾牌與劍。

column1: Well, la-dee-da.  And I am the Emperor of Rome.
column2: 喔，了不起啊。那我還是羅馬皇帝呢。

column1: That rose smells of woman's magick.  I will not touch it.
column2: 那朵玫瑰散發著女人的魔法氣息，我不會去碰它。

column1: I know that sleeve well.  It tells me that you are a great warrior, but less wise than you could be.
column2: 那袖子我再熟悉不過。它告訴我，你是位偉大的戰士，卻不如你原本能有的那般睿智。

column1: Men in armour make me nervous. Go away.
column2: 身披盔甲的男人讓我心神不寧。走開。

column1: As you can see, I am but an old, poor, helpless monk seeking enlightenment through solitude.  I am amazed you have passed the riddle stones, for your own face betrays no great intelligence.
column2: 如你所見，我不過是個年邁、貧困、無助的僧侶，藉獨處尋求開悟。你竟能通過謎語石的考驗，真教我驚訝——畢竟從你的面相看不出有多少才智。

column1: They were once five poets, but the witch turned them to stone. Had you heard their poetry, you would understand why.
column2: 他們原是五位詩人，卻被女巫化為石頭。你若聽過他們的詩作，便會明白緣由。

column1: I will only say that there is someone who wants it a great deal more than I.
column2: 我只能說，有人比我更想要它，想要得多。

column1: The altar is ancient and has been here since the Druids worshipped upon this hill.
column2: 這座祭壇年代久遠，自德魯伊人在此山上禮拜的時代便已存在。

column1: They tell wondrous secrets, but only to me.
column2: 它們訴說著奇妙的秘密，但只對我一人訴說。

column1: I will never reveal my secrets!
column2: 我絕不會洩露我的秘密！

column1: I cannot fathom what you mean, pilgrim.
column2: 我猜不透你的意思，朝聖者。

column1: It is a ruined, desolate, lonely place. You cannot be enjoying it, so go away.
column2: 這是個殘破、荒涼、孤寂之地。你不可能樂在其中，走開吧。

column1: I believe that I shall live forever.
column2: 我相信自己將會永生不死。

column1: I believe the world revolves around my navel.
column2: 我相信這世界是繞著我的肚臍轉的。

column1: I believe you are the nosiest man I ever met.
column2: 我相信你是我此生遇過最愛多管閒事的人。

column1: Do you hear the chanting?  Aye, day and night they chant, the ghosts of the Old Ones.  I am never free of it.
column2: 你聽見那吟誦聲了嗎？正是，古代幽靈日夜不停地吟誦著，我從未能擺脫過它。

column1: When I am left alone, I can seek enlightenment. If you wish to help me attain that exalted state, you will go away.
column2: 獨處之時，我才能追求開悟。你若真想助我達到那崇高的境界，就該離開。

column1: I did not become a monk just so I could stand around answering your questions all day.
column2: 我出家為僧，可不是為了整天站在這裡回答你的問題。

column1: I have no use for such a trinket.
column2: 這種小玩意兒，我用不著。

column1: I should have expected no less from an armed barbarian.
column2: 從一個全副武裝的野蠻人身上，我本就不該有更高的期待。

column1: You have been hacked to death by the Saracen.  Let us hope you will be a better swordsman in your next life.
column2: 你已被撒拉遜武士砍死。但願你來世能成為更出色的劍士。

column1: Ah. The rat's poison has caught up with you. You have lost your desperate battle against time. Now, you shall have eternity to regret it.
column2: 啊，老鼠的毒液終究追上了你。你與時間的殊死搏鬥已然落敗。如今，你將有永恆的時光可以悔恨。

column1: Now that the fight is over, the helmet also disappears.
column2: 如今戰鬥已然結束，頭盔也隨之消失。

column1: You grow steadily weaker. Seek triumph from strategy, my king, as your strength wanes.
column2: 你正逐漸虛弱下去。吾王，趁你氣力尚未耗盡，當從謀略中尋求勝機。

column1: Your death is near! You must win now or lose all.
column2: 你已命懸一線！此刻不勝，便將盡失所有。

column1: Arthur, you are over-exerting yourself. Slow down, or you will lack the strength to fight.
column2: 亞瑟，你已過度耗力。放慢下來，否則你將無力再戰。

column1: Your sword feels as heavy as lead. Defend yourself with your shield until some of your strength returns.
column2: 你的劍沉如鉛塊。且以盾牌自守，靜候氣力回復幾分。

column1: Excaliber flashes in your skilled hands. Victory is imminent!
column2: 聖劍在你嫻熟的手中閃耀光芒，勝利已近在眼前！

column1: The Saracen weakens under your skillful attack. Keep fighting like this and you will be victorious.
column2: 撒拉遜武士在你精湛的攻勢下逐漸虛弱。照這樣打下去，你必將獲勝。

column1: Your skull is cracked, Your body dead, Your brains are gone, Your spirit fled, The Monk played tag Upon your head.
column2: 你的顱骨碎裂，你的軀體已亡，你的腦漿四散，你的魂魄已散，僧侶在你頭頂，戲耍了一場。

column1: Arrghh...in vino veritas...
column2: 啊啊……酒後吐真言……

column1: Well done, Arthur!
column2: 做得好，亞瑟！

column1: We are the Old Ones and you have killed the monk, our servant, the only servant we have had for centuries.
column2: 我們是古代幽靈，你殺了那僧侶——我們的僕人，數百年來，他是我們僅有的一位僕人。

column1: You must take his place.  You will never leave here, unless you can appease us for this loss.
column2: 你必須取代他的位置。除非你能平息我們因此喪失而生的怒火，否則你將永遠困在此地。

column1: In this section of the temple there are four broken and fallen pillars.
column2: 神殿的這一區域，有四根斷裂倒塌的柱子。

column1: In this section of the Temple there are three broken pillars and an indentation where a fourth pillar once stood.
column2: 神殿的這一區域，有三根斷裂的柱子，以及第四根柱子原本立足處留下的凹痕。

column1: These steps must be the only remnant of the original door to the Temple. At the threshold there is a lunar spiral engraved in the marble.
column2: 這些石階想必是神殿原本大門僅存的遺跡。門檻的大理石上，刻著一道月亮螺紋。

column1: There are also three broken pillars and an indentation where a fourth pillar once stood.
column2: 此處同樣有三根斷裂的柱子，以及第四根柱子原本立足處留下的凹痕。

column1: An interesting idea, if one can find a way to do so.
column2: 這想法有趣，前提是得找到辦法做到。

column1: You cannot see beyond the walls surrounding the Temple except for a glimpse of tree tops and tiled roofs in the distance.
column2: 神殿四周高牆之外，你什麼也看不見，只能瞥見遠方的樹梢與瓦頂一角。

column1: No part of the Temple's roof remains. Only the sky arches overhead.
column2: 神殿的屋頂已蕩然無存，唯有天空在頭頂上方拱起。

column1: The floor of the Temple is made of marble, weathered from the ages and invaded by weeds.
column2: 神殿的地面以大理石鋪成，歷經歲月風化，如今已被雜草侵佔。

column1: You will never see her again.
column2: 你將再也見不到她了。

column1: She will reveal herself to you only when she is ready.
column2: 唯有等她準備好了，才會向你現身。

column1: This part of the Temple of Aphrodite is surrounded by high walls without doors or windows. There is no way out from this direction.
column2: 阿芙羅黛蒂神殿的這一部分，四周高牆環繞，既無門也無窗，這個方向無路可通。

column1: By all that is sacred, King Arthur, go where the dove leads you and forget all else!
column2: 以一切神聖之名起誓，亞瑟王，隨鴿子引領你的方向前行，其餘一概拋諸腦後！

column1: Arthur, pay attention! A powerful foe awaits you. This is no time to play at being Sampson.
column2: 亞瑟，打起精神來！強敵正等著你。此刻不是逞英雄學參孫的時候。

column1: The pedestal is immovable.
column2: 這座基座紋風不動。

column1: I sense that the power of the Goddess keeps you from treading there, where once her holy of holies must have been kept.
column2: 我感覺到女神的力量，正阻止你踏入那處——那裡想必曾是她的至聖之所。

column1: Die, infidel
column2: 去死吧，異教徒

column1: I was going to make a remark about using your brains, Arthur, but since I see they are all over the ground, along with your blood, heart, kidneys, liver, lungs and intestines, I guess there is no point.
column2: 我原想說幾句要你多動動腦子的話，亞瑟，可我見你的腦漿已灑滿一地，連同你的血、心臟、腎臟、肝臟、肺臟與腸子，看來也沒什麼意義了。

column1: YOU MAY NOT PASS THIS WAY!  Do not annoy us, infidel.
column2: 你不得從此路通行！休得惹惱我們，異教徒。

column1: What utterly stupid animals they are!
column2: 牠們真是群徹頭徹尾的蠢畜生！

column1: Aye, the woman is herding away her sheep.  What utterly stupid animals they are.
column2: 正是，那女人正把她的羊群趕開。牠們真是群徹頭徹尾的蠢畜生。

column1: She shows not the least interest in talking to you.
column2: 她絲毫沒有興趣跟你說話。

column1: Sheep are the most brainless creatures upon the face of the earth.  That does not bode well for someone who wants to talk to them.
column2: 羊是這世上最沒腦子的生物。這對想跟牠們交談的人來說，可不是什麼好兆頭。

column1: You missed.  A large, heavy sword is not the best method for this, perhaps.
column2: 你揮空了。一把又大又重的劍，或許並非對付這個的最佳方式。

column1: Fast little devils, are they not?
column2: 這些小傢伙動作真快，不是嗎？

column1: If you mean the legged creature that scurried past, it was a lizard.
column2: 你若是指那隻疾竄而過、生著腿的生物，那是一隻蜥蜴。

column1: It is not worth the effort...unless you are well and truly desperate enough.
column2: 這不值得費這番功夫……除非你已當真走投無路。

column1: This lizard is moving too fast for you.
column2: 這隻蜥蜴動作太快，你追不上。

column1: The lizard is too far away.
column2: 這隻蜥蜴離得太遠了。

column1: Aye, you see Launcelot making love to Gwenhyver, but it is only a mirage, a torment from your own mind.
column2: 正是，你看見蘭斯洛特與昆海兒繾綣纏綿，但那不過是海市蜃樓，是你自己心中生出的折磨。

column1: You see the image of Gwenhyver making love to Launcelot, but it is only a mirage created from your inner fears in your fevered state.
column2: 你看見昆海兒與蘭斯洛特相擁纏綿的景象，但那不過是海市蜃樓，出自你發熱昏沉中內心的恐懼。

column1: The mirage takes the shapes of Gwenhyver and Launcelot in a lovers' embrace.  This is a delusion, Arthur, caused by the torment of your own mind.
column2: 那幻象化作昆海兒與蘭斯洛特相擁的模樣。這只是幻覺，亞瑟，是你自己心神煎熬所致。

column1: It is indeed an illusion, created by your own eyes, shaped by your fevered and tormented mind.
column2: 這確實只是幻覺，是你自己的眼睛所造，被你發熱煎熬的心神所形塑。

column1: Your land and your people will die unless you fulfill your quest.  Do not give up.
column2: 除非你完成使命，否則你的國土與子民都將滅亡。莫要放棄。

column1: Images shimmer and appear in the veils of rising heat.  It is Gwenhyver and Launcelot embracing.
column2: 影像在蒸騰的熱浪薄紗中閃爍浮現，是昆海兒與蘭斯洛特相擁的身影。

column1: This image is but a vision of your own fears and jealousies, driven to the surface by your fevered, desperate brain.
column2: 這幅景象不過是你自身恐懼與嫉妒的幻象，被你發熱絕望的腦海逼上了表面。

column1: Survival is more important than good taste, Arthur.
column2: 生存比講究品味更為要緊，亞瑟。

column1: That was rather revolting, but at least the lizard's blood has revived you a tiny bit.
column2: 那滋味著實令人作嘔，但至少蜥蜴的血讓你稍稍回過了些氣力。

column1: The lizard slipped past you.
column2: 那隻蜥蜴從你身邊溜走了。

column1: Alas, you did not find water in time!  You die as parched as a piece of old leather, and soon your bones will adorn the sands.
column2: 唉，你未能及時尋得水源！你乾涸而死，如同一塊陳舊的皮革，不消多久，你的骸骨便將裝點這片沙地。

column1: Alas, your strength failed and you died at the very edge of the water you so desperately needed. Truly, there is no justice in life.
column2: 唉，你的氣力耗盡，就死在你朝思暮想的水源近旁。人生當真毫無公道可言。

column1: To add insult to injury, the scoundrel Jabir robs your corpse.
column2: 更教人氣憤的是，那無賴賈比耳竟洗劫了你的屍身。

column1: That shimmer looks suspiciously like water.
column2: 那片閃爍，看起來很像是水。

column1: It is indeed an illusion, created by your own eyes in the heat and thirst of the moment.
column2: 這確實只是幻覺，是你此刻酷熱難耐、口渴難當之下，自己的眼睛所造。

column1: 800 years before the birth of Christ, King Hezekiah ruled a city built on the large hill above this tunnel.
column2: 在基督誕生前八百年，希西家王統治著一座建於此地道上方大山丘上的城市。

column1: The Assyrians were coming to attack the city, and the only source of water, the Spring of Gihon, lay before them at the base of the city.
column2: 亞述人正兵臨城下，而城中唯一的水源——基訓泉，就位於城基之前，正對著他們。

column1: Hezekiah sent two teams of men to dig a tunnel.  One began at the Spring, the other from the opposite side of the hill.
column2: 希西家派遣兩隊人馬挖掘地道，一隊自泉源起工，另一隊則從山丘的另一側動工。

column1: It is an amazing feat of that age that they dug through solid rock and met in the middle, thus forming this underground aqueduct.
column2: 他們鑿穿堅硬的岩石，在中途會合，造就了這條地下水道——這在當時堪稱驚人的工程壯舉。

column1: The water flowed then from the Spring, which was covered over from sight, to the Pool of Siloam, hidden upon the far side of the hill.
column2: 泉水自此隱而不見，流經地道，直抵藏於山丘另一側的西羅亞池。

column1: When the enemy arrived, they found no water and were forced to give up their seige.  Thus did King Hezekiah save his city.
column2: 敵軍抵達時遍尋不著水源，只得放棄圍城。希西家王便是如此保全了他的城池。

column1: And yet, of that city no trace remains, and in its place the city now known as Jerusalem was built upon a larger hill to the north.
column2: 然而，那座城如今已不留一絲痕跡，取而代之的，是如今名為耶路撒冷的城市，建於北方一座更大的山丘之上。

column1: If only you had a waterskin, but you do not.  You must drink your fill and reach Jerusalem as quickly as possible.
column2: 你若備有水袋就好了，可惜沒有。你必須在此暢飲個夠，並儘快趕往耶路撒冷。

column1: They were foes of King Hezekiah.
column2: 他們是希西家王的敵人。

column1: You may as well get started.  You have a long walk back.
column2: 你不妨這就動身，回程還有很長一段路要走。

column1: It must be near.
column2: 想必就在附近。

column1: You are under a hill at present.
column2: 你此刻正位於一座山丘之下。

column1: The Spring of Gihon lies upon the far side of the large hill through which this aqueduct was dug.  It was hidden by King Hezekiah centuries ago.
column2: 基訓泉位於這座大山丘的另一側，這條水道正是穿山而鑿。數百年前，希西家王將它隱藏了起來。

column1: The Pool of Siloam is fed by the Spring of Gihon through Hezekiah's Aqueduct.
column2: 西羅亞池的水源，正是透過希西家水道由基訓泉引來。

column1: The cold water within this cool tunnel sends a shiver running through your body.
column2: 這條清涼地道裡的冰冷泉水，讓你渾身一陣寒顫。

column1: The waters of the Pool of Siloam are cold and pure and fill you with relief.
column2: 西羅亞池的池水清冷純淨，讓你頓覺舒暢。

column1: I fear the sight of you was too much for that poor girl.  She ran as though you were an evil djin.
column2: 恐怕是你的模樣把那可憐的女孩嚇壞了，她逃跑的樣子，彷彿把你當成了邪惡的精靈。

column1: Such profane thoughts betray a moral weakness which may make you unworthy to find or possess the Grail.  You must control yourself.
column2: 如此褻瀆的念頭，暴露出你心志上的軟弱，恐怕會讓你失去尋得聖杯、持有聖杯的資格。你必須克制自己。

column1: The girl, and her jug, have vanished over the hill.
column2: 那女孩連同她的水罐，已消失在山丘另一頭。

column1: The girl has no interest in coming near you, let alone taking your money.
column2: 那女孩絲毫不想靠近你，更別說收下你的錢了。

column1: She clearly has no desire to speak to you.
column2: 她顯然不想跟你說話。

column1: The girl found you most frightening and wanted nothing to do with you.
column2: 那女孩覺得你十分嚇人，不想跟你有任何瓜葛。

column1: The girl's jar was designed for carrying water.
column2: 那女孩的罐子是用來盛水的。

column1: Do watch your step, Arthur.  You cannot afford to be careless.
column2: 亞瑟，走路留神些。你可經不起一時大意。

column1: I doubt the natives will appreciate the mess you have made for them to clean up.  In your next life, do be more careful about where you step.
column2: 我看當地人未必會感激你留下這攤爛攤子讓他們收拾。下輩子，走路前可得看清楚些。

column1: You are ignored, perhaps because you are obviously a 'foreign devil.'
column2: 沒人理睬你，或許是因為你一望即知是個「洋鬼子」。

column1: No one is here.
column2: 此處無人。

column1: I do not know of it.
column2: 我對此一無所知。

column1: Never heard of him.
column2: 從未聽聞此人。

column1: That brings you nothing but a look of confusion.
column2: 你這麼做，換來的只有一臉困惑。

column1: They are here to look for thieves.
column2: 他們在此是為了緝查竊賊。

column1: I am not certain who you mean.
column2: 我不確定你指的是誰。

column1: It would be best to ask a merchant about the price of a certain thing.
column2: 若想知道某樣東西的價錢，最好去問商人。

column1: I have nothing to say about him.
column2: 關於他，我無話可說。

column1: I have nothing to say about her.
column2: 關於她，我無話可說。

column1: Those who spend money are always welcome here.
column2: 願意花錢的人，在此永遠受歡迎。

column1: You must not draw a weapon without good cause in this bazaar. The Muslims will not tolerate it and there are many of them and only one of you.
column2: 在這市集裡，切莫無故拔出武器。穆斯林絕不會容忍此事，況且他們人多勢眾，你孤身一人。

column1: The apple works its spell. Your hunger and thirst vanish. The heaviness of your limbs is lightened.
column2: 這顆蘋果發揮了它的魔力。你的飢渴頓時消散，四肢的沉重也隨之減輕。

column1: Often great wisdom and power may be hidden in a most ordinary guise.
column2: 偉大的智慧與力量，往往深藏在最平凡的外表之下。

column1: Waste no time. Go to Fatima at once.
column2: 莫再耽擱，速速前去見法提瑪。

column1: The Truth Spell of the Seeress provides you with the means to learn what a person wants. How you act upon that knowledge is the test placed before you.
column2: 女預言家的真言之術，能讓你窺知他人所求為何。至於如何運用這份洞悉，正是擺在你面前的試煉。

column1: In Camelot, you may go anywhere you like, but not in Jerusalem.
column2: 在肯萊特，你可隨心所欲，任意通行；但在耶路撒冷卻不然。

column1: Are you sure you have the right merchant for that?
column2: 你確定找對商人了嗎？

column1: No-one answers to that title here.
column2: 此處無人以此稱謂應答。

column1: She warned you it was delicate. Since you failed to eat it, it has fallen apart.
column2: 她警告過你這東西很脆弱。你既未及時吃下，它便已散壞。

column1: You need to buy one, before you can eat it.
column2: 你得先買下一個，才能吃它。

column1: I do not think she heard you.
column2: 我想她沒聽見你的話。

column1: Most of it is written in Hebrew, of which I know very little.
column2: 這上頭大多以希伯來文寫成，我所知甚少。

column1: I cannot quite tell precisely what the Hebrew graffiti says, but some of it, I believe, mentions dysentery.
column2: 我說不準這希伯來文塗鴉確切寫著什麼，但依我看，其中有些提到了痢疾。

column1: Habib means simply "friend", but "habibi" is a warmer greeting, like saying "my friend".
column2: 「Habib」單純意為「朋友」，但「habibi」則是更親暱的問候語，如同說「我的朋友」。

column1: Do not even consider it.
column2: 切莫存此念頭。

column1: In this dangerous land, that would be as good as death.
column2: 在這險惡之地，那無異於尋死。

column1: You are fit only to be a warrior in this land and Jerusalem has all the warriors it needs.
column2: 在此地，你唯一適合的身分是戰士，而耶路撒冷戰士已經足夠，不缺你一個。

column1: You must use your wits if you hope to obtain money.
column2: 若盼望取得錢財，你得靠智謀行事。

column1: Use carefully what you have. That is more important than how much you can accumulate.
column2: 善用你手頭所有之物，這比你能積攢多少更為重要。

column1: That was a bloody waste.
column2: 那簡直是白白糟蹋。

column1: That is beneath your dignity.
column2: 那有失你的尊嚴。

column1: You have neither the means nor the need.
column2: 你既無此財力，也無此需要。

column1: It is made of metal. You cannot break it.
column2: 它是金屬打造，你破壞不了。

column1: It would not suit you.
column2: 那並不適合你。

column1: I challenge you to find a use for this piece of cheap tin you have bought so dearly.
column2: 我倒要看看，你這花大錢買來的破錫片，究竟能派上什麼用場。

column1: The birds already eat their fill from the grain merchant's spillage.
column2: 那些鳥兒早已從穀商灑落的穀粒中吃得飽飽的。

column1: It is a foolish man who scatters grain upon barren ground for no reason.
column2: 無故將穀粒撒在貧瘠之地，實乃愚人所為。

column1: I do not think you would enjoy eating raw grain.
column2: 我想你不會喜歡生嚼穀粒的滋味。

column1: Eat raw meat? In THIS climate? I think not.
column2: 生吃肉？在這種氣候底下？我看還是免了。

column1: First, you must have money.
column2: 首先，你得有錢才行。

column1: You should be able to find what you need within this bazaar.
column2: 你所需要的東西，這市集裡應該找得到。

column1: The many and varied smells of Jerusalem are, uhm, interesting, to say the least.
column2: 耶路撒冷這五花八門的氣味，嗯，至少可以說是別有一番趣味。

column1: Nay! Jerusalem is ruled by the laws of Islam where they will cut off the hand of a thief.
column2: 不可！耶路撒冷奉行伊斯蘭律法，竊賊在此是要被斬去手掌的。

column1: Do not be disgusting.
column2: 休得如此噁心。

column1: Sa'alam aleikem. Peace be unto you.
column2: Sa'alam aleikem. 願平安與你同在。

column1: How can you tell a man is a hierophant merely by looking? You must seek words or deeds for such a judgment.
column2: 你怎能單憑外表便看出一人是祭司？要下此判斷，得從言語或行止中尋找端倪。

column1: It is a word from ancient Greece meaning one who has knowledge of sacred mysteries.
column2: 這是源自古希臘的字眼，意指通曉神聖奧秘之人。

column1: The gutter which runs down the center of the Street of David is most unsavory.
column2: 大衛街正中央那條水溝，氣味著實難聞。

column1: The water in the gutter is unfit for any use.
column2: 水溝裡的水，什麼用途都派不上。

column1: The street is paved of ancient stones, many hundreds of years older than Camelot.
column2: 這條街道由古老的石塊鋪成，比肯萊特還要年長上好幾百歲。

column1: Nearly all of Jerusalem is made of the same, buff- coloured stone.
column2: 耶路撒冷幾乎清一色由同一種淺褐色的石塊建成。

column1: The walls are mainly of the buff-coloured stone predominant here, or brick and plaster.
column2: 這裡的牆多半以當地常見的淺褐色石塊砌成，也有磚造與灰泥牆面。

column1: There is nothing unusual about it.
column2: 這東西並無異常之處。

column1: You mean that girl with the cage of doves? Pretty little thing, was she not?
column2: 你是說那個帶著鴿籠的女孩？生得挺俊俏的，不是嗎？

column1: What girl? Did I miss something?
column2: 什麼女孩？我是不是錯過了什麼？

column1: The coins of Jerusalem are the dinar which is gold, the dirham which is silver, and the fals which is copper.
column2: 耶路撒冷通行的錢幣有三種：金幣、銀幣，以及銅幣。

column1: I can add nothing more to what you already know.
column2: 你已知曉之事，我再無可補充。

column1: I shall know who and what she is when you do.
column2: 待你查明她是誰、是何身分之時，我自然也就知曉了。

column1: You are not standing near that merchant.
column2: 你並未站在那位商人附近。

column1: The city guards roam the bazaar, restless for any excuse to use their swords.
column2: 城中衛兵在市集裡巡邏遊走，一逮到藉口便迫不及待要拔劍。

column1: You no longer have a purse, Arthur. You are alone in a strange city in a distant land without so much as a single copper coin.
column2: 亞瑟，你已沒有錢囊了。你孤身一人，身處異地陌生的城市，連一枚銅板都不剩。

column1: I doubt if that thief would dare to show his face here again.
column2: 我看那賊人不敢再在此地露面了。

column1: I have said all I ever care to say about the mule.
column2: 關於那頭騾子，我該說的都已說完。

column1: She continues to follow you.
column2: 她仍舊跟隨著你。

column1: She was with you when you entered Jerusalem. You had better look for her.
column2: 你進入耶路撒冷時，她本與你同行。你最好找找她的下落。

column1: It is a common form of headdress in such a hot climate.
column2: 在這般炎熱的氣候下，這是常見的頭飾樣式。

column1: The sun bakes the streets of Jerusalem.
column2: 烈日烤炙著耶路撒冷的街道。

column1: Please attempt to control this rampage of excessive generosity.
column2: 還請你克制一下這股揮金如土的衝動。

column1: I do not think that will be of interest to this merchant. Usually merchants wish to sell, not buy.
column2: 我想這位商人不會感興趣。商人通常是想賣東西，而非買東西。

column1: You must have a buyer first.
column2: 你得先找到買家才行。

column1: I do not have that for sale.
column2: 這東西我沒有要賣。

column1: Difficult, since you are not dealing with anyone at the moment.
column2: 難辦，因為你此刻並未與任何人交易。

column1: It might be of better use elsewhere.
column2: 這東西放在別處，或許更能派上用場。

column1: That would be cruel, Arthur.
column2: 那未免太過殘忍了，亞瑟。

column1: The doves are safely in their cage.
column2: 鴿子已安然待在籠中。

column1: There are some doves up on the awning above you.
column2: 你頭頂的遮篷上，停著幾隻鴿子。

column1: There are some doves up on the awning and balcony above you.
column2: 你頭頂的遮篷與陽台上，停著幾隻鴿子。

column1: They are in the cage. You have caught them all.
column2: 牠們都在籠子裡了，你已經全數捉齊。

column1: You would be taken for a lunatic if you stood here making bird calls.
column2: 你若站在這裡學鳥叫，旁人只會當你是個瘋子。

column1: How bitterly this poor girl weeps! She is much distressed.
column2: 這可憐的女孩哭得好傷心！她十分苦惱。

column1: She waits for you to follow her advice.
column2: 她等著你依她的話去做。

column1: Six doves sit in the cage.
column2: 籠裡棲著六隻鴿子。

column1: The cage is empty.
column2: 籠子空無一物。

column1: Your tasks are done. Go now to the Seeress, for she awaits you.
column2: 你的任務已了。去見女預言家吧，她正等著你。

column1: The poor girl is crying too much to speak again.
column2: 那可憐的女孩哭得說不出話來。

column1: Money will not solve this poor girl's problem.
column2: 金錢解決不了這可憐女孩的難題。

column1: As an initiate of the Goddess, I may not accept money from a man.
column2: 身為女神的入門弟子，我不得收受男子的錢財。

column1: But, sir, of what use is grain to me?
column2: 但，大人，穀物對我有何用處？

column1: How do you intend to feed them?
column2: 你打算如何餵養牠們？

column1: Ione will take care of them now.
column2: 艾歐妮這下會照顧牠們了。

column1: But what would that accomplish? Perhaps if you explained more clearly.
column2: 但那樣做能有何用處？或許你該解釋得更清楚些。

column1: But I have no money.
column2: 但我身無分文。

column1: And how do you propose to do that, Arthur?
column2: 那你打算如何做到，亞瑟？

column1: She does not need any help.
column2: 她不需要任何協助。

column1: Perhaps once her problem is solved, the poor girl will feel more like having a casual conversation.
column2: 或許等她的難題解決後，這可憐的女孩會更願意閒話幾句。

column1: She is too distraught to speak.
column2: 她傷心欲絕，無法言語。

column1: Only the Seeress can answer this question.
column2: 唯有女預言家能回答這個問題。

column1: Seek your answers from the Seeress.
column2: 去向女預言家尋求答案吧。

column1: That would not help.
column2: 那樣做無濟於事。

column1: You thought me only a simple girl, but I am an initiate of the Goddess sent to watch and test you.
column2: 你以為我不過是個尋常女孩，但我其實是女神的入門弟子，奉命前來窺看並試煉你。

column1: King Arthur, you have finished your tasks with this act of cleverness. Return to the Seeress for her judgment.
column2: 亞瑟王，你以此番機智完成了考驗。回去見女預言家，聽候她的裁定吧。

column1: I dropped the cage and all my mistress' doves escaped. They will not come back and they are prize doves, hand fed by my mistress from hatchlings!
column2: 我把鳥籠摔了，我家主人的鴿子全飛走了。牠們不會回來的，而那些可是主人從雛鳥起親手餵養的名貴鴿子啊！

column1: She trusted me with them. I dare not go back without them! Oh, misery!
column2: 她把牠們託付給我，我不敢空手回去見她！唉，我好命苦！

column1: Mmmmm, so who are you, with lungs like the hamsin, the all-powerful wind? I see you are a foreigner, but from the look of you, not a very rich one. I only have time for rich men.
column2: 唔……你算什麼人物，說起話來竟像哈馬辛風那般氣勢逼人？看你是個外邦人，但瞧你這模樣，也不是什麼有錢人。我只有空應付有錢人。

column1: Oh, it is you again. The mirror is wonderful. Well, what do you want? Speak up, I have a customer arriving soon.
column2: 喔，又是你。這面鏡子真是美極了。好吧，你想要什麼？快說，我馬上就有客人要到了。

column1: You grow annoying. What do you want, infidel?
column2: 你越來越惹人厭了。你想要什麼，異教徒？

column1: I do not think the word "girl" is appropriate for this strumpet.
column2: 『女孩』這個詞，用在這個蕩婦身上恐怕不太合適。

column1: From the layers of paint upon her face, the excessive jewelry, the dyed hair and other signs, I would call this woman more than a trifle vain.
column2: 從她臉上厚厚的脂粉、滿身的首飾、染過的頭髮等種種跡象看來，我會說這女人虛榮得可不只一點點。

column1: The woman, Mari, is not shy about displaying her attributes.
column2: 這女人，瑪麗，展露自己身段可是一點也不害臊。

column1: The smell of her cheap ointments overwhelms even the odors of the gutter.
column2: 她那廉價脂粉的氣味，濃得連溝渠的臭味都蓋過去了。

column1: She pays no attention to you at the moment.
column2: 她此刻並未理會你。

column1: Chalas! Enough! I can hear you.
column2: 夠了！夠了！我聽得見你說話。

column1: Ooh, big tough man. I am soooooo frightened. Better put away your sword, stupid infidel. One scream from me and the city guards will come running.
column2: 喔，好一個彪悍的男子漢，我可害怕得要死呢。你最好把劍收起來，蠢異教徒。我只消尖叫一聲，城裡的衛兵就會蜂擁而至。

column1: I cannot stand here talking all day. I have business to do. If you want something, speak up.
column2: 我不能站在這裡跟你聊一整天，我還有生意要做。你若想要什麼，快說。

column1: I am very unhappy right now. I know I am very beautiful, but I have no way to see my own beauty as others see it.
column2: 我此刻很不開心。我知道自己美豔動人，卻無從像旁人那樣，親眼見到自己的美貌。

column1: And curse that wretched Ibrahim. He left me for his wife, of all things! At least I have kept his precious veil for revenge.
column2: 還有，去他的易布拉興，那個可惡的傢伙！他竟然為了自己的妻子甩了我！至少我留著他那條寶貝面紗，好好報復他。

column1: My arms are not that long, foolish man, but... mmmm...I would dearly love to have that mirror.
column2: 我的手可沒那麼長，笨男人，不過……嗯……我倒是很想要那面鏡子。

column1: If it were only money I wanted, I could have taken money from Ibrahim. But he dared to say I was vain because I wish to see my own beauty and he would have no part of it.
column2: 若我要的只是錢，大可直接向易布拉興要。但他竟敢說我虛榮，只因我想親眼見到自己的美貌，還說他不願插手這種事。

column1: He probably gave you money, hoping to trick me. But it will not work. I will get what I want, or you get nothing.
column2: 他大概給了你錢，指望能騙過我。但這招行不通。我要拿到我想要的，否則你什麼也別想得到。

column1: What would I want with a mule, silly man?
column2: 我要一頭騾子做什麼，傻男人？

column1: I do not want that. Quit wasting my time.
column2: 我不要那個。別再浪費我的時間了。

column1: Since you gave me the mirror, I will give you the veil as a favor. Wait a moment.
column2: 既然你給了我鏡子，我就賣你個人情，把面紗給你。等一下。

column1: Well.....since you gave me the mirror, I will do you this favor. Wait a moment.
column2: 好吧……既然你給了我鏡子，我就賞你這個面子。等一下。

column1: If you are a friend of Ibrahim, you are no friend of mine. He prefers his wife to me, the scoundrel. Let him suffer. He will never get the veil from me.
column2: 你若是易布拉興的朋友，那就不是我的朋友。那個無賴，寧可要他妻子也不要我。就讓他受苦去吧，這面紗他休想從我這裡拿走。

column1: Unless, of course, you care to bring me something of greater value. Something that would allow me to see my great beauty as others see it.
column2: 當然，除非你願意帶些更有價值的東西來給我。能讓我像旁人一樣，親眼看見自己絕世美貌的東西。

column1: I told you, I will exchange it for a way to see for myself how beautiful I am.
column2: 我說過了，我只肯用它換一樣能讓我親眼看見自己有多美的東西。

column1: Whatever for? Your sword and armour are unequaled in quality.
column2: 何必呢？你的劍與盔甲，品質可是無與倫比。

column1: You are more a boy than a man if you think that is what I sell.
column2: 你若以為我賣的是那種東西，那你不過是個乳臭未乾的男孩，稱不上男人。

column1: I shudder to think what you would catch if you were to do so.
column2: 光是想到你那麼做會染上什麼病，我就不寒而慄。

column1: Open my door to you? You could not afford me.
column2: 為你開門？你可付不起我的價碼。

column1: I do not want to talk about the scoundrel. I hope he suffers because he will never get the veil from me.
column2: 我不想談那個無賴。我但願他不好過，因為這面紗他休想從我這裡拿走。

column1: Mmmmm, I would dearly love him as a customer, but he has no time for me.
column2: 嗯……我倒很樂意讓他當我的客人，可惜他沒空理我。

column1: He is a fat, prudish pig who will not do business with me.
column2: 他是個又胖又假正經的豬，不肯跟我做生意。

column1: I only have time for rich men.
column2: 我只有空應付有錢人。

column1: I will only be happy when I can see for myself how beautiful I am.
column2: 唯有能親眼看見自己有多美，我才會開心。

column1: A woman as beautiful as me should have a mirror.
column2: 像我這樣美麗的女人，該有一面鏡子才是。

column1: Her? Hah! Men think she is so beautiful, but she is nothing compared to me!
column2: 她？哼！男人們都以為她有多美，跟我一比，她算什麼！

column1: Oh, quit wasting my time.
column2: 喔，別再浪費我的時間了。

column1: My, Ibrahim must grow desperate indeed to send you after his precious veil. You may tell him it is not for sale.
column2: 哎呀，易布拉興想必是急壞了，才會派你來討他那條寶貝面紗。你可以告訴他，這東西不賣。

column1: This overpainted trollop can do without that.
column2: 這濃妝豔抹的浪貨，沒有那個東西也活得下去。

column1: You truly are a pest. Go away.
column2: 你真是煩人得很。走開。

column1: This damsel is not in distress, Arthur.
column2: 這位小姐可不是什麼待救的佳人，亞瑟。

column1: So, you are smarter than you look.
column2: 看來你比外表聰明些。

column1: When I have the mirror, you may have the veil.
column2: 等我拿到鏡子，你就能拿到面紗。

column1: It is true! I am as beautiful as they say! Even more so!
column2: 果然如此！我真如傳聞般美麗！甚至猶有過之！

column1: Hmmph. And they say mirrors cannot lie. Hah!
column2: 哼，都說鏡子不會說謊。哈！

column1: A most formidable looking man, but with an honest face. I would say he was previously a soldier who has gone into business selling what he knows best.
column2: 這人模樣威猛懾人，卻有一張誠實的臉。我猜他過去是個軍人，如今改行做起自己最擅長的買賣。

column1: He wears an extremely good scimitar and dagger and from the looks of him, he knows how to use them.
column2: 他佩著一把上好的彎刀與一把匕首，看模樣，這兩樣兵器他都使得順手。

column1: Mohammed is busy closing his shop.
column2: 穆罕默德正忙著打烊。

column1: Perhaps you should move closer
column2: 或許你該再靠近一些

column1: There is no-one inside my shop. I have closed up.
column2: 我店裡沒人了，我已經打烊了。

column1: I would not annoy Mohammed by trying that when his shop is clearly closed.
column2: 店都明明已經打烊了，我可不會做這種事去惹惱穆罕默德。

column1: Thought I would wait and see how you fared, warrior. I take it things do not go well. I am sorry to see it. If I were not about to leave on a long journey, I would take you in as my guest.
column2: 我想著在此等等，看你這一路走得如何，戰士。看來事情並不順利，我深感遺憾。若不是即將啟程遠行，我定會請你作客。

column1: It does not seem to me that you have much use for your mule now. And a fine mule she is, too. Just the kind of mule I could use on a long journey.
column2: 依我看，你現在對這頭騾子似乎沒什麼用處了。而且是頭好騾子，正是我遠行路上用得著的那種。

column1: I am sure you value your mule too highly to part with her. I certainly would.
column2: 我料想你太看重這頭騾子，捨不得割愛。換作是我，也是如此。

column1: Your mule is safe, habib. I thought I had best remain and guard her against other thieves. They are a plague in Jerusalem.
column2: 你的騾子很安全，朋友。我想著最好留下來守著她，以防其他竊賊——耶路撒冷這種人可多得很。

column1: I am not surprized you returned for her. She is an exceptionally well bred and well mannered mule. I use many mules in my travels and am a good judge.
column2: 你回來找她，我一點也不意外。她血統優良、性情又好，我行旅多用騾子，看得出好壞。

column1: That truly is a very good mule. You undoubtedly value her very highly. If that were my mule, I would never sell her.
column2: 那真是頭上好的騾子。你想必十分珍視她。若換作是我的騾子，我絕不會出售。

column1: You are wise not to waste your time chasing after him, habib. The thieves of Jerusalem are as slippery as eels.
column2: 你聰明，沒有浪費時間去追他，朋友。耶路撒冷的竊賊個個滑溜得像鰻魚。

column1: A shame I must leave soon to join a caravan to Cairo, or you could be my guest. That is a very fine mule you have there, I notice. You must prize her highly.
column2: 真可惜我很快就得動身，加入前往開羅的商隊，不然你大可作我的客人。我注意到你那頭騾子相當出色，想必你十分珍視她。

column1: I will ask Allah to aid you.
column2: 我會祈求阿拉助你一臂之力。

column1: I fear you waited too long, Arthur. He is gone.
column2: 恐怕你等得太久了，亞瑟。他已經走了。

column1: You would give me this excellent mule?! Habibi, you are either a holy man or a mad man. Still, you have my undying gratitude.
column2: 你願意把這頭上好的騾子送給我？！我的朋友啊，你不是聖人便是瘋子。但無論如何，我對你感激不盡。

column1: You would not last long in Jerusalem without a sword. I could not consider buying your only weapon, magnificent though it is.
column2: 在耶路撒冷沒有劍，你撐不了多久。你僅有的這件武器，儘管精良，我實在不能買下它。

column1: I have many shields to sell and yours, though well made, has been through much travel and battle. Besides, you may well need it.
column2: 我這裡有許多盾牌可賣，你這面盾牌雖做工精良，卻已歷經長途跋涉與征戰。再者，你恐怕還用得上它。

column1: It is good armor, made after the fashion of the Romans, I see. But I am in the business of selling, not buying.
column2: 這副盔甲不錯，看樣式是仿羅馬人打的。不過，我做的是賣的生意，不做買的。

column1: You look well equipped, habib, and I have closed up shop to go on a journey.
column2: 你裝備齊全，朋友，而我已經關店，準備啟程遠行了。

column1: I sell only weapons and armor.
column2: 我只賣兵器與盔甲。

column1: The mule looks very happy with Mohammed.
column2: 那頭騾子跟著穆罕默德，看來挺開心的。

column1: She is yours, warrior. I am simply guarding her for you.
column2: 她是你的，戰士。我不過是替你看守著她罷了。

column1: I do not know of such things. I am only a simple soldier turned merchant.
column2: 這種事我一概不知，我不過是個棄武從商的普通軍人。

column1: There was another like you, but that was a some time ago. I do not know what became of him.
column2: 曾經有個跟你類似的人，不過那是好一陣子前的事了。我不知道他後來怎麼了。

column1: She is a fine mule. I can see she has good bloodlines.
column2: 她是頭好騾子，一看便知血統優良。

column1: That mongrel? He waits outside the gate and tries to trick people into paying him to enter! He is not very good at his fraud and most people are too smart to pay him.
column2: 那個混混？他守在城門外，想騙人付錢才讓人進城！他這騙術並不高明，大多數人都精明得不會上當。

column1: I sell weapons of all kinds - swords, daggers, bows, maces, axes, spears and many other weapons. But I regret I have locked up as I must depart very soon to join a caravan.
column2: 我什麼兵器都賣——劍、匕首、弓、狼牙棒、斧頭、長矛，還有許多其他兵器。但可惜我已經上鎖打烊了，因為我很快就得動身加入商隊。

column1: I deal with weapons only.
column2: 我只做兵器生意。

column1: I travel with a caravan to Cairo.
column2: 我隨商隊前往開羅。

column1: It is in Egypt.
column2: 它在埃及。

column1: The wench lives above me, but I would avoid her company, if I were you.
column2: 那丫頭住在我樓上，但若我是你，我會少跟她來往。

column1: I am sorry for your loss. That thief has done much mischief in the bazaar.
column2: 你的損失，我深感遺憾。那竊賊在市集裡沒少幹壞事。

column1: It is a city of great interest, if one is careful enough.
column2: 只要夠謹慎，這是座頗值得一探的城市。

column1: Eh? You jest. You know that means weapons.
column2: 咦？你在說笑吧。你明知道那指的是兵器。

column1: I am not the wisest of men, habib, so I say as little as possible to hide my ignorance.
column2: 我算不上什麼聰明人，朋友，所以我盡量少開口，好掩飾自己的無知。

column1: Not wise, habib. There are mercenary guards all over this city, eager to cut into pieces any foreigner foolish enough to cause trouble. I know. I have done it.
column2: 這可不明智，朋友。城裡到處都是雇傭衛兵，巴不得把任何蠢到惹事的外邦人剁成碎片。我很清楚，因為我幹過這種事。

column1: Habibi, if you would truly part with this excellent mule, I will gladly give you all the money I have upon me. It is a goodly sum, but this fine mule is worth every coin.
column2: 我的朋友，你若真捨得割愛這頭上好的騾子，我樂意把身上所有的錢都給你。這是一筆不小的數目，但這頭好騾子值得每一枚錢幣。

column1: In this purse you will find two dinars, that which is our gold coin. There are also dirhams, and these are silver, and some fals. A fals is a copper coin.
column2: 這錢囊裡有兩枚第納爾，也就是我們的金幣。此外還有些迪爾罕，那是銀幣，另外還有幾枚法爾斯。法爾斯是銅幣。

column1: Since I see you do not understand, here is the way of it--4 fals are worth 1 dirham. 4 dirham are worth 1 dinar.
column2: 既然你不明白，我就把換算講給你聽——四法爾斯值一迪爾罕，四迪爾罕值一第納爾。

column1: And now I must go and meet the caravan that awaits me. May Allah grant you good fortune.
column2: 現在我得去與等候我的商隊會合了。願阿拉賜你好運。

column1: I must hurry now to meet my caravan. May Allah guide you.
column2: 我現在得快去與商隊會合。願阿拉指引你。

column1: You wish to waste time with your lodestone when a thief has just stolen your purse?!
column2: 竊賊才剛偷走你的錢囊，你竟還想浪費時間擺弄指北針？！

column1: So this is the bazaar of Jerusalem. Tiny shops line both sides of the street. And such smells! Delicious foods combined with the raw sewage in the gutter. Watch where you step.
column2: 這便是耶路撒冷的市集了。街道兩旁擠滿了小小的店鋪。那氣味真是——美味的食物混雜著溝渠裡的污穢，走路可得看清腳下。

column1: Arthur! That little thief has grabbed your purse!
column2: 亞瑟！那個小賊搶走了你的錢囊！

column1: There he goes, into an alley!
column2: 他往那條巷子跑了！

column1: He does not look like he is stopping for anything.
column2: 看樣子他不會為任何事停下腳步。

column1: You...you have brought this for me simply because I wanted it? No-one has ever shown me a kindness like this before.
column2: 你……你帶這個來給我，只因為我想要它？從沒有人曾這樣善待過我。

column1: Your good example makes me ashamed! To think that I should be as callous as those I criticize and let this poor boy go hungry when I have food to spare.
column2: 你這番身教，讓我羞愧難當！我竟和自己譴責的那種人一樣冷漠，明明還有餘糧，卻放任這可憐的男孩挨餓。

column1: Come here, little one. I will feed you and clothe you and raise you as my son in honor of this good man.
column2: 過來，孩子。我會給你飯吃、給你衣穿，並收養你為我的兒子，以此紀念這位善心人。

column1: I shall name him Joshua.
column2: 我要為他取名約書亞。

column1: Buy it? Does no-one do anything in this world without seeking gain? Very well, I will give you 3 fals for it, since you have gone to the trouble.
column2: 買下它？這世上難道人人做事都得圖點好處嗎？也罷，既然你費了這番工夫，我就給你三枚法爾斯。

column1: Ya'Allah! It is the veil, the very veil! Habibi, you are forever my brother!
column2: 呀，阿拉啊！是這面紗，正是這面紗！我的兄弟，你永遠是我的兄弟！

column1: I have had time to dwell upon my foolishness. I will never be unfaithful to my beloved wife again. Thank you! May you live long and bear many sons!
column2: 我已有時間好好反省自己的愚蠢。我再也不會對心愛的妻子不忠了。謝謝你！願你長命百歲，兒孫滿堂！

column1: So, you are a scoundrel and a friend of Mari, no doubt. Expect no gratitude from me. Here is 1 dirham and be gone, or I will call the city guard to deal with you.
column2: 看來你是個無賴，想必還是瑪麗的朋友。休想從我這裡得到感激。這裡有一枚迪爾罕，快滾，否則我就叫城衛來對付你。

column1: What shall I do? What shall I do? I have been betrayed by Mari the wicked, Mari the vain. For my brief moment of weakness, I shall lose my beloved wife.
column2: 我該如何是好？我該如何是好？我被瑪麗那惡毒又虛榮的女人給出賣了。只因我一時軟弱，就要失去我心愛的妻子。

column1: You are a man. You will understand. I dallied but once with the woman, Mari, who lives above the shop of Mohammed. But I left behind a silken veil.
column2: 你是個男人，你會懂的。我只不過與那個住在穆罕默德店樓上的女人瑪麗鬼混過一次，卻把一條絲質面紗給留在了那裡。

column1: Not any veil. A veil supreme in the mastery of the weaver's art, of glorious color and pattern. Mari refuses to return it to me.
column2: 那可不是普通的面紗，而是織藝登峰造極之作，色彩與紋樣皆美輪美奐。瑪麗死活不肯還給我。

column1: I promised this veil to my wife as proof of my devotion. If I fail to bring it to her, she will leave me. I would do anything, pay anything, to avert that.
column2: 我曾答應把這面紗獻給妻子，作為我忠貞的憑證。若我拿不回它交給她，她便會離我而去。為了避免這件事，我什麼都願意做，什麼代價都願意付。

column1: Poor thing probably cannot speak properly. Well, give him time. Sometimes silence is the greater virtue, eh?
column2: 這可憐人大概說不好話。罷了，給他點時間吧。有時候，沉默才是更大的美德，不是嗎？

column1: No good trying to talk him. He never says a word. Not a tooth left in his head, anyway. He has been there for days, begging for crumbs.
column2: 跟他說話沒有用，他從不開口。反正他滿口牙也掉光了。他已經在那待了好幾天，乞討些殘羹剩飯。

column1: Ah, it is a cruel world when no-one will help one another.
column2: 唉，這世道真是殘酷，竟沒有人願意互相幫助。

column1: He is afraid to take money. It must remind him of some evil happening from his past.
column2: 他不敢收錢，想必是勾起了他過去某段不堪的往事。

column1: He cannot eat it for he has lost most of his teeth, doubtless from starvation and hardship.
column2: 他吃不了這個，因為他的牙齒幾乎都掉光了，想必是飢餓與苦難所致。

column1: Do not worry about him. He will have all the felafels his heart desires.
column2: 別擔心他了，他想吃多少法拉費都有。

column1: Do not torment the boy, Arthur. You can see he is starving.
column2: 別折磨這男孩了，亞瑟。你也看得出他正忍飢挨餓。

column1: He cannot eat the it for he has lost most of his teeth, doubtless from starvation and hardship.
column2: 他吃不了這個，因為他的牙齒幾乎都掉光了，想必是飢餓與苦難所致。

column1: You have nothing to feed him, Arthur, though it is a worthy thought.
column2: 你身上沒有東西可以餵他，亞瑟，不過這份心意值得嘉許。

column1: He is too afraid to take it.
column2: 他害怕得不敢收下。

column1: A noble thought, but you must find a practical way to do this.
column2: 這番心意可嘉，但此事你須想個切實可行的辦法才是。

column1: You cannot care for this boy yourself and still succeed in your mission, nor do I think he would go with you willingly.
column2: 你既要親自照料這孩子，便難以達成你的使命，況且我也不認為他會心甘情願隨你同行。

column1: That was a good deed, Arthur.
column2: 此舉是件善行，亞瑟。

column1: The city guard does not look friendly.
column2: 這名城衛看來不甚友善。

column1: Do so, if you think it wise.
column2: 你若認為明智，便這麼做吧。

column1: Do not trifle with these city guards. They would as soon kill you as look at you.
column2: 莫要招惹這些城衛，他們殺你如同看你一眼般毫不猶豫。

column1: We have orders to find a thief!
column2: 我們奉命緝拿一名竊賊！

column1: And we have never seen YOU before.
column2: 而我們從未見過你這號人物。

column1: He must be the one! Kill him!
column2: 必是此人無疑！殺了他！

column1: Did I not warn you against this? But do you listen? Nay, you are too stubborn. Now you are reduced to shish kebab.
column2: 我不是警告過你不可如此？可你何曾聽從？不，你太過固執。如今你已被戳成了肉串。

column1: You did not even try to defend yourself, nor can I blame you, after the Seeress crushed any hope of finding the Grail.
column2: 你連自衛都未曾嘗試，這我也不能怪你——畢竟女預言家早已擊碎了你尋得聖杯的一切希望。

column1: Perhaps you will be wiser in your next life.
column2: 或許來世的你，會更有智慧。

column1: You die in poverty, mistaken for a common thief. In your next life, listen more carefully to Mohammed's hints. He is not short of a coin.
column2: 你窮困潦倒而死，被誤認作尋常竊賊。來世，且更用心聽穆罕默德的提點，他從不缺一文錢。

column1: The reward for greed is death. In your next life, consider fulfilling the tasks of the Seeress in a more worthwhile manner.
column2: 貪婪的報應便是死亡。來世，且想想該用更值得的方式完成女預言家交付的任務。

column1: Ah, please excuse me one moment, habibi.
column2: 啊，容我失陪片刻，朋友。

column1: My apologies. I must have sold the last piece. But I have a special on saints' relics.
column2: 抱歉，最後一件想必已經賣出了。不過我這裡聖徒聖物正有特價。

column1: Wait but one instant.
column2: 稍候片刻。

column1: A great pleasure to do business with you! Oh, did I mention that I have also a cup called the Grail?
column2: 與你做生意真是一大樂事！噢對了，我可曾提過，我這裡也有一只名喚聖杯的杯子？

column1: A great pleasure to do business with you!
column2: 與你做生意真是一大樂事！

column1: You refer to the Christian legend of the cup from which the prophet Jesus drank before he was martyred. I know it well. Come close and listen.
column2: 你說的是基督教傳說中，先知耶穌殉道前所飲之杯。此事我熟知得很，靠近些，聽我道來。

column1: This is not well known, but I possess the very cup, this Holy Grail you seek. It was entrusted to me by an ancient priest who died in my care.
column2: 此事鮮為人知，但你所尋的這只聖杯，正在我手中。它是一位年邁的祭司託付給我的，此後便在我的照料下辭世。

column1: And I told myself, "Ismail, this Grail must never go to an ordinary man, but one day a great warrior will ask for it and you must be ready."
column2: 我便對自己說：「艾思美啊，這只聖杯絕不能落入尋常人之手，但終有一日，會有一位偉大的戰士前來求取，你須時刻備好。」

column1: And so I have waited. Clearly you are the man destined to have this Grail. It is a thing beyond value. But for you, only 1 dinar!
column2: 於是我便一直等候。顯然你正是命中註定要擁有這只聖杯之人。此物本是無價之寶，但對你，僅收一枚金幣！

column1: I will fetch it at once.
column2: 我這就去取來。

column1: Heh heh, sorry, habibi. I must have sold it. But I have a very good deal on saints' fingerbones! And for you, at half price!
column2: 嘿嘿，抱歉了，朋友。想必已經賣出了。不過我這裡聖徒指骨正划算得很！對你，還打對折！

column1: Aye, a girl is inside, probably the butcher's daughter. And she is...ahem...Arthur, she is taking a bath.
column2: 正是，裡頭有位姑娘，想必是屠夫的女兒。而她……咳……亞瑟，她正在沐浴。

column1: Have you no shame? She is naked! Avert your eyes, quickly!
column2: 你就不知羞恥嗎？她可是一絲不掛！快把眼睛移開！

column1: EEEEEEEEEEK!
Hmm...it looks like someone is in there.
column2: 嗯……看來裡頭似乎有人。

column1: Here.
column2: 拿去。

column1: Pretty women always did go to your head, though seldom with such an impact.
column2: 美貌向來容易讓你沖昏了頭，只是這回的力道，倒是少見。

column1: A rat has bitten you! You may not feel the effects of its poison for a long time, yet the hierophant warned that it means certain death.
column2: 一隻老鼠咬了你！你或許一時感覺不出毒性發作，但祭司曾警告過，此毒必致死無疑。

column1: Another rat has bitten you! The poison will now act twice as quickly!
column2: 又一隻老鼠咬了你！如今毒性發作的速度將加快一倍！

column1: You have been bitten yet again! Now your time is truly limited.
column2: 你再度遭到咬傷！如今你的時間，是真的所剩無幾了。

column1: Your fate is sealed, as is this room. I cannot bear to remain and watch the slow, lingering death that awaits you within this dusty tomb. Farewell, Arthur.
column2: 你的命運已成定局，一如此室已然封閉。我不忍留下，眼看你在這座塵封的墓穴裡緩緩死去。永別了，亞瑟。

column1: It was so old, it crumbled to dust upon hitting the floor.
column2: 它太過古老，一觸及地面便碎成了塵土。

column1: It is a terribly old, moldering bone. I cannot imagine why you want it.
column2: 這是一根極其古老、業已朽爛的骨頭。我實在想不透你要它做什麼。

column1: There is no water behind the rocks.
column2: 岩石後方並無水源。

column1: Arthur!  Something terrible is happening to you.
column2: 亞瑟！  有可怕的事正在你身上發生。

column1: Too late the signs are clear.  This water is poisoned.  It killed the camel who had not the sense of your mule.  But then, neither did you.
column2: 徵兆已然明顯，只是為時已晚。這水有毒，連駱駝都因它喪命——牠可沒有你那頭騾子的靈性。不過話說回來，你也沒有。

column1: Do not despair so easily, seeker. I entreat you to return and take the Test again or you will regret leaving here in failure.
column2: 求索者啊，莫要輕言絕望。我懇求你歸來，再度接受考驗，否則你將悔恨自己敗興而歸。

column1: Truly you are the most worthy of all men who have passed my door. Go with my blessings and find the hierophant.
column2: 你確實是曾踏入我門下之人中，最為配得的一位。帶著我的祝福前去，尋找那位祭司吧。

column1: There is no-one within. Only I can open that door.
column2: 此門之內空無一人，唯有我能將它開啟。

column1: It rests in your hand, doing nothing unusual for a stone dove. You may as well put it away again.
column2: 它靜靜躺在你手中，作為一隻石鴿，並無異狀。你不妨將它收起來吧。

column1: The dove leads you on. Do not lose sight of it!
column2: 那隻鴿子引領著你前行，切莫讓牠脫離視線！

column1: You fool, Arthur! You will lose the dove! Hurry after it!
column2: 你這個傻子，亞瑟！你要跟丟那隻鴿子了！快追上去！

column1: OK. Here.
column2: 好的，拿去。

column1: The stone dove feels oddly warm. 'Tis changing! By the power of Aphrodite, it turns to a living dove within your very hands!
column2: 這隻石鴿摸起來竟有些溫熱。它正在變化！憑藉阿芙羅黛蒂的力量，牠就在你手中化作了一隻活生生的鴿子！

column1: Follow my dove and you shall have your soul's desire.
column2: 追隨我的鴿子，你便將得償心中所願。

column1: I have brought you to water, habib.  Drink, before the heat overcomes you.
column2: 我已帶你來到水源之處，朋友。快飲用吧，趁著暑熱還未將你擊倒。

column1: By custom, I must wait for those I guide to drink first, so please, drink your fill.
column2: 依照慣例，我必須等我所引導之人先飲水，所以，請儘管暢飲吧。

column1: I am happy to see you again!  You were lucky to find this water without me.
column2: 能再見到你，我很高興！你竟能不靠我便找到這處水源，實在幸運。

column1: I have quenched my thirst already.  Please, drink your fill.
column2: 我已解過渴了，請你儘管暢飲吧。

column1: **** Can't do it.
**** OmiGod!  What IS this shit!
column2: **** 我的天哪！這是什麼鬼東西！

column1: Arthur!  Defend yourself!
column2: 亞瑟！  自衛！

column1: That has put a well-needed end to this false guide at last.  You have surely avenged many previous victims.
column2: 此舉終於為這名虛偽嚮導的性命畫下了亟需的句點。你想必已為許多先前的受害者報了仇。

column1: You will see neither the dove nor Aphrodite again.
column2: 你再也見不到那隻鴿子，也見不到阿芙羅黛蒂了。

column1: You still carry the stone dove given to you by the statue of Aphrodite. I hope you paid attention to the statue's instructions.
column2: 你身上仍帶著阿芙羅黛蒂神像贈予你的石鴿。希望你當時有留心神像的指示。

column1: Spirals are very ancient symbols. They represent the unending cycle of life. A solar spiral turns to the right. A lunar spiral turns to the left.
column2: 螺形紋飾是極為古老的符號，象徵著生命無盡的循環。太陽螺紋向右旋轉，月亮螺紋向左旋轉。

column1: Had you searched the catacombs, you might have found him. I fear now it is too late for such thoughts.
column2: 若你早些搜索過地下墓窖，或許便能尋得他的下落。恐怕如今，此念已是為時已晚。

column1: He will recover soon enough. Look to your own needs. You must find the Grail before you die of the rat's poison!
column2: 他很快便會康復。且先顧好你自己——你得趕在老鼠的毒發作致死之前，尋得聖杯！

column1: He is dead and his death weighs heavily upon your soul.
column2: 他已身故，他的死沉沉壓在你的靈魂之上。

column1: The Seeress said that eating the apple would relieve hunger and thirst and give you renewed strength. How long such an effect will last is another question, however.
column2: 女預言家曾說，食用這顆蘋果能解飢解渴，並讓你重獲氣力。至於效果能持續多久，則是另一回事了。

column1: The bone is gone. You must have dropped it on the stairs. Just as well. It was a useless thing to carry around.
column2: 那根骨頭已經不見了，想必是你落在了樓梯上。倒也罷了，那本就是件沒用的東西，帶著也是白帶。

column1: Her presence is here. She waits for you to prove yourself with sword and shield, as she requires.
column2: 她的氣息就在此處。她正等著你依她所要求的，以劍與盾證明自己。

column1: Only you can summon her, Arthur. And waste no time going about it!
column2: 唯有你能召喚她，亞瑟。且莫要浪費時間！

column1: She has abandoned this place at last and will not return.
column2: 她終究已離棄此地，不會再回來了。

column1: You must locate this pillar by yourself.
column2: 這根柱子，你得靠自己找出來。

column1: If you follow Aphrodite's instructions, the Grail will surely be yours.
column2: 若你依循阿芙羅黛蒂的指示，聖杯必將歸你所有。

column1: You must unravel Aphrodite's words for yourself.
column2: 阿芙羅黛蒂所言，你須自行解開。

column1: You should know Aphrodite's sacred number by now.
column2: 此刻你應已知曉阿芙羅黛蒂的聖數。

column1: Not even I know such secrets, though certainly the Sacred Cup was one of them.
column2: 這等秘密，連我也無從得知，不過那只聖杯，確實是其中之一。

column1: I see no thief. Perhaps your experience with the thief in the bazaar still preys upon your mind.
column2: 我未見有竊賊。或許你在市集遭遇竊賊的那段經歷，仍縈繞在你心頭。

column1: You vanquished him, as you must surely remember.
column2: 你已將他擊敗，這你想必還記得。

column1: He looks to be a formidable opponent. And he is no ordinary mortal, but a mystic guardian. Defeating him will require strategy and wits more than brute strength.
column2: 他看來是個強悍的對手。而且他並非尋常凡人，而是一名神秘的守護者。要擊敗他，靠的與其說是蠻力，不如說是謀略與機智。

column1: There is no Saracen here.
column2: 此處並無撒拉遜武士。

column1: It has no further use for the moment.
column2: 此刻它已無其他用處。

column1: Nay, keep it. It is a valuable talisman.
column2: 不可，留著它。這是件珍貴的護符。

column1: Only you can do that. As for when and how, your own wits must guide you.
column2: 唯有你能辦到此事。至於何時、如何，你須靠自己的機智判斷。

column1: I suspect that when the time comes, it will be the Goddess who does the talking, not you.
column2: 我猜想，等時機來臨，開口說話的會是女神，而非你。

column1: She does not answer. I cannot imagine why she would.
column2: 她並未回應。我實在想不出她有何理由要回應。

column1: Aye, that IS the purpose of your mission.
column2: 正是，那正是你此行的目的。

column1: If you dredge your feeble memory, you may recall that you have killed him.
column2: 你若翻找一下自己薄弱的記憶，或許能想起你已殺了他。

column1: Ahem. Arthur, there is no Saracen here.
column2: 咳。亞瑟，此處並無撒拉遜武士。

column1: She would have no interest in mortal trinkets.
column2: 她對凡人的小玩意兒不會有興趣。

column1: See?  Now you have gone and lost your head.  But I am sure the mukhtar's men will find a use for it--to adorn a spike, no doubt.
column2: 瞧見了吧？現在你已然掉了腦袋。不過我敢說，村長的手下必會替它找個用處——想必是拿去插在尖樁上示眾。

column1: Excellent!  Let us waste no time!  Follow me.
column2: 好極了！咱們別浪費時間了！跟我來。

column1: I knew you must come this way, and see, I have gotten here before you and waited.
column2: 我早知你必會經此路而來，你瞧，我已搶先一步到此等候。

column1: You will never survive this desert without my help.  Hire me and I will be your guide.
column2: 少了我相助，你絕無可能在這片沙漠中活下來。雇用我，我便為你引路。

column1: I thank you, habib.  You need not pay me until we reach Jerusalem.
column2: 多謝了，朋友。你不必現在付錢，等我們抵達耶路撒冷再說即可。

column1: But I take it that your intent is to hire me as your guide.
column2: 但我料想，你的意思是要雇我作你的嚮導。

column1: It is a hard climb.  Rest here, if you like.  I shall wait for you just ahead.
column2: 這一段路難行得很。你若想歇息，就在這裡歇著吧，我會在前方等你。

column1: Jabir liked not the sound of your steel being drawn.
column2: 賈比耳不喜歡聽見你拔劍出鞘的聲音。

column1: The buildings rise all around you to a narrow band of sky overhead.
column2: 四周的建築聳立而起，頭頂只剩一線狹窄的天空。

column1: You trod upon hard-packed earth as firm as stone.
column2: 你腳下踩著的，是堅硬如石的夯土地面。

column1: I doubt you will see the Goddess in this alley.
column2: 我不認為你會在這條巷子裡見到女神。

column1: I cannot tell if these buildings are empty or occupied, but they seem deliberately built to prevent anyone from entering or even seeing the Temple.
column2: 我看不出這些建築是空置還是有人居住，但它們似乎是刻意建來阻擋任何人進入，甚至望見神殿的。

column1: Merely common weeds, of no consequence.
column2: 不過是些尋常雜草，無關緊要。

column1: The Goddess said to use it after you had proven yourself by sword and shield.
column2: 女神曾說，待你以劍與盾證明自己之後，再使用它。

column1: These are brick walls covered with plaster.
column2: 這是幾面覆著灰泥的磚牆。

column1: There is none.
column2: 並無此物。

column1: Ahem, there is no-one in this alley but you, Arthur.
column2: 咳，這條巷子裡除了你，亞瑟，再無他人。

column1: Who? There is no-one else here.
column2: 誰？此處並無旁人。

column1: It does nothing here.
column2: 在此處它毫無作用。

column1: It would be a waste of time, even if you had the means.
column2: 就算你有辦法，那也只是白費工夫。

column1: I am not here to answer questions, infidel. To win the Grail, you must do battle with me. Draw your sword!
column2: 異教徒，我不是來此回答問題的。若要贏得聖杯，你必須與我一戰。拔劍吧！

column1: This Saracen is clearly an honorable foe, to offer you this helmet. Accept it or not, according to your own common sense.
column2: 這名撒拉遜武士顯然是位重榮譽的對手，竟願意將這頂頭盔讓給你。收下與否，憑你自己的判斷。

column1: You cannot fight the saracen from here.
column2: 你無法從這裡與撒拉遜武士交手。

column1: Infidel, you must defeat me if you would win the Grail. Here, in this Temple of Aphrodite, we must match sword and shield, strength and skill, until one of us is dead.
column2: 異教徒，若你要贏得聖杯，就必須擊敗我。就在此地，這座阿芙羅黛蒂神殿之中，我們須以劍盾相搏、以力與技相較，直至一方倒下為止。

column1: But I wish for an equal fight and you do not have a helmet. Therefore, I offer you one that is a strong as my own. Wear it or not, as you please.
column2: 但我盼望一場勢均力敵的較量，而你並無頭盔。因此，我願獻上一頂與我自己的一樣堅固的頭盔。戴與不戴，任憑你意。

column1: Face me, coward! We must fight until one of us lies dead upon these sacred stones.
column2: 懦夫，來面對我！我們須戰至一方倒臥在這片聖石之上為止。

column1: With your brain sliced in twain, I am sure you are having second thoughts about not taking the helmet offered to you by the Saracen.
column2: 腦袋被劈成兩半之際，我敢說你此刻定是後悔，當初未收下撒拉遜武士所贈的那頂頭盔。

column1: Interesting tactic, letting your opponent kill you without the least resistance. Not terribly effective for you, however.
column2: 有意思的戰術——毫無抵抗地任由對手殺死你。只是，對你而言，成效實在不怎麼樣。

column1: You cannot reach the helmet from here.
column2: 你從這裡構不著那頂頭盔。
