column1: Where you stand, once my priestesses stood. My name was spoken with reverence. My statue and holy of holies were housed within, where only that bare pedestal remains.
column2: 你如今立足之處，昔日曾是我的女祭司們所站之地。我的名字曾被人以敬畏之心提起。我的神像與至聖之所，便供奉在這殿內——如今僅餘那座空蕩蕩的基座。

column1: The last thing my worshippers would see as they left my temple was this leftward spiral upon the threshold, reminder of life turning ever onwards.
column2: 我的信徒離開神殿時，最後所見的，便是門檻上這個向左旋的螺形紋飾，提醒著生命恆常向前流轉。

column1: As with life, so too does power pass onward. Even gods and goddesses fall prey to the endless cycle. My reign here is ended. I shall never return.
column2: 如同生命一般，權柄也終將流轉而去。就連神祇，也逃不過這無盡的循環。我在此地的統治已然終結，我不會再回來了。

column1: You have won the Sacred Cup by your determination and persistence, by cleverness and skill of arms. I surrender it to you.
column2: 你憑著自身的決心與堅持、機智與武藝，贏得了這只聖杯。我將它交予你。

column1: But beware, the power of the Grail itself will pass final judgment upon your worthiness to possess it.
column2: 但你須當心，聖杯本身的力量，終將對你是否配得擁有它，做出最終的裁決。

column1: Start where you should start, turn as you should turn and count the places of the pillars until you reach my sacred number. Beneath that pillar you shall find what you seek.
column2: 自你該起始之處起始，依你該轉的方向而轉，數過各根柱子的位置，直至你數到我的聖數。在那根柱子之下，你便將尋得你所求之物。

column1: I HATE to be ignored! And by a mortal! It is too great an insult to bear!
column2: 我最痛恨被人漠視！竟還是被一介凡人如此對待！這份侮辱，實在難以承受！

column1: Hell hath no fury like a Goddess peeved.
column2: 地獄的怒火，也比不過一位被激怒的女神。

column1: I warn you, mortal, do NOT keep me waiting!.
column2: 我警告你，凡人，休得讓我久候！

column1: Aye, it moves!
column2: 正是，它動了！

column1: You have found it! You have found the Grail!
column2: 你找到了！你找到聖杯了！

column1: One hand barely touches the sacred cup through a tiny gap in the white cloth that covers it. The Grail's power pours through you and restores you instantly to perfect health!
column2: 你的一隻手，隔著覆蓋其上的白布一道細縫，堪堪觸及了那只聖杯。聖杯的力量霎時貫穿你全身，將你的身體瞬間恢復至完美的康健！

column1: You are dazed with the Grail's power, but you must recover yourself and find a way out of here. Camelot must be saved before--
column2: 聖杯的力量令你暈眩不已，但你必須打起精神，設法從此地脫身。肯萊特必須在……之前得救——

column1: The Thief has struck again! Stop him!
column2: 那名竊賊再度出手了！快阻止他！

column1: Alas! The Grail has judged you and found you unworthy. Too great was the burden of sin upon your soul.
column2: 哀哉！聖杯已對你做出裁決，判定你不配擁有它。你靈魂所背負的罪孽，太過沉重了。

column1: You let Gawaine die an ignoble death in the Forest Perilous.
column2: 你讓高文死於派瑞樂斯森林，落得一個不光彩的下場。

column1: You sacrificed Launcelot to the curse of your jealousy.
column2: 你因一己妒念的詛咒，犧牲了蘭斯洛特。

column1: You did nothing to save the noble Galahad within the catacombs.
column2: 你未曾伸出援手，任由高尚的葛拉漢死在地下墓窖之中。

column1: And so you, your kingdom, and all your poor people perish for lack of a king with moral strength. We end not in glory, but with the bitter taste of ashes and dust and black defeat.
column2: 於是你、你的王國，以及所有可憐的子民，都因缺了一位有德行的君王而滅亡。我們的旅程並非終於榮耀，而是終於灰燼、塵土與黑暗敗亡的苦澀滋味。

column1: Your mule has had the sense to run away from the cobras.
column2: 你的騾子倒有幾分見識，懂得躲開眼鏡蛇逃走。

column1: If that is truly your wish, that is what you shall have of me.
column2: 若這確實是你的心願，我便如你所願。

column1: Alas! You are helpless, completely under Fatima's fatal spell. And here is the reward for your weakness, being strangled to death by Fatima.
column2: 唉！你已無力反抗，全然受制於法提瑪的致命咒法。而你軟弱的下場，便是被法提瑪活活勒死。

column1: How will I ever explain this to the queen? Tsk- tsk.
column2: 我該如何向王后解釋這一切？嘖，嘖。

column1: By giving this purse, you show further proof that you are free of the need to gain material wealth. You grow more and more worthy in my eyes.
column2: 交出這個錢囊，更加證明你已超脫對財富的貪求。在我眼中，你愈發顯得堪當此任。

column1: The Test awaits behind this door. Six tablets, each engraved with a symbol of a Goddess, rest next to a stone plaque with six niches.
column2: 考驗就在這扇門後等著你。六塊石板，各刻著一位女神的標識，靜置於一塊有六個凹龕的石匾旁。

column1: Six questions I will pose. You must know to which Goddess the question belongs and place her symbol into the proper niche.
column2: 我將提出六個問題。你必須辨明每個問題屬於哪位女神，並將她的標識放入正確的凹龕。

column1: When all six symbols have been placed, I will tell you whether you have passed or failed. If you fail, you may try again.
column2: 待六個標識全數安放，我便會告訴你成敗。若是失敗，你可以再試一次。

column1: But there is one more thing I require of you, a gesture to show that you are not bound by material possessions. Give me your purse.
column2: 但我還要求你做一件事——以此表明你不受身外之物所束縛。把你的錢囊交給我。

column1: The door is opened. The Test awaits you.
column2: 門開了。考驗正等著你。

column1: Arthur?  Arthur.
column2: 亞瑟？亞瑟。

column1: Arthur, WAKE UP!
column2: 亞瑟，醒醒！

column1: You slept through the entire docking and unloading of the ship.  You indulged too heavily in foreign wine.
column2: 你把整段靠港卸貨的過程都睡過去了。你貪杯，喝了太多異國美酒。

column1: If your head is pounding, blame no one but yourself.
column2: 若你頭痛欲裂，也怪不得別人，只能怪你自己。

column1: Sir, I am Hazm.  My master sends his respects and invites you to accept his hospitality.  My Master--
column2: 大人，小的是哈慈。我家主人向您致意，邀您接受他的款待。我家主人——

column1: Ignore this boy.  You are lucky he did not make off with your mule.  I am Jabir ibn Hamid.  I overheard some sailors say you need a guide through the desert to Jerusalem.
column2: 別理這孩子。算你走運，他沒把你的騾子順手牽走。我是賈比耳·伊本·哈米德。我聽幾個水手說，你需要一位嚮導，帶你穿越沙漠前往耶路撒冷。

column1: Please, sir, my Master is Al-Sirat and he is very wise and he asks--
column2: 大人，求求您，我家主人是 Al-Sirat，他非常睿智，他想問——

column1: Al-Sirat is an impoverished old scholar of no use to anyone.  But I, Jabir, know the desert, every rock, wadi, and waterhole.  Trust me in all things.
column2: Al-Sirat 不過是個窮困潦倒、百無一用的老學究。但我，賈比耳，熟知這片沙漠的一草一木——每塊岩石、每條旱谷、每處水潭。凡事都信任我便是。

column1: Sir, I beg you to accept my Master's hospitality.  He heard of you from the Captain of the ship and he sends warning that the mukhtar of Gaza--
column2: 大人，求您接受我家主人的款待。他從船長那裡聽聞您的事，特地遣人示警，說加薩的村長——

column1: Allow ME to explain.  The mukhtar is the man who governs this port.  He hates all foreigners and if he catches you here, he will throw you in prison.  We should leave at once.
column2: 讓「我」來解釋吧。村長是治理這座港口的人。他痛恨一切外邦人，若被他逮到你在此，會把你關進大牢。我們該立刻離開。

column1: I can take you to my Master by secret ways and Al-Sirat will protect and tell you--
column2: 我能帶您走密道去見我家主人，Al-Sirat 會保護您，並告訴您——

column1: Get out of here, boy! We men have business together and have no need of chattering pests.  Be off!
column2: 滾開，臭小子！我們大人有正事要談，用不著你這種嘮叨的討厭鬼。走開！

column1: Stranger, you will never survive the desert without my help.  I ask for no payment now.  When we reach Jerusalem safely, I will accept a fair payment.
column2: 陌生人，沒有我的幫助，你絕不可能在這片沙漠中活下來。我現在分文不取，待我們平安抵達耶路撒冷，再收一份公道的酬勞。

column1: Hire me and I shall guide you to Jerusalem at once.
column2: 雇用我，我立刻帶你前往耶路撒冷。

column1: Sir, I beg you, ask to see my Master and all will be well.
column2: 大人，求求您，去見見我家主人吧，一切自會安好。

column1: May I advise caution here? Do not rush to use the elixir until it seems absolutely necessary.
column2: 容我在此進一言：切莫急著用掉解藥，除非確有絕對必要。

column1: Aye, do what you will with it. Though it will cure the poison, it will never cleanse you of the crime of noble Galahad's death.
column2: 正是，這藥你便隨意處置吧。它雖能解毒，卻永遠洗刷不了高尚的葛拉漢因你而死這樁罪過。

column1: The miraculous elixir burns like fire through your veins as it purges you of the poison. You are entirely cured....as long as you are not bitten again.
column2: 這神奇的解藥在你血脈中如火燒灼，將毒素滌盡。你已痊癒……只要別再被咬一次。

column1: The apple's potent spell has relieved your hunger and thirst and given you a new surge of strength.
column2: 蘋果那股強效的魔力，解去了你的飢渴，也為你注入一股新生的力量。

column1: But alas, it cannot stop the poison of the rat's bite from killing you, it can only delay the final end.
column2: 但可惜，它擋不住老鼠咬傷的毒性致你於死地，只能延緩那最終的結局。

column1: Alas, the rat's poison has taken its toll and the cold hand of Death has closed upon you forever.
column2: 唉，老鼠的毒液終究奪去了你的性命，死神冰冷的手，永遠攫住了你。

column1: Your horse has no desire to swim in the harbour.
column2: 你的坐騎毫無興致在港灣裡游泳。

column1: Your armour and steel drags you to the bottom and there you will lie until you are rotten, soggy and pulpy and truly forgotten.
column2: 你的盔甲與鋼鐵把你拖向海底，你將長眠於此，直至腐朽、泡爛、化為爛泥，徹底被人遺忘。

column1: As fortune would have it, this ship is the very one you need.  Ignore the Greek name.  It was sold by a Greek trader and the new owner has yet to paint in the new name.
column2: 幸運的是，這艘船正是你所需要的那艘。別在意那個希臘船名，它是一個希臘商人賣出的，新船主還沒來得及漆上新名字。

column1: May your journey be safe and swift, god willing.  You may board now.
column2: 願神保佑你此行平安順遂。你現在可以上船了。

column1: Well, at last you have learned to take my advice.
column2: 好，你總算學會聽我的勸告了。

column1: You cannot do that from here.
column2: 你在此處無法這麼做。

column1: Nothing remains of the pillar here but the indentation where its base once rested.
column2: 這根石柱如今只剩下柱基原本所在的凹痕，別無他物。

column1: This pillar did not move. Pause and think before your next choice.
column2: 這根石柱紋風不動。下一步之前，先停下來想清楚。

column1: The pillar did not move. I hope you do not intend to waste more of your valuable energy in such pointless exercise.
column2: 石柱依然不動。希望你不打算再把寶貴的力氣，浪費在這種徒勞之舉上。

column1: There is no where to go from here. High walls without windows or doors bar the way.
column2: 從這裡無路可去。高牆聳立，既無窗也無門，擋住了去路。

column1: Truly you are a hardy man to have come so far.  But you need water!   Waste no time.  Follow me at once.
column2: 你確實是個堅毅之人，才能走到這一步。但你需要水！別再耽擱，立刻跟我來。

column1: You have killed the Saracen in a fair fight, and now his soul transforms into a dove and rises into the sky and vanishes from sight.
column2: 你在公平的決鬥中殺死了撒拉遜武士，此刻他的靈魂化作一隻鴿子，直上雲霄，消失在天際。

column1: You would not enjoy that.  These rocks are hot enough to toast nuts.
column2: 你不會喜歡這麼做的。這些岩石燙得足以烤熟堅果。

column1: The ground is rocky and as hot as the furnaces of Hades.
column2: 地面遍佈岩石，炙熱得如同冥府的熔爐。

column1: Hot as it is, you are better off wearing it than carrying it, and you must not even consider leaving it behind.
column2: 儘管炙熱難耐，穿著它總比扛著它好，你更不該考慮把它丟下。

column1: In this heat, such a burden would soon kill her.
column2: 在這種酷熱之下，這樣的負擔很快就會要了她的命。

column1: You sold the mule, Arthur.
column2: 亞瑟，你已經把騾子賣了。

column1: The mule is not here.
column2: 騾子不在此處。

column1: You have no waterskin, sad to say.
column2: 說來遺憾，你身上沒有水袋。

column1: First you must find one.
column2: 你得先找到一個才行。

column1: There is no snake here.
column2: 此處並無蛇蹤。

column1: The last thing you need to carry is a rock hot enough to burn your fingers.
column2: 你最不需要的，就是帶著一塊燙得能灼傷手指的石頭。

column1: It would be a staggering waste of energy, even if it were possible, but these cliffs are steep and offer no grip for hand or foot.
column2: 就算辦得到，也是白白浪費驚人的力氣，何況這些懸崖陡峭，手腳都無處可攀。

column1: It is a terrible shame that Gaza was closed to you, or you might have obtained a waterskin there.
column2: 加薩對你緊閉城門，實在可惜，否則你或許能在那裡弄到一個水袋。

column1: Now???
column2: 現在？？？

column1: We are here, habib, at the water.
column2: 我們到了，朋友，這裡就是水源。

column1: We are on our way to water now, habib.
column2: 我們現在正往水源去，朋友。

column1: You waste precious breath talking to the air.
column2: 你對著空氣說話，白白浪費寶貴的力氣。

column1: Rather redundant, Arthur, since he is dead.
column2: 亞瑟，這話說了也是多餘，他已經死了。

column1: The heat must be affecting your brain.  There is no sign of Jabir.
column2: 這暑熱想必是影響了你的腦子。此處毫無賈比耳的蹤跡。

column1: You would find only barren ground.
column2: 你只會找到一片荒蕪的地面。

column1: It broke under the ferocity of your assault and is of no use whatsoever.
column2: 它在你猛烈的攻擊下碎裂，如今毫無用處。

column1: You can hardly do that from here.
column2: 你在此處幾乎無法這麼做。

column1: The heat has affected your thinking, I perceive.
column2: 依我看，這酷熱已經影響了你的思緒。

column1: Aye, an excellent idea, provided you can find some.
column2: 正是，這主意再好不過了，前提是你得先找得到。

column1: You must return to Jerusalem at once and finish your dealings with Fatima.
column2: 你必須立刻返回耶路撒冷，把與法提瑪之間的事了結。

column1: I can give you little more than encouragement and observation where this desert is concerned.
column2: 說到這片沙漠，我能給你的，不過是幾句鼓勵與觀察罷了。

column1: This is a desert of extreme terrain.  Sudden cliffs rise and block your way, while wadis unexpectedly appear in the ground.
column2: 這是一片地形險惡的沙漠。峭壁驟然聳起擋住去路，旱谷也會在地面上不經意地冒出來。

column1: She is well.  She prays daily for your safety and ministers to Launcelot as he recovers from the Ice Maiden's spell.
column2: 她安好。她日日為你的平安祈禱，並照料著蘭斯洛特，他正從冰霜仙子的咒法中康復。

column1: She prays daily for your well-being and success, and for the safe return of Launcelot.
column2: 她日日祈禱你平安順遂、大功告成，也祈禱蘭斯洛特平安歸來。

column1: With the tender help of Gwenhyver and her ladies, he is recovering very well from his frozen sojourn.
column2: 有昆海兒與她的侍女悉心照料，他從那段冰封的遭遇中恢復得相當好。

column1: Alas, you have not saved Launcelot.  Thus you have jeopardized the success of your entire mission.
column2: 唉，你未能救回蘭斯洛特。如此一來，你已使整趟使命的成敗陷入危殆。

column1: I hope you remember the way back to Jerusalem.  It would not do to get lost now.
column2: 希望你還記得回耶路撒冷的路。事到如今，可不能迷路。

column1: There is no sign of Jerusalem yet.
column2: 目前還看不見耶路撒冷的蹤影。

column1: You should avoid the huge, flat areas of desert plateau, unless you have reason to think there is water there.
column2: 你該避開那片廣袤平坦的沙漠台地，除非你有理由相信那裡有水。

column1: There are some hills in the distance, and the ground rises steadily toward the north and east.
column2: 遠處有幾座丘陵，地勢朝北方與東方緩緩升高。

column1: There is no snake here, fortunately, for the cobras of this desert are quite lethal.
column2: 幸好此處並無蛇蹤，這片沙漠裡的眼鏡蛇可是相當致命。

column1: The lizards in this area are swift and harmless.
column2: 這一帶的蜥蜴行動敏捷，但無害。

column1: That is not important now.  You must get back to Jerusalem.
column2: 這事眼下並不要緊。你必須回到耶路撒冷去。

column1: I have no knowledge of where water may be hidden in a wadi or oasis.  You must search.
column2: 旱谷或綠洲裡的水究竟藏在何處，我毫無所知。你得自己找。

column1: Well, you know where the Pool of Siloam is.
column2: 好吧，你知道西羅亞池在哪裡。

column1: I cannot help you find water.  I have no such intimate knowledge of this desert.
column2: 我幫不了你找水，我對這片沙漠沒有那樣深入的了解。

column1: Let us hope you remember the way well enough.
column2: 但願你把路記得夠清楚。

column1: There is no hint of where to go in this trackless desert.
column2: 在這片無跡可循的沙漠裡，看不出該往哪裡走。

column1: Even the shadows provide little relief from the heat.
column2: 就連陰影也難以緩解這股酷熱。

column1: The shifting sands erase any traces of where you have been.
column2: 流動的沙丘抹去了你曾經走過的一切痕跡。

column1: You have most prudently slain him.
column2: 你極為明智地殺了他。

column1: Jabir waits for you to follow him.
column2: 賈比耳等著你跟上他。

column1: There is no apparent sign of him, but that means little with such a cunning desert dweller.
column2: 表面上不見他的蹤影，但面對這樣狡猾的沙漠住民，這說明不了什麼。

column1: Your brain invents delusions from lack of water and the intense heat.  Do not dwell upon it.
column2: 缺水與酷暑，讓你的腦子憑空生出幻象。別放在心上。

column1: A mirage is usually an illusion of water, a bizarre phenomenon of the deserts.
column2: 海市蜃樓通常是水的幻象，是沙漠裡一種奇特的現象。

column1: Copper or tin!  Copper or tin! Copper or tin for Widdershins! I am no troll but that is my toll! Copper or tin for Widdershins! Give me my way or a trick I will play!
column2: 銅幣或錫幣！銅幣或錫幣！銅幣或錫幣，敬獻 Widdershins！我不是山怪，這是我的買路錢！銅幣或錫幣，敬獻 Widdershins！依我便罷，不然就讓你嚐嚐我的把戲！

column1: Copper or tin!  Copper or tin! Copper or tin for Widdershins! I am no troll but that is my toll! Copper or tin for Widdershins!
column2: 銅幣或錫幣！銅幣或錫幣！銅幣或錫幣，敬獻 Widdershins！我不是山怪，這是我的買路錢！銅幣或錫幣，敬獻 Widdershins！

column1: The trick has been played and I fear the sprite's bolt of mischief was aimed squarely at your purse.
column2: 詭計已然使出，恐怕這妖精那道搗蛋的咒力，正好衝著你的錢囊而來。

column1: You were thrown back by a sorcerous barrier of great power. Yet there must be a way to pass it.
column2: 你被一道法力強大的魔障彈了回來。但想必總有通過它的辦法。

column1: I suspect these five stones are a part of the riddle you must solve to breach the barrier.
column2: 我懷疑，這五塊石頭正是你破解那道魔障必須解開的謎題的一部分。

column1: Eh, what is this? Why are you--ah, what a wonderful smell these herbs have! How very potent and aromatic! I shall hang them up at once.
column2: 咦，這是什麼？你怎麼——啊，這些藥草的香氣真是絕妙！好濃郁、好芬芳！我這就把它們掛起來。

column1: What, are you a merchant, too? What do I want with herbs? Ah, but they do smell good. In fact, they are so strongly aromatic, they might help disguise the smell of my fish.
column2: 什麼，你也是個商人？我要藥草做什麼？啊，不過它們聞起來確實不錯。說真的，香氣這麼濃郁，說不定還能蓋過我這些魚的氣味。

column1: Very well, I will take them. Here are 2 fals, all I can afford. I am a poor man.
column2: 好吧，我收下了。這是兩枚銅幣，我只出得起這些了。我是個窮人。

column1: You have taught me something, habibi. Rather than dwelling only upon my problems, had I but sought a solution, I would have been a happier man.
column2: 你教會了我一件事，朋友。與其一味沉溺於自己的難題，倒不如尋求解方，那樣我早該活得更快樂。

column1: I thank you for this piece of wisdom, which will benefit my neighbors as well as myself. Sa'alam aleikem.
column2: 感謝你賜下這番智慧之言，這對我的鄰人與我自己都有益處。Sa'alam aleikem。

column1: You cannot go this way.  There is a thief loose in the bazaar and many merchants are complaining.  The Jaffa Gate will be locked while we search for him.
column2: 你不能走這條路。市集裡出了個賊，許多商人都在抱怨。賈法城門將封閉，直到我們找到他為止。

column1: We do not know who he is, but when we find him, he is a dead man.  Now move along, before we begin to suspect that YOU may be the thief.
column2: 我們還不知道他是誰，但一旦找到，他就是個死人。現在快走開，免得我們開始懷疑「你」就是那個賊。

column1: You may enter, stranger, but you may not leave until we have finished searching the city for thieves.
column2: 陌生人，你可以進去，但在我們搜遍全城捉賊之前，你不得離開。

column1: Aye, and if you are a thief, you will wish you had never come here.
column2: 正是，你若是賊，必會後悔自己踏進這裡。

column1: No, Arthur, no!
column2: 不，亞瑟，不要！

column1: Alas! You are helpless, completely under Fatima's fatal spell. And here is the reward for your weakness, being smothered to death by a perfumed pillow.
column2: 唉！你已無力反抗，全然受制於法提瑪的致命咒法。而你軟弱的下場，便是被一只薰香的枕頭活活悶死。

column1: Gladly will I sell you relic. But first you must tell me -- what is the name of the saint whose relic you wish to buy?
column2: 我很樂意賣你聖物。但你得先告訴我——你想買的是哪位聖徒的聖物？

column1: Saint %s! Yes, I do have a relic of Saint %s. Normally, 3 dinar, on sale today for 2 dinars. But I like you. You have an honest face. So for you, only 1 dinar!
column2: 聖%s！沒錯，我這裡確實有聖%s的聖物。原價三枚金幣，今日特價兩枚金幣。不過我喜歡你，你長了一張老實臉，所以就便宜賣你，只要一枚金幣！

column1: No, no. I must have the name of the saint whose relic you wish to buy. Nothing else will do. Think it over. If you are still interested in buying a relic, just say so.
column2: 不，不對。我必須知道你想買的聖物是哪位聖徒的。別的都不算數。你好好想想，若還想買聖物，儘管開口。

column1: Greetings, King Arthur.
column2: 亞瑟王，向您致意。

column1: That was quick m'lord.
column2: 好快啊，吾王。

column1: Well we meet again, m'lord.  Alas, you have not recovered your mule, I see.
column2: 咱們又見面了，吾王。唉，看來你還沒找回你的騾子。

column1: M'lord, your mule has bolted!
column2: 吾王，您的騾子脫韁跑了！

column1: How colourful!
column2: 好個生動的用詞！

column1: I am sure you never learned such language from me.
column2: 我確信這種言語，你絕非跟我學的。

column1: It would seem that being a king does not guarantee gentility.
column2: 看來身為國王，未必就保證了溫文儒雅。

column1: May your mouth rot and your tongue wither.
column2: 願你嘴巴腐爛，舌頭枯萎。

column1: No wonder Gwenhyver prefers Launcelot, from whose refined lips such words were never spoken.
column2: 難怪昆海兒偏愛蘭斯洛特，他那雙優雅的嘴唇，從不曾吐出這種話。

column1: You are speaking gibberish.
column2: 你說的是無意義的胡言亂語。

column1: This must be some strange foreign tongue.
column2: 這想必是某種陌生的異邦語言。

column1: There are times when even I, Merlin, am without an answer.
column2: 即便是我，梅林，也有無言以對的時候。

column1: Your words are clear enough, but your meaning eludes me.
column2: 你的話語清楚明白，但你的用意，我卻捉摸不透。

column1: I feel I should know what you want, but your purpose is not clear.
column2: 我覺得自己該明白你想要什麼，但你的意圖並不清晰。

column1: You don't see anything particularly interesting.
column2: 你沒看見什麼特別有趣的東西。

column1: You look, but it doesn't hold your interest.
column2: 你看了看，卻提不起興致。

column1: This is no time for idle chatter.
column2: 此刻不是閒聊的時候。

column1: I am not in the mood for small talk.
column2: 我沒有心情閒話家常。

column1: If I have something to say, I will say it.
column2: 我若有話要說，自會開口。

column1: That is not the proper invocation.
column2: 那並非正確的咒語。

column1: I would not advise that.
column2: 我不建議如此。

column1: That is not wise.
column2: 此舉並不明智。

column1: That would be most foolish.
column2: 此舉實屬愚昧。

column1: Even a king should not throw money away frivolously.
column2: 即便貴為國王，也不該任意揮霍金錢。

column1: You know what they say about a fool and his money.
column2: 俗話說得好：愚人與錢財，總是易散難聚。

column1: I have nothing to tell you now.
column2: 我此刻無話可說。

column1: Your purse is as empty as a fool's mind.
column2: 你的錢囊，空得如同愚人的腦袋。

column1: Your purse is as empty as a maiden's womb.
column2: 你的錢囊，空得如同少女的腹中。

column1: It is dark and dreary in your purse, rather like a miser's curse.
column2: 你的錢囊裡陰暗淒涼，恰似守財奴的詛咒。

column1: Your purse is as empty as an abbot's heart.
column2: 你的錢囊，空得如同修道院長那顆冷淡的心。

column1: Your purse holds naught. Which is a naughty state of affairs for a king.
column2: 你的錢囊分文不剩，這般寒酸光景，對一位國王來說實在不成體統。

column1: Your purse is as empty as the devil's conscience. And that is very empty indeed.
column2: 你的錢囊，空得如同魔鬼的良心——那可是空得徹底。

column1: There is nothing here to fight.
column2: 此處無物可戰。

column1: A wise warrior knows when it is time to fight and when it is not.
column2: 智勇的戰士，懂得何時該戰、何時該忍。

column1: Save your readiness for a time when danger is upon you.
column2: 留著你的戒備，待危險當前之時再用。

column1: Three lives have I. Gentle enough to soothe the skin, Light enough to caress the sky, Hard enough to crack rocks.      What am I?
column2: 我有三種樣貌：溫柔時能撫平肌膚，輕盈時能拂過長空，堅硬時能裂開頑石。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「water」）

column1: Lighter than what I am made of, More of me is hidden Than is seen.      What am I?
column2: 我比造就我的東西更輕盈，藏於水下的我，遠比露出水面的我更多。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「iceberg」）

column1: When I am filled I can point the way, When I am empty Nothing moves me, I have two skins One without and one within.      What am I?
column2: 填滿之時，我能為你指路；空空之時，任誰也無法驅動我；我有兩層皮——一層在外，一層在內。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「gloves」）

column1: If a man carried my burden He would break his back. I am not rich, But leave silver in my track.      What am I?
column2: 若讓一個人扛起我的重擔，他的脊背定會斷裂；我並不富有，行過之處卻總留下一道銀痕。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「snail」）

column1: My life can be measured in hours, I serve by being devoured. Thin, I am quick Fat, I am slow Wind is my foe.      What am I?
column2: 我的一生以時辰計量，我在被吞噬中盡我職責；瘦時，我燃得快；胖時，我燃得慢；風，是我的天敵。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「candle」）

column1: To unravel me You need a simple key, No key that was made By locksmith's hand, But a key that only I Will understand.      What am I?
column2: 要解開我，你需要一把鑰匙；那並非鎖匠打造的鑰匙，而是唯獨我才懂的那一把。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「riddle」）

column1: Weight in my belly, Trees on my back, Nails in my ribs, Feet I do lack.      What am I?
column2: 腹中裝載重物，背上立著樹木，肋骨間釘著鐵釘，卻沒有一雙腳。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「ship」）

column1: If you break me I do not stop working, If you touch me I may be snared, If you lose me Nothing will matter.      What am I?
column2: 縱使破碎，我仍不停跳動；輕觸於我，我便可能為之淪陷；失去了我，世間再無一物要緊。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「heart」）

column1: I turn around once, What is out will not get in. I turn around again, What is in will not get out      What am I?
column2: 我轉動一次，門外之物便進不來；我再轉動一次，門內之物便出不去。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「key」）

column1: I am only useful When I am full, Yet I am always Full of holes.      What am I?
column2: 唯有滿載之時，我才派得上用場，但我渾身上下，卻始終佈滿了孔洞。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「net」）

column1: You can see nothing else When you look in my face, I will look you in the eye And I will never lie.      What am I?
column2: 望進我的臉龐，你便再看不見其他事物；我會直視你的雙眼，且從不欺瞞。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「mirror」）

column1: I drive men mad For love of me, Easily beaten, Never free.      What am I?
column2: 世人為愛我而癡狂，我輕易便能被錘打成形，卻永遠不得自由。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「gold」）

column1: Glittering points That downward thrust, Sparkling spears That never rust.      What am I?
column2: 閃爍的尖端向下垂刺，晶亮的長矛永不生鏽。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「icicle」）

column1: When set loose I fly away, Never so cursed As when I go astray.      What am I?
column2: 一旦脫手，我便振翅飛去；一旦偏離了目標，便再沒有比那更該受詛咒的了。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「arrow」）

column1: When young, I am sweet in the sun. When middle-aged, I make you gay. When old, I am valued more than ever.      What am I?
column2: 年輕之時，我在陽光下香甜可口；到了中年，我能令你歡欣暢懷；待到年邁，世人卻對我愈發珍視。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「wine」）

column1: I am always hungry, I must always be fed, The finger I lick Will soon turn red.      What am I?
column2: 我永遠飢餓，總須被人餵養；被我舔過的手指，很快便會泛紅。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「fire」）

column1: Each morning I appear To lie at your feet, All day I follow No matter how fast you run, Yet I nearly perish In the midday sun.      What am I?
column2: 每日清晨，我伏於你的腳邊現身；終日跟隨，任你跑得多快也甩不開我；然而正午豔陽下，我卻幾近消散。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「shadow」）

column1: Bright as diamonds, Loud as thunder, Never still, A thing of wonder.      What am I?
column2: 亮如鑽石，響若雷鳴，從不靜止，是造化的奇景一樁。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「waterfall」）

column1: You heard me before, Yet you hear me again, Then I die, 'Til you call me again.      What am I?
column2: 你曾聽過我的聲音，如今又再度聽見；隨後我便消逝，直到你再次呼喚我。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「echo」）

column1: Lovely and round, I shine with pale light, grown in the darkness, A lady's delight.      What am I?
column2: 美麗而渾圓，我泛著蒼白微光，於幽暗中孕育而成，是淑女鍾愛的珍寶。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「pearl」）

column1: Until I am measured I am not known, Yet how you miss me When I have flown.      What am I?
column2: 在被量度之前，無人識得我；然而一旦我飛逝而去，你才驚覺自己多麼想念我。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「time」）

column1: All about, but cannot be seen, Can be captured, cannot be held, No throat, but can be heard.      What am I?
column2: 我無處不在，卻無形無跡；能被捕捉，卻無法握住；沒有喉嚨，卻能被聽見。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「wind」）

column1: I am seen in the water If seen in the sky, I am in the rainbow, A jay's feather, And lapis lazuli.      What am I?
column2: 若我現於天際，也會映在水中；我存在於彩虹裡、松鴉的羽翼上，也存在於青金石中。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「blue」）

column1: I go around in circles But always straight ahead, Never complain No matter where I am led.      What am I?
column2: 我不斷繞著圈子打轉，卻始終一路向前；無論被引往何方，我從不埋怨。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「wheel」）

column1: At the sound of me, men may dream Or stamp their feet At the sound of me, women may laugh Or sometimes weep.      What am I?
column2: 聽見我的聲音，男子或陷入遐想，或隨之踏步；聽見我的聲音，女子或展顏而笑，或潸然落淚。      我是什麼？（請以英文作答：「music」）

column2: 她的別名尚有 Astroarche、Attar-Samayin，以及伊絲塔。

column1: The Israelites burned incense, offered wine and baked cakes in her honor.
column2: 以色列人焚香、獻酒、烤製糕餅，以示對她的尊崇。

column1: She had a great shrine at Aphaca.
column2: 她在阿法卡建有一座宏偉的聖殿。

column1: King Solomon built a sanctuary in her honor in Jerusalem.
column2: 所羅門王在耶路撒冷為她建造了一座聖所。

column1: Her priestesses were famous for their skill in astrology.
column2: 她的女祭司以精通占星之術聞名。

column1: She was earlier known as a Goddess in the country of Libya.
column2: 她起初是利比亞人所信奉的女神。

column1: According to Greek legends, she was born from the forehead of Zeus.
column2: 依希臘傳說，她是從宙斯的額頭誕生的。

column1: She was the patron of architects, sculptors, spinners and weavers.
column2: 她是建築師、雕刻家、紡織工與織工的守護神。

column1: The element of brimstone was associated with her.
column2: 硫磺這項元素，與她有所關聯。

column1: The name of her major temple means "virgin-house."
column2: 她主要神殿的名字，意為「處女之屋」。

column1: She was renowned for her wisdom, which was often represented in the form of an owl sitting upon her shoulder.
column2: 她以智慧聞名於世，常以一隻棲於肩頭的貓頭鷹作為象徵。

column1: To the Egyptians, she was known as Hathor.
column2: 埃及人稱她為哈索爾。

column1: Another title for her is Giver of Life.
column2: 她的另一個稱號是「生命的賜予者」。

column1: Another title for her is The One Who Is All.
column2: 她的另一個稱號是「萬物合一者」。

column1: She gave birth to the sun and granted immortality to rulers.
column2: 她誕育了太陽，並賜予統治者不朽之身。

column1: The yearly flood of the Nile was caused by the tears she cried.
column2: 尼羅河的年年氾濫，據說便是她所流下的眼淚所致。

column1: Her priests and servants were knowns as Pastophori.
column2: 她的祭司與侍者被稱為「帕斯托弗里」。

column1: The Romans knew her by the name Aphrodite.
column2: 羅馬人稱她為阿芙羅黛蒂。

column1: Mirrors are considered her sacred objects.
column2: 鏡子被視為她的聖物。

column1: The Morning Star and Evening Star are named for her.
column2: 晨星與昏星，都是以她之名命名。

column1: Her sacred day is Friday on which day her followers would eat fish.
column2: 她的聖日是星期五，信徒會在這天食魚。

column1: Her sacred element is copper.
column2: 她的聖屬元素是銅。

column1: One of her most important shrines was on the island of Cyprus.
column2: 她最重要的聖殿之一，座落於賽普勒斯島。

column1: She was known to the Romans as Hestia.
column2: 羅馬人稱她為赫斯提亞。

column1: In the ancient language of Sanscrit, her name means "shining."
column2: 在古梵語中，她的名字意為「明亮」。

column1: She is the Guardian of Innermost Things.
column2: 她是萬物核心的守護者。

column1: Her sacred fire was tended by six women who took vows of chastity for thirty years.
column2: 她的聖火，由六名發願守貞三十年的女子看管。

column1: Her hearth fire is thought to be the center of the earth.
column2: 她的爐火，被視為大地的中心。

column1: She is the guardian of home and hearth.
column2: 她是家庭與爐灶的守護者。

column1: To the Romans she was known as Mother of the Harvest.
column2: 羅馬人稱她為「豐收之母」。

column1: In Greek, her name was Kore or Demeter.
column2: 在希臘語中，她被稱為柯瑞或狄蜜特。

column1: She was a guardian of grains and the field.
column2: 她是穀物與田野的守護者。

column1: Her major festival was celebrated on April 19th.
column2: 她的重大節慶於四月十九日慶祝。

column1: She was renowned as The Lawgiver and her priestesses helped to found the legal system of Rome.
column2: 她以「立法者」之名著稱，她的女祭司協助奠定了羅馬的法律體系。

column1: Her sacred women were titled Matronae and ruled Rome for hundreds of years.
column2: 她座下的聖女被尊稱為「瑪特羅娜」，統領羅馬達數百年之久。

column1: ST. LEONARD'S FOREST\nIt is said that here the holy hermit, St. Leonard, did slay a most fearsome dragon. Where the saint's blood fell upon the ground, lillies-of-the-valley sprouted and flourished in his honor.
column2: 聖倫納德森林\n傳說在此地，聖潔的隱士聖倫納德曾斬殺一頭極為凶惡的巨龍。聖徒鮮血灑落之處，鈴蘭遂萌芽茂盛，以紀念此事。

column1: WINDSOR\nThese fertile hunting grounds have long been protected by Cernunnos, Celtic god of the underworld. He has large stag's antlers upon his head and wears a golden torc about his neck.
column2: 溫莎\n這片豐饒的獵場，長久以來受凱爾特冥界之神 Cernunnos 所庇護。祂頭上頂著碩大的雄鹿犄角，頸間戴著一只黃金項圈。

column1: OT MOOR\nThough the waters of the moor are not deep, they are reputed to have healing powers. This is where the Lady of the Lake currently dwells. Her wisdom and power rivals my own.
column2: 奧特摩爾\n沼澤之水雖不深，卻據傳具有療癒之力。湖中女神此刻便棲居於此，她的智慧與力量，堪與我匹敵。

column1: AVEBURY\nOn this site stands the largest of the stone circles, the remains of an ancient place of worship. It is surrounded by a bank and ditch with a diameter of 1400 ft. The circle is formed of almost 100 megaliths, some weighing up to 60 tons.
column2: 埃夫伯里\n此地矗立著現存最大的環狀巨石陣，是一處古代祭祀場所的遺跡。四周環繞著一道堤岸與壕溝，直徑達一千四百呎。整座石環由近百塊巨石構成，有些重達六十噸。

column1: MOTTISTONE\nUpon the Isle of Wight, Druid priests are reputed to have sacrificed white bulls. In this place are two great stones: an upright stone representing their God and a horizontal stone representing their Goddess. Mottistone means "the speaker's stone".
column2: 莫蒂斯通\n在懷特島上，德魯伊祭司據傳曾在此獻祭白牛。此地立有兩塊巨石：一塊豎立，代表他們的男神；一塊橫臥，代表他們的女神。「莫蒂斯通」意即「言說者之石」。

column1: BATH\nOver 800 years before the birth of Christ, Prince Bladud, son of a king, contracted the dread disease of leprosy. Unable to remain in human company, he turned to tending swine, but they, too, caught the disease. One day the swine ran wild and plunged into the dark, foul-smelling waters of a bog. When Bladud pulled them out, he discovered that the waters had healed both the animals and himself. The healing waters of Bath are famous to this day.
column2: 巴斯\n在基督誕生前八百多年，一位國王之子——布拉德王子——染上了痲瘋這等可怕的惡疾。他無法再與世人共處，只得去放豬，豬群卻也染上了病。一日，豬群狂奔，一頭栽進一處幽暗惡臭的泥沼水塘。布拉德把牠們拉出來時，發現這水竟同時治好了牲畜與他自己。巴斯的療癒之水，至今仍負盛名。

column1: KEYNSHAM\nA 6th century prince of Wales named Braglan had a daughter named Keyne. She came to a town wherein the lord gave her a piece of land that she might preach Christianity, but the land was heavily infested with large, venomous snakes. She at once turned the snakes into stone. She is remembered as St. Keyne and the town is named after her.
column2: 凱恩沙姆\n六世紀時，威爾斯有位名叫布拉格蘭的親王，育有一女，名喚基恩。她來到一座城鎮，鎮上的領主賜她一塊地，讓她得以傳揚基督信仰，怎料那地毒蛇為患，遍地都是巨大的毒蛇。她當場便將這些毒蛇化為石頭。後人尊她為聖基恩，這座城鎮也以她為名。

column1: WINCHESTER\nI have heard tell that St. Swithun, the bishop of Winchester, is a performer of miracles. One story has come to my ears that he saw a poor woman on her way to a market with a basket of eggs. She bumped into a monk and all her eggs were broken. St. Swithun took pity upon her and made the eggs whole again. Or so they say.
column2: 溫徹斯特\n我聽聞溫徹斯特的主教聖斯威辛，是位能行神蹟之人。有個故事傳到我耳中：他見一名窮苦婦人提著一籃雞蛋要上市集，途中撞上一名僧侶，滿籃雞蛋盡數摔破。聖斯威辛見她可憐，便讓那些蛋一一恢復原狀。至少，傳說是如此。

column1: SOUTHAMPTON\nThe legend goes that Sir Bevis, a hero of long ago, killed the evil giant Ascapart here. This is also the port from which one would take ship to sail to all parts of the known world.
column2: 南安普頓港\n傳說古時的英雄貝維斯爵士，便是在此地殺死了邪惡的巨人阿斯卡帕特。這裡也是啟航前往已知世界各地的港口。

column1: CAMELOT\nYou are here, m'lord, as you surely know.
column2: 肯萊特\n你此刻便身在此處，吾王，這點你自然知曉。

column1: GLASTONBURY TOR\nThis hill has been revered for countless centuries. To the Celts, it was Ynys-Witrin, the Island of Glass, so-called because the lands around it were often flooded. It is also said that Joseph of Arimathea, who supervised the burial of Jesus, brought the Grail here and that where he stuck his staff into the ground, a Holy Thorn tree grew. Many religious orders have since come and gone and left their ruins behind. To reach the tor now, one must travel through the Forest Perilous.
column2: 格列斯登伯利山\n這座山丘歷經無數世紀，備受尊崇。在凱爾特人口中，它喚作「Ynys-Witrin」，意即玻璃島，因四周土地常年遭水淹沒而得名。傳說監督耶穌安葬的亞利馬太的約瑟，曾將聖杯帶到此地；他將手杖插入地面之處，長出了一株聖荊棘樹。此後歷經無數教派興衰，只留下斷垣殘壁。如今要抵達此山，必須穿越派瑞樂斯森林。

column1: SHAPWICK\nSt. Indractus, along with his sister, Drusa and other pilgrims, were passing through here on their way back to Ireland from Rome. They were carrying bags of seed corn to give to the poor. Saxon outlaws murdered them, thinking their bags were filled with gold. The crime was discovered when a beam of light shone for 3 days and 3 nights upon the burial pit. Confronted with their deed, the Saxons went mad and destroyed one another.
column2: 夏普威克\n聖印德拉克圖斯與他的妹妹杜路莎，以及其他朝聖者，當年從羅馬返回愛爾蘭途中，行經此地。他們身上背著要分送給窮人的穀種。撒克遜盜匪誤以為袋中裝的是黃金，將他們盡數殺害。後來一道光芒連續三天三夜照耀在他們的埋屍坑上，罪行方才敗露。撒克遜人得知自己所為之後，發了瘋似地自相殘殺。

column1: HALSTOCK\nA pious woman, St. Juthware, would open her house to pilgrims on their way to a nearby shrine. This so enraged her brother that he took up his sword and cut off her head. The story says that Juthware picked up her own head and carried it to the local altar before she finally died.
column2: 哈爾斯托克\n虔誠的聖裘斯薇兒，總會敞開家門，接待前往附近神龕朝聖的信眾。此事激怒了她的兄長，他拔劍砍下了她的頭顱。傳說裘斯薇兒撿起自己的頭顱，一路帶到當地的祭壇，才終於氣絕身亡。

column1: BRAUNTON\nMany miracles dealing with animals are connected to St. Brannoc, who reportedly sailed from Wales in a stone coffin. A sow and piglets showed him where to establish his chapel. He used wild deer to pull his plough and taught the natives how to till soil. He brought back to life a cow which had been stolen from him, killed and dismembered, but at his call it reassembled itself and returned to give him milk for the rest of its life.
column2: 布勞頓\n許多與動物有關的神蹟，都與聖布拉諾克有關，據說他乘著一具石棺從威爾斯航行而來。一頭母豬與豬崽，為他指出建立教堂之處。他以野鹿拉犁耕田，並教導當地人耕作之法。他有頭母牛被人偷走、宰殺分屍，他一聲呼喚，那頭牛竟重新聚合、復活歸來，此後終其一生都為他產乳。

column1: HARTLAND POINT\nThe original name of this place was the Headland of Hercules, from a legend that Hercules did battle there with British giants. Another legend says that St. Nectan, a Welsh hermit, had his head cut off by robbers, but he carried his head to his well and dropped it in. Foxgloves grew wherever his blood fell.
column2: 哈特蘭角\n此地原名「海克力斯海角」，傳說海克力斯曾在此與不列顛的巨人交戰。另有一則傳說：威爾斯隱士聖尼克坦，遭盜匪砍下頭顱，他卻將自己的頭顱帶到井邊，投入井中。他的血滴落之處，此後都長出了毛地黃。

column1: EXETER\nJust outside this city is a well and a chapel dedicated to St. Sidwell. Sidwell was a girl who had inherited some land that her stepmother wanted. The stepmother hired two men to kill the girl as she prayed in a field. They cut off her head with scythes. The spring gushes forth from the place where her head fell.
column2: 艾克塞特\n這座城市外緣有一口井與一座小教堂，都是為了紀念聖西德威爾而建。西德威爾是名少女，繼承了一塊她繼母覬覦已久的土地。繼母雇了兩名男子，趁她在田間祈禱時將她殺害，用長柄鐮刀砍下她的頭顱。她頭顱落地之處，如今仍有泉水湧出。

column1: TOTNES\nLong ago a Trojan warrior named Brutus arrived and named this place Totnes. The story goes that he said: 'Here I am and here I rest, and this town shall be called Totnes.' He subdued two giants, Gog and Magog, and made them stand guard at his palace. Brutus is considered the legendary founder of London.
column2: 托特尼斯\n古時有位名叫布魯特斯的特洛伊勇士來到此地，將此處命名為托特尼斯。傳說他曾言：『我在此地落腳，在此地安歇，這座城鎮便叫做托特尼斯。』他降服了歌革與瑪各兩名巨人，命他們在自己的宮殿前守衛。布魯特斯被尊為倫敦的傳說創建者。
